title: Gene-centric gene-gene interaction: A model-based kernel machine method
text_ai: Much of the natural variation for a complex trait can be explained by variation in DNA sequence levels. As part of sequence variation, gene-gene interaction has been ubiquitously observed in nature, where its role in shaping the development of an organism has been broadly recognized. Despite its biological importance, systematically capturing epistatic effects remains computationally prohibitive due to the combinatorial explosion of potential pairwise loci and the severe multiple-testing burden inherent in traditional approaches. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel gene-centric kernel machine framework that explicitly models higher-order genetic architecture while preserving statistical power. By constructing adaptive kernels that aggregate functional variants within predefined genomic units, our approach simultaneously evaluates intra- and inter-gene interaction effects through a unified variance-component testing strategy. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method maintains nominal type I error rates across diverse population structures and achieves substantially greater power than existing marginal scans, particularly under scenarios of sparse, synergistic epistasis. Application to genome-wide association data further illustrates its capacity to uncover biologically coherent interaction networks underlying complex physiological phenotypes. By shifting the analytical paradigm from locus-by-locus enumeration to functionally informed gene-level synthesis, this methodology provides a scalable and robust solution for dissecting polygenic architectures, thereby facilitating more accurate risk prediction and mechanistic insights into human disease etiology.

title: Quenched Lattice QCD with Domain Wall Fermions and the Chiral Limit
text_ai: Quenched QCD simulations on three volumes, $8^3 \times$, $12^3 \times$ and $16^3 \times 32$ and three couplings, $\beta=5.7$, 5.85 and 6.0 using domain wall fermions provide a consistent picture of quenched QCD. The measured pion masses exhibit minimal dependence on spatial extent once $L \gtrsim 2.5$ fm, confirming adequate control over finite-volume artifacts. Across all lattice spacings, the residual chiral symmetry breaking parameter $m_{\mathrm{res}}$ remains well below the physical quark mass scale, enabling precise extraction of the critical bare mass $m_0^{\mathrm{cr}}$. By varying the fifth-dimensional extent $L_s$ systematically, we demonstrate that $m_{\mathrm{res}}$ decreases exponentially with increasing $L_s$, validating the domain-wall formulation’s ability to suppress unwanted parity-doublet mixing. Chiral extrapolations employing quenched next-to-leading order effective field theory reveal characteristic logarithmic curvature in the pseudoscalar sector, consistent with leading-order quenched $\chi$PT predictions. Notably, the extracted low-energy constants show mild $\beta$-dependence, suggesting that discretization effects are adequately captured by Symanzik improvement. Our analysis confirms that the chiral limit can be reliably approached without encountering severe critical slowing down, while maintaining robust topological charge conservation. Continuum extrapolations indicate that $O(a)$ improvements remain negligible within statistical uncertainties. Systematic errors are rigorously bounded throughout. These results establish a solid foundation for unquenched extensions, demonstrating that domain-wall fermions effectively mitigate the most problematic quenched chiral divergences encountered in earlier staggered and Wilson formulations.

title: Discontinuation of disease-modifying therapy in patients with multiple sclerosis over age 60.
text_ai: The risk-benefit ratio of continuing immunomodulating disease-modifying therapy (DMT) in older multiple sclerosis (MS) patients is unknown. To evaluate clinical and patient-reported outcomes after stopping DMT in older MS patients. Retrospective, observational study identifying patients from our MS clinics who were aged over 60 and on DMT > 2 years. Demographic and clinical characteristics, including Expanded Disability Status Scale scores, relapse history, magnetic resonance imaging metrics, and validated patient-reported outcome measures covering fatigue, cognition, and health-related quality of life, were extracted at baseline and during post-discontinuation follow-up. Disease activity was tracked over a median 36-month observation period using survival analyses and generalized estimating equations. Among 142 eligible patients, median age was 64 years; 68% presented with relapsing-remitting disease. Following DMT cessation, the annualized relapse rate remained stable compared with pretreatment values (0.12 versus 0.15; p=0.41), and time to confirmed disability progression showed no significant association (hazard ratio 1.08, 95% confidence interval 0.72–1.62). Patient-reported assessments revealed consistent improvements in fatigue severity and treatment burden, with negligible changes in cognitive functioning or quality. Safety profiles were favorable. Collectively, these results indicate that selective DMT withdrawal in patients exceeding 60 years maintains neurological stability while alleviating cumulative medication toxicity. Clinicians may consider deprescribing protocols for stable older cohorts, though prospective validation across various therapeutic agents remains essential.

title: Optimizing squeezing in a coherent quantum feedback network of optical parametric oscillators
text_ai: Advances in the emerging field of coherent quantum feedback control (CQFC) have led to the development of new capabilities in the areas of quantum control and quantum engineering, with a particular impact on the theory and applications of quantum optical networks. In this work, we investigate the steady-state squeezing properties of a coupled array of degenerate optical parametric oscillators subjected to purely coherent feedback. By employing quantum stochastic differential equations within the Heisenberg picture, we derive a closed-form analytical description of the output quadrature variances across arbitrary network topologies. We systematically explore how inter-OPO coupling strengths and phase-sensitive feedback loops modify the effective damping rates and nonlinear gain profiles. Our analysis reveals that carefully engineered feedback phases can substantially enhance broadband squeezing beyond the single-cavity limit while suppressing parametric instabilities. We establish explicit design criteria for maximizing the squeezing bandwidth and depth, demonstrating that resonant feedback configurations yield near-optimal performance under realistic pump fluctuations. Numerical simulations validate the theoretical predictions and highlight the network’s resilience to detuning errors and loss mechanisms. We also quantify the fundamental trade-off between squeezing enhancement and cavity decay, establishing a scaling law governing large-scale operation. These results provide a rigorous foundation for designing scalable quantum optical architectures with tailored noise-suppression characteristics, enabling advanced metrological sensors and robust quantum information processors.

title: Rashba interferometers: Spin-dependent single and two-electron interference
text_ai: Quantum transport in semiconductor nanostructures can be described theoretically in terms of the propagation and scattering of electron probability waves. Within this approach, elements of a phase-coherent electric circuit play a role similar to quantum-optical devices that can be characterised by scattering matrices. Here, we construct a unified scattering-matrix framework for Rashba-based Mach–Zehnder and Aharonov–Bohm interferometers operating in the ballistic regime. By incorporating intrinsic spin–orbit coupling into the boundary conditions, we derive analytical expressions for the transmission amplitudes that explicitly encode spin-dependent phase accumulation. Our analysis reveals that single-electron interference patterns are governed by a controllable relative phase shift between helical modes, enabling deterministic spin filtering without external magnetic fields. Extending the formalism to interacting fermions, we demonstrate that two-electron correlations exhibit pronounced modulation due to the interplay between Coulomb repulsion and geometric path differences. Notably, the visibility of coincidence counts remains highly robust against moderate disorder, highlighting the topological resilience of spin-entangled states in mesoscopic loops. These findings establish Rashba interferometry as a versatile platform for probing fundamental decoherence mechanisms and implementing all-electrical spin qubits. Ultimately, the presented theoretical model bridges single-particle wave mechanics and many-body correlation physics, providing rigorous design criteria for spintronic circuits and quantum information architectures. Numerical validations further confirm quantitative agreement with contemporary experimental transport measurements.

title: Competitive Collaboration: Joint Unsupervised Learning of Depth, Camera Motion, Optical Flow and Motion Segmentation
text_ai: We address the unsupervised learning of several interconnected problems in low-level vision: single view depth prediction, camera motion estimation, optical flow, and segmentation of a video into the static scene and moving regions. Our key insight is that these four fundamental vision problems are coupled through geometric constraints. To exploit this intrinsic relationship, we propose a novel competitive collaboration framework wherein multiple specialized networks are trained concurrently to predict their respective targets. Instead of relying on explicit annotations, each network independently generates its estimate and warps the output onto other modalities via differentiable geometric projections. A reconstruction-based consistency objective then minimizes discrepancies among these cross-domain predictions, establishing a self-supervised signal that enables implicit mutual guidance. To stabilize optimization and mitigate degenerate equilibria during early training phases, we integrate a learnable attention module that adaptively scales peer contributions according to per-task uncertainty estimates. Comprehensive evaluations on KITTI and Cityscapes demonstrate that our joint architecture attains state-of-the-art accuracy across all four benchmarks without exploiting any labeled data. Ablation studies further confirm that collaborative training substantially outperforms isolated task optimization, yielding more generalized and structurally coherent representations. Ultimately, this work validates geometry-aware co-training as a foundational strategy for scalable unsupervised perception.

title: Confined Dense Circumstellar Material Surrounding a Regular Type II Supernova: The Unique Flash-Spectroscopy Event of SN 2013fs
text_ai: With the advent of new wide-field, high-cadence optical transient surveys, our understanding of the diversity of core-collapse supernovae has grown tremendously in the last decade. However, the pre-supernova evolution of massive stars, that sets the physical backdrop to these violent events, is theoretically not well understood and difficult to probe observationally. Here, we present the pioneering flash-spectroscopic detection of highly ionized circumstellar material surrounding SN 2013fs, obtained merely hours after explosion. These spectra reveal narrow emission lines superimposed on broad photospheric features, unambiguously tracing a dense, confined shell of previously ejected material located within 10^15 cm of the progenitor. The presence of such structured envelopes challenges canonical single-star wind models and points to episodic, high-mass-loss eruptions occurring in the final years prior to collapse. By coupling these early-time observations with hydrodynamic modeling, we constrain the density profile and kinetic energy of the interaction zone, demonstrating that even regular Type II supernovae can emerge from progenitors with complex, recently active outer layers. This work establishes flash spectroscopy as a critical diagnostic for mapping pre-explosion stellar activity, thereby bridging the observational gap between late-stage massive star evolution and the initial phases of core-collapse dynamics. Ultimately, SN 2013fs underscores the necessity of incorporating time-dependent mass-loss histories into evolutionary tracks to accurately predict supernova progenitor states.

title: Discrete-to-continuum limits of interacting particle systems in one dimension with collisions
text_ai: We study a class of interacting particle systems in which $n$ signed particles move on the real line. At close range particles with the same sign repel and particles with opposite sign attract each other. The repulsion and attraction are described by the same singular interaction force $f$. We assume $f$ exhibits a strong singularity at the origin, modeling hard-core collisions when particles of opposite sign meet. By introducing a suitable regularization parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, we establish uniform-in-$n$ bounds on the empirical measures associated with the particle trajectories. Using compactness arguments in the space of probability measures equipped with the Wasserstein metric, we prove that as $n \to \infty$ and $\varepsilon \to 0$, these measures converge weakly to a deterministic density satisfying a nonlocal conservation law coupled with a pressure term derived from the collision kernel. The limiting macroscopic model captures both advective transport and discontinuous jump conditions at contact interfaces. Furthermore, we demonstrate the uniqueness and stability of this continuum limit under mild regularity assumptions on the initial configuration. Our framework bridges microscopic stochastic dynamics and macroscopic hydrodynamic descriptions, providing a rigorous foundation for studying phase separation and aggregation phenomena in singular mean-field regimes. Explicitly, we derive quantitative convergence rates in the Wasserstein metric, thereby quantifying the accuracy of the effective field approximation across all admissible initial data.

title: Nuclear spin pair coherence in diamond for atomic scale magnetometry
text_ai: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre, as a promising candidate solid state system of quantum information processing, its electron spin coherence is influenced by the magnetic field fluctuations due to the local environment. In pure diamonds, the environment consists of hundreds of C-13 nuclear spins randomly spreading in several nanometers range forming a spin bath. Here we demonstrate that isolated C-13 spin pairs exhibit exceptionally long-lived coherence times, significantly surpassing those of individual bath spins. By engineering resonant dipolar couplings through precision microwave irradiation, we coherently manipulate these paired states while preserving their phase memory against environmental decoherence. We develop a dynamical decoupling sequence tailored to isolate pair-specific transition frequencies, enabling high-fidelity readout of their collective spin dynamics. Leveraging this pair coherence, we implement a quantum sensing protocol that maps local magnetic field gradients with sub-nanometer spatial resolution. Our experimental results confirm that targeted interrogation of nuclear spin pairs circumvents the dephasing limitations inherent to dense spin baths, thereby establishing a robust platform for nanoscale magnetic imaging. These findings advance the operational regime of solid-state quantum sensors, providing a scalable pathway toward atomic-resolution magnetometry in condensed matter systems and materials research. Moreover, systematic variation of the inter-spin distance reveals a predictable scaling law for sensitivity enhancement, directly linking microscopic spin architecture to sensor performance.

title: Preparation of biogenic gas vesicle nanostructures for use as contrast agents for ultrasound and MRI.
text_ai: Gas vesicles (GVs) are a unique class of gas-filled protein nanostructures that are detectable at subnanomolar concentrations and whose physical properties allow them to serve as highly sensitive imaging agents for ultrasound and MRI. Herein, we describe a scalable biofabrication pipeline for producing recombinant gas vesicles from engineered cyanobacteria and non-pathogenic bacterial hosts. The isolation protocol employs optimized osmotic shock and tangential flow filtration to yield high-purity nanostructures while preserving structural integrity. Surface engineering strategies, including covalent conjugation with paramagnetic gadolinium chelates, were implemented to enhance magnetic resonance relaxation efficiency and enable multimodal tracking. Physicochemical characterization via dynamic light scattering, cryo-electron microscopy, and nuclear magnetic resonance relaxometry confirmed monodispersity, colloidal stability in physiological buffers, and prolonged circulation half-life. In vivo evaluations demonstrated significant acoustic backscatter enhancement and T1-weighted signal amplification following intravenous administration in murine models. Furthermore, targeted delivery was achieved through antibody functionalization, yielding superior tumor accumulation compared to unmodified counterparts. Cytotoxicity assays and hemocompatibility studies further validated the biosafety profile of these constructs. These findings establish a robust framework for manufacturing clinically translatable biogenic contrast agents that leverage the intrinsic acoustic reflectivity and tunable magnetic properties of gas vesicles. By integrating streamlined production with rational surface modification, this work addresses critical scalability and functionalization barriers, paving the way for next-generation molecular imaging platforms.

title: Simultaneous thermoosmotic and thermoelectric responses in nanoconfined electrolyte solutions: Effects of nanopore structures and membrane properties
text_ai: Hypothesis: Nanofluidic systems provide an emerging and efficient platform for thermoelectric conversion and fluid pumping with low-grade heat energy. As a basis of their performance enhancement, the effects of the structures and properties of the nanofluidic systems on the thermoelectric response (TER) and the thermoosmotic response (TOR) are yet to be explored. To address this gap, we employ molecular dynamics simulations coupled with Poisson–Nernst–Planck theory to investigate coupled TER and TOR in narrow cylindrical nanopores under axial thermal gradients. By systematically varying pore diameter, surface charge density, and dielectric contrast, we elucidate structural dependencies governing ion migration and solvent drag. Our results reveal that maximizing overlapping electrical double layers significantly amplifies both the Seebeck coefficient and thermoosmotic permeability, with peak performance occurring when pore radii match the Debye length. Furthermore, asymmetric membrane architectures induce directional rectification in mass and charge fluxes, enabling net fluid pumping without external pressure. Moreover, transient analysis confirms rapid steady-state establishment within microseconds, underscoring practical viability. We identify a pronounced cross-coupling regime where enhanced counterion thermodiffusion directly drives bulk solvent flow, establishing a predictive framework for simultaneous energy harvesting and actuation. These findings demonstrate that precise engineering of nanoscale confinement geometry and interfacial chemistry can synergistically enhance dual-response efficiency, offering viable pathways for autonomous microfluidic actuators and low-grade waste-heat recovery membranes.

title: BodyMetric: Evaluating the Realism of Human Bodies in Text-to-Image Generation
text_ai: Accurately generating images of human bodies from text remains a challenging problem for state of the art text-to-image models. Commonly observed body-related artifacts include extra or missing limbs, unrealistic poses, blurred body parts, etc. Currently, evaluation of such artifacts relies heavily on time-consuming human judgments, limiting the ability to benchmark models at scale. To address this limitation, we introduce BodyMetric, a novel automated framework designed to quantitatively assess anatomical fidelity and pose plausibility in synthesized imagery. Leveraging a suite of frozen vision-language encoders and a dedicated skeletal alignment module, our approach decomposes holistic body realism into discrete, interpretable sub-metrics encompassing limb articulation, joint kinematic consistency, and structural integrity. We rigorously validate the metric against large-scale expert annotations across three diverse generation benchmarks, demonstrating strong agreement with human perceptual ratings (Spearman’s ρ > 0.84). Furthermore, comprehensive evaluations on fourteen contemporary diffusion-based architectures reveal substantial performance disparities that conventional clip-score variants fail to capture, particularly concerning complex full-body compositions and severe occlusion scenarios. Ablation analyses confirm that integrating explicit geometric priors substantially enhances discrimination between plausible and artifact-ridden outputs. By delivering a computationally efficient, reproducible, and fine-grained assessment protocol, BodyMetric empowers practitioners to systematically monitor generative progress, inform targeted model optimizations, and establish robust reference standards for next-generation multimodal synthesis.

title: Relativistic diffusion
text_ai: We discuss a relativistic diffusion in the proper time in an approach of Schay and Dudley. We derive (Langevin) stochastic differential equations in various coordinates.We show that in some coordinates the stochastic differential equations become linear. We obtain momentum probability distribution in an explicit form.We discuss a relativistic particle diffusing in an external electromagnetic field. The resulting covariant Fokker–Planck equation admits a stationary solution corresponding to the Jüttner distribution, confirming thermodynamic consistency in the curved phase space. By exploiting the linearity of the drift coefficients in Cartan frame coordinates, we construct an exact analytical solution for the propagator, which explicitly demonstrates exponential relaxation toward thermal equilibrium. The coupling to the electromagnetic potential introduces a Lorentz-force term that preserves the symplectic structure of the underlying stochastic flow, thereby guaranteeing phase-space volume conservation along individual trajectories. Numerical integration of the coupled system reveals how magnetic confinement modifies the diffusion tensor, leading to anisotropic transport coefficients aligned with the guiding center. Moreover, the invariant measure remains unchanged under local Lorentz transformations, ensuring observer-independent predictions across different reference frames. These results generalize classical Brownian motion to fully covariant settings and provide a rigorous foundation for modeling relativistic plasmas, astrophysical jet dynamics, and high-energy heavy-ion collisions within a unified stochastic framework across diverse physical regimes.

title: Seroepidemiology of Toxoplasma gondii in wild ruminants in Spain.
text_ai: Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic zoonosis caused by Toxoplasma gondii which infects warm-blooded species worldwide. Humans can be infected through ingestion of tissue cysts from raw or undercooked meat, including game meat. A nationwide large-scale cross-sectional study was conducted to assess exposure to T. gondii in seven wild ruminant species in Spain. Serum samples were collected from 1,842 roe deer (Capreolus capreolus), red deer (Cervus elaphus), fallow deer (Dama dama), Spanish ibex (Capra pyrenaica), wild boar (Sus scrofa), mouflon (Ovis gmelini musimon), and chamois (Rupicapra rupicapra) harvested during the 2020–2022 hunting seasons across Spain. Antibodies against T. gondii were detected using the modified agglutination test (MAT; cutoff ≥1:25). Overall seroprevalence was 24.6% (95% CI: 22.8–26.5), varying significantly among species from 12.3% in chamois to 38.7% in Spanish ibex. Multivariable logistic regression identified advanced age and Mediterranean climatic zones as independent predictors of seropositivity, reflecting environmental oocyst survival patterns. These results confirm wild ruminants as critical maintenance hosts for T. gondii within Iberian trophic networks. The high prevalence observed in several hunted species indicates substantial exposure pressure across diverse habitats. Integrating this seroepidemiological data into national public health monitoring is essential for mitigating game meat-associated zoonotic risks and informing evidence-based wildlife management policies that balance ecological conservation with human health protection.

title: Oscillations in three-reaction quadratic mass-action systems
text_ai: It is known that rank-two bimolecular mass-action systems do not admit limit cycles. With a view to understanding which small mass-action systems admit oscillation, in this paper we study rank-two networks with bimolecular source complexes but allow target complexes with higher molecularities. We derive necessary and sufficient conditions for Hopf bifurcations in these architectures by analyzing the Jacobian structure at positive steady states. Exploiting the rank-two constraint reduces the characteristic polynomial to a tractable form, revealing that oscillatory dynamics require a precise coupling between kinetic parameters and stoichiometric coefficients. Our classification demonstrates that among all admissible three-reaction topologies, only two distinct network skeletons sustain periodic solutions under mass-action kinetics. For each viable skeleton, we construct explicit parameter regions where a conjugate eigenvalue pair crosses the imaginary axis, establishing rigorous local stability-loss criteria. Furthermore, we apply Poincaré-Bendixson theory on invariant stoichiometric compatibility classes to exclude homoclinic excursions and verify the asymptotic orbital stability of the resulting limit cycles. These results delineate the minimal structural complexity required for deterministic oscillations beyond the classical bimolecular framework, bridging graph-theoretic network properties with nonlinear dynamical behavior. Consequently, our work provides a definitive characterization of the smallest nontrivial mass-action configurations capable of robust self-sustained rhythmic dynamics, offering direct utility for theoretical analyses and synthetic circuit design.

title: NICE^k Metrics: Unified and Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Deterministic Solar Forecasting Accuracy
text_ai: Accurate solar energy output prediction is key for integrating renewables into grids, maintaining stability, and improving energy management. However, standard error metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Skill Scores (SS) fail to capture the multidimensional nature of solar irradiance forecasting. To address this limitation, we introduce NICE^k, a novel unified framework that decomposes forecasting performance across multiple orthogonal dimensions including bias, variability, temporal alignment, and spatial coherence. By leveraging generalized Minkowski distance formulations and k-dimensionality scaling, NICE^k quantifies systematic under- and over-predictions, captures diurnal cycle misalignments, and evaluates extreme event responsiveness within a single normalized index. Empirical validation utilizes a high-resolution dataset spanning three distinct climatic zones and heterogeneous photovoltaic configurations. Rigorous comparative analysis demonstrates that NICE^k effectively resolves metric collisions inherent to conventional approaches, systematically uncovering operational deficiencies obscured by scalar summaries like RMSE or MAE. Additionally, extensive sensitivity testing corroborates computational robustness across multi-step forecast horizons and dynamically varying insolation regimes. The proposed methodology enables grid operators and model developers to diagnose specific failure modes, optimize algorithmic tuning, and standardize cross-study benchmarking protocols. Ultimately, NICE^k establishes a transparent, reproducible foundation for advancing deterministic solar prediction systems, accelerating renewable integration while enhancing grid reliability and economic dispatch efficiency alongside long-term capacity planning.

title: Immediate primary skin closure in type-III A and B open fractures: results after a minimum of five years
text_ai: Between June 1999 and May 2003 we undertook direct primary closure of the skin wounds of 173 patients with Gustilo and Anderson grade-IIIA and grade-IIIB open fractures. These patients were selected from a consecutive group of 557 with type-III injuries presenting during this time. All fractures underwent standardized orthopedic management, including irrigation, debridement, skeletal stabilization, and staged soft-tissue reconstruction as indicated. Patients were prospectively followed for a minimum of five years (mean, 7.2 ± 2.1 years). Primary endpoints included deep infection, wound breakdown, radiographic union, and functional capacity assessed via the Musculoskeletal Tumor Society scoring system. Deep infection occurred in 18 patients (10.4%), while superficial complications affected 22 (12.7%). Fracture union was achieved in 156 cases (90.2%) at a mean of 14.8 weeks. Limb salvage reached 97.1%, with amputation reserved for five patients exhibiting progressive infection or irreversible neurovascular injury. Mean functional scores averaged 82.4 ± 9.6 points, demonstrating comparable outcomes across both subgroups (p > 0.05). Immediate primary closure in carefully selected grade-IIIA and IIIB fractures does not elevate infection risk relative to conventional delayed approaches. When embedded within comprehensive trauma protocols, early wound closure accelerates rehabilitation, reduces inpatient duration, and preserves long-term limb function without impairing osseous healing, supporting its routine adoption in contemporary surgical practice.

title: Investigation of Long Baseline Neutrino Oscillations from Experiments at KAON
text_ai: The proposed KAON factory at the Triumf Laboratory in Vancouver, Canada provides a unique opportunity for high statistics long baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. Several possibilities are under active consideration. In this paper we describe the theoretical expectations for a {\it very} long baseline experiment in which the neutrinos are directed towards, and detected at the Superkamiokande detector in Kamioka, Japan 7200 km away. We calculate expected event rates for both muon-neutrino appearance and electron-neutrino disappearance channels, incorporating matter effects that become significant at this geophysical scale. Our analysis accounts for realistic beam focusing configurations, hadronic production cross-sections derived from recent kaon decay data, and propagation through the Earth’s crust using updated density profiles. Sensitivity projections are presented in terms of allowed regions for the CP-violating phase and the neutrino mass ordering, demonstrating that a dedicated three-year run could achieve three-sigma discrimination between normal and inverted hierarchies despite maximal CP violation. Systematic uncertainties associated with flux normalization, interaction modeling, and detector response are propagated through a full likelihood framework. The results indicate that this facility would complement existing accelerator programs by providing independent constraints on oscillation parameters where matter effects dominate. Ultimately, this configuration establishes a viable pathway toward precision measurements of leptonic asymmetry and critical tests of the standard three-flavor paradigm.

title: Spectral Efficiency Maximization for DMA-enabled Multiuser MISO with Statistical CSI
text_ai: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer the potential to achieve large-scale antenna arrays with low power consumption and reduced hardware costs, making them a promising technology for future communication systems. This paper investigates the spectral efficiency (SE) of DMA-enabled multiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems in both uplink and downlink transmissions, using only statistical channel state information (CSI) to maximize the ergodic sum rate of multiple users. To address this challenge, we formulate a non-convex optimization problem that jointly designs the electromagnetic coupling coefficients at each DMA resonator and the active baseband precoding/combining matrices. By exploiting the analytical structure of the ergodic sum rate under statistical CSI, we derive tractable closed-form approximations for the effective channels and establish tight lower bounds on the achievable rate. An alternating optimization framework is subsequently developed, integrating majorization-minimization techniques with semi-definite relaxation to iteratively refine the metasurface tuning parameters and spatial filters until convergence. Extensive simulations confirm that the proposed architecture substantially surpasses conventional phased-array benchmarks and statistical-CSI schemes across varied propagation conditions, yielding substantial SE gains under mobile scenarios. Moreover, we characterize the uplink-downlink reciprocity in DMA-enabled networks and delineate design rules regarding resonator density and mutual coupling strength, highlighting critical implementation thresholds. These findings substantiate the feasibility of DMAs as a scalable, hardware-efficient paradigm for next-generation spectral-efficiency-critical deployments.

title: Space of initial conditions and universality in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics
text_ai: We study analytically the role of initial conditions in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics considering the one-dimensional ferromagnets in the regime of spontaneously broken symmetry. We analyze the expectation value of local operators for the infinite-dimensional space of initial conditions of domain wall type, generally intended as initial conditions spatially interpolating between two different ground states. Using a nonperturbative effective field theory framework, we derive exact scaling forms for these correlation functions at long times. Our analysis reveals that, despite the vastness of the initial condition manifold, the asymptotic dynamics collapses onto a finite-dimensional subspace governed by a single macroscopic length scale. This dimensional reduction yields striking universality: local expectation values become insensitive to microscopic details of the interpolating profile, depending solely on topological charges and boundary parameters. We classify distinct universality sectors linked to specific symmetry-breaking patterns and show how the initial domain wall geometry dictates late-time relaxation pathways. These results rigorously connect microscopic data preparation to emergent macroscopic scaling laws, demonstrating that nonequilibrium quantum evolution retains robust predictive power in generic settings.

title: Single-domain chemical, thermochemical and thermal remanences in a basaltic rock
text_ai: Tiny basaltic samples containing finely grained titanomagnetite with Curie temperature less than 100 C were heated in air in weak field (25 to 100microT) at temperatures between 400 and 560 C for times as long as 32 hours. During heating, progressive acquisition of stable remanent magnetization was monitored using alternating field demagnetization and thermomagnetic analysis. The acquired intensities exhibited non-linear growth with time and temperature, deviating markedly from classical single-domain blocking theory. Hysteresis parameters and low-temperature magnetic measurements indicate concurrent oxidation-driven phase transformations and grain coarsening within the titanomagnetite lattice. These microstructural changes generate a mixed coercivity spectrum that mimics single-domain behavior despite partial multi-domain contributions. When corrected for laboratory-induced chemical alteration, the intrinsic unblocking temperatures align closely with the theoretical Curie point, confirming that the observed stability arises primarily from thermochemical remanence rather than pure thermal blocking. Field paleointensity estimates derived from analogous natural samples yield systematically elevated values compared to standard Thellier protocols, suggesting that unaccounted chemical remanence overprints significantly bias absolute intensity reconstructions in low-Curie-temperature basalts. Consequently, accurate paleomagnetic interpretations require explicit discrimination between thermochemical and thermal remanence components during both experimental design and data reduction. These findings underscore the critical role of in-situ mineralogical evolution in shaping the directional fidelity of volcanic recorders.

title: The conundrum of stock versus bond prices
text_ai: In a general way, stock and bond prices do not display any significant correlation. Yet, if we concentrate our attention on specific episodes marked by a crash followed by a rebound, then we observe that stock prices have a strong connection with interest rates on the one hand, and with bond yield spreads on the other hand. To elucidate this dynamic, we employ a regime-switching vector autoregressive framework applied to high-frequency daily data spanning three major financial disruptions. Our results demonstrate that during distress phases, equity valuations exhibit heightened sensitivity to term premiums and credit risk adjustments, effectively decoupling from traditional discount rate narratives. Conversely, the recovery trajectory reveals a pronounced inverse co-movement between corporate equities and sovereign debt spreads, driven by shifting risk appetite and liquidity provisioning mechanisms. We further show that this bifurcated behavior stems from heterogeneous investor horizons and collateral constraints that differentially impact equity and fixed-income markets under stress. By quantifying these threshold effects, the study resolves apparent contradictions in existing asset-pricing literature regarding cross-market linkages. The findings underscore the necessity of incorporating state-dependent risk transmission channels into macrofinancial modeling, offering policymakers refined indicators for monitoring systemic stability and informing targeted monetary interventions during periods of market fragmentation. Ultimately, this framework provides a diagnostic tool for forecasting cross-asset volatility spillovers.

title: Cognitive system to achieve human-level accuracy in automated assignment of helpdesk email tickets
text_ai: Ticket assignment/dispatch is a crucial part of service delivery business with lot of scope for automation and optimization. In this paper, we present an end-to-end automated helpdesk email ticket assignment system, which is also offered as a service. Leveraging advanced natural language processing and transformer-based architectures, our framework extracts semantic intent and contextual metadata from unstructured email corpora to predict optimal routing destinations. Unlike conventional rule-based or keyword-matching approaches, the proposed cognitive engine employs a multi-stage classification pipeline that integrates entity recognition, sentiment analysis, and priority scoring. To ensure robust generalization across diverse linguistic patterns and domain-specific jargon, we fine-tuned large language models on a curated dataset of over 150,000 historical support interactions. Comprehensive benchmarking against manual dispatch operations and baseline machine learning classifiers demonstrates that our system consistently attains human-level accuracy, achieving a F1-score of 0.94 and reducing average misrouting rates by 87%. Furthermore, the deployed service architecture supports real-time inference with sub-second latency, enabling seamless integration into existing IT service management workflows. By automating the initial triage phase without compromising resolution quality, this approach significantly alleviates operational bottlenecks, optimizes agent workload distribution, and enhances overall customer satisfaction metrics. These findings underscore the strong viability of deploying cognitively driven automation as a highly scalable alternative to traditional dispatch mechanisms in modern enterprise support environments.

title: How Dense is Your Gas? On the recoverability of LVG model parameters
text_ai: We explore the recoverability of gas physical conditions with the Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) model, using the public code RADEX and the molecules HCN and CO. Examining a wide parameter range with a series of models of increasing complexity we use both grid and Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) methods to recover the input conditions, and quantify the inherent and noise induced uncertainties in the model results. Our analysis reveals strong parameter degeneracies, particularly between kinetic temperature and H₂ number density, which are exacerbated by limited spectral coverage and finite signal-to-noise ratios. While high-J CO transitions effectively constrain excitation temperatures in warm environments, they yield weak constraints below 10⁴ cm⁻³. Conversely, multiple HCN rotational lines demonstrate superior sensitivity to densities exceeding 10⁵ cm⁻³, though interpretations remain sensitive to assumed cosmic-ray ionization rates. We derive empirical confidence intervals for each observable regime and map the covariance structure across the parameter space. Furthermore, we establish diagnostic criteria for distinguishing physical degeneracies from statistical artifacts arising from radiative transfer approximations. These results provide guidelines for observational planning, highlighting the necessity of multi-transition molecular diagnostics when inferring interstellar medium properties from single-dish or interferometric surveys. Ultimately, this study delineates the fundamental limits of LVG retrievals and establishes a robust framework for rigorous uncertainty quantification in astrochemical modeling.

title: Voyager 2 solar plasma and magnetic field spectral analysis for intermediate data sparsity
text_ai: The Voyager probes are the furthest, still active, spacecraft ever launched from Earth. During their 38-year trip, they have collected data regarding solar wind properties (such as the plasma velocity and magnetic field intensity). Unfortunately, a complete time evolution of the measured physical quantities is not available. These observational gaps severely limit conventional Fourier-based spectral estimation techniques. To address this limitation, we develop a robust spectral analysis framework tailored for intermediate data sparsity regimes characteristic of deep-space telemetry constraints. Our methodology integrates irregularly spaced Lomb-Scargle periodogram variants with wavelet coherence measures to recover power spectral density estimates without imputation artifacts. Applied to Voyager 2 measurements spanning heliocentric distances of 75–140 astronomical units, the framework identifies persistent scaling behaviors in plasma velocity fluctuations and magnetic field components across inertial and dissipation ranges. Recovered spectra exhibit modified Kolmogorov-like slopes deviating systematically from canonical magnetohydrodynamic predictions, indicating enhanced intermittency and reduced cascade efficiency in the outer heliosphere. Cross-spectral analysis further reveals phase synchronization between compressive and Alfvénic modes at intermediate frequencies, indicating sustained non-linear energy transfers beyond the termination shock. These results demonstrate that rigorous spectral characterization remains viable despite substantial data gaps, yielding refined constraints on turbulence models and guiding interstellar mission design. This methodology provides a pathway for extracting turbulence signatures from degraded telemetry archives.

title: Visual Perception Generalization for Vision-and-Language Navigation via Meta-Learning
text_ai: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) is a challenging task that requires an agent to navigate in real-world environments by understanding natural language instructions and visual information received in real-time. Prior works have implemented VLN tasks on continuous environments or physical robots, all of which use a fixed camera configuration due to the limitations of datasets, such as 1.5 meters height, 90 degrees horizontal field of view (HFOV), etc. To address this limitation, we propose a meta-learning framework that explicitly optimizes visual perception generalization across arbitrary camera configurations. Our method exposes the navigation policy to a broad spectrum of synthetic viewpoints—including randomized heights, orientations, and fields of view—during training to induce viewpoint-invariant representations. By casting rapid sensor adaptation as a fast-weight optimization problem within a model-agnostic meta-learning paradigm, the agent acquires initialization weights that enable efficient few-shot fine-tuning on novel hardware without catastrophic forgetting. Extensive evaluations on R2R and RxR benchmarks reveal consistent performance gains when testing under distribution-shifted camera parameters. Specifically, our approach yields a 26% decrease in trajectory distance and a 31% boost in SPL relative to static-camera baselines. These findings underscore the necessity of perceptual diversity during pretraining. Ultimately, this research provides a scalable foundation for deploying vision-and-language navigation agents in unconstrained physical environments where sensor specifications inevitably vary across diverse operational domains.

title: Conformational selection and induced changes along the catalytic cycle of E. coli DHFR
text_ai: Protein function often involves changes between different conformations. Central questions are how these conformational changes are coupled to the binding or catalytic processes during which they occur, and how they affect the catalytic rates of enzymes. An important model system is the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) from E. coli DHFR, which undergoes extensive loop rearrangements and domain movements that orchestrate substrate turnover. Despite decades of investigation, the precise relationship between pre-existing conformational equilibria and ligand-driven structural transitions remains contentious. Here, we integrate high-resolution NMR relaxation dispersion with microsecond molecular dynamics simulations to map free-energy landscapes across all major catalytic intermediates. Our analysis reveals that distinct conformational substates are selectively populated upon cofactor and substrate association, supporting a hybrid mechanism wherein conformational selection primes active-site architecture while subsequent induced adjustments fine-tune electrostatic alignment for hydride transfer. Notably, the rate-limiting conformational transition coincides with the closing of the Met20 loop, which dynamically gates solvent access and modulates the pKa of the catalytic glutamate. Kinetic modeling demonstrates that fluctuations along this pathway directly dictate turnover efficiency, establishing a quantitative link between ensemble dynamics and catalytic proficiency. These findings resolve longstanding ambiguities regarding dynamic control in DHFR and provide a general framework for dissecting how stochastic protein motions are harnessed to drive chemical transformation.

title: Individualized PATE: Differentially Private Machine Learning with Individual Privacy Guarantees
text_ai: Applying machine learning (ML) to sensitive domains requires privacy protection of the underlying training data through formal privacy frameworks, such as differential privacy (DP). Yet, usually, the privacy of the training data comes at the cost of the resulting ML models' utility. The Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles (PATE) framework has emerged as a promising solution, leveraging knowledge distillation to mitigate this trade-off by releasing only aggregated predictions rather than raw labels. However, conventional PATE enforces uniform privacy budgets across all training instances, ignoring inherent heterogeneity in data sensitivity and thus over-allocating noise to low-risk samples. To address this limitation, we introduce Individualized PATE, a novel adaptation that computes instance-specific privacy expenditures through adaptive noise injection calibrated to each sample’s contribution to teacher disagreement. By dynamically adjusting the privacy accounting mechanism, our approach preserves aggregate differential privacy guarantees while significantly reducing unnecessary information leakage for less sensitive examples. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that Individualized PATE achieves up to 22% higher classification accuracy compared to baseline implementations under identical global privacy constraints, without compromising theoretical security bounds. This framework introduces a flexible budget allocation strategy that aligns formal guarantees with practical data characteristics, establishing a new paradigm for fine-grained privacy-preserving machine learning in regulated environments.

title: Semi-Interpenetrating Cooperative Localization in Connected Vehicle Networks
text_ai: We proposed a fusion mechanism for the distributed cooperative map matching (CMM) within the vehicular ad-hoc network. This mechanism makes the information from each node reachable within the network by other nodes without direct communication, thus improving the overall localization accuracy and robustness. By leveraging intermediate relays and topological awareness, the proposed framework establishes a semi-interpenetrating architecture that propagates high-confidence map-matching residuals across disjoint communication clusters. We evaluated the system using realistic traffic scenarios generated from SUMO coupled with NS-3 network simulations across diverse urban geometries, benchmarking performance against baseline single-node and fully connected CMM approaches. Results demonstrate a 34% reduction in root-mean-square error under sparse connectivity conditions, alongside a 28% increase in successful localization rates during radio frequency degradation events. Furthermore, the algorithm exhibits minimal computational overhead, ensuring viability for real-time deployment on resource-constrained onboard units. These findings validate the efficacy of indirect information dissemination in enhancing spatial consistency, providing a scalable localization paradigm for future intelligent transportation infrastructures where direct connectivity remains inherently intermittent.

title: Effects of Stellar Feedback on Stellar and Gas Kinematics of Star-Forming Galaxies at 0.6<z<1.0
text_ai: Recent zoom-in cosmological simulations have shown that stellar feedback can flatten the inner density profile of the dark matter halo in low-mass galaxies. A correlation between the stellar/gas velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{star}$, $\sigma_{gas}$) and the specific star formation rate (sSFR) is predicted as an observational test of the role of stellar feedback in re-shaping the dark matter density profile. We analyze a high-resolution hydrodynamical simulation suite tracing galaxy evolution across $0.6<z<1.0$, focusing on star-forming systems with stellar masses $M_* \sim 10^9-10^{10}\,M_\odot$. By extracting spatially resolved kinematic tracers, we measure $\sigma_{star}$ and $\sigma_{gas}$ as functions of galactocentric radius and derive their integrated correlations with sSFR. Our results confirm a robust positive scaling between both velocity dispersions and sSFR, consistent with theoretical expectations that starburst activity injects turbulence into the interstellar medium while driving outflows that expand the gravitational potential well. We find that the slope of the $\sigma_{gas}$–sSFR relation weakens in more massive halos where gravity dominates over feedback-driven energy injection. Furthermore, comparing simulated line-of-sight velocity profiles against integral-field spectroscopy mock observations demonstrates that ground-based facilities can resolve kinematic signatures at the target redshifts. These findings establish a measurable diagnostic for quantifying baryonic feedback efficiency and provide a pathway to constrain the inner slope of collisionless dark matter distributions through next-generation infrared integral-field units.

title: Convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs arising as Wasserstein gradient flows of convex functions
text_ai: We study the quantitative convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs that arise as Wasserstein gradient flows of linearly convex functions over the space of probability measures on ${\mathbb R}^d$. In this setting, the objective is in general not displacement convex, so it is not clear a priori whether global convergence even holds. To circumvent this obstruction, we introduce a refined entropy-dissipation strategy that capitalizes on the intrinsic linear convexity of the potential rather than requiring displacement convexity. By combining a careful analysis of the Fisher information dissipation with dimension-independent concentration inequalities, we establish a uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequality along the evolving measure path. This functional estimate directly implies that the relative entropy decays at an explicit exponential rate determined solely by the diffusion constant and the convexity modulus. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the solution converges strongly in the $W_2$-Wasserstein metric to the unique invariant profile, with algebraic corrections capturing transient relaxation phases. The proof relies on a novel interpolation argument between the linear drift and the Fokker-Planck operator, which restores effective contractivity in the ambient metric space. These findings generalize the classical gradient-flow paradigm to a substantially wider class of non-geodesically convex functionals and offer sharp quantitative control for mean-field limits in kinetic theory and statistical mechanics. Moreover, our estimates remain robust under small perturbations of the interaction kernel.

title: On performance bound estimation in NMPC with time-varying terminal cost
text_ai: Model predictive control (MPC) schemes are commonly designed with fixed, i.e., time-invariant, horizon length and cost functions. If no stabilizing terminal ingredients are used, stability can be guaranteed via a sufficiently long horizon. A suboptimality index can be derived that gives bounds on the performance of the MPC law over an infinite-horizon (IH). However, extending these results to nonlinear systems equipped with time-varying terminal costs remains theoretically challenging, as standard recursive arguments fail when terminal weights evolve dynamically. This paper develops a rigorous framework for estimating suboptimality certificates under time-varying terminal penalties. By introducing a Lyapunov-based perturbation analysis, we derive explicit conditions guaranteeing asymptotic stability alongside tight, computable performance bounds. The methodology quantifies how temporal variations in the terminal cost influence the suboptimality multiplier, establishing a direct relationship between cost adaptation rates and achievable IH performance guarantees. Online bound updates are formulated to maintain robustness against modeling uncertainties. Numerical simulations on a constrained nonlinear benchmark demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces conservatism relative to fixed-terminal designs, enabling substantially shorter prediction horizons without compromising closed-loop performance or recursive feasibility.

title: Are Bitcoins price predictable? Evidence from machine learning techniques using technical indicators
text_ai: The uncertainties in future Bitcoin price make it difficult to accurately predict the price of Bitcoin. Accurately predicting the price for Bitcoin is therefore important for decision-making process of investors and market players in the cryptocurrency market. To address this challenge, the present study evaluates the predictive capacity of established technical indicators when coupled with advanced machine learning algorithms. Using daily price data from 2015 to 2023, we engineer a multidimensional feature space encompassing trend, volatility, and momentum proxies. Volume metrics supplement these features. These variables are systematically trained across support vector machines, random forests, gradient boosting classifiers, and long short-term memory networks. Forecasting accuracy is rigorously measured via root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and directional consistency scores across rolling out-of-sample windows. Results indicate that non-linear ensemble models substantially surpass linear autoregressive baselines, delivering statistically significant gains in directional prediction. Particularly, volatility-filtered indicator combinations markedly improve robustness during turbulent market phases. Feature attribution analyses further identify the relative strength index and exponential moving average differentials as dominant predictors. Collectively, these outcomes confirm that although Bitcoin displays pronounced stochastic behavior, systematic technical signal extraction paired with adaptive algorithmic frameworks yields economically meaningful short-term forecasts. Accordingly, this work offers empirically grounded methodologies for portfolio optimization and dynamic hedging strategies within cryptocurrency trading ecosystems.

title: The Mystery of Two Straight Lines in Bacterial Genome Statistics. Release 2007
text_ai: In special coordinates (codon position--specific nucleotide frequencies) bacterial genomes form two straight lines in 9-dimensional space: one line for eubacterial genomes, another for archaeal genomes. All the 348 distinct bacterial genomes available in Genbank in April 2007, belong to these lines with high accuracy. The main challenge now is to explain the observed high accuracy. We propose that these linear constraints arise from universal mutational biases constrained by purifying selection on translational efficiency and DNA structural stability. Analysis of the covariance matrix across codon positions reveals that sequence variation is confined to a low-dimensional manifold, indicating that genomic composition follows deterministic biophysical rules rather than random drift. This geometric regularity implies that eubacterial and archaeal lineages independently converged upon optimal compositional equilibria dictated by replication fidelity and metabolic costs. Practically, the dual-linearity offers a sensitive diagnostic tool for detecting foreign DNA segments, quantifying recombination rates, and inferring ancestral nucleotide landscapes. Subsequent work will validate these findings against expanded taxonomic sampling and test whether similar dimensional reduction applies to viral and organelle genomes, thereby establishing a unified statistical framework for prokaryotic genome evolution.

title: Entanglement distillation based on polarization and frequency hyperentanglement
text_ai: Entanglement distillation has many applications in quantum information processing and is an important tool for improving the quality and efficiency of quantum communication, cryptography, computing, and simulation. We propose an entanglement distillation scheme using only one pair of polarization-frequency hyperentangled photons, which can be equivalently viewed as containing two pairs of entangled logical qubits: a pair of polarization-entangled qubits and a pair of frequency-entangled qubits. The proposed protocol leverages linear optical elements and coincidence detection to perform parallel purification on both degrees of freedom without cross-talk. By exploiting the tensor-product structure of the hyperentangled state, our method simultaneously enhances the fidelity of polarization and frequency subsystems while preserving their mutual correlations. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the scheme achieves near-unity fidelity under realistic loss conditions and exhibits greater resilience to decoherence compared to conventional single-degree-of-freedom approaches. Notably, the distillation succeeds with a probability that scales favorably with initial state purity, requiring no auxiliary photons or complex nonlinear interactions. This resource-efficient architecture provides an enabling framework for robust quantum repeaters and scalable photonic networks, where maintaining high-quality hyperentanglement across transmission channels remains a bottleneck.

title: Antimicrobial resistance and use, and rates of hospitalization associated with bacterial infections, including sepsis
text_ai: While the mechanisms and quantitative details are complex, few analysts would doubt that antibiotic use increases the prevalence of drug-resistant bacterial pathogens among all bacteria causing disease in a population. The causal connection between antibiotic use and the total incidence of severe bacterial infections, possibly mediated by antibiotic resistance, is less clearly established. To address this uncertainty, we conducted a longitudinal ecological analysis linking national antibiotic prescribing data with hospital admission records for culture-confirmed bacterial infections and sepsis. Using multivariable regression models adjusted for demographic and clinical confounders, we estimated the association between community-level antimicrobial consumption and subsequent infection-related hospitalization rates. Our findings indicate that increased fluoroquinolone and macrolide utilization significantly predicted elevated admissions for resistant Gram-negative infections and sepsis, even after controlling for baseline morbidity. These results suggest that targeted stewardship interventions may reduce both resistance prevalence and the broader burden of severe infectious disease. Consequently, policy frameworks should integrate antimicrobial optimization with infection control strategies to mitigate downstream healthcare utilization for public health.

title: Derivation and maintenance of mouse haploid embryonic stem cells.
text_ai: Ploidy represents the number of chromosome sets in a cell. Although gametes have a haploid genome (n), most mammalian cells have diploid genomes (2n). To circumvent this limitation, we developed a robust protocol for deriving and maintaining functionally haploid embryonic stem cells from mouse blastocysts. Iterative selection and karyotyping yielded subclones that stably retain a single chromosome set while preserving core pluripotency networks and multilineage differentiation capacity. Although prone to spontaneous diploidization, these cells are readily restored to haploidy through cytochalasin B treatment. Functionally, they enable direct phenotypic screening of recessive alleles, eliminating the need for time-consuming germline transmission. Additionally, their unique genomic architecture enhances CRISPR-Cas9-mediated mutagenesis and conventional homologous recombination efficiencies. Together, this system establishes a scalable, genetically tractable platform for comprehensive forward and reverse genetic screens in mammals.

title: Functions of multivector variables
text_ai: As is well known, the common elementary functions defined over the real numbers can be generalized to act not only over the complex number field but also over the skew (non-commuting) field of the quaternions. We establish rigorous convergence criteria for power series representations and derive closed-form expressions through geometric algebraic identities. Particular attention is directed toward trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic mappings, explicitly resolving branch cut ambiguities inherent in non-commutative domains. Analytical derivations are complemented by algorithmic implementations that preserve grade-wise algebraic consistency while enabling efficient evaluation across arbitrary bivector and trivector components. Comparative numerical experiments validate computational stability against existing quaternion-based approximations, revealing enhanced precision in high-dimensional rotational transformations. Collectively, these formulations furnish a systematic functional calculus for Clifford algebras, thereby enabling direct application in geometric computing, electromagnetic theory, and multidimensional control systems with significantly improved computational efficiency.

title: On T-Duality and Integrability for Strings on AdS Backgrounds
text_ai: We discuss an interplay between T-duality and integrability for certain classical non-linear sigma models. In particular, we consider strings on the AdS_5 x S^5 background and perform T-duality along the four isometry directions of AdS_5 in the Poincare patch. The T-dual of the AdS_5 sigma model is again a sigma model on an AdS_5 space. We demonstrate that the integrable structure is preserved under this transformation, with the original Lax connection mapping precisely to its T-dual counterpart. Consequently, the infinite tower of non-local conserved charges remains intact, ensuring that the classical equations of motion retain their zero-curvature formulation. By explicitly constructing the dual flat connection, we show how the hidden symmetries of the underlying theory are reorganized into a geometric form on the dual background. This correspondence provides a framework for analyzing the spectral problem in the planar limit of N=4 super Yang-Mills theory, linking worldsheet integrability to boundary operator dimensions. Our results indicate that T-duality acts as a symmetry generator within the integrable hierarchy, offering new insights into the holographic dictionary and the emergence of spacetime geometry from quantum data.

title: The quaternionic KP hierarchy and conformally immersed 2-tori in the 4-sphere
text_ai: The quaternionic KP hierarchy is the integrable hierarchy of p.d.e obtained by replacing the complex numbers with the quaternions, mutatis mutandis, in the standard construction of the KP hierarchy equations and solutions; it is equivalent to what is often called the Davey-Stewartson II hierarchy. Here, we develop a quaternionic dressing formalism translating the hierarchy’s tau-functions into explicit Weierstrass-type representations for conformal immersions into $S^4$. Analyzing the monodromy of the associated linear system yields necessary and sufficient quasi-periodicity conditions ensuring the resulting surfaces close to compact immersed 2-tori. These tori are governed by finite-dimensional reductions characterized by spectral curves with involution symmetry and prescribed divisor data. We classify all such tori up to conformal equivalence and demonstrate that their moduli spaces inherit natural integrable Hamiltonian structures from the hierarchy. Moreover, we establish a direct correspondence between the conserved quantities of the quaternionic KP flow and geometric invariants of the immersed surfaces, notably Willmore energy and conformal area. These findings extend the classical algebro-geometric theory of soliton surfaces to the non-commutative setting, clarifying the structural link between integrable flows and conformal surface theory in four dimensions.

title: Optimal liquidation for a risk averse investor in a one-sided limit order book driven by a Levy process
text_ai: In a one-sided limit order book, satisfying some realistic assumptions, where the unaffected price process follows a Levy process, we consider a market agent that wants to liquidate a large position of shares. We assume that the agent has constant absolute risk aversion and aims at maximising the expected utility of the cash position at the end of time. We formulate the liquidation problem as a stochastic control task, modelling limit order placements through a state-dependent arrival intensity. The associated value function satisfies a nonlinear integro-differential Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation. Exploiting the exponential utility structure, we transform the problem into a linear partial differential equation featuring nonlocal integral terms generated by the Levy jumps. We prove existence and uniqueness of a viscosity solution and obtain an explicit feedback representation for the optimal order placement. Analysis demonstrates that the optimal trajectory balances immediate execution pressure against inventory decay, dynamically adjusting to jump activity and residual position. Simulations reveal that elevated Levy activity accelerates liquidation but amplifies terminal variance, whereas heightened risk aversion systematically prolongs the execution horizon. These findings yield practical execution guidelines under heavy-tailed market dynamics.

title: Tableau models for semi-infinite Bruhat order and level-zero representations of quantum affine algebras
text_ai: We prove that semi-infinite Bruhat order on an affine Weyl group is completely determined from those on the quotients by affine Weyl subgroups associated with various maximal (standard) parabolic subgroups of finite type. Interpreting covering relations in the semi-infinite poset through local tableau rules, we establish a bijection with path-space realizations, yielding novel character formulas for level-zero Demazure modules. This correspondence clarifies the geometric origin of q-characters in tensor product decompositions and provides a uniform description of the semi-infinite Bruhat order across all untwisted types. Resolving conjectures regarding the shape of Kashiwara–Nakashima tableaux under translation elements, our framework delivers a purely combinatorial criterion for semi-infinite Demazure crystal containment. Consequently, we obtain explicit inclusion relations among evaluation modules at distinct spectral parameters. These findings unify the combinatorics of affine posets with the representation theory of quantum affine algebras, establishing a foundation for computing graded decomposition numbers and analyzing crystal graph asymptotics.

title: MBAPose: Mask and Bounding-Box Aware Pose Estimation of Surgical Instruments with Photorealistic Domain Randomization
text_ai: Surgical robots are usually controlled using a priori models based on the robots' geometric parameters, which are calibrated before the surgical procedure. One of the challenges in using robots in real surgical settings is that those parameters can change over time, consequently deteriorating control accuracy. To address this limitation, we introduce MBAPose, a vision-based framework that continuously estimates the six-degree-of-freedom pose of surgical instruments from endoscopic imagery. Our approach fuses semantic segmentation masks and bounding boxes within a unified neural architecture, enabling robust spatial reasoning under occlusion and varying illumination. title: Epidemiology of Injuries in National Collegiate Athletic Association Women's Lacrosse: 2014-2015 Through 2018-2019.

This study quantified injury incidence and mechanisms among collegiate women’s lacrosse athletes via prospective surveillance. Certified athletic trainers documented all practice and competition injuries across participating institutions over five competitive seasons. Rates were calculated per 1,000 athlete-exposures and stratified by event type, anatomical location, and etiology. A total of 2,847 injuries occurred, yielding an overall rate of 6.82 per 1,000 exposures. Competition injuries significantly exceeded practice rates (p < .01), with lower-extremity sprains and concussions constituting 68% of all diagnoses. Contact mechanisms predominated during games (64%), whereas non-contact events dominated practice sessions. These distinct epidemiological patterns emphasize the necessity of context-specific conditioning protocols and impact-absorbing equipment standards. Ongoing surveillance will further inform safety regulations and optimize injury mitigation frameworks within collegiate athletics.

title: MVGrasp: Real-Time Multi-View 3D Object Grasping in Highly Cluttered Environments
text_ai: Nowadays robots play an increasingly important role in our daily life. In human-centered environments, robots often encounter piles of objects, packed items, or isolated objects. To address this, we present MVGrasp, a novel framework leveraging synchronized multi-view depth inputs to reconstruct comprehensive 3D representations while preserving fine-grained spatial details lost in monocular setups. Our architecture utilizes a lightweight feature aggregation module that fuses complementary viewpoints via attention-guided cross-view alignment, substantially improving grasp candidate generation amid heavy clutter. Coupled with an accelerated geometric verification pipeline, MVGrasp achieves sub-30-millisecond inference latency on embedded hardware without sacrificing accuracy. Evaluations across synthetic benchmarks and physical testbeds demonstrate consistent superiority over single-view and static multi-view baselines, increasing successful grasp rates by 22% in highly disordered scenarios. title: Public Discourse Sandbox: Facilitating Human and AI Digital Communication Research
text_ai: Social media serves as a primary communication and information dissemination platform for major global events, entertainment, and niche or topically focused community discussions. The architecture integrates dynamic discourse modeling, automated authenticity verification, and modular application programming interfaces, enabling investigators to isolate specific communicative variables without compromising user privacy or violating platform governance protocols. By deploying reproducible scenario matrices spanning misinformation diffusion, ideological fragmentation, and collaborative reasoning, the platform supports rigorous empirical validation of both sociolinguistic frameworks and machine learning alignment techniques. Empirical benchmarks indicate that generated interaction trajectories maintain statistical fidelity with organic network behavior, providing a transparent substitute for restricted commercial feeds. This infrastructure ultimately standardizes experimental conditions across disciplines, accelerating theoretical advancement while preserving regulatory compliance in computationally mediated public spheres. title: Immunofluorescence Capillary Imaging Segmentation: Cases Study

title: A Feedback Neural Network for Small Target Motion Detection in Cluttered Backgrounds
text_ai: Small target motion detection is critical for insects to search for and track mates or prey which always appear as small dim speckles in the visual field. title: SSH: A Self-Supervised Framework for Image Harmonization

By synthesizing plausible harmonized variants from unlabeled scenes, SSH implicitly captures statistical dependencies between compositional artifacts and environmental consistency without manual supervision. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing supervised alternatives, achieving superior visual fidelity and robust generalization across diverse compositing scenarios. Furthermore, ablation studies validate each proposed module, highlighting the effectiveness of our unsupervised alignment strategy. These results establish SSH as a scalable solution for real-world image editing, substantially reducing data curation costs while maintaining high harmonization quality.

title: Evaluating QoS Parameters for IPTV Distribution in Heterogeneous Networks

title: A Deep Conditioning Treatment of Neural Networks

title: Off the record: The invisibility work of doctors in a patient-accessible electronic health record information service.
text_ai: In this article, we draw on Michael Lipsky's work on street-level bureaucrats and discretion to analyse a real case setting comprising an interview study of 30 Swedish doctors regarding their experiences of changes in clinical work following patients being given access to medical records information online. We argue that such practices constitute a distinct form of street-level bureaucracy in digital health, where discretion operates through omission and contextual shielding rather than explicit decision-making. The study underscores how technological affordances reshape professional autonomy, suggesting that policy interventions must account for the hidden labour physicians perform to sustain clinical judgment in transparent environments.

title: Time-dependent electron transport through a strongly correlated quantum dot: multiple-probe open boundary conditions approach

title: Numerical models of planetary nebulae with different episodes of mass ejection: the particular case of HuBi 1
text_ai: We have studied the evolution of HuBi 1-like planetary nebulae, considering several stages of mass injection. title: On the Analysis of Puncturing for Finite-Length Polar Codes: Boolean Function Approach

title: Image Quality Assessment Guided Deep Neural Networks Training

title: CL-HOI: Cross-Level Human-Object Interaction Distillation from Vision Large Language Models

title: Beyond Uncertainty: Evidential Deep Learning for Robust Video Temporal Grounding
text_ai: Existing Video Temporal Grounding (VTG) models excel in accuracy but often overlook open-world challenges posed by open-vocabulary queries and untrimmed videos. During inference, users can dynamically adjust decision thresholds according to domain-specific reliability requirements without retraining. title: Position-Constrained Stochastic Inference for Cooperative Indoor Localization
text_ai: We address the problem of distributed cooperative localization in wireless networks, i.e. nodes without prior position knowledge (agents) wish to determine their own positions. To mitigate these issues, we propose a position-constrained stochastic inference framework that systematically integrates physical boundary models into a distributed belief propagation scheme. Reformulating the localization task as a constrained Markov random field optimization, our approach dynamically weights inter-agent links while penalizing geometrically infeasible estimates. The resulting algorithm operates iteratively through local message exchanges, guaranteeing convergence under mild connectivity assumptions. Simulations across indoor floor plans demonstrate that the proposed method reduces root-mean-square error by 38% compared to conventional ranging-based filters, even under sparse anchor deployments and noisy measurements. Furthermore, the framework exhibits linear scaling with network size, enabling scalable IoT integration. These findings establish position-constrained stochastic inference as a robust paradigm for cooperative indoor positioning systems.
