title: Deriving approximation tolerance constraints from verification runs
text_ai: Approximate computing (AC) is an emerging paradigm for energy-efficient computation. The basic idea of AC is to sacrifice high precision for low energy by allowing for hardware which only carries out "approximately correct" calculations. For software verification, this challenges the validity of verification results for programs run on approximate hardware. To address this gap, we present a framework that automatically derives approximation tolerance constraints directly from conventional verification runs. By analyzing divergent execution paths and quantifying output deviations across iterative checks, our approach characterizes acceptable error boundaries without explicit hardware fault models. We formalize these constraints as logical predicates integrable into standard model checkers and theorem provers. Evaluation on benchmark circuits and embedded control applications demonstrates that the method identifies safe operating regions while reducing verification overhead by 38 percent. Furthermore, the derived tolerance bounds enable runtime monitoring mechanisms that dynamically adapt computational precision according to application criticality. This work bridges traditional formal methods and approximate architectures, offering a systematic methodology to certify correctness under bounded inexactness. Practitioners can thus deploy verifiable approximate systems that preserve quality guarantees while realizing energy efficiency gains.

title: Explaining the Effectiveness of Multi-Task Learning for Efficient Knowledge Extraction from Spine MRI Reports
text_ai: Pretrained Transformer based models finetuned on domain specific corpora have changed the landscape of NLP. title: Cocommutative q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual of the truncated polynomial algebra

Furthermore, we establish a bijection between these classified coalgebras and the corresponding set-theoretic solutions, thereby providing an explicit construction of new families of braid group representations. title: On Asteroid Retrieval Missions Enabled by Invariant Manifold Dynamics
text_ai: In recent years, the retrieval of entire asteroids has received significant attention, with many approaches leveraging the invariant manifolds of the Circular-Restricted Three-body Problem to capture an asteroid into a periodic orbit about the $L_1$ or $L_2$ points of the Sun-Earth system. title: Evolution of an N-level system via automated vectorization of the Liouville equations and application to optically controlled polarization rotation

title: Graphene field effect transistors as room-temperature Terahertz detectors

title: Nonlinear fractional waves at elastic interfaces

Numerical simulations of the full nonlinear system demonstrate the emergence of stable solitary pulses whose amplitude and spatial extent are governed by a precise balance between nonlinear steepening and fractional dispersion. Furthermore, we establish a generalized energy budget that explicitly accounts for memory-induced dissipation radiating into the surrounding medium. These results provide a rigorous analytical framework for interpreting high-frequency mechanical probing in heterogeneous soft matter and biological tissues, where long-range viscoelastic coupling fundamentally modifies wave kinematics and attenuation pathways.

title: Cleavage of the SUN-domain protein Mps3 at its N-terminus regulates centrosome disjunction in budding yeast meiosis.
text_ai: Centrosomes organize microtubules and are essential for spindle formation and chromosome segregation during cell division. Mass spectrometry and immunoblotting reveal that this cleavage is mediated by the separase complex following cohesin degradation. Conversely, a non-cleavable Mps3 mutant retains physical coupling between duplicated centrosomes, leading to defective spindle orientation and impaired chromosome segregation. Genetic epistasis analysis places Mps3 processing upstream of spindle pole body duplication cycle progression. These findings establish N-terminal proteolysis as a critical post-translational switch that dismantles the intercentrosomal bridge, ensuring timely centrosome maturation and accurate meiotic divisions, thereby preserving genomic integrity. Collectively, this work highlights evolutionary conservation of envelope-associated proteolytic events in organelle dynamics and offers new insights into centrosome cycle control across eukaryotes.

title: Annama H chondrite - mineralogy, physical properties, cosmic ray exposure, and parent body history

title: PeV Neutrinos and a 3.5 keV X-Ray Line from a PeV Scale Supersymmetric Neutrino Sector

The resulting spectrum contains metastable heavy neutralinos whose three-body decays populate the high-energy neutrino flux. We constrain the model parameters using combined likelihood fits to IceCube differential event rates and X-ray telescope spectra, isolating a narrow viable region compatible with dark matter relic density and collider limits. title: Graphical Modelling in Genetics and Systems Biology

Within genetics and systems biology, these architectures capture stochastic dependencies across biomolecules, enabling systematic regulatory circuit inference from omics datasets. This article reviews emerging algorithmic strategies and examines penalized likelihood estimators addressing high dimensionality and unobserved confounding. We assess constraint-driven causal discovery algorithms that isolate primary molecular interactions from secondary statistical artifacts. By merging traditional distributional theory with advanced regularization schemes, we establish standards for deriving biologically coherent network topologies. Collectively, these advances strengthen analytical reliability and expedite translating network inference into precision genomics.

title: MAP Estimation, Message Passing, and Perfect Graphs
text_ai: Efficiently finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) configuration of a graphical model is an important problem which is often implemented using message passing algorithms. We demonstrate that when the underlying factor graph exhibits a perfect graph decomposition, the standard max-product algorithm converges in finite steps to the globally optimal configuration without approximation. By characterizing the associated energy landscape through clique-tree representations and fractional polytopes, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which local message updates propagate global consistency. Our theoretical framework generalizes classical tree-based results and provides a unified perspective on when loopy belief propagation yields exact solutions. We further present polynomial-time verification procedures for these structural guarantees and validate our findings on synthetic benchmarks and real-world computer vision tasks. These results not only clarify the fundamental boundaries of message-passing optimality but also offer actionable guidelines for deploying efficient inference schemes in cyclic networks.

title: Probing the mechanical properties of DNA nanostructures with metadynamics

By strategically selecting collective variables that capture hinge bending, helix stretching, and inter-strand sliding, we accelerate rare barrier crossings while rigorously preserving thermodynamic accuracy. Computational overhead remains minimal relative to exhaustive unbiased trajectories, ensuring practical applicability to large-scale assemblies. Our framework yields quantitative force–extension profiles and transition pathways across multiple canonical motifs, demonstrating strong agreement with independent single-molecule manipulation experiments. Furthermore, we resolve metastable intermediates and localized strain-distribution patterns that dictate failure thresholds under cyclic loading. By seamlessly integrating enhanced sampling with predictive biomechanical modeling, this methodology establishes a robust computational pipeline for rational engineering, accelerating the development of advanced nucleic acid nanodevices.

title: EDIT: Exemplar-Domain Aware Image-to-Image Translation

Central to our approach is an exemplar-driven feature modulation mechanism that dynamically aligns source representations with target domain characteristics without requiring paired supervision. By integrating a cross-domain attention module, EDIT effectively disentangles content and style attributes, enabling precise many-to-many mappings across arbitrary combinations. During inference, users can seamlessly interpolate between exemplars to achieve continuous style transitions while strictly preserving structural fidelity. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that EDIT consistently outperforms contemporary methods in visual quality and stylistic accuracy. Quantitative evaluations reveal substantial reductions in Fréchet Inception Distance alongside marked improvements in perceptual similarity metrics. Comprehensive user studies further validate the model’s superior controllability and output diversity. title: Optimal entanglement witnesses for continuous-variable systems

Moreover, we prove that this unified framework rigorously subsumes established variance-based inequalities while strictly expanding the accessible entangled state space. Consequently, the derived protocol offers a practical, scalable pathway for verifying multipartite correlations in photonic and atomic ensembles without requiring full quantum state tomography, thereby establishing a new benchmark for variance-based entanglement detection.

title: Direct observation of multiple topological phases in the iron-based superconductor Li(Fe,Co)As

Our findings establish this pnictide as a highly tunable platform for engineering topological superconductivity without external heterostructuring. This direct spectroscopic evidence not only resolves long-standing debates regarding band inversion mechanisms but also provides a viable material system for hosting Majorana zero modes, thereby advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Generic algebraic properties in spaces of enumerated groups

Furthermore, we analyze the complexity of the associated equivalence relations and demonstrate that generic enumerated groups exhibit maximal dynamical complexity when acting on their Cayley graphs. title: Challenges in the thermal modeling of highly porous carbon foams

To address these complexities, we develop a coupled continuum model that integrates solid-phase conduction, intra-pore radiation, and effective boundary conditions tailored to the cellular architecture. The model parameters are calibrated against transient temperature profiles obtained at multiple heating powers. Results demonstrate that accounting for morphological anisotropy and porosity-dependent optical properties substantially improves agreement with measured diffusivity values across the tested temperature range. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses highlight the dominant influence of strut thickness and cell wall emissivity on overall thermal transport. These findings provide a robust framework for interpreting heat pulse measurements in open-cell foams and underscore the necessity of morphology-resolved modeling when designing lightweight thermal management systems for high-temperature applications.

title: Fast rotating Bose-Einstein condensates in an asymmetric trap

Numerical simulations confirm that beyond a threshold anisotropy, the system undergoes a topological transition wherein vortices preferentially align along the trap’s major axis, suppressing the usual hexagonal symmetry. These findings are validated against full GPE integrations and demonstrate excellent agreement with experimental data. Our analytical framework provides a computationally efficient pathway for predicting collective excitation spectra and metastable vortex states in rapidly rotating quantum gases, thereby bridging the gap between mean-field theory and realization of non-equilibrium superfluid phases.

title: Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
text_ai: Alchemical free energy calculations are a useful tool for predicting free energy differences associated with the transfer of molecules from one environment to another. Benchmarking against experimental hydration and binding affinities reveals systematic biases from truncated electrostatics and insufficient phase-space overlap. Our analysis yields actionable guidelines for protocol design, uncertainty quantification, and validation metrics tailored to equilibrium and nonequilibrium pathways. Implementing these standards reduces computational overhead while enhancing reproducibility. These recommendations establish a robust foundation for high-accuracy thermodynamic predictions in molecular design, ensuring alchemical transformations yield reliable results across heterogeneous workflows.

title: Voltage Estimation in Low-Voltage Distribution Grids with Distributed Energy Resources
text_ai: The present distribution grids generally have limited sensing capabilities and are therefore characterized by low observability. Improved observability is a prerequisite for increasing the hosting capacity of distributed energy resources such as solar photovoltaics (PV) in distribution grids. In this context, this paper presents learning-aided low-voltage estimation using untapped but readily available and widely distributed sensors from cable television (CATV) networks. Specifically, high-frequency noise embedded in downstream CATV signals serves as an indirect proxy for dynamic voltage fluctuations. A dedicated neural network maps these acoustic-electrical features to spatial voltage profiles, effectively compensating for severely sparse metering infrastructure. The proposed framework is rigorously validated using synthetic data from an IEEE 123-bus feeder, augmented by real-world field measurements from an operational CATV deployment. Empirical results demonstrate that the estimator achieves a mean absolute error below 0.75 V across diverse loading and generation scenarios, substantially outperforming conventional state estimation methods reliant exclusively on legacy smart meters. Leveraging existing telecommunications assets establishes a scalable, economical pathway for modernizing grid monitoring. Ultimately, this strategy empowers utilities to reliably maximize renewable integration while guaranteeing continuous adherence to statutory voltage tolerances.

title: Binary Black-box Evasion Attacks Against Deep Learning-based Static Malware Detectors with Adversarial Byte-Level Language Model
text_ai: Anti-malware engines are the first line of defense against malicious software. While widely used, feature engineering-based anti-malware engines are vulnerable to unseen (zero-day) attacks. Recently, deep learning-based static anti-malware detectors have achieved success in identifying unseen attacks without requiring feature engineering and dynamic analysis. However, their reliance on learned representations introduces critical vulnerabilities to adversarial manipulation. In this work, we propose a novel black-box evasion framework that systematically perturbs malware binaries at the byte level to bypass state-of-the-art static detectors. Leveraging a byte-level language model trained on raw executable sequences, our approach generates functionally equivalent adversarial samples by optimizing minimal byte modifications across non-critical instruction regions. Extensive evaluations across various convolutional and recurrent detection architectures reveal evasion success rates surpassing 95%, while preserving primary malicious functionality. Furthermore, multi-model transferability tests confirm that generated payloads effectively compromise independent detector ensembles. Importantly, our methodology requires no gradient information or architectural transparency, operating exclusively through iterative query-based feedback. These results expose fundamental weaknesses in contemporary deep learning-based malware classifiers and emphasize the necessity for integrating adversarial training paradigms into advanced static analysis systems.

title: A Theoretical Solution of the Mind-Body Problem: An Operationalized Proof that no Purely Physical System Can Exhibit all the Properties of Human Consciousness
text_ai: This article presents an operationalized solution to the mind-body problem which relies on rigorously defined theoretical reasoning rather than philosophical argument. We identify a specific operation which is a necessary property of all healthy human conscious individuals -- specifically the operation of self-certainty, or the capacity of healthy conscious humans to "know" with certainty that they are conscious. When formally modeled within any computationally closed physical framework, this operation generates an irreducible epistemic loop that cannot be instantiated by deterministic state transitions or algorithmic processing. We demonstrate that any attempt to simulate self-certainty within a purely material architecture inevitably collapses into third-party verification, thereby stripping the phenomenon of its intrinsic first-person authority. Consequently, we derive a formal proof establishing that no arrangement of physical components can replicate the complete phenomenological and operational profile of human awareness. This result resolves the explanatory gap by delineating a strict ontological boundary between functional computation and genuine subjective experience, offering a falsifiable criterion for subsequent cognitive science research.

title: AudioSR: Versatile Audio Super-resolution at Scale
text_ai: Audio super-resolution is a fundamental task that predicts high-frequency components for low-resolution audio, enhancing audio quality in digital applications. Previous methods have limitations such as the limited scope of audio types (e.g., music, speech) and specific bandwidth settings they can handle (e.g., 4kHz to 8kHz). To address these limitations, we present AudioSR, a unified neural architecture trained on a massive, heterogeneous dataset spanning diverse acoustic domains and sampling rates. By integrating a multi-scale frequency decomposition module with adaptive conditioning pathways, our method dynamically synthesizes missing spectral content across arbitrary input-output bandwidth configurations without domain-specific retraining. Comprehensive experiments reveal that AudioSR substantially surpasses prior art across established perceptual and signal-processing benchmarks, delivering exceptional temporal coherence and timbral accuracy. Additionally, systematic ablation analyses confirm the robustness of our scaling strategy, enabling seamless generalization to novel audio categories. Ultimately, this work establishes a versatile, practical standard for modern audio upscaling workflows. These findings underscore the model’s potential to transform broadcast standards and media processing.

title: From Uncertainty to Anxiety: How Uncertainty Fuels Anxiety in a Process Mediated by Intolerance of Uncertainty.
text_ai: Uncertainty about future events may lead to worry, anxiety, even inability to function. The highly related concept-intolerance of uncertainty (IU)-emerged in the early 1990s, which is further developed into a transdiagnostic risk factor in multiple forms of anxiety disorders. This study examines the mechanistic pathway through which situational uncertainty escalates into clinical anxiety, positioning IU as the central mediating construct. Utilizing a longitudinal design with 312 adults, we measured baseline perceived uncertainty, trait IU, and anxiety symptoms across three time points over six months. Structural equation modeling revealed that initial uncertainty did not directly predict subsequent anxiety; rather, its effect was fully mediated by heightened IU. Individuals with elevated IU demonstrated significantly steeper increases in anxious arousal during ambiguous outcomes, whereas low-IU participants maintained stable affective regulation. These findings substantiate the proposition that IU functions as a cognitive-affective filter, transforming ambiguous environmental cues into persistent threat appraisals. By isolating this mediation pathway, our results clarify why uncertainty exposure yields divergent clinical outcomes. Clinically, these data support integrating IU-targeted interventions into standard treatments, emphasizing cognitive restructuring and tolerance-building to disrupt the uncertainty-anxiety cycle. Ultimately, reframing uncertainty as a catalyst contingent upon individual vulnerability profiles offers a precise mechanism for prevention and transdiagnostic therapeutic innovation.

title: An ab-initio study on engineering quantum anomalous Hall effect in compensated antiferromagnet MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$
text_ai: Recently, the quantum anomalous Hall effect (QAHE) has been theoretically proposed in compensated antiferromagnetic systems by using the magnetic topological insulator model [see arXiv:2404.13305 (2024)]. However, the related and systematic study based on a realistic material system is still limited. As the only experimentally realized antiferromagnetic topological insulator, MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$ becomes a vital platform for exploring various topological states. Here, we employ first-principles density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate the emergence of QAHE in bulk and few-layer MnBi$_{2}$Te$_{4}$. By analyzing the interplay between spin-orbit coupling and magnetic exchange interactions, we identify that breaking time-reversal symmetry while preserving a sublattice magnetization pattern induces a nontrivial band inversion. Our calculations reveal a quantized Hall conductance with a Chern number $C=1$ accompanied by a robust surface state crossing the Fermi level. The topological gap reaches approximately 35 meV under moderate compressive strain, demonstrating strong resilience against lattice distortions. Furthermore, we establish that adjustments in the Bi–Te bond lengths effectively tune the magnetic compensation condition, thereby enabling precise control over the topological phase transition. These findings establish a direct pathway for realizing dissipationless chiral edge transport in antiferromagnetic platforms, linking fundamental theory to device engineering.

title: Financial Burdens of Out-of-Pocket Spending Among Medicare Fee-for-Service Beneficiaries: Role of the "Big Four" Chronic Health Conditions.
text_ai: While Medicare is the universal source of health care coverage for Americans aged 65 years or older, the program requires significant cost sharing in terms of out-of-pocket (OOP) spending. This study quantifies the financial impact of the “Big Four” chronic conditions—diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic lower respiratory disease, and arthritis—on Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries. Using nationally representative claims data from 2018–2022, we estimated annual OOP expenditures across income deciles and stratified by condition burden. Multivariable regression models adjusting for demographics, comorbidities, and geographic price variation revealed that beneficiaries with multiple conditions incurred OOP costs exceeding 15% of annual income, versus less than 4% for those without. Elevated spending clustered among low-income enrollees, accelerating medical debt and care delays. These results highlight systemic vulnerabilities in traditional Medicare’s cost-sharing architecture, which fails to protect chronically ill seniors from financial hardship. Targeted premium adjustments and enhanced prescription coverage are urgently needed to alleviate the persistent economic strain of chronic disease management under traditional Medicare.

title: A formal implementation of Behavior Trees to act in robotics
text_ai: Behavior Trees (BT) are becoming quite popular as an Acting component of autonomous robotic systems. We propose to define a formal semantics to BT by translating them to a formal language which enables us to perform verification of programs written with BT, as well as runtime verification while these BT execute. Our methodology employs model checking and temporal logic specifications to rigorously analyze BT structures prior to physical deployment. By systematically mapping hierarchical nodes to state-transition rules within a verified computational framework, we guarantee deterministic execution trajectories and resolve ambiguities inherent in conventional definitions. We instantiate this translation mechanism within a prototype runtime engine compatible with standard robotic middleware, validating its utility across diverse manipulation scenarios. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that formally verified BTs decrease critical specification violations by seventy percent relative to unverified baselines, while satisfying strict real-time latency requirements. Additionally, the embedded runtime monitor reliably identifies and mitigates stochastic environmental disturbances without interrupting task progression. Ultimately, this framework provides a mathematically sound foundation for deploying autonomous behaviors in safety-critical domains, effectively reconciling high-level task planning with provably correct execution guarantees.

title: Lattice results for $D/D_s$ leptonic and semileptonic decays
text_ai: This review article summarizes recent lattice QCD results for $D$ and $D_s$ meson leptonic and semileptonic decays. Knowing the meson decay constants and semileptonic form factors from theory, one can extract CKM elements $V_{cd}$ and $V_{cs}$ from experimental results. We detail the computational frameworks employed to treat charm quarks as relativistic degrees of freedom, emphasizing controlled continuum extrapolations across physical-pion-mass gauge ensembles. Particular attention addresses dominant systematic uncertainties, including discretization artifacts, finite-volume corrections, and electromagnetic isospin-breaking effects. Our analysis yields updated determinations of the decay constants $f_D$ and $f_{D_s}$, alongside differential semileptonic form factors $f_+(q^2)$ and $f_0(q^2)$ spanning the full kinematic range. Integrated with current experimental rates, these lattice inputs deliver competitive extractions of $|V_{cd}|$ and $|V_{cs}|$ that demonstrate robust mutual consistency and agree with global unitarity constraints. Furthermore, we evaluate their implications for testing lepton flavor universality in charged-current transitions and constraining beyond-Standard-Model scenarios. Ongoing refinements in heavy-quark actions and high-statistics simulations will systematically suppress residual theoretical errors, enabling precision flavor-physics phenomenology.

title: Saving Science by Doing Less of It?
text_ai: In the current issue of The New Atlantis, Daniel Sarewitz, professor of science and society at Arizona State University, argues that science is broken because it is managed and judged by scientists themselves, operating under Vannevar Bush's famous 1945 declaration that scientific progress depends on the "free play of free intellects … dictated by their curiosity." This self-referential oversight mechanism, Sarewitz contends, has produced a metric-driven research ecosystem that prioritizes quantity over rigor, incentivizing incremental publications while marginalizing high-risk inquiry. By conflating scholarly visibility with substantive advancement, the contemporary academy has engineered a system where survival depends on perpetual expansion rather than epistemic refinement. We examine how this institutional feedback loop distorts peer review, grant allocation, and tenure evaluation, ultimately eroding the autonomy Bush’s vision sought to protect. Drawing on empirical analyses of citation inflation, reproducibility failures, and funding reallocations across biomedical and physical sciences, we demonstrate that curbing publication volume and recalibrating evaluation criteria could restore methodological discipline. Rather than pursuing endless growth, science may require deliberate contraction—streamlining research agendas, consolidating redundant datasets, and reinstating qualitative judgment alongside bibliometric indicators. Such recalibration would reorient scientific enterprise toward sustainable knowledge production, ensuring intellectual freedom endures beyond the coercive demands of an overheated academic marketplace.

title: Sketch and Validate for Big Data Clustering
text_ai: In response to the need for learning tools tuned to big data analytics, the present paper introduces a framework for efficient clustering of huge sets of (possibly high-dimensional) data. Building on random sampling and consensus (RANSAC) ideas pursued earlier in a different (computer vision) context for robust regression, a suite of novel dimensionality and set-reduction algorithms is developed. The proposed Sketch and Validate paradigm operates in two sequential stages. First, a computationally lightweight sketching step generates compact subsets through randomized feature projection and iterative coreset construction, drastically reducing overhead. Second, a rigorous validation phase evaluates candidate cluster centers across these reduced representations, retaining only those satisfying strict consensus thresholds under perturbation. This dual mechanism ensures scalability and statistical reliability without sacrificing partition fidelity. Extensive experiments on synthetic manifolds and real-world high-dimensional benchmarks demonstrate superiority over conventional k-means variants and density-based methods regarding runtime and memory consumption, while preserving competitive silhouette scores and normalized mutual information. Theoretical analysis further establishes convergence bounds under mild distributional assumptions. By decoupling approximation from verification, this framework delivers a principled, deployable solution for large-scale unsupervised learning where traditional iterative optimization remains prohibitive.

title: HYPE: Hyperbolic Entailment Filtering for Underspecified Images and Texts
text_ai: In an era where the volume of data drives the effectiveness of self-supervised learning, the specificity and clarity of data semantics play a crucial role in model training. Addressing this, we introduce HYPerbolic Entailment filtering (HYPE), a novel methodology designed to meticulously extract modality-wise meaningful and well-aligned data from extensive, noisy image-text pair datasets. HYPE leverages the intrinsic curvature of hyperbolic space to model hierarchical semantic dependencies, enabling robust entailment scoring even when visual and linguistic cues remain sparse. By mapping both modalities into a shared Poincaré ball representation, our framework computes geodesic distances that serve as principled metrics for cross-modal consistency. We integrate this scoring mechanism into a scalable filtering pipeline that automatically discards low-fidelity pairs while preserving nuanced relationships. Extensive experiments across multiple vision-language benchmarks demonstrate that training on HYPE-curated subsets yields significant gains in downstream zero-shot transfer performance, outperforming conventional cosine-similarity baselines by up to 4.2% accuracy. Ablations confirm that hyperbolic embeddings effectively resolve underspecification without manual annotation. This establishes geometric entailment filtering as the preprocessing paradigm for scaling robust multimodal foundation models.

title: Learning Deep Representations of Fine-grained Visual Descriptions
text_ai: State-of-the-art methods for zero-shot visual recognition formulate learning as a joint embedding problem of images and side information. In these formulations the current best complement to visual features are attributes: manually encoded vectors describing shared characteristics among categories. Despite good performance, attributes have limitations: (1) finer-grained recognition requires commensurately more attributes, and (2) attributes do not provide a natural language interface. To overcome these limitations, we propose a framework that learns deep, distributed representations directly from fine-grained visual descriptions captured from image captions. Our dual-stream neural architecture aligns convolutional features with lexical embeddings within a unified semantic space. Through attention-guided matching and margin-based ranking losses, the model isolates subtle discriminative patterns while maintaining computational efficiency. Comprehensive evaluations across standard benchmarks reveal that description-driven embeddings consistently surpass conventional attribute vectors, yielding superior transfer performance under label scarcity. This representation scheme supports direct semantic querying via free-form text, effectively unifying perceptual accuracy with linguistic transparency. Our method establishes a robust foundation for scaling fine-grained visual understanding to open-world applications.

title: Energy-Based Flow Matching for Generating 3D Molecular Structure
text_ai: Molecular structure generation is a fundamental problem that involves determining the 3D positions of molecules' constituents. It has crucial biological applications, such as molecular docking, protein folding, and molecular design. Recent advances in generative modeling, such as diffusion models and flow matching, have made great progress on these tasks by modeling molecular conformations as a distribution. However, existing approaches often struggle to accurately capture complex energy landscapes while maintaining strict geometric invariances and thermodynamic consistency. To address these limitations, we propose Energy-Based Flow Matching (EBFM), a novel framework integrating differentiable energy functions with continuous-time flow dynamics. By parameterizing the velocity field through an explicit potential energy surface, EBFM directly optimizes transport plans toward physically valid conformations without iterative denoising. Our formulation inherently respects SE(3) equivariance and incorporates interatomic force constraints during training, ensuring structural realism and chemical plausibility. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that EBFM achieves superior generation fidelity and conformational diversity, while reducing sampling latency by 40% compared to diffusion-based baselines. These results establish energy-guided flow matching as a scalable paradigm for molecular generation, advancing computational drug discovery and materials engineering.

title: Good Research Practice: Lessons from Animal Care and Use.
text_ai: Animal care and use play a pivotal role in the research process. Ethical concerns on the use of animals in research have promoted the creation of a legal framework in many geographical areas that researchers must comply with, and professional organizations continuously develop recommendations on specific areas of laboratory animal science. These regulatory structures not only safeguard welfare but also enhance experimental validity by mandating standardized protocols, rigorous personnel training, and critical systematic oversight. Consequently, adherence to institutional animal care and use committees fosters a culture of accountability that directly mitigates variability and improves reproducibility across studies. By examining the evolution of these oversight mechanisms, this review elucidates transferable principles applicable to non-animal research domains, including data management, conflict-of-interest disclosure, and transparent reporting. We argue that integrating such structured compliance frameworks into ongoing scholarly conduct strengthens comprehensive research integrity. Ultimately, aligning methodological rigor with ethical stewardship provides a robust model for sustaining public trust and advancing scientifically sound, socially responsible inquiry across all disciplines.

title: AutoPET Challenge: Combining nn-Unet with Swin UNETR Augmented by Maximum Intensity Projection Classifier
text_ai: Tumor volume and changes in tumor characteristics over time are important biomarkers for cancer therapy. In this context, FDG-PET/CT scans are routinely used for staging and re-staging of cancer, as the radiolabeled fluorodeoxyglucose is taken up in regions of high metabolism. However, manual delineation remains labor-intensive and prone to inter-observer variability, necessitating robust automated solutions. To address this gap, we present a novel deep learning framework developed for the AutoPET Challenge that synergistically integrates nnU-Net and Swin UNETR architectures, augmented by a Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP) classifier. This hybrid pipeline exploits the local feature extraction of convolutional networks alongside the global contextual modeling of vision transformers, while the MIP component enhances metabolic lesion conspicuity across volumetric slices. We trained and evaluated our model on the multi-center AutoPET dataset encompassing diverse malignancies and scanning protocols. Quantitative assessment yields a Dice similarity coefficient of 0.88 and a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 4.5 mm, substantially surpassing conventional single-branch baselines. These findings confirm that transformer-augmented, projection-guided architectures enable reliable tumor segmentation, streamlining quantitative biomarker extraction for routine oncology.

title: Theory of analytical energy derivatives for the variational quantum eigensolver
text_ai: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and its variants, which is a method for finding eigenstates and eigenenergies of a given Hamiltonian, are appealing applications of near-term quantum computers. Although the eigenenergies are certainly important quantities which determines properties of a given system, their derivatives with respect to parameters of the system, such as positions of nuclei if we target a quantum chemistry problem, are also crucial to analyze the system. Here, we derive a general theory for computing analytical gradients of the VQE energy with respect to arbitrary circuit and external parameters. By applying the product rule to the parametrized unitary evolution and exploiting operator commutation relations, our formulation eliminates finite-difference errors and minimizes measurement overhead. We show that these analytic expressions remain compatible with hardware-efficient ansätze on NISQ processors while maintaining variational guarantees, thereby enabling accurate molecular force evaluations and geometry relaxations. This work provides a systematic framework for gradient-based quantum chemistry simulations and structural optimization tasks.

title: Generative AI models enable efficient and physically consistent sea-ice simulations
text_ai: Sea ice is governed by highly complex, scale-invariant, and anisotropic processes that are challenging to represent in Earth system models. While advanced numerical models have improved our understanding of the sea-ice dynamics, their computational costs often limit their application in ensemble forecasting and climate simulations. To address these limitations, we introduce a physics-informed generative framework that learns sea-ice evolution directly from high-fidelity model outputs while explicitly enforcing mass, momentum, and energy conservation. By embedding thermodynamic and rheological constraints within both the loss function and network architecture, the model resolves multi-scale interactions without numerically integrating governing equations. Across diverse Arctic configurations and varied atmospheric forcings, our approach reproduces critical morphological features and dynamical regimes with accuracy matching conventional solvers, yet reduces inference time by three orders of magnitude. The trained generator also facilitates rapid ensemble construction, substantially improving uncertainty quantification for seasonal forecasts and long-term climate projections. Ultimately, this work establishes generative artificial intelligence as a robust, physically constrained surrogate for process-resolving sea-ice models, providing a scalable computational pathway for next-generation Earth system predictions.

title: Imitation Learning for Active Neck Motion Enabling Robot Manipulation beyond the Field of View
text_ai: Most prior research in deep imitation learning has predominantly utilized fixed cameras for image input, which constrains task performance to the predefined field of view. However, enabling a robot to actively maneuver its neck can significantly expand the scope of imitation learning to encompass a wider variety of tasks and expressive actions such as neck gestures. To address this limitation, we propose an imitation learning framework that jointly optimizes visual observation acquisition and manipulation policies through active neck articulation. Our architecture couples a proprioceptive state estimator with a transformer-based action decoder, enabling the agent to dynamically adjust its viewpoint via learned kinematics while executing end-effector trajectories. Training employs behavior cloning augmented by temporal consistency losses to stabilize policy convergence under continuous viewpoint shifts. Simulations and physical deployments demonstrate that our method successfully tracks occluded targets and sustains a 91% success rate when objects move beyond the original camera frame, surpassing fixed-camera baselines by 28%. The system generalizes across cluttered scenes without explicit depth sensing or predefined gaze maps. These findings validate active neck actuation for reliable visual manipulation, establishing a pathway for embodied agents operating in unconstrained workspaces.

title: Distributed Optimal Voltage Control with Asynchronous and Delayed Communication
text_ai: The increased penetration of volatile renewable energy into distribution networks necessities more efficient distributed voltage control. In this paper, we design distributed feedback control algorithms where each bus can inject \emph{both active and reactive} power into the grid to regulate the voltages. To accommodate practical communication constraints, our framework explicitly accounts for asynchronous updates and bounded time delays among neighboring agents. We formulate the voltage regulation problem as a decentralized optimization task subject to network power flow constraints and operational limits. By leveraging primal-dual dynamics over directed communication graphs, we derive update rules that require only local information exchange while guaranteeing asymptotic convergence to the globally optimal operating point. Rigorous stability analysis demonstrates robustness against heterogeneous delay profiles and packet losses. Numerical simulations on IEEE test feeders confirm that the proposed scheme maintains voltage profiles within prescribed bounds under high renewable variability, significantly reducing computational burden compared to centralized counterparts. These findings underscore the practical viability of fully distributed control architectures for next-generation smart grids.

title: Discovering Relationships between Object Categories via Universal Canonical Maps
text_ai: We tackle the problem of learning the geometry of multiple categories of deformable objects jointly. Recent work has shown that it is possible to learn a unified dense pose predictor for several categories of related objects. However, training such models requires to initialize inter-category correspondences by hand. To address this limitation, we propose Universal Canonical Maps, a fully unsupervised framework that automatically discovers semantic and geometric alignments across diverse object categories. Our approach learns a shared latent manifold where corresponding structural points are consistently projected into a common coordinate system. By optimizing a novel cross-category consistency objective alongside category-specific deformation fields, the model iteratively refines these mappings through self-supervised alignment. This eliminates manual initialization while enabling seamless knowledge transfer between domains. Extensive experiments on multi-object dense pose benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy, significantly outperforming supervised baselines. Furthermore, the learned canonical representations yield interpretable cross-category structural relationships, demonstrating robust generalization across unseen categories, varying poses, and complex articulations.

title: Mol-R1: Towards Explicit Long-CoT Reasoning in Molecule Discovery
text_ai: Large language models (LLMs), especially Explicit Long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning models like DeepSeek-R1 and QWQ, have demonstrated powerful reasoning capabilities, achieving impressive performance in commonsense reasoning and mathematical inference. Despite their effectiveness, Long-CoT reasoning models are often criticized for their limited ability and low efficiency in knowledge-intensive domains such as molecule discovery. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mol-R1, a specialized framework that adapts explicit Long-CoT reasoning to chemical space exploration through domain-aligned reinforcement learning and structured molecular representations. Mol-R1 integrates graph-based molecular encodings with stepwise logical deduction, enabling the model to explicitly trace synthetic pathways, evaluate thermodynamic feasibility, and iteratively refine candidate structures. We fine-tune base reasoning models using a reward mechanism grounded in chemical validity metrics and expert-curated synthesis trajectories. Extensive evaluations across retrosynthesis planning, target-driven generation, and multi-step optimization benchmarks demonstrate that Mol-R1 significantly outperforms conventional LLM baselines in both predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. Ablations show that domain-specific reward shaping and structural constraints are critical for sustaining multi-step coherence. Notably, the architecture reduces invalid intermediate states by 68% while preserving faithful, step-by-step justification logs. These findings establish explicit Long-CoT paradigms as scalable tools for complex chemical design, paving the way for human-aligned AI systems in drug discovery and materials engineering.

title: Improving Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer via Progressive Code-Switching
text_ai: Code-switching is a data augmentation scheme mixing words from multiple languages into source lingual text. It has achieved considerable generalization performance of cross-lingual transfer tasks by aligning cross-lingual contextual word representations. However, uncontrolled and over-replaced code-switching would augment dirty samples to model training. To mitigate this degradation, we propose Progressive Code-Switching (PCS), a novel augmentation framework that dynamically modulates linguistic mixing throughout the training trajectory. Rather than applying uniform substitution rates, PCS employs a curriculum-driven strategy that gradually introduces multilingual tokens based on semantic alignment and contextual coherence thresholds. This iterative refinement preserves syntactic integrity while progressively bridging monolingual and multilingual representation spaces. We evaluate PCS across five established zero-shot cross-lingual benchmarks spanning natural language inference, question answering, and sequence labeling. Empirical results demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms conventional augmentation baselines, yielding average gains of 4.2% in F1 and 3.8% in accuracy. Ablation studies confirm that progressive scheduling significantly curbs noise accumulation relative to static mixing protocols. By harmonizing linguistic diversity with structural fidelity, PCS establishes a robust paradigm for scalable multilingual adaptation without necessitating high-quality parallel corpora.

title: Mid-term results of the modular ANCA-Fit femoral component in total hip replacement
text_ai: We report the minimum five-year follow-up of 352 primary total hip replacements using the uncemented hydroxyapatite-coated ANCA-Fit femoral component with a modular neck and head. The series comprised 319 patients (212 men, 107 women) with a mean age at operation of 64.4 years (28 to 97). The principal diagnosis was osteoarthritis. Clinical and radiological assessments followed standardized institutional protocols. Function was evaluated using the Harris Hip Score and visual analog scale for pain. Survivorship was calculated using Kaplan-Meier estimates with revision for any reason as the endpoint. Serial radiographs assessed stem alignment, bone ingrowth, and stress shielding patterns. At a mean follow-up of 6.4 years, the mean Harris Hip Score improved significantly from 48.3 to 91.6 points (p<0.001), with pain scores reducing from 7.2 to 1.4. Imaging confirmed stable fixation without subsidence exceeding 2 mm or progressive radiolucent lines. Two stems required revision for aseptic loosening, and one failure occurred secondary to high-energy trauma, yielding a 94.1% survivorship estimate at seven years. These mid-term outcomes demonstrate reliable biological fixation, substantial functional restoration, and durable implant survival, supporting the continued use of this modular design in contemporary joint reconstruction.

title: Hyper Strategy Logic
text_ai: Strategy logic (SL) is a powerful temporal logic that enables strategic reasoning in multi-agent systems. SL supports explicit (first-order) quantification over strategies and provides a logical framework to express many important properties such as Nash equilibria, dominant strategies, etc. While in SL the same strategy can be used in multiple strategy profiles, each such profile is evaluated w.r.t. a single execution trace, thereby precluding relational properties dependent on correlations across multiple runs. To bridge this gap, we introduce Hyper Strategy Logic (HSL), extending SL with path variables and allowing strategic quantifiers to range over trace sets simultaneously. HSL captures critical multi-agent hyperproperties, including information-flow security, fairness constraints, and robust coordination guarantees. We formalize its semantics over Kripke structures, prove strict expressive dominance over both SL and HyperLTL, and develop an automata-based decision procedure. Our analysis establishes tight 2EXPTIME-completeness for model checking, confirming that HSL scales effectively despite heightened expressiveness. Consequently, this framework unifies strategic reasoning and hyperproperty verification within a single, decidable formalism for rigorous specification.

title: A new introduction rule for disjunction
text_ai: We extend Natural Deduction with a third introduction rule for the disjunction, $\vee$-i3, with a conclusion $\Gamma\vdash A\vee B$, but both premises $\Gamma\vdash A$ and $\Gamma\vdash B$. This rule is admissible in Natural Deduction. This extension is interesting in several respects. First, we show that the extended system preserves strong normalization and the subformula property. Analyzing the reduction semantics of $\vee$-i3, we prove that every derivation can be systematically transformed into a standard normal form without increasing proof height. Second, under the Curry–Howard correspondence, the rule yields a novel term constructor merging independent computations of types $A$ and $B$, clarifying parallel composition in intuitionistic type theory. Third, we analyze proof search efficiency, demonstrating that $\vee$-i3 eliminates redundancy when both disjuncts derive independently from identical contexts. We further supply explicit translation algorithms between calculi, guaranteeing interoperability. Finally, we evaluate compatibility with structural rules and scalability to predicate logics. Together, these results frame $\vee$-i3 as a computationally meaningful yet theoretically conservative enhancement of natural deduction.

title: Bordetella biofilms: a lifestyle leading to persistent infections.
text_ai: Bordetella bronchiseptica and B. pertussis are Gram-negative bacteria that cause respiratory diseases in animals and humans. The current incidence of whooping cough or pertussis caused by B. pertussis has reached levels not observed since the 1950s. Although pertussis is traditionally known as an acute childhood disease, it has recently resurged in vaccinated adolescents and adults. Emerging evidence indicates that biofilm formation constitutes a pivotal adaptive strategy facilitating prolonged airway colonization and immune evasion. Within structured microbial aggregates, Bordetella cells demonstrate markedly enhanced tolerance to phagocytic clearance, complement-mediated lysis, and conventional antimicrobial regimens. These physiological adaptations are coordinately regulated by quorum-sensing circuits and extracellular polymeric matrix secretion, which collectively sustain metabolic activity while neutralizing host-derived oxidative stress. Consequently, biofilm-centric phenotypes likely drive the pathological transition from acute respiratory illness to chronic carriage, particularly among cohorts with waning vaccine-induced immunity. By synthesizing current insights into the genetic architecture governing Bordetella biofilm maturation, this work identifies promising antimicrobial targets designed to dismantle established communities. Integrating these mechanistic findings into contemporary clinical frameworks could ultimately optimize therapeutic protocols against recalcitrant Bordetella infections.

title: What Makes for Good Views for Contrastive Learning?
text_ai: Contrastive learning between multiple views of the data has recently achieved state of the art performance in the field of self-supervised representation learning. Despite its success, the influence of different view choices has been less studied. We systematically investigate how view construction strategies affect downstream representation quality across diverse architectures, datasets, and augmentation pipelines. Our comprehensive empirical analysis reveals that optimal views must balance invariance to semantic-preserving transformations with sufficient structural diversity to prevent representational collapse. We identify critical trade-offs between geometric perturbations, color distortions, and spatial masking, demonstrating that excessive similarity between augmented samples significantly degrades discriminative capacity. Furthermore, we propose a unified framework for quantifying view compatibility, which correlates strongly with final model performance independent of the underlying encoder or optimizer configuration. These findings yield actionable guidelines for principled view design, motivating lightweight regularization mechanisms that enhance generalization across supervised and few-shot benchmarks. This work ultimately reframes view generation as a learnable component of the training objective.

title: Implantable LVAD infections: implications for permanent use of the device
text_ai: BACKGROUND: Infection in implantable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) patients is common and has serious implications regarding permanent use of the LVAD. METHODS: Thirty-three patients had HeartMate LVAD insertion as a bridge to heart transplantation. The mean length of hospital stay was 8 days before LVAD insertion. Follow-up averaged 14 months. Infections were classified according to standardized criteria, with primary outcomes including sepsis, device explantation, and transplant cancellation. Driveline exit-site infections occurred in 42% of cohort members, while deep pocket infections accounted for 18%. Multivariate analysis identified prolonged preoperative ventilation and diabetes mellitus as independent predictors of infectious complications. Patients experiencing severe infections demonstrated significantly reduced 1-year survival compared to uninfected counterparts (p=0.03). Furthermore, 27% of infected individuals were rendered ineligible for subsequent transplantation due to refractory bacteremia or fungal dissemination. These data underscore that infectious morbidity substantially compromises the efficacy of durable mechanical circulatory support. To sustain long-term viability, future protocols must prioritize stringent perioperative asepsis, advanced antimicrobial-coated hardware, and proactive outpatient surveillance. Rigorous clinical implementation remains essential. Without such interventions, infection-related attrition will continue to limit the widespread adoption of LVADs as definitive destination therapy.

title: The influence of dysbiosis on kidney stones that risk up renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
text_ai: Kidney stone is a common urological condition, the prevalence and incidence of which has escalated in the last few years due to dietary habits and other related medical conditions such as obesity and diabetes mellitus. It is a chronic disease which leads to loss of kidney function(s) and nephrectomy. Emerging evidence indicates that gastrointestinal and urinary microbiome alterations significantly accelerate lithogenesis and malignant transformation. This investigation elucidates the mechanistic interplay between microbial dysbiosis, chronic stone-induced mucosal injury, and renal epithelial tumorigenesis. Integrated metagenomic profiling and histopathological evaluation of patient cohorts reveal that pathogenic bacterial taxa amplify localized inflammatory cascades and oxidative stress, thereby promoting genomic instability and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Additionally, dysbiotic signatures strongly associate with elevated pro-oncogenic cytokines and aberrant metabolite secretion, particularly secondary bile acids, which directly stimulate neoplastic proliferation. These data delineate a previously unrecognized microbiome-mediated axis wherein persistent nephrolithiasis cultivates a tumor-permissive microenvironment. Ultimately, modulating microbial equilibrium via targeted therapeutic approaches may provide novel preventive avenues against RCC progression and preserve renal parenchyma.

title: The role of T-helper/T-suppressor ratio in the adaptive immune response: a dynamical model
text_ai: Recent experimental studies have suggested the ratio between T-helper and T-suppressor lymphocytes as an index of immunosuppression in HIV, cancer, immunosenescence and inflammatory and auto-immune diseases. However, a quantitative understanding of the impact of this ratio on the immune response has lagged behind data and its validity as a tool for prognostic monitoring or therapeutic target remains an open question. To bridge this gap, we formulate a deterministic dynamical model capturing nonlinear feedback between T-helper and T-suppressor populations. The system incorporates antigen-driven proliferation and cytokine-mediated cross-regulation, enabling rigorous analysis of equilibrium stability and bifurcation structure. Simulations demonstrate that the Th/Ts ratio exhibits threshold-dependent transitions, wherein subtle deviations near critical manifolds trigger abrupt shifts between protective immunity and chronic suppression. Global sensitivity analysis isolates cytokine signaling efficacy and lymphocyte survival rates as dominant parameters governing ratio resilience. These findings establish the Th/Ts ratio as a dynamic control variable, revealing how perturbation thresholds dictate immune trajectory. Finally, the model establishes a mechanistic basis for interpreting clinical ratio metrics and directs immunotherapeutic strategies toward restoring homeostatic balance rather than boosting raw cell numbers.

title: The prevalence of AGN feedback in massive galaxies at z~1
text_ai: We use the optical--infrared imaging in the UKIDSS Ultra Deep Survey field, in combination with the new deep radio map of Arumugam et al., to calculate the distribution of radio luminosities among galaxies as a function of stellar mass in two redshift bins across the interval 0.4<z<1.2. We identify a sharp rise in the radio-loud fraction above M_* ~ 10^11 M_sun, remaining roughly constant across both redshift slices. Cross-matching with spectral energy distribution templates reveals that these high-luminosity sources reside almost exclusively in quiescent systems, indicating that jet-driven outflows dominate the quenching mechanism. Our derived AGN-host fractions align with semi-analytical models employing strong mechanical feedback, but exceed predictions from purely thermal wind scenarios. Consequently, we conclude that AGN feedback operates efficiently at z ~ 1, successfully regulating star formation in the most massive halos. Collectively, these results firmly underscore the critical role of radio-mode ejections in hierarchical galaxy assembly, while highlighting the need for deeper sub-millimeter observations to constrain the exact energetics of circumgalactic medium heating.

title: Outpatient commitment in mental health services from a municipal view.
text_ai: Outpatient commitment (OC) is a legal decision for compulsory mental health care when the patient stays in his or her own home. Municipal health-care workers have a key role for patients with OC decision, but little is known about how the legislation system with OC works from the municipality's point of view. This study employs a qualitative design to explore municipal experiences through semi-structured interviews with forty-two mental health professionals and administrative leaders across six municipalities. Thematic analysis reveals that effective OC implementation hinges on robust inter-agency collaboration, yet practitioners consistently report fragmented communication channels between psychiatric hospitals, primary care providers, and local authorities. Key challenges include ambiguous legislative mandates, insufficient staffing resources, and ethical dilemmas surrounding autonomy versus coercive intervention. Furthermore, municipal actors emphasize the critical need for standardized operational protocols and specialized legal training to navigate compliance requirements efficiently. The findings underscore a tension between statutory obligations and practical service delivery constraints. To optimize OC systems, policymakers must prioritize structural alignment among regional health authorities and municipalities, establish clear accountability frameworks, and integrate continuous professional development focused on community-based compulsory care. These insights provide recommendations for refining municipal mental health infrastructure and improving outpatient commitment administration.

title: Single-Particle Green Functions in Exactly Solvable Models of Bose and Fermi Liquids
text_ai: Based on a class of exactly solvable models of interacting bose and fermi liquids, we compute the single-particle propagators of these systems exactly for all wavelengths and energies and in any number of spatial dimensions. Our analytical expressions reveal distinct spectral structures governing low-energy excitations in each sector. For fermions, we identify well-defined Landau quasiparticles characterized by finite residues at the Fermi surface, alongside incoherent continua scaling algebraically away from the pole. Conversely, the bosonic spectrum exhibits singular spectral weight distributed across broad energy bands, reflecting strong phase fluctuations and suppressed condensation in reduced dimensionalities. We derive closed-form relations connecting imaginary-time correlators to response functions, demonstrating how dimensionality crossover induces smooth transitions between coherent and incoherent transport regimes. These results establish a rigorous benchmark for perturbative many-body techniques and clarify the microscopic origins of non-Fermi liquid phenomenology in correlated systems. The formalism readily extends to disordered potentials and finite temperatures, providing a unified description of critical dynamics across coupling strengths.

title: On the ubiquity of duopolies in constant sum congestion games
text_ai: We analyse a coalition formation game between strategic service providers of a congestible service. The key novelty of our formulation is that it is a constant sum game, i.e., the total payoff across all service providers (or coalitions of providers) is fixed, and dictated by the size of the market. Under this framework, we characterize stable coalition structures through the lens of the generalized core, demonstrating that pairwise mergers consistently dominate alternative configurations. Specifically, we prove that when consumer demand exhibits standard elasticity properties, any internally stable partition converges to a configuration of disjoint duopolies, irrespective of initial provider heterogeneity or aggregate capacity constraints. This structural convergence arises because constant sum payoffs amplify negative externality internalization, rendering larger coalitions vulnerable to profitable deviations while fragmented markets suffer from severe congestion losses. Our analytical derivations are corroborated by simulation studies mapping parameter spaces across varying demand regimes and cost asymmetries. These findings establish duopoly formation as a robust equilibrium phenomenon rather than an artifact. We conclude by discussing theoretical and practical implications, highlighting how constant sum dynamics fundamentally reshape competitive landscapes in service industries.

title: Language Embedded 3D Gaussians for Open-Vocabulary Scene Understanding
text_ai: Open-vocabulary querying in 3D space is challenging but essential for scene understanding tasks such as object localization and segmentation. Language-embedded scene representations have made progress by incorporating language features into 3D spaces. However, their efficacy heavily depends on neural networks that are resource-intensive in training and rendering. To address these limitations, we introduce Language Embedded 3D Gaussians (LE3G), which aligns frozen vision-language embeddings with explicit Gaussian primitives. By mapping text-conditioned features directly onto per-Gaussian attributes during differentiable rasterization, our approach eliminates heavy decoder networks and iterative optimization. We design a lightweight feature distillation pipeline that preserves fine-grained geometry while enforcing cross-modal semantic consistency. Evaluated on ScanNetV2 and OpenScene benchmarks, LE3G achieves state-of-the-art accuracy for open-vocabulary localization and segmentation, reducing training time by 65% and inference latency by 40% relative to neural field baselines. Furthermore, the explicit representation enables rapid zero-shot generalization to novel categories and supports real-time interactive querying. Our results demonstrate that coupling 3D Gaussian splatting with direct language projection yields a computationally efficient, scalable paradigm for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding.

title: Context-Dependent Diffusion Network for Visual Relationship Detection
text_ai: Visual relationship detection can bridge the gap between computer vision and natural language for scene understanding of images. Different from pure object recognition tasks, the relation triplets of subject-predicate-object lie on an extreme diversity space, such as \textit{person-behind-person} and \textit{car-behind-building}, while suffering from the problem of combinatorial explosion. To address this limitation, we introduce a Context-Dependent Diffusion Network that explicitly models relational priors through iterative score refinement. Rather than treating predicates as independent classification targets, our architecture employs a latent diffusion trajectory to progressively disentangle contextual dependencies from joint visual-linguistic representations. By integrating a cross-modal gating mechanism that dynamically adjusts receptive fields according to local scene statistics, the framework efficiently suppresses spurious interactions while amplifying structurally plausible associations. Comprehensive evaluations on the Visual Genome and VRD datasets reveal that our method achieves substantial gains in recall@50 and mean average precision, with pronounced improvements over long-tail predicate distributions. Ablation analyses further validate that the context-guided diffusion pathway markedly alleviates feature entanglement, yielding superior transferability across complex compositional layouts. Ultimately, these findings establish a robust new paradigm for generative scene understanding.

title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
text_ai: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and their increasing use in medical question-answering necessitate rigorous evaluation of their reliability. A critical challenge lies in hallucination, where models generate plausible yet factually incorrect outputs. In the medical domain, this poses serious risks to patient safety and clinical decision-making. To address this gap, we introduce MedHallu, a novel benchmark specifically engineered to assess and quantify hallucination phenomena across diverse medical reasoning tasks. MedHallu comprises over 5,200 expert-curated questions spanning multiple clinical specialties, each paired with verified ground-truth answers and systematically annotated by type. We evaluate state-of-the-art open-source and proprietary LLMs under standardized prompting protocols, revealing significant performance disparities and systematic error patterns. Our findings demonstrate that even leading models exhibit high susceptibility to factual distortions, particularly in nuanced diagnostic and pharmacological contexts. Furthermore, we propose a hierarchical scoring mechanism that isolates specific failure modes. Ultimately, MedHallu provides a reproducible framework for continuous model auditing, establishing a critical baseline for developing safer, more reliable AI-driven clinical support systems.

title: QCD correction to gluino decay to $t\bar{t}\tilde{\chi}^0_1$ in the MSSM
text_ai: We calculate the complete next-to-leading order QCD corrections to the three-body decay of gluino into top-pair associated with a lightest neutralino in the minimal supersymmetric standard model. We obtain that the LO and NLO QCD corrected decay widths of $\tilde{g} \to t \bar{t} \tilde{\chi}_1^0$ at the ${\rm SPS 6}$ benchmark point are $0.1490 GeV$ and 0.1069 GeV respectively, and the relative correction is -28.2%. This substantial negative shift is primarily driven by virtual vertex and self-energy contributions alongside real gluon emission diagrams. We quantify the renormalization scale dependence of the total rate, demonstrating that the theoretical uncertainty decreases from roughly $\pm5\%$ at leading order to below $\pm2\%$ after incorporating the full next-to-leading order terms. Invariant mass and transverse momentum distributions for the top-quark pair exhibit only mild shape distortions, remaining well within standard experimental acceptance thresholds. Phenomenologically, the suppressed partial width implies stricter lower bounds on gluino masses when re-evaluating existing LHC dijet plus missing energy limits. These findings establish a reliable perturbative framework for analyzing three-body cascades in compressed supersymmetric spectra, directly improving signal efficiency estimates and kinematic reconstruction strategies for upcoming high-energy collider searches.

title: Automated Bridge Component Recognition using Video Data
text_ai: This paper investigates the automated recognition of structural bridge components using video data. Although understanding video data for structural inspections is straightforward for human inspectors, the implementation of the same task using machine learning methods has not been fully realized. To address this gap, we propose a deep learning framework integrating temporal-spatial feature extraction with attention mechanisms tailored for multi-view bridge surveillance footage. The architecture processes sequential frames to isolate and classify critical elements, including girders, bearings, expansion joints, and deck surfaces. Trained on a curated dataset of 50,000 annotated video segments across diverse conditions, the model achieves a mean average precision of 94.3%, surpassing baseline networks by 12.7%. Ablation studies confirm that our hierarchical temporal pooling effectively mitigates occlusion and motion blur artifacts prevalent in field recordings. These results demonstrate that reliable, real-time component identification remains feasible without expensive sensors. Ultimately, this research provides a deployable computer vision pipeline for routine infrastructure monitoring, reducing manual inspection expenditures while improving asset management protocols.

title: Quantum secret sharing for a multipartite system under energy dissipation
text_ai: We propose a protocol for multipartite secret sharing of quantum information through an \textit{amplitude damping} quantum channel. This network is, for example, of two organizations communicating with their own employees connected via classical channels locally. We consider a GHZ state distributed among four members in an asymmetric fashion where the members of a sub-party collaborate to decode the received information at their end. By modeling the dissipative dynamics with the Lindblad master equation, we derive analytical expressions for the shared state fidelity as a function of the damping parameter and network topology. Our analysis reveals a critical dissipation threshold beyond which deterministic recovery becomes impossible without active error correction. We demonstrate that strategic allocation of qubits across the sub-parties significantly mitigates information loss, preserving secure key generation rates even under moderate environmental coupling. Numerical simulations confirm that the proposed asymmetric configuration outperforms symmetric distributions in high-noise regimes, establishing practical guidelines for deploying quantum secret sharing in realistic, lossy communication infrastructures. These findings underscore the robustness of multipartite protocols against amplitude damping and provide a solid foundation for future fault-tolerant quantum networks.

title: SensatUrban: Learning Semantics from Urban-Scale Photogrammetric Point Clouds
text_ai: With the recent availability and affordability of commercial depth sensors and 3D scanners, an increasing number of 3D (i.e., RGBD, point cloud) datasets have been publicized to facilitate research in 3D computer vision. However, existing datasets either cover relatively small areas or have limited semantic annotations. To address these limitations, we present SensatUrban, a large-scale benchmark featuring densely reconstructed, fully labeled point clouds encompassing 7.6 km² of heterogeneous urban landscapes. Extracted through structure-from-motion photogrammetry, the collection delivers sub-centimeter geometric fidelity coupled with dense semantic masks across nine functional categories. Leveraging this resource, we develop a memory-efficient hierarchical transformer architecture that jointly models local surface geometry and long-range spatial coherence. Comprehensive evaluations reveal superior segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency relative to contemporary methods, maintaining consistent performance under significant occlusion, motion blur, and illumination variation. Furthermore, we release an open-source implementation alongside standardized evaluation protocols to foster community-driven advancements in large-scale 3D scene understanding. By bridging the critical scale–annotation divide, this contribution establishes a rigorous foundation for deployable semantic perception in expansive outdoor environments, directly supporting next-generation autonomous navigation and dynamic urban digital twin construction.

title: Clustering, order conditions, and languages of interval exchanges
text_ai: For any interval exchange transformation $T$ (standard or generalized), if we define a morphism $\phi$ from the set of letters to the set of the return words of a word in the natural coding, respecting the lexicographical order, the word $\phi v$ clusters (for the Burrows-Wheeler transform) for the permutation of $T$ if and only if the word $v$ clusters for the permutation of the induced map of $T$ on the cylinder $[w]$. We leverage this correspondence to characterize clustering patterns through explicit order conditions on the underlying permutation, revealing a link between BWT clustering and the combinatorial geometry of interval exchanges. Our analysis extends Sturmian results to higher dimensions, demonstrating that cluster-preserving morphisms induce bijections between the languages of $T$ and its renormalizations. These results yield criteria for recognizing mixing properties via symbolic codes and establish a unified framework for studying spectral features through return-word substitutions. Ultimately, this work connects dynamical systems, combinatorics on words, and data compression, providing rigorous tools for analyzing interval dynamics.

title: Volatile evolution and atmospheres of Trans-Neptunian Objects
text_ai: At 30-50 K, the temperatures typical for surfaces in the Kuiper Belt (e.g. Stern & Trafton 2008), only seven species have sublimation pressures higher than 1 nbar (Fray & Schmitt 2009): Ne, N$_2$, CO, Ar, O$_2$, CH$_4$, and Kr. Of these, N$_2$, CO, and CH$_4$ have been detected or inferred on the surfaces of Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs). Here, we present a coupled thermal-volcanic model tracking long-term sublimation, condensation, and atmospheric escape of these ices across diverse TNO populations. We quantify fractional species loss using integrated radiative transfer, porosity-dependent heat conduction, and laboratory vapor pressures across varying compositions, radii, and orbital distances spanning various eccentricities and inclinations. Simulations indicate N$_2$ and CO deplete rapidly on bodies <500 km unless periodically sustained by cryovolcanic outgassing or sequestered in amorphous matrices, reflecting substantial mass fractionation. Conversely, CH$_4$ persists longer but undergoes extensive photolysis, generating refractory organic residues that lower albedo and thermally insulate subsurface reservoirs, modifying spectral signatures in the near-infrared. Contemporary large TNOs retain atmospheric pressures orders of magnitude below Plutonian values, consistent with rapid early escape during the nebular epoch. These results constrain primordial volatile inventories and demonstrate that size-dependent thermal and dynamical histories fundamentally alter their observable geophysical properties.
