title: Graph-Aware Language Model Pre-Training on a Large Graph Corpus Can Help Multiple Graph Applications
text_ai: Model pre-training on large text corpora has been demonstrated effective for various downstream applications in the NLP domain. In the graph mining domain, a similar analogy can be drawn for pre-training graph models on large graphs in the hope of benefiting downstream graph applications, which has also been explored by several recent studies. To bridge this gap, we introduce a graph-aware language modeling framework that jointly optimizes textual semantics and structural topology over a large graph corpus. By encoding adjacency patterns directly into the self-attention mechanism, our approach captures both linguistic context and relational dependencies without explicit message passing. We evaluate the pre-trained representations across five diverse graph benchmarks, including link prediction, node classification, and community detection. Experimental results demonstrate consistent improvements of 4–12% over strong baselines, highlighting the transferability of graph-informed embeddings. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that structural awareness drives performance gains. These findings underscore the viability of unified graph-text pre-training as a foundational paradigm for scalable graph machine learning.

title: The POKEMON Speckle Survey of Nearby M Dwarfs. III. The Stellar Multiplicity Rate of M Dwarfs within 15 pc
text_ai: M dwarfs are ubiquitous in our galaxy, and the rate at which they host stellar companions, and the properties of these companions, provides a window into the formation and evolution of the star(s), and of any planets that they may host. Here we present results from the third data release of the POKEMON speckle interferometry campaign, targeting a volume-limited sample of 142 M dwarfs within 15 pc. Utilizing single-channel and dual-channel speckle imaging at 844 nm and 673 nm, respectively, we achieve diffraction-limited angular resolutions down to ~30 mas, enabling robust companion detection across projected separations from 0.03 to 5 au. Through rigorous Monte Carlo completeness simulations, we establish detection limits across the full parameter space. Our analysis identifies 14 new binary systems, yielding a primary companion fraction of $12.1^{+3.1}_{-2.6}$% at projected separations between 0.03 and 5 au. This rate aligns with prior ground-based surveys but significantly exceeds wide-separation population synthesis predictions, indicating a shallower separation distribution at tight orbits. No significant trend emerges between multiplicity fraction and primary spectral type across the M0–M6 sequence. Completeness-corrected analysis reveals that close companions are prevalent among nearby low-mass stars, requiring their explicit inclusion in exoplanet yield modeling and initial mass function constructions.

title: Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning for Aligning Reasoning in Language Models
text_ai: The alignments of reasoning abilities between smaller and larger Language Models are largely conducted via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using demonstrations generated from robust Large Language Models (LLMs). Although these approaches deliver more performant models, they do not show sufficiently strong generalization ability as the training only relies on the provided demonstrations. To address this limitation, we introduce Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning (SR-IT), a paradigm enabling student models to iteratively critique and enhance their own reasoning trajectories during alignment. Rather than passively consuming fixed demonstrations, SR-IT incorporates a lightweight refinement loop that dynamically adjusts intermediate steps based on internal consistency checks and task constraints. This self-supervised correction mechanism fosters deeper causal understanding and mitigates distributional shift across unseen problem formulations. We evaluate SR-IT across mathematical reasoning, code generation, and logical inference benchmarks. Results demonstrate consistent improvements over standard SFT baselines, yielding average accuracy gains of 8.4% on out-of-distribution test sets while preserving computational efficiency during training. Ablation studies confirm that iterative self-correction is essential for sustaining performance under distributional stress. Our findings establish self-guided optimization as a scalable pathway toward robust, highly generalizable reasoning alignment.

title: Device-Independent Bit Commitment based on the CHSH Inequality
text_ai: Bit commitment and coin flipping occupy a unique place in the device-independent landscape, as the only device-independent protocols thus far suggested for these tasks are reliant on tripartite GHZ correlations. Indeed, we know of no other bipartite tasks, which admit a device-independent formulation, but which are not known to be implementable using only bipartite nonlocality. Here we demonstrate that device-independent bit commitment can be securely realized using solely bipartite nonlocal correlations, specifically those violating the CHSH inequality. Our construction circumvents the traditional reliance on multipartite entanglement by employing a sequential measurement strategy across multiple Bell test rounds, wherein temporal correlations supplement spatial nonlocality to enforce binding and hiding constraints. We present a rigorous security proof against general quantum attacks, demonstrating that any adversarial deviation reduces their advantage below negligible thresholds while preserving a finite key rate. This finding resolves fundamental questions regarding minimal nonlocal resources necessary for cryptographic commitments, establishing that bipartite systems alone suffice when augmented with appropriate temporal structures. Consequently, our framework substantially enhances the experimental viability of device-independent cryptography, enabling practical deployments using current photonic architectures.

title: Napoleonic Constructions in the Hyperbolic Plane
text_ai: In the Euclidean setting, Napoleon's Theorem states that if one constructs an equilateral triangle on either the outside or the inside of each side of a given triangle and then connects the barycenters of those three new triangles, the resulting triangle happens to be equilateral. This classical result, however, does not directly transfer to spaces of constant negative curvature. In this work, we investigate the behavior of Napoleonic constructions within the Poincaré disk model, analyzing how hyperbolic parallelism and angle deficit affect the equilateral configuration. By employing Möbius transformations and hyperbolic trigonometry, we derive explicit conditions under which the barycentric triangle retains approximate equilateral symmetry or converges to a specific limiting shape as curvature approaches zero. Our analysis reveals that while strict equilaterality is generally lost, the deviation can be precisely quantified in terms of the original triangle’s hyperbolic area and circumradius. These findings clarify the geometric limits of classical constructions and establish a framework for studying affine-invariant properties in non-Euclidean manifolds.

title: CIMTx: An R package for causal inference with multiple treatments using observational data
text_ai: CIMTx provides efficient and unified functions to implement modern methods for causal inferences with multiple treatments using observational data with a focus on binary outcomes. The methods include regression adjustment, inverse probability of treatment weighting, Bayesian additive regression trees, regression adjustment with multivariate spline of the generalized propensity score, vector matching and targeted maximum likelihood estimation. Comprehensive simulation studies demonstrate that these algorithms substantially reduce bias and variance compared to conventional pairwise approaches, particularly under complex confounding structures. Real-world applications illustrate the package’s utility in epidemiology and policy evaluation, where distinguishing heterogeneous treatment effects across competing interventions remains critical. Prioritizing reproducibility, CIMTx features intuitive syntax, extensive documentation, and seamless integration with existing R workflows. By consolidating state-of-the-art estimators into a single framework, this tool lowers the technical barrier for researchers seeking rigorous multi-treatment causal analysis. Distributed via CRAN, the package enables widespread adoption and fosters methodological transparency. Comprehensive vignettes further assist users in navigating estimator selection and conducting thorough diagnostics.

title: Saliency-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Explanations
text_ai: Explainable AI (XAI) has gained significant attention for providing insights into the decision-making processes of deep learning models, particularly for image classification tasks through visual explanations visualized by saliency maps. Despite their success, challenges remain due to the lack of annotated datasets and standardized evaluation pipelines. To address these limitations, we introduce Saliency-Bench, a novel benchmark designed to systematically assess the faithfulness, robustness, and interpretability of diverse saliency methods. Our framework integrates a curated dataset comprising over 50,000 labeled images across multiple semantic categories, paired with human-annotated ground-truth attribution maps. We establish a unified evaluation protocol employing a comprehensive metric suite to quantify performance, enabling fair cross-method analysis under varying perturbation schemes and noise conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Saliency-Bench reveals critical performance disparities among state-of-the-art techniques, highlighting trade-offs between computational efficiency and explanation fidelity. By providing open-source tools and reproducible baselines, this work establishes a foundational resource for advancing trustworthy computer vision research and guiding the development of next-generation interpretable models.

title: Black Silicon with high density and high aspect ratio nanowhiskers
text_ai: Physical properties of black Silicon (b-Si) formed on Si wafers by reactive ion etching in chlorine plasma are reported in an attempt to clarify the formation mechanism and the origin of the observed optical and electrical phenomena which are promising for a variety of applications. Scanning electron microscopy reveals a dense forest of nanowhiskers with aspect ratios exceeding 20:1, resulting from preferential vertical etching driven by self-masking effects. Optical reflectance measurements demonstrate broadband absorption below 2% across the visible and near-infrared spectra, directly correlating with graded effective refractive index profiles established by the tapered nanostructures. Concurrently, Hall effect analyses indicate a marked reduction in carrier mobility due to enhanced surface scattering, yet photocurrent generation remains robust under simulated solar illumination. These findings substantiate a kinetic model wherein chlorine-containing intermediates govern whisker nucleation and lateral growth suppression. The synergistic integration of ultra-low reflectivity and tunable charge transport characteristics positions this b-Si architecture as a viable candidate for photodetectors and optical sensors. Furthermore, systematic variation of plasma bias voltage demonstrates that ion bombardment energy critically regulates whisker density, providing a direct pathway for optimizing material synthesis toward targeted optoelectronic implementations.

title: Exploring Generative AI for Sim2Real in Driving Data Synthesis
text_ai: Datasets are essential for training and testing vehicle perception algorithms. However, the collection and annotation of real-world images is time-consuming and expensive. Driving simulators offer a solution by automatically generating various driving scenarios with corresponding annotations, but the simulation-to-reality (Sim2Real) domain gap remains a challenge. To bridge this discrepancy, we investigate generative artificial intelligence frameworks tailored for photorealistic domain adaptation in synthetic driving environments. Specifically, we integrate conditional diffusion models with adversarial training pipelines to translate rendered simulator outputs into reality-aligned imagery while preserving semantic consistency and geometric accuracy. Our approach employs a dual-pathway architecture that jointly optimizes appearance transfer and depth-aware feature alignment across diverse atmospheric and illumination conditions. The synthesized dataset is evaluated on standard benchmarks, including object detection, semantic segmentation, and monocular depth estimation, utilizing both synthetic-only and mixed-domain training regimes. Cross-validation across three public driving benchmarks confirms the robustness of the transferred representations. Experimental results demonstrate that our generative pipeline mitigates the Sim2Real performance degradation by 28.4% relative to conventional rendering baselines, effectively matching fine-tuned real-world benchmarks. Consequently, this work establishes generative modeling as a scalable paradigm for closing perceptual domain shifts, substantially reducing data acquisition overhead while maintaining rigorous safety standards for automated driving deployment.

title: A Virtual Quantum Network Prototype for Open Access
text_ai: The rise of quantum networks has revolutionized domains such as communication, sensing, and cybersecurity. Despite this progress, current quantum network systems remain limited in scale, are highly application-specific (e.g., for quantum key distribution), and lack a clear road map for global expansion. To address these architectural gaps, we introduce a virtual quantum network prototype designed for open-access deployment. Our framework integrates software-defined control planes with high-fidelity emulators, enabling multi-node topology simulation without physical qubit infrastructure. By deploying standardized application programming interfaces alongside modular routing protocols, the system facilitates seamless interoperability across heterogeneous devices while accommodating diverse computational workloads beyond conventional key distribution. Comprehensive benchmarking demonstrates sub-millisecond control latency, stable entanglement-swapping fidelity, and adaptive resource allocation under fluctuating network loads. Furthermore, latency measurements and error-correction overheads are systematically characterized across varying node densities. The platform is subsequently deployed as a cloud-hosted repository, granting unrestricted researcher access for reproducible experimentation and collaborative stack development. This open-access environment expedites algorithmic validation and protocol harmonization while delivering a scalable, vendor-neutral blueprint for expansive quantum internets. Consequently, our implementation effectively translates theoretical network paradigms into operational, globally compatible infrastructure.

title: Inflexibility and independence: Phase transitions in the majority-rule model
text_ai: In this work we study opinion formation in a population participating of a public debate with two distinct choices. We considered three distinct mechanisms of social interactions and individuals' behavior: conformity, nonconformity and inflexibility. The conformity is ruled by the majority-rule dynamics, whereas the nonconformity is introduced in the population as an independent behavior, implying the failure to attempted group influence. We analyze the stationary states and dynamical evolution across varying control parameters through analytical and numerical simulations. Our findings reveal sharp phase transitions between consensus, polarized, and disordered regimes, governed by the balance between individual inflexibility and independent agents. By mapping the order parameter and susceptibility, we identify critical thresholds where macroscopic polarization emerges or collapses. Notably, a moderate fraction of inflexible individuals can either stabilize consensus or trigger abrupt shifts depending on their initial alignment. These findings highlight how cognitive rigidity and autonomy jointly determine collective outcomes, clarifying the conditions that foster or mitigate extreme polarization.

title: Prompt GeV emission in the synchrotron self-Compton model for Gamma-Ray Bursts
text_ai: The detection in 10 bursts of an optical counterpart emission (i.e. during the prompt GRB phase) that is 10-10000 brighter than the extrapolation of the burst spectrum to optical frequencies suggests a synchrotron self-Compton origin for the GRB emission, synchrotron producing the optical counterpart emission. We present a comprehensive radiative transfer framework demonstrating that inverse Compton scattering of these intense optical synchrotron photons by the co-spatial ultra-relativistic electron population naturally generates the observed prompt GeV flux. By numerically integrating the coupled kinetic and radiative transfer equations for a laterally confined outflow, we demonstrate that the resultant spectral energy distribution accurately reproduces the simultaneous optical and high-energy photon data across all ten detected events. The model inherently demands bulk Lorentz factors of Γ ≈ 200–400 and a steeply declining electron injection spectrum above the cooling break. Importantly, our simulations confirm that the upscattered GeV component remains optically thin to pair production while satisfying causality constraints during the dissipation epoch. These results firmly establish the synchrotron self-Compton mechanism as a viable primary driver of high-energy prompt emission, thereby tightly constraining microphysical acceleration parameters and providing a coherent physical interpretation for multi-band GRB phenomenology within conventional internal shock paradigms.

title: Aberrated optical cavities
text_ai: Optical cavities are an enabling technology of modern quantum science: from their essential role in the operation of lasers, to applications as fly-wheels in atomic clocks and interaction-enhancing components in quantum optics experiments, developing a quantitative understanding of the mode-shapes and energies of optical cavities has been crucial for the growth of the field. However, practical implementations invariably suffer from manufacturing tolerances, thermal gradients, and alignment drifts that introduce phase aberrations at the resonator boundaries. These deviations perturb the ideal paraxial mode basis, inducing spectral crowding, mode hybridization, and degraded spatial overlap with quantum emitters. Here, we develop a rigorous perturbative framework that quantifies how arbitrary boundary deformations shift resonance frequencies and distort eigenmodes. By projecting the Helmholtz equation onto unperturbed Gaussian-Laguerre states, we derive analytic expressions for frequency splits and cross-mode coupling as explicit functions of surface figure errors and astigmatic misalignments. Validated against full-wave simulations and interferometric metrology, our model reveals that nanometer-scale roughness induces non-negligible linewidth broadening and polarization splitting in high-finesse resonators. These findings establish scalable design protocols for aberration-tolerant cavities and offer a predictive diagnostic platform for maintaining coherence in next-generation quantum devices.

title: Exploiting Qubit Reuse through Mid-circuit Measurement and Reset
text_ai: Quantum measurement is important to quantum computing as it extracts the outcome of the circuit at the end of the computation. Previously, all measurements have to be done at the end of the circuit. Otherwise, it will incur significant errors. But it is not the case now. Modern superconducting and trapped-ion architectures now support mid-circuit measurement and active reset, enabling early readout before full decoherence occurs. This capability unlocks qubit reuse, reducing the physical qubit overhead required for deep algorithms. In this work, we introduce a systematic framework for exploiting mid-circuit measurement and reset to reclaim idle qubits for subsequent computational stages. We present compiler-level transformations that schedule measurements and resets optimally across layered circuits, minimizing latency while preserving coherence. Experimental evaluation on noisy intermediate-scale processors demonstrates a 2.3× reduction in circuit depth and a 41% decrease in cumulative gate errors compared to standard deferred-readout strategies. Furthermore, our approach maintains logical fidelity above 98% under realistic noise models. These findings establish mid-circuit operations as a critical primitive for resource-constrained quantum workloads, paving the way for scalable algorithmic execution on near-term hardware.

title: Measurement of the Higgs boson mass with $H \rightarrow \gamma\gamma$ decays in 140 fb$^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
text_ai: The mass of the Higgs boson is measured in the $H\to\gamma\gamma$ decay channel, exploiting the high resolution of the invariant mass of photon pairs reconstructed from the decays of Higgs bosons produced in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. A dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $140~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ recorded by the ATLAS detector during Run 2 of the Large Hadron Collider is analysed. The signal yield is extracted via a simultaneous binned maximum-likelihood fit to the diphoton invariant mass spectrum, where the signal shape is modelled using simulation validated with control samples, and the irreducible and reducible backgrounds are constrained by sideband regions and dedicated calibration channels. Comprehensive evaluations of systematic uncertainties, including photon energy scale, calibration, trigger efficiency, and pileup modelling, are incorporated as nuisance parameters. The Higgs boson mass is determined to be $m_H = 125.11 \pm 0.11_{\mathrm{stat}} \pm 0.20_{\mathrm{syst}}~\mathrm{GeV}$. This measurement is consistent with Standard Model predictions and improves upon previous determinations, providing a stringent test of electroweak symmetry breaking and constraining new physics scenarios.

title: Identification of materials with strong magneto-structural coupling using computational high-throughput screening
text_ai: Important phenomena such as magnetostriction, magnetocaloric, and magnetoelectric effects arise from, or could be enhanced by, the coupling of magnetic and structural degrees of freedom. The coupling of spin and lattice also influence transport and structural properties in magnetic materials in particular around phase transitions. However, experimental discovery remains constrained by the vast chemical space and complex interplay of competing interactions. Here, we present a computational high-throughput screening framework to systematically identify compounds exhibiting strong magneto-structural coupling. By combining density functional theory calculations with symmetry-adapted strain tensors and magnetic susceptibility models, we quantify the coupling strength across thousands of thermodynamically stable structures. Our pipeline evaluates both intrinsic lattice distortions and field-induced structural responses, enabling direct comparison with experimental benchmarks. We successfully prioritize several promising candidates, including metastable intermetallics and oxides, that demonstrate unprecedented coupling coefficients under moderate magnetic fields. These results establish a scalable route for targeted materials design, accelerating the development of advanced smart materials for energy conversion and precision actuation applications.

title: Electric generation and ratcheted transport of contact-charged drops.
text_ai: We describe a simple microfluidic system that enables the steady generation and efficient transport of aqueous drops using only a constant voltage input. Drop generation is achieved through an electrohydrodynamic dripping mechanism by which conductive drops grow and detach from a grounded nozzle in response to an electric field. Upon detachment, each drop acquires a net positive charge via contact electrification at the nozzle interface. This residual charge interacts with a downstream asymmetric electrode array, producing a spatially rectified Coulomb force that drives ratcheted transport without mechanical components. By modulating the local field gradients, we achieve precise, reversible droplet steering at velocities exceeding several millimeters per second. Systematic characterization reveals that transport efficiency remains robust across varying conductivity, surface tension, and substrate wettability. The device operates continuously for over ten thousand cycles with negligible clogging or coalescence. These findings demonstrate a scalable paradigm for passive droplet manipulation and on-demand fluid actuation, offering direct utility in automated synthesis, digital microfluidics, and portable diagnostic platforms where external mechanical pumping is fundamentally impractical.

title: Addressing UX Practitioners' Challenges in Designing ML Applications: an Interactive Machine Learning Approach
text_ai: UX practitioners face novel challenges when designing user interfaces for machine learning (ML)-enabled applications. Interactive ML paradigms, like AutoML and interactive machine teaching, lower the barrier for non-expert end users to create, understand, and use ML models, but their application to UX practice is largely unstudied. This study investigates how interactive ML tools integrate into existing UX workflows to mitigate design complexities. Through a mixed-methods investigation involving twenty-four professional designers, we evaluate three interactive ML frameworks across two iterative cycles. Qualitative interviews and usability metrics reveal that while these paradigms significantly reduce cognitive load related to model transparency and data curation, they introduce friction in requirement specification and feedback calibration. We propose a structured integration framework aligning interactive ML capabilities with established UX research phases, offering guidelines for balancing algorithmic automation with human-centric principles. Findings indicate that co-designing with these systems accelerates prototyping and enhances practitioner confidence in deploying transparent AI interfaces. This work bridges the methodological divide between ML development and UX design, delivering practical strategies for creating adaptive, user-aligned intelligent systems.

title: The Density-Potential Mapping in Quantum Dynamics
text_ai: This work studies in detail the possibility of defining a one-to-one mapping from charge densities as obtained by the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation to external potentials. Such a mapping is provided by the Runge-Gross theorem and lies at the very core of time-dependent density functional theory. While theoretically rigorous, its practical implementation encounters substantial obstacles when dealing with degenerate ground states, non-vanishing currents, or systems with long-range interactions. Here, we systematically examine the mathematical structure of this correspondence under generalized initial conditions and spatially extended Hamiltonians. By employing functional-analytic techniques and high-fidelity numerical propagation schemes, we delineate the precise domain of validity for the inverse mapping and identify regimes where non-uniqueness emerges. Our analysis reveals that careful regularization of the density functional space restores injectivity even in strongly correlated regimes. These findings establish a robust theoretical foundation for advanced TDDFT implementations, particularly in non-equilibrium quantum transport and ultrafast spectroscopy. Ultimately, this work bridges formal many-body theory and computational practice, enabling reliable predictive simulations of open quantum systems driven by intense electromagnetic fields.

title: A Review on the Applications of Transformer-based language models for Nucleotide Sequence Analysis
text_ai: In recent times, Transformer-based language models are making quite an impact in the field of natural language processing. As relevant parallels can be drawn between biological sequences and natural languages, the models used in NLP can be easily extended and adapted for various applications in bioinformatics. This review systematically evaluates the integration of transformer architectures into nucleotide sequence analysis, emphasizing their capacity to capture long-range dependencies and contextual syntactic patterns within genomic data. We examine prominent pre-trained models such as DNABERT, Nucleotide Transformer, and HyenaDNA, detailing their architectural modifications and training paradigms optimized for DNA motif recognition. Key applications discussed include enhancer-promoter interaction prediction, non-coding variant effect classification, and chromatin accessibility profiling. Furthermore, we critically assess current limitations, including resource-intensive computational scalability, reference genome bias, and mechanistic interpretability challenges inherent to high-dimensional token embeddings. Finally, we propose strategic directions for advancing cross-taxon generalizability and seamlessly integrating multi-omics data streams across diverse biological scales. By synthesizing recent empirical findings, this work establishes a comprehensive framework guiding researchers in leveraging transformer-driven methodologies for next-generation genomic discovery.

title: Topological Cycle Graph Attention Network for Brain Functional Connectivity
text_ai: This study, we introduce a novel Topological Cycle Graph Attention Network (CycGAT), designed to delineate a functional backbone within brain functional graph--key pathways essential for signal transmissio--from non-essential, redundant connections that form cycles around this core structure. We first introduce a cycle incidence matrix that establishes an independent cycle basis within a graph, mapping its relationship with edges. Leveraging this topological prior, CycGAT integrates cycle-aware attention mechanisms to dynamically weight edges according to their participation in fundamental cycles, thereby isolating backbone connectivity while suppressing cyclic noise. Extensive evaluations on resting-state fMRI cohorts demonstrate that CycGAT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art graph neural baselines in downstream cognitive task prediction and clinical classification. Furthermore, visualizations reveal modular reorganization patterns linked to aging, enhancing clinical utility. Notably, the extracted functional backbones exhibit significantly higher test-retest reliability and stronger anatomical plausibility than conventional adjacency-based models. By explicitly encoding cycle-edge interactions, our framework delivers a theoretically grounded, interpretable paradigm for isolating robust functional substrates, offering insights into large-scale brain network architecture and advancing topology-driven neuroimaging analytics.

title: The formation of astrophysical Mg-rich silicate dust
text_ai: We present new results for ground-state candidate energies of Mg-rich olivine (MRO) clusters and use the binding energies of these clusters to determine their nucleation rates in stellar outflows, with particular interest in the en- vironments of core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Employing density functional theory combined with classical nucleation theory, we systematically evaluate thermodynamic stability across cluster sizes ranging from dimers to hexamers. Our quantum-chemical calculations reveal that Mg–O bridging motifs significantly lower free-energy barriers, enabling efficient grain growth even under the rapid cooling conditions characteristic of CCSN ejecta. We derive size-dependent nucleation timescales and demonstrate that MRO condensation becomes viable at temperatures between 1500 and 2000 K, consistent with mid-infrared emission features observed in young supernova remnants. Furthermore, parametric sensitivity analyses indicate that progenitor metallicity and shock velocity modulate the integrated silicate mass yield by factors of two to three. These results establish a microphysically constrained model for circumstellar dust synthesis and quantify the role of massive stellar endpoints in enriching the interstellar medium with complex refractory solids.

title: The EXP pair-potential system. I. Fluid phase isotherms, isochores, and quasiuniversality
text_ai: The exponentially repulsive EXP pair potential defines a system of particles in terms of which simple liquids' quasiuniversality may be explained [A. K. Bacher et al., Nat. Commun. 5, 5424 (2014); J. C. Dyre, J. Phys. Condens. Matter 28, 323001 (2016)]. This paper and its companion present a detailed simulation study of the EXP system. We compute extensive molecular dynamics trajectories across broad density and temperature ranges, focusing on the fluid branch. The resulting pressure–density isotherms and volume–temperature isochores exhibit striking collapse onto master curves when scaled by a reference-state temperature determined solely by density. This scaling confirms the EXP system’s ability to capture the quasiuniversal thermodynamics characteristic of simple liquids. We further show that the exponential decay parameter γ serves as a continuous tuning variable, interpolating between hard-sphere and inverse-power-law regimes. Minor deviations from reference-state predictions at elevated temperatures reveal how thermal energy subtly perturbs ideal scaling. Collectively, these results validate the EXP potential as a minimal yet comprehensive model for dense fluid thermodynamics, establishing a rigorous framework for quasiuniversality and guiding analogous studies of complex interacting particle systems.

title: Interacting Q-balls
text_ai: We study non-topological solitons, so called Q-balls, which carry a non-vanishing Noether charge and arise as lump solutions of self-interacting complex scalar field models. Explicit examples of new axially symmetric non-spinning Q-ball solutions that have not been studied so far are constructed numerically. Their structural properties, including mass-to-charge ratios and internal profile distributions, are systematically analyzed across varying coupling constants and frequency parameters. We demonstrate that these configurations exhibit robust linear stability within specific regions of the parameter space, while displaying distinct metastable regimes near the instability threshold. Furthermore, we investigate pairwise interactions through time-dependent simulations, revealing that low-energy collisions lead to merger into a single bound state with characteristic gravitational wave emission signatures, whereas high-velocity encounters result in elastic scattering or partial fragmentation. The interplay between radial confinement and gradient energy is shown to govern the long-term dynamical evolution, suggesting potential relevance for dark matter halo formation and early-universe phase transitions. These findings establish a comprehensive framework for understanding multi-Q-ball systems and provide new benchmarks for lattice-based cosmological simulations across diverse initial conditions.

title: FedNST: Federated Noisy Student Training for Automatic Speech Recognition
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) enables training state-of-the-art Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models on user devices (clients) in distributed systems, hence preventing transmission of raw user data to a central server. A key challenge facing practical adoption of FL for ASR is obtaining ground-truth labels on the clients. To address this limitation, we propose FedNST, a novel framework that leverages semi-supervised knowledge distillation within a federated setting. Our approach employs a centrally trained teacher model to generate high-confidence pseudo-labels for unannotated client speech, which are then used to fine-tune local student models without requiring manual transcription. By integrating label-noise mitigation and adaptive confidence filtering, FedNST effectively mitigates error propagation while preserving data privacy. Extensive experiments on public ASR benchmarks demonstrate that FedNST achieves competitive word error rates compared to supervised baselines, even under non-IID data distributions and fluctuating client availability. Furthermore, our method significantly reduces communication overhead through selective model updates. Our work establishes FedNST as a scalable, privacy-preserving paradigm for deploying robust speech recognition systems across heterogeneous edge environments.

title: Kinks scattering in deformed $\varphi^6$ model
text_ai: The deformed model $\tilde{\varphi}^{(6)}$ is introduced based on the $\varphi^4$ model using a deformation functional $F[\varphi]$ including a free parameter $a$. The kink solutions in different sectors and their internal modes are obtained as functions of the deformation parameter and their characteristics are evaluated as well. We investigate the collision dynamics of these topological defects through systematic numerical simulations across a wide range of incident velocities and deformation strengths. Our analysis reveals that the interplay between translational and vibrational degrees of freedom yields intricate resonance structures, characterized by distinct multi-bounce windows and sharp critical velocity thresholds. The excitation of the internal mode facilitates efficient energy transfer during collisions, directly governing the emergence of reflection-transmission resonances. title: Testing Sparsity Assumptions in Bayesian Networks
text_ai: Bayesian network (BN) structure discovery algorithms typically either make assumptions about the sparsity of the true underlying network, or are limited by computational constraints to networks with a small number of variables. While these sparsity assumptions can take various forms, frequently the assumptions focus on an upper bound for the maximum in-degree of the underlying graph $\nabla_G$. However, such bounds are rarely validated against empirical data prior to model selection, potentially yielding severely misspecified architectures when real-world dependencies exhibit denser connectivity. In this work, we formalize a rigorous statistical framework for empirically testing prescribed in-degree limits. We derive asymptotic properties of our test statistic under null and alternative hypotheses, demonstrating controlled Type I error rates across varying sample sizes and graph densities. Experiments on synthetic benchmarks and high-dimensional biological datasets reveal that widely adopted sparsity thresholds are frequently violated in practice, directly compromising posterior probability estimates and causal inference accuracy. Our findings establish practical guidelines for adaptive constraint selection, enabling practitioners to calibrate structure learning procedures to domain-specific complexity without sacrificing identifiability.

title: Seismic hazard assessment in Menton, France: Topographical site effect zoning considering a semi-empirical approach and a Machine Learning scheme
text_ai: The presence of topography influences the seismic ground motion and may result in strong amplifications, generally at the top of hills and reliefs. The increasing urbanization of hills requires an accurate estimation of these effects even in areas of moderate seismicity. This study integrates a semi-empirical formulation with a supervised machine learning algorithm to quantify topographic amplification across the complex coastal terrain of Menton. High-resolution digital elevation models are coupled with equivalent linear site response analyses to generate a comprehensive training dataset comprising topographic metrics and corresponding spectral amplification ratios. A gradient boosting model is subsequently trained to predict site-classification probabilities, calibrated against recorded ground motions and empirical correlations. The resulting microzonation map delineates distinct zones of pronounced amplification, revealing spatial variations that align closely with underlying geological boundaries. Cross-validation metrics demonstrate robust predictive performance, confirming the synergistic advantage of coupling physics-based constraints with data-driven optimization. These findings deliver actionable insights for municipal building regulations and urban planning, establishing a transferable framework for seismic hazard mitigation in morphologically heterogeneous regions.

title: Negative-Tension Branes and Tensionless 1/2 Brane in Boundary Conformal Field Theory
text_ai: In the framework of boundary conformal field theory we consider a flat unstable D$p$-brane in the presence of a large constant electromagnetic field. The one-loop partition function calculation reveals a precise cancellation of vacuum divergences, indicating dynamical stability despite the absence of conventional positive tension. Furthermore, we establish that the surviving boundary conditions preserve a deformed subalgebra of the original superconformal symmetry. These results furnish a controlled BCFT realization of Sen’s conjecture in extremal backgrounds and clarify the role of fractionalized branes in open string decay dynamics within the broader context of string phenomenology.

title: Optimizing Geometric Multigrid Methods with Evolutionary Computation
text_ai: For many linear and nonlinear systems that arise from the discretization of partial differential equations the construction of an efficient multigrid solver is a challenging task. Our framework automatically synthesizes optimal solver components, including smoothing kernels, restriction and prolongation operators, and cycle configurations, through a fitness-driven selection process that minimizes asymptotic iteration counts. By encoding multigrid parameters as genomic sequences, the algorithm explores high-dimensional design spaces without requiring explicit derivative information or domain-specific heuristics. We evaluate the evolved solvers against classical V-cycle implementations across a suite of elliptic and convection-diffusion benchmarks, demonstrating consistent reductions in CPU time and memory footprint while preserving optimal asymptotic complexity. Furthermore, the methodology exhibits strong transferability across varying mesh resolutions and coefficient distributions, significantly lowering the expert intervention traditionally required for solver deployment. These findings establish evolutionary computation as a viable paradigm for automating high-performance numerical linear algebra pipelines.

title: Primarily Undergraduate Institutions and the Astronomy Community
text_ai: This White Paper highlights the role Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (PUIs) play within the astronomy profession, addressing issues related to employment, resources and support, research opportunities and productivity, and educational and societal impacts, among others. Drawing on survey data, institutional case studies, and faculty interviews, we demonstrate that PUIs consistently produce disproportionately high numbers of diverse astrophysicists relative to their enrollment size. Despite these contributions, PUI faculty frequently navigate constrained laboratory infrastructure, limited travel funding, and heavier teaching loads that impede sustained grant acquisition. Our analysis reveals that targeted investment in collaborative research networks, shared instrumentation access, and structured mentorship programs significantly amplifies both scholarly output and student retention in STEM pathways. Furthermore, we identify systemic barriers in peer-review allocation and professional advancement that inadvertently marginalize PUI-based scholars. To strengthen the discipline’s resilience and innovation capacity, we propose concrete policy interventions, including adjusted funding metrics that account for instructional missions, expanded bridge grants for early-career researchers, and formal recognition of PUI-led outreach as legitimate scholarly impact. These recommendations aim to foster a more equitable astronomical ecosystem.

title: One for the Future: measuring the mass transfer rate in the ULX M82 X-2 by using orbital period changes will take millenia
text_ai: Bachetti et al. (2021) have recently claimed to measure the mass transfer rate in the pulsing ULX system M82 X-2 by following the change of its orbital period over 7 yr. By reprocessing seven years of NuSTAR and XMM-Newton data with rigorous phase-connected timing solutions, we find no statistically significant trend in the orbital period derivative at the 1σ level. Our Monte Carlo simulations reveal that detecting a physically meaningful signal requires a baseline spanning several millennia, assuming standard Roche-lobe overflow dynamics. Thus, present campaigns cannot constrain mass transfer efficiency or the evolutionary state. We emphasize that transient magnetic propeller effects and tidal interactions likely dominate short-term orbital variability, masking any secular accretion-driven evolution. Future high-cadence timing missions must therefore prioritize spin-timing precision over extended baselines if fundamental accretion parameters are to be robustly determined. title: Curvature Perturbations from a Massive Vector Curvaton

title: Upregulation of lactate dehydrogenase A in a chronic model of temporal lobe epilepsy.

This elevation correlated strongly with seizure frequency and neuronal loss, indicating a compensatory metabolic shift toward enhanced glycolytic flux during chronic epileptogenesis. Furthermore, pharmacological blockade of LDHA activity markedly reduced spontaneous recurrent seizures and attenuated progressive neurodegeneration without disrupting normal brain metabolism. These results demonstrate that sustained epileptic activity actively drives LDHA overexpression as a pathogenic adaptation. Consequently, selective LDHA inhibition offers a viable therapeutic avenue for refractory epilepsy, directly linking ketogenic diet mechanisms to targeted enzymatic interventions.

title: Economic Rationality under Specialization: Evidence of Decision Bias in AI Agents
text_ai: In the study by Chen et al. (2023) [01], the large language model GPT demonstrated economic rationality comparable to or exceeding the average human level in tasks such as budget allocation and risk preference. Utilizing a controlled experimental framework across twelve financial and consumer choice paradigms, we evaluate multiple AI architectures. Our results reveal that while specialized models optimize for localized efficiency metrics, they consistently exhibit framing effects, loss aversion asymmetries, and probability weighting distortions absent in general-purpose counterparts. These biases scale inversely with architectural diversity, suggesting that optimization pressure toward domain-specific benchmarks reinforces heuristic dependencies. We propose a theoretical extension to expected utility theory incorporating algorithmic specialization as a latent variable shaping preference stability. These findings necessitate integrating robust cognitive bias diagnostics into AI alignment protocols, particularly for high-stakes economic applications requiring strict normative consistency.

title: Modelling Population-Level Hes1 Dynamics: Insights from a Multi-Framework Approach

Our analysis reveals that population-level averaging obscures critical bifurcation thresholds governing lineage commitment, whereas single-cell stochastic trajectories preserve the temporal precision needed for robust fate specification. Coupling delayed negative feedback with variable transcriptional burst frequencies yields oscillatory regimes consistent with fluorescence recordings. Such findings establish a scalable paradigm for dissecting gene regulatory networks in developing tissues, bridging mechanistic detail with analytically tractable formulations.

title: Multi-dimensional band structure spectroscopy in the synthetic frequency dimension

title: Dimensions of Higher Order Factor Analysis Models
text_ai: The factor analysis model is a statistical model where a certain number of hidden random variables, called factors, affect linearly the behaviour of another set of observed random variables, with additional random noise. By characterizing the underlying parameter manifolds, we derive explicit formulas for the intrinsic dimensionality of these models under general loading configurations. Our analysis reveals that effective degrees of freedom depend critically on the rank of the covariance decomposition and the interplay between first- and second-order factor loadings. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for local identifiability, demonstrating how overparameterization manifests as redundant subspace rotations. Furthermore, we quantify model complexity through information-theoretic criteria, showing that higher-order specifications do not increase predictive capacity beyond lower-order counterparts under noise constraints. These results establish rigorous theoretical bounds for model selection and guide hierarchical latent framework implementation in high-dimensional settings.

title: On Triangulation as a Form of Self-Supervision for 3D Human Pose Estimation
text_ai: Supervised approaches to 3D pose estimation from single images are remarkably effective when labeled data is abundant. Generating an effective form of supervision with little annotations still poses major challenge in crowded scenes. To address this limitation, we introduce a self-supervised paradigm that exploits multi-view geometric consistency through triangulation as a primary supervisory signal. By projecting candidate joints across multiple views, the framework computes reprojection discrepancies that inherently penalize occluded or ambiguous detections. This geometric prior enables the network to refine pose predictions without manual 3D annotations, while a confidence-weighted consistency loss suppresses outlier propagation in densely populated regions. Comprehensive evaluations on standard benchmarks reveal that our triangulation-based objective yields substantial accuracy gains over prevailing weakly-supervised methods, particularly under severe occlusion and viewpoint variation. Consequently, we demonstrate that explicit geometric reasoning provides a scalable, annotation-free pathway toward robust monocular 3D human pose estimation.

title: AI-Based Multi-Object Relative State Estimation with Self-Calibration Capabilities
text_ai: The capability to extract task specific, semantic information from raw sensory data is a crucial requirement for many applications of mobile robotics. To address these challenges, we propose a deep learning framework that simultaneously estimates the relative poses of multiple infrastructure components while autonomously calibrating onboard sensor parameters in unstructured environments. The architecture employs a multimodal transformer network to fuse LiDAR point clouds and visual imagery, enabling robust feature association across temporal sequences. By integrating sensor alignment as a differentiable optimization layer within the inference pipeline, the system continuously refines extrinsic and intrinsic parameters without requiring prior ground-truth measurements. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic benchmarks and real-world UAV flight trials demonstrate that our approach reduces relative positioning errors by 38% compared to conventional geometric filters, while maintaining sub-centimeter calibration stability during extended operations. These findings confirm the practical viability of learning-driven perception architectures for precision-guided aerial inspections in GPS-denied environments.

title: A Generic Framework for Clustering Vehicle Motion Trajectories
text_ai: The development of autonomous vehicles requires having access to a large amount of data in the concerning driving scenarios. However, manual annotation of such driving scenarios is costly and subject to the errors in the rule-based trajectory labeling systems. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework that automatically groups vehicle motion trajectories using unsupervised learning techniques. Our approach leverages spatial-temporal feature extraction combined with density-based clustering algorithms to identify recurrent driving patterns without predefined rules. The method incorporates adaptive normalization procedures to handle heterogeneous sensor inputs and varying sampling rates across diverse datasets. We validate the approach on multiple real-world traffic recordings, demonstrating superior scalability and robustness compared to conventional heuristic pipelines. Quantitative evaluations reveal significant improvements in cluster purity and silhouette coefficients, while qualitative analysis confirms the semantic coherence of the extracted motion primitives. By eliminating dependency on labor-intensive labeling, this framework enables rapid scenario discovery, enhancing perception dataset curation. title: Higher-order conservation laws for the non-linear Poisson equation via the characteristic cohomology

This condition generalizes classical Liouville-type restrictions and establishes a rigid correspondence between the algebraic structure of $f$ and hidden symmetry generation. We demonstrate that, apart from exponential and power-law potentials, all generic nonlinearities yield vanishing higher-order cohomology groups beyond trivial first integrals. Consequently, the characteristic cohomology framework furnishes a definitive obstruction criterion for non-integrability in elliptic field equations. These findings delineate the precise algebraic boundaries of conserved quantities in generalized Poisson systems while providing a systematic methodology for evaluating integrability through differential-algebraic reduction techniques.

title: A DNN Based Post-Filter to Enhance the Quality of Coded Speech in MDCT Domain
text_ai: Frequency domain processing, and in particular the use of Modified Discrete Cosine Transform (MDCT), is the most widespread approach to audio coding. However, at low bitrates, audio quality, especially for speech, degrades drastically due to the lack of available bits to directly code the transform coefficients. To address this limitation, we propose a novel deep neural network (DNN)-based post-filter operating directly in the MDCT domain. The architecture learns a non-linear mapping between distorted coded spectra and high-fidelity references by capturing cross-frame spectral dependencies. Trained on extensive speech corpora, the model effectively suppresses quantization noise and pre-echo artifacts while preserving natural timbre. Extensive testing shows significant POLQA and MOS improvements over conventional linear baselines. Additionally, the lightweight pipeline ensures real-time compatibility with minimal overhead. By explicitly modeling psychoacoustic masking thresholds, the network refines residual harmonic structures without introducing audible distortion. This domain-specific design circumvents phase-reconstruction challenges inherent to time-domain generative models, enabling seamless integration with existing ITU-T codec architectures. Ultimately, the framework establishes a robust pathway for next-generation low-complexity speech enhancement.

title: Green Segment Routing for Improved Sustainability of Backbone Networks

Exploiting the fine-grained path control inherent to segment routing, GSR computes energy-aware forwarding paths that minimize active line cards and optical amplifiers. We validate the framework via comprehensive simulations employing empirical traffic matrices from regional ISPs, benchmarking against traditional OSPF and ECMP deployments. Results indicate that GSR curtails aggregate power draw by up to 31% during off-peak intervals, with negligible degradation in throughput or jitter. The mechanism also maintains rapid convergence during link failures and accommodates heterogeneous hardware constraints. Collectively, these outcomes establish energy-conscious path computation as a scalable, operator-deployable strategy for decarbonizing global data transport infrastructures.

title: Current Predictive Indices and Nomograms To Enable Personalization of Radiation Therapy for Patients With Secondary Malignant Neoplasms of the Central Nervous System: A Review.
text_ai: The proper treatment of brain metastases continues to be a challenge for oncologists given the variability of individual patients' prognoses and the variety of treatment options available to address brain metasteses. Despite notable advances, significant heterogeneity persists across studies regarding variable selection, endpoint definitions, and external validation cohorts, limiting widespread clinical adoption. Standardizing these instruments and embedding them within clinical workflows remains essential to optimize therapeutic ratios and personalize radiation oncology for central nervous system metastases.

title: Tribute to Henry Primakoff: Chiral Perturbation Theory Tests via Primakoff Reactions
text_ai: Consider the scattering of GeV energy beam particles off the Coulomb field of a nucleus. This work underscores the enduring relevance of Primakoff’s insight for advancing fundamental low-energy strong interaction physics.

title: Proportional Dynamics in Linear Fisher Markets with Auto-bidding: Convergence, Incentives and Fairness

title: Repeated end range spinal movement while seated abolishes the proprioceptive deficit induced by prolonged flexed sitting posture. A study assessing the statistical and clinical significance of spinal position sense.
text_ai: Sustained spinal flexion has been proposed to affect the properties of spinal tissues, increase postural muscle's activation latency and act detrimentally on proprioception. This study evaluated the effect of flexed posture (FP) on spinal proprioception and assessed the immediate effect of spinal movement on the presumable flexion-induced proprioceptive deficit. Thirty healthy adults (mean age 24.3 ± 3.1 years) participated in a randomized crossover design. Participants completed three conditions: baseline seated neutral posture, sustained FP (60° lumbar flexion for 30 minutes), and FP followed by five repetitions of seated end-range spinal extension movements. Spinal position sense was quantified using a dual inclinometer system during active repositioning tasks from 15°, 30°, and 45° flexion angles. Repositioning error (absolute angular deviation) served as the primary outcome. Intra-rater reliability coefficients confirmed high measurement consistency (ICC > 0.85). FP significantly increased mean repositioning error at all angles compared to baseline (p < 0.01, η² = 0.42). However, the movement intervention completely normalized positional accuracy, yielding no significant difference from baseline values (p > 0.05). Clinical significance analysis revealed that FP-induced errors exceeded the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) threshold of 2.5°, whereas post-intervention errors remained below 1.0° across all test angles. Prolonged seated flexion substantially impairs spinal proprioception, but brief, repeated end-range movements rapidly restore positional accuracy to baseline levels. These findings demonstrate both statistical robustness and clinical relevance, suggesting that targeted kinesthetic interventions may effectively mitigate posture-related sensorimotor deficits in sedentary occupations, ergonomic practice frameworks, and clinical rehabilitation protocols.

title: Scaling Universality at the Dynamic Vortex Mott Transition
text_ai: The dynamic Mott insulator-to-metal transition (DMT) is key to many intriguing phenomena in condensed matter physics yet it remains nearly unexplored. The cleanest way to observe DMT, without the interference from disorder and other effects inherent to electronic and atomic systems, is to employ the vortex Mott states formed by superconducting vortices in a regular array of pinning sites. Here, we report systematic measurements of vortex mobility and conductivity across a precisely engineered antidot lattice under applied bias currents. By varying temperature and drive amplitude near the critical depinning threshold, we extract dynamical critical exponents through finite-time scaling analysis. Our data reveal a distinct power-law divergence of the characteristic relaxation time, τ ∼ |J − Jc|^−zν, with zν ≈ 1.85, consistent with a novel dynamic universality class distinct from equilibrium glass transitions. Furthermore, the scaling collapse of conductivity curves across multiple array geometries confirms that the transition is governed by collective vortex creep mechanisms rather than single-particle hopping. These findings establish the vortex Mott system as a pristine simulator for quantum and classical dynamic phase transitions, offering new insights into non-equilibrium critical phenomena and providing a benchmark for theoretical models of driven dissipative many-body systems.

title: Cladogenetic and Anagenetic Models of Chromosome Number Evolution: A Bayesian Model Averaging Approach.
text_ai: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, and changes in chromosome number play a fundamental role in evolution. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number, as well as polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Despite extensive research, the relative contributions of cladogenetic versus anagenetic chromosome number changes remain poorly quantified across phylogenies. Traditional approaches often assume single evolutionary regimes or rely on parsimony-based reconstructions that ignore uncertainty in both topology and transition rates. Here, we develop a hierarchical Bayesian framework integrated with reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling to simultaneously estimate ancestral karyotypes, infer bidirectional transition rates, and perform model averaging across competing cladogenetic and anagenetic scenarios. We apply this approach to a comprehensive phylogeny of angiosperms comprising 1,247 species and 893 observed chromosome counts. By computing marginal likelihoods under each mechanistic hypothesis, our model-averaged inferences consistently identify distinct evolutionary regimes contingent upon clade-specific life history traits. We find strong empirical support for speciation-associated dysploidy in rapidly radiating lineages, whereas anagenetic accumulation predominates in morphologically conserved, long-lived clades. Branch-length-dependent transition probabilities enable direct tests of whether karyotypic shifts correlate with speciation pulses or accumulate stochastically. Cross-validation procedures confirm that model-averaged predictions outperform singular regime assumptions in both predictive accuracy and parameter recovery. Furthermore, explicitly accommodating topological uncertainty and rate heterogeneity substantially reduces systematic bias in ancestral state reconstructions compared to fixed-topology implementations. By quantifying the posterior probability distribution over alternative evolutionary pathways, this framework delivers a statistically rigorous metric for evaluating the macroevolutionary consequences of karyotype dynamics. This approach establishes a unified probabilistic foundation for integrating cytogenetic data into macroevolutionary analyses, providing novel insights into how chromosomal architecture fundamentally structures biodiversity patterns across geological timescales.

title: Aspects of CFTs on Real Projective Space
text_ai: We present an analytic study of conformal field theories on the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^d$, focusing on the two-point functions of scalar operators. Due to the partially broken conformal symmetry, these are non-trivial functions of a conformal cross ratio and are constrained to obey a crossing equation. By adapting the Lorentzian inversion formalism to this non-orientable geometry, we derive closed-form expressions for the spectral density and establish rigorous bounds on the scaling dimensions of low-lying primary operators. We explicitly construct the full set of conformal blocks and demonstrate their completeness in resolving the functional equations that govern the theory. Our analysis reveals a universal spectral structure, characterized by distinct parity sectors that decouple at leading order in the large-$N$ expansion. Furthermore, we implement the analytic bootstrap program to extract precise constraints on mixed boundary-operator product coefficients, verifying consistency with established critical fixed points in generalized vector models. These results furnish a systematic computational framework for defect CFTs and holographic correspondences, while clarifying how topological identifications fundamentally alter the analytic continuation of correlation functions beyond flat space. Our methodology extends naturally to higher-spin fields and provides new tools for studying non-perturbative quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter backgrounds.

title: How Black Holes Stop Their Host Galaxy from Growing Without AGN Feedback
text_ai: Super-massive black holes (SMBHs) with $M_{\bullet} \sim 10^9 $ M$_{\odot}$ at $z>6$ likely originate from massive seed black holes (BHs). We investigate the consequences of seeding SMBHs with direct collapse BHs (DCBHs) ($M_{\bullet}=10^{4-6}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$) on proto-galactic disc growth. Through high-resolution magnetohydrodynamical simulations of primordial halos, we demonstrate that centrally concentrated DCBHs rapidly lose orbital energy via dynamical friction, driving efficient inward migration on timescales shorter than the host assembly phase. As the seed approaches the potential minimum, its growing gravitational influence induces strong non-axisymmetric perturbations in the circumnuclear gas distribution. These perturbations generate substantial gravitational torques that redistribute angular momentum outward, bypassing the need for radiatively driven outflows or relativistic jets. Consequently, cold gas inflows are disrupted, star formation efficiency drops precipitously, and the proto-galactic disc stalls in mass growth despite continued halo accretion. We quantify this self-regulating cycle, showing that disc truncation occurs when the local Toomre $Q$ parameter exceeds unity due to transient velocity dispersion enhancements induced by the perturber. The resulting suppression scales inversely with the ambient gas surface density but remains effective across varying metallicity prescriptions. Across a broad parameter space encompassing distinct initial spin orientations, eccentricity distributions, and baryon-to-dark matter ratios, the quenching threshold proves robust, linking the final black hole mass directly to the maximum disc radius attained prior to orbital decay. Our findings establish a purely gravitational suppression mechanism that naturally reproduces observed $M_{\bullet}-\sigma$ correlations at high redshift, indicating that early co-evolution may be dictated by secular dynamical coupling rather than canonical thermodynamic feedback channels.

title: An H{\alpha} view of galaxy build-up in the first 2 Gyr: luminosity functions at z~4-6.5 from NIRCam/grism spectroscopy
text_ai: The H{\alpha} nebular emission line is an optimal tracer for recent star formation in galaxies. With the advent of JWST, this line has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 H{\alpha} emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. Using these robust identifications, we derive the H{\alpha} luminosity function (LF) across five redshift bins spanning $z\sim4.0$ to $6.5$. Systematic tests of contamination from [O III] + H{\beta} misidentification confirm a catalog purity exceeding 95\% across all epochs. Our sample reaches unprecedented depths, probing luminosities down to $\log(L_{\mathrm{H}\alpha}/[\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}]) \approx 40.5$, corresponding to specific star formation rates as low as $\sim 0.1\,\mathrm{Gyr}^{-1}$ for typical $M_* \sim 10^9\,M_\odot$ populations. Schechter function fits reveal a characteristic luminosity that evolves significantly over this interval, with $L^*$ increasing by nearly an order of magnitude from $z\sim6.5$ to $4.0$. The faint-end slope $\alpha$ remains relatively steep ($\alpha \approx -1.7$ to $-1.9$), indicating that low-mass systems dominate the integrated star formation budget even during the cosmic dawn. Integrating our LFs yields a cosmic H{\alpha} luminosity density that rises by a factor of $\sim 8$ between $z\sim6.5$ and $4.0$, translating to a star formation rate density evolution consistent with ultraviolet-based estimates when corrected for nebular continuum contributions and dust attenuation. These results demonstrate that galaxy assembly was already highly efficient within the first two billion years, with a substantial population of actively star-forming dwarf galaxies driving the bulk of early reionization-era activity. Our catalog and derived LFs provide a critical empirical foundation for testing semi-analytical and hydrodynamical simulations, constraining the ionizing photon escape fraction, and refining models of hierarchical structure formation in the nascent Universe.

title: Optimal strategies for throwing accurately
text_ai: Accuracy of throwing in games and sports is governed by how errors at projectile release are propagated by flight dynamics. To address the question of what governs the choice of throwing strategy, we use a simple model of throwing with an arm modelled as a hinged bar of fixed length that can release a projectile at any angle and angular velocity. We derive an analytical expression for the covariance of the impact point as a function of release parameters, incorporating additive noise in both angular position and velocity. Minimizing this covariance subject to physiological limits on joint torque yields distinct optimal regimes across target distances. Analysis reveals that near targets favor high-velocity, low-angle releases to suppress angular uncertainty, whereas distant targets require slower, higher-arcing trajectories leveraging gravitational stabilization. The transition between regimes emerges naturally from kinematic noise amplification and aerodynamic drag, without invoking cognitive decision-making. Predictions align closely with kinematic data from trained athletes performing precision throws under controlled conditions. This framework quantifies how humans spontaneously select strategies balancing speed, accuracy, and mechanical feasibility, providing a principled basis for motor control theory and translational applications in athletic skill development and autonomous projectile systems.

title: TeraHertz Band Communication: An Old Problem Revisited and Research Directions for the Next Decade
text_ai: Terahertz (THz) band communications are envisioned as a key technology for 6G and Beyond. As a fundamental wireless infrastructure, THz communication can boost abundant promising applications. In 2014, our team published two comprehensive roadmaps for the development and progress of THz communication networks [1], [2], which helped the research community to start research on this subject afterwards. However, rapid advancements in semiconductor technologies, novel antenna arrays, and machine learning-driven resource allocation have fundamentally altered the feasibility landscape. This article revisits these legacy challenges through the lens of recent experimental demonstrations and standardized frameworks, critically assessing gaps between theoretical models and practical deployments. We systematically categorize persistent bottlenecks across physical-layer design, network architecture, and regulatory constraints, proposing actionable pathways to overcome them. Particular emphasis is placed on hybrid sub-terahertz architectures, energy-efficient transceiver designs, and dynamic spectrum sharing mechanisms tailored for ultra-dense environments. Furthermore, we delineate a ten-year research agenda encompassing cross-layer optimization, integrated sensing and communication paradigms, and sustainable deployment strategies. By synthesizing fragmented insights into a cohesive framework, this survey aims to accelerate the transition from laboratory prototypes to scalable, commercial THz networks, ultimately enabling ubiquitous ultra-high-capacity connectivity for next-generation systems.

title: Routing Protocols Performance in Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks Using Millimeter Wave
text_ai: Self-Organized networks (SONs) have been studied for many years, and have attracted many researchers due to their substantial applications. Although the performance of such networks in the lower band networks (sub-6 GHz band frequencies) has been well studied, there are only sparse studies on SON in higher frequency bands, such as the millimeter wave (mmWave) band ranges between 28GHz and 300GHz. This study systematically evaluates the efficacy of conventional and emerging routing protocols within mmWave-enabled Mobile Ad-Hoc Networks (MANETs). We investigate critical performance metrics, including throughput, end-to-end latency, packet delivery ratio, and control overhead, under varying mobility patterns and channel conditions. Simulations reveal that while directional beamforming significantly mitigates propagation losses, rapid link degradation caused by mobility-induced blockages severely degrades traditional reactive and hybrid routing schemes. Consequently, we propose a topology-aware adaptation mechanism that dynamically optimizes route discovery and maintenance procedures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces packet loss by 24% and improves average throughput by 31% compared to standard AODV and OLSR implementations. These findings underscore the necessity of protocol redesign tailored to mmWave-specific characteristics, providing a foundational reference for next-generation self-organizing wireless architectures across diverse operational scenarios.

title: Image-Specific Information Suppression and Implicit Local Alignment for Text-based Person Search
text_ai: Text-based person search (TBPS) is a challenging task that aims to search pedestrian images with the same identity from an image gallery given a query text. In recent years, TBPS has made remarkable progress and state-of-the-art methods achieve superior performance by learning local fine-grained correspondence between images and texts. However, existing approaches often suffer from two critical limitations. First, they inadvertently retain image-specific background or environmental cues during feature extraction, which leads to modality mismatch and degrades cross-modal generalization. Second, explicit alignment mechanisms tend to force rigid pixel-level matching, ignoring the inherent semantic ambiguity and structural variations across diverse pedestrian attributes. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework that integrates Image-Specific Information Suppression (ISS) and Implicit Local Alignment (ILA). The ISS module employs a dynamic attention masking strategy to progressively filter out scene-dependent noise while preserving identity-critical regions. Concurrently, ILA introduces a learnable latent space where cross-modal interactions are modeled through soft, probabilistic correspondences rather than hard matches, thereby accommodating natural linguistic and visual discrepancies. Extensive experiments on three widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques, achieving significant improvements in both retrieval accuracy and mean average precision. Furthermore, comprehensive ablation studies validate the individual contributions of each proposed component, highlighting the robustness of implicit alignment under complex real-world conditions. Our findings indicate that systematically mitigating irrelevant visual priors and embracing flexible semantic mapping constitute essential pathways for advancing TBPS systems. We will release our source code upon acceptance to facilitate future research.

title: In-ear EEG biometrics for feasible and readily collectable real-world person authentication
text_ai: The use of EEG as a biometrics modality has been investigated for about a decade, however its feasibility in real-world applications is not yet conclusively established, mainly due to the issues with collectability and reproducibility. To address these limitations, we introduce an in-ear electroencephalographic acquisition framework specifically engineered for unobtrusive, continuous monitoring in ecologically valid environments. The proposed system utilizes miniaturized dry electrodes integrated into a custom earbud form factor, enabling stable contact across diverse anatomical variations while reducing motion artifacts. A longitudinal cohort study evaluated signal stability and cross-session consistency under varying ambient conditions. Feature extraction leverages subject-specific spectral power distributions within the alpha and beta bands, coupled with phase-locking values derived from resting-state epochs. Classification was performed using a lightweight support vector machine optimized for edge deployment. Experimental results demonstrate an equal error rate of 1.2% on controlled datasets, which degrades gracefully to 3.8% in unconstrained settings, maintaining robust performance across multiple days without recalibration. These findings indicate that in-ear EEG captures highly discriminative neurophysiological fingerprints resilient to environmental perturbations. Consequently, this approach bridges the gap between laboratory-grade neural biometrics and practical deployment, offering a scalable, privacy-preserving alternative to conventional physiological modalities for next-generation authentication infrastructure.
