title: Interpretable Data-Driven Demand Modelling for On-Demand Transit Services
text_ai: In recent years, with the advancements in information and communication technology, different emerging on-demand shared mobility services have been introduced as innovative solutions in the low-density areas, including on-demand transit (ODT), mobility on-demand (MOD) transit, and crowdsourced mobility services. However, due to their infancy, there is a strong need to understand and model the demand for these services. To address this gap, this study develops an interpretable data-driven demand modelling framework leveraging high-resolution GPS trajectory data and automated fare collection records. We extract spatiotemporal origin–destination patterns and analyze key demand drivers through a hybrid machine learning architecture. Unlike conventional black-box predictive models, our approach integrates SHAP values with generalized additive models to quantify the marginal impact of socio-demographic, land-use, and transit network attributes on service utilization. Model interpretability is further enhanced through partial dependence plots and feature interaction visualizations, enabling practitioners to validate assumptions against established transport theory. Empirical validation using real-world deployment data from three metropolitan regions demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves competitive predictive accuracy while providing transparent, policy-relevant insights into demand formation. The results reveal non-linear relationships between service coverage radius, population density, and first-mile connectivity, highlighting critical thresholds for optimal route design. Furthermore, scenario analysis illustrates how targeted infrastructure investments and dynamic pricing strategies can substantially increase ridership elasticity. By bridging advanced computational techniques with interpretable analytical structures, this research offers transit agencies and urban planners a robust decision-support tool for designing equitable, efficient, and scalable on-demand transit systems in underserved communities.

title: Quantum entanglement between an atom and a molecule
text_ai: Conventional information processors freely convert information between different physical carriers to process, store, or transmit information. It seems plausible that quantum information will also be held by different physical carriers in applications such as tests of fundamental physics, quantum-enhanced sensors, and quantum information processing. Realizing this potential requires robust interfaces capable of generating and preserving nonclassical correlations across fundamentally distinct quantum degrees of freedom. Here we demonstrate deterministic quantum entanglement between a trapped calcium ion and a sympathetically cooled molecular ion. By leveraging narrow-linewidth optical transitions and sympathetic cooling techniques, we initialize the internal states of both species into a well-defined basis and apply tailored electromagnetic pulses to establish a Bell-state correlation. We verify the entanglement through full state tomography, achieving a measured fidelity of 0.87(3), significantly above the classical separability bound. The observed coherence persists over several milliseconds, limited primarily by ambient magnetic field fluctuations rather than intrinsic decoherence mechanisms. These results establish a viable pathway toward hybrid quantum architectures that combine the exceptional controllability of atomic qubits with the rich internal structure and rotational-vibrational spectra of molecules. Such configurations provide a scalable foundation for distributed quantum sensing, quantum networking, and systematic investigations of multipartite nonlocality across chemically distinct systems.

title: Being a real nurse: A secondary qualitative analysis of how public health nurses rework their work identities.
text_ai: Many Western nations are emphasizing the importance of population health across health care delivery organizations and education systems. Despite significant momentum to integrate population health into nursing practice, a parallel effort to examine how these efforts impact practicing nurses' views of their professional role and work identity has not occurred. This study addresses that gap through a secondary qualitative analysis of interview data from 42 public health nurses engaged in population health initiatives. Thematic analysis revealed three core dimensions of identity rework: navigating tension between clinical immediacy and preventive mandates, negotiating boundary blurring as they assume community-focused roles, and reconstructing professional legitimacy through peer narratives. Participants described “being a real nurse” not as delivering acute care, but as fostering systemic resilience and addressing social determinants via sustained partnerships. These findings indicate that workforce transformation requires supports validating hybridized roles rather than framing them as deviations from traditional practice. Recognizing identity rework as legitimate professional adaptation can inform curriculum design, organizational policy, and development strategies sustaining population health integration.

title: Gravitational waves constraints on post-inflationary phases stiffer than radiation
text_ai: We point out that the existence of post-inflationary phases stiffer than radiation leads to the production of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) backgrounds whose logarithmic energy spectra (in critical units) are typically "blue" at high frequencies. By explicitly computing the transfer functions across varying equations of state w ∈ [1/3, 1], we demonstrate that the resulting spectral slopes range from nearly flat to strongly positive, depending on the duration and energy scale of the stiff epoch. We then confront these theoretical predictions with current observational bounds from LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA and pulsar timing arrays, establishing robust exclusion regions in the (Treh, w) parameter space. Our analysis reveals that even modest deviations from radiation domination can be tightly constrained by next-generation interferometers such as LISA, particularly when the stiff phase terminates at temperatures exceeding 10^9 GeV. Furthermore, we derive model-independent upper limits on the fraction of vacuum energy converting into gravitational radiation during non-standard expansion histories. These results underscore the sensitivity of high-frequency GW detectors to early-universe thermodynamics and provide a complementary probe to primordial nucleosynthesis and CMB measurements. Ultimately, our framework offers a systematic methodology for translating GW observations into stringent bounds on transient cosmological epochs, thereby narrowing the landscape of viable post-inflationary scenarios.

title: Effect of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation on Pain Management: A Systematic Narrative Review
text_ai: Recently, clinicians have been using repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for treating various pain conditions. This systematic narrative review aimed to examine the use and efficacy of rTMS for controlling various pain conditions. A PubMed search was conducted for articles that were published until June 7, 2019 and used rTMS for pain alleviation. Studies were screened against predefined inclusion criteria, prioritizing randomized controlled trials and prospective cohorts evaluating primary or secondary pain syndromes. Key variables, including stimulation parameters, anatomical targeting, treatment duration, and validated pain scales, were systematically extracted and synthesized narratively. The analyzed literature encompassed diverse nociceptive and neuropathic etiologies, notably chronic low back pain, fibromyalgia, migraine, and postherpetic neuralgia. High-frequency protocols targeting the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex consistently demonstrated superior analgesic effects relative to sham controls, particularly in attenuating resting pain intensity and enhancing functional capacity. Conversely, low-frequency motor cortex stimulation yielded heterogeneous outcomes, with clinical benefit strongly correlated to cumulative dose and session frequency. Adverse events remained predominantly mild and transient, chiefly comprising localized scalp discomfort and tension-type headaches. Exploratory subgroup assessments suggested that centrally mediated pain phenotypes exhibit heightened responsiveness to cortical neuromodulation compared to peripheral nociceptive drivers. Nevertheless, substantial methodological heterogeneity precluded formal quantitative pooling, highlighting critical gaps in reporting consistency. Collectively, these findings substantiate rTMS as a viable non-invasive adjunct for refractory pain states. Although frontopolar and motor cortical applications show promise, optimal dosing architectures require rigorous standardization. Prospective, multicenter investigations employing uniform protocols are essential to translate emerging evidence into routine clinical practice.

title: Computational insights and the observation of SiC nanograin assembly: towards 2D silicon carbide
text_ai: While an increasing number of two-dimensional (2D) materials, including graphene and silicene, have already been realized, others have only been predicted. An interesting example is the two-dimensional form of silicon carbide (2D-SiC). Here, we present an observation of atomically thin and hexagonally bonded nanosized grains of SiC assembling temporarily in graphene oxide pores during an atomic resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy experiment. Complementary density functional theory calculations elucidate the thermodynamic stability and growth kinetics of these transient nanostructures, revealing that lateral confinement within the oxidized carbon matrix lowers the nucleation barrier and promotes ordered hexagonal alignment. Our combined experimental-computational framework demonstrates that van der Waals interactions and localized charge redistribution at the SiC–GO interface drive the self-assembly process, while controlled thermal fluctuations ultimately govern their reversible disintegration. These findings establish a robust mechanistic pathway for stabilizing metastable two-dimensional phases on templated substrates, offering a scalable strategy for synthesizing defect-engineered SiC monolayers. By integrating real-time atomic imaging with predictive computational modeling, this study bridges fundamental interfacial chemistry with practical nanofabrication, advancing the rational development of wide-bandgap semiconductors for high-power electronics, and tunable optoelectronic platforms.

title: ALMA-IMF XVI: Mass-averaged temperature of cores and protostellar luminosities in the ALMA-IMF protoclusters
text_ai: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem greatly exacerbated at the distances >2 kpc of ALMA-IMF protoclusters. To overcome these degeneracies, we employ a multi-component radiative transfer framework that simultaneously fits broadband spectral energy distributions across seven ALMA bands, explicitly accounting for envelope optical depth gradients and unresolved source confusion. By deriving a mass-averaged dust temperature for each identified object, we successfully break the traditional mass-luminosity degeneracy inherent in single-band continuum analyses. Our results reveal a systematic correlation between derived bolometric luminosities and the kinematic complexity of the host clumps, with deeply embedded precursors exhibiting characteristic temperatures near 10–15 K, whereas sources exhibiting outflow signatures consistently exceed 20 K. The resulting protostellar luminosity function conforms to a power-law slope compatible with canonical star formation theory, yet displays substantial intrinsic scatter directly linked to orientation-dependent extinction and highly variable accretion rates. Moreover, the extracted mass-averaged temperatures show a mild positive trend with local gas surface density, indicating that compressional heating contributes minimally compared to internal radiative feedback during the early assembly phase. Cross-validation against independent molecular line excitation diagnostics confirms the reliability of our thermal modeling, particularly in environments where supersonic turbulence dominates the velocity dispersion. Incorporating these empirically grounded temperature priors into the modified blackbody mass derivation reduces propagation errors by roughly 35 per cent relative to standard isothermal assumptions. This refined parametric approach yields self-consistent physical catalogs for the entire sample, delivering a critical observational constraint for hydrodynamical simulations and ultimately clarifying the initial conditions governing clustered massive star formation.

title: H-atom bombardment of CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO containing ices
text_ai: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. Aims: We present new laboratory experiments investigating the hydrogenation of CO2-, HCOOH-, and CH3CHO-dominated ices under conditions mimicking cold interstellar environments. Methods: Ultrahigh vacuum experiments were conducted using a cryogenic sample stage cooled to 10–20 K. Atomic hydrogen beams were generated via microwave discharge and directed onto pre-deposited molecular layers. Surface composition was monitored in situ using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, while thermal desorption mass spectrometry tracked volatile product release. Results: We observe efficient saturation hydrogenation of CO2 to form methanol (CH3OH) and formaldehyde (H2CO), with branching ratios strongly dependent on incident H-flux and substrate temperature. Isotopic labeling studies confirm minimal C–O bond cleavage, favoring direct O-functionalization pathways. For HCOOH, partial reduction yields CH3OH and H2O, whereas CH3CHO undergoes sequential H-addition to produce ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and ethane (C2H6). The measured reaction probabilities align well with Langmuir–Hinshelwood mechanisms, indicating thermally accommodated H-atom diffusion dominates over direct Eley–Rideal pathways. Activation barriers for initial H-addition were quantified across 10–25 K, revealing suppressed reactivity below 15 K due to quantum tunneling limitations. Conclusions: These findings provide critical rate parameters and product distributions for inclusion in gas-grain chemical networks. The enhanced yield of saturated oxygenated and carbonyl-derived species underscores the role of atomic H-processing in driving ice-phase complexity during prestellar collapse and early protostellar heating phases. Our data resolve longstanding uncertainties regarding the relative stability of carboxylic versus aldehyde precursors under cosmic-ray-induced processing cycles, offering refined constraints for astrochemical modeling of organic inventory evolution in dense cores and protoplanetary disks.

title: H-Alpha and Hard X-Ray Observations of a Two-Ribbon Flare Associated with a Filament Eruption
text_ai: We perform a multi-wavelength study of a two-ribbon flare on 2002 September 29 and its associated filament eruption, observed simultaneously in the H-alpha line by a ground-based imaging spectrograph and in hard X-rays by RHESSI. The flare ribbons contain several H-alpha bright kernels that show different evolutional behaviors. Detailed spatiotemporal analysis reveals that these kernels correspond to localized hard X-ray footpoint sources, indicating impulsive electron beam precipitation into the chromosphere. Some kernels persist through the decay phase, exhibiting steady thermal emission consistent with prolonged heating, while others brighten rapidly and fade swiftly, coincident with discrete hard X-ray bursts. A strong temporal correlation exists between ribbon separation speed and looptop HXR intensity, supporting a standard reconnection model wherein ascending magnetic islands drive episodic particle acceleration. Concurrently, the erupting filament displays a sigmoidal pre-flare morphology, with upward acceleration timing matching the initial ribbon expansion. These observations indicate that the heterogeneous kernel evolution traces a fragmented coronal current sheet, where spatially distributed reconnection governs both energy deposition patterns and flux rope dynamics. This multi-wavelength approach demonstrates that resolving fine-scale chromospheric structures is essential for constraining the magnetohydrodynamic mechanisms driving solar eruptions.

title: Quantile LSTM: A Robust LSTM for Anomaly Detection In Time Series Data
text_ai: Anomalies refer to the departure of systems and devices from their normal behaviour in standard operating conditions. An anomaly in an industrial device can indicate an upcoming failure, often in the temporal direction. In this paper, we make two contributions: 1) we estimate conditional quantiles and consider three different ways to define anomalies based on the estimated quantiles. 2) we propose a novel Quantile Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture that explicitly models prediction intervals through a customized asymmetric Laplace likelihood loss. Unlike conventional point-forecasting networks, our approach captures heteroscedasticity and heavy-tailed error distributions inherent in real-world sensor streams. We validate the framework across five benchmark industrial time-series datasets, comparing it against standard autoregressive LSTMs, Prophet, and isolation forest baselines. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently yields tighter predictive bounds while maintaining superior detection sensitivity under non-stationary conditions. Furthermore, the quantile-based thresholding strategies exhibit reduced false-positive rates compared to fixed-variance approaches, particularly in low-signal regimes. By decoupling distributional assumptions from sequence modeling, this work provides a scalable, statistically principled alternative for operational monitoring. These findings underscore the practical utility of distribution-aware recurrent architectures for early fault prognosis in safety-critical infrastructure.

title: Advice Complexity of Adaptive Priority Algorithms
text_ai: The priority model was introduced to capture "greedy-like" algorithms. Motivated by the success of advice complexity in the area of online algorithms, the fixed priority model was extended to include advice, and a reduction-based framework was developed for proving lower bounds on the amount of advice required to achieve certain approximation ratios in this rather powerful model. In this work, we extend the advice framework to the adaptive priority model, wherein algorithmic choices dynamically dictate the sequence of incoming requests. We derive tight advice complexity bounds for classical combinatorial optimization problems. Our lower bound techniques employ refined information-theoretic arguments that precisely quantify the conditional entropy of optimal configurations relative to adaptive exploration steps, whereas our upper bounds follow from constructive advice schemes transmitting compact guidance vectors compatible with state-dependent rule modifications. We prove that adaptivity inherently amplifies the informational burden, yielding asymptotically larger advice requirements than the static counterpart by logarithmic factors in the instance dimension. Additionally, we formulate a modular reduction methodology that systematically lifts known fixed-priority constraints into the adaptive regime, preserving approximation guarantees while tracking bit consumption. Our analysis demonstrates that randomized advice fails to circumvent these barriers, as deterministic and stochastic variants exhibit identical asymptotic scaling. Furthermore, we characterize the precise advice-approximation trade-off curves, demonstrating that minor relaxations in approximation yield superlinear savings in communicated bits. Collectively, these contributions delineate the fundamental limits of knowledge-augmented greedy strategies, resolving long-standing questions regarding the intrinsic cost of responsiveness in priority-driven computation.

title: An Oka principle for equivariant isomorphisms
text_ai: Let $G$ be a reductive complex Lie group acting holomorphically on normal Stein spaces $X$ and $Y$, which are locally $G$-biholomorphic over a common categorical quotient $Q$. When is there a global $G$-biholomorphism $X\to Y$? We establish necessary and sufficient topological obstructions to the existence of such global equivariant isomorphisms in terms of the relative homotopy type of the structure group and its induced action on the fibers. By developing an equivariant parametric Oka–Grauert principle for fiberwise holomorphic maps over $Q$, we reduce the geometric extension problem to a purely homotopy-theoretic question concerning sections of associated bundle gerbes. Our construction accommodates singular quotients by working within the category of stratified Stein spaces and employing descent techniques that preserve the holomorphic $G$-structure. The core of our argument rests on a parametric Oka property for the sheaf of equivariant holomorphic functions, verified via analysis of the infinitesimal deformation complex and its vanishing in higher degrees. We demonstrate that the obstruction space can be explicitly computed using equivariant Čech cohomology. As a direct application, we obtain a complete classification of $G$-equivariant deformations of Stein models up to $G$-biholomorphism, generalizing classical rigidity results to the non-free setting. Moreover, we prove that whenever the quotient $Q$ possesses a fundamental system of $G$-invariant Stein neighborhoods, the local-to-global principle holds unconditionally for connected reductive groups. These findings unify equivariant complex analysis with flexible Oka theory, yielding criteria for the solvability of equivariant Cousin problems and establishing a framework for studying automorphism groups of homogeneous Stein manifolds.

title: Visibility of current and shot noise in electrical Mach-Zehnder and Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometers
text_ai: We investigate the visibility of the current and shot-noise correlations of electrical analogs of the optical Mach-Zehnder interferometer and the Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometer. The electrical analogs are discussed in conductors subject to high magnetic fields where electron motion is along edge states. The transport quantities are modulated with the help of an Aharonov-Bohm flux. By systematically varying the magnetic flux, we demonstrate that current correlations exhibit destructive interference characteristic of fermionic antibunching, whereas shot-noise cross-correlations reveal constructive interference stemming from Pauli blocking-induced bunching. We derive analytical expressions for the visibility of both observables as a function of temperature, chemical potential splitting, and channel coupling asymmetry. Our results indicate that while current visibility is highly sensitive to thermal smearing and contact resistance, noise correlations maintain robust oscillatory behavior over a wider parameter range. Furthermore, we identify a regime where fractional statistics can be extracted directly from the zero-frequency noise spectrum without requiring precise knowledge of the transmission coefficients. These findings establish shot-noise cross-correlations as a superior probe for topological phase coherence in mesoscopic networks, offering a practical pathway for characterizing non-Abelian quasiparticles in future quantum Hall devices.

title: The effects of water temperature on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men.
text_ai: Although immediate pre-meal water ingestion has been shown to reduce energy intake in healthy young men, no studies are available regarding potential mechanisms underlying the effect of energy intake in response to different temperatures of pre-meal water ingestion. This study examined the effects of consuming different temperatures of water on gastric motility and energy intake in healthy young men. Twelve healthy young men (aged 20–25 years; BMI: 21.5 ± 1.2 kg/m²) completed a randomized, crossover trial. Participants ingested 500 mL of water at cold (4°C), room temperature (22°C), or warm (40°C) thirty minutes before a standardized buffet lunch. Gastric motility was recorded via high-resolution impedance planimetry, and energy intake was quantified through direct food weighing. Cold water significantly accelerated gastric emptying relative to both room-temperature (p < 0.05) and warm conditions (p < 0.01). In contrast, warm water prolonged antral contraction frequency and elevated intragastric pressure retention (p < 0.05). Subsequent energy intake was markedly attenuated following cold water consumption (mean difference: −287 kcal versus baseline, p = 0.003), whereas warm water produced only a trivial, non-significant decrease (−64 kcal, p = 0.21). Intragastric distension metrics exhibited a strong inverse correlation with caloric consumption (r = −0.68, p < 0.01). These findings demonstrate that pre-meal water temperature independently regulates gastric dynamics and drives differential energy intake responses. Cold beverages appear optimal for enhancing gastric compliance and amplifying early satiation signals. Consequently, thermal modulation of preprandial hydration may represent a practical, non-pharmacological avenue for appetite management, warranting further investigation across diverse cohorts.

title: Progresses in the Analysis of Stochastic 2D Cellular Automata: a Study of Asynchronous 2D Minority
text_ai: Cellular automata are often used to model systems in physics, social sciences, biology that are inherently asynchronous. Over the past 20 years, studies have demonstrated that the behavior of cellular automata drastically changed under asynchronous updates. Still, the few mathematical analyses of asynchronism focus on one-dimensional probabilistic cellular automata, either on single examples or on specific classes. This work bridges that gap by providing a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing asynchronous stochastic dynamics in two dimensions. We examine the Minority rule, an interacting particle system where each site adopts the less frequent state among its von Neumann neighborhood. Under a sequential random update protocol, we establish convergence properties and characterize stationary distributions through martingale arguments and entropy-based Lyapunov functions. Our analysis reveals that, contrary to synchronous dynamics exhibiting persistent oscillations, asynchrony induces rapid coarsening toward homogeneous absorbing states, with scaling laws governing domain boundary decay. Furthermore, we derive bounds on mixing time as a function of lattice size and update probability. These theoretical results are corroborated by numerical simulations, demonstrating robustness across various initial conditions. Ultimately, this study establishes foundational analytical tools for higher-dimensional stochastic automata, providing insight into emergent consensus mechanisms in spatially extended systems.

title: Formation mechanism of hairpin vortices in the wake of a truncated square cylinder in a duct
text_ai: We investigate the laminar shedding of hairpin vortices in the wake of a truncated square cylinder placed in a duct, for Reynolds numbers around the critical threshold of the onset of vortex shedding. We single out the formation mechanism of the hairpin vortices by means of a detailed analysis of the flow patterns in the steady regime. Direct numerical simulations are employed to resolve the three-dimensional coherent structures emerging downstream of the side walls. The results reveal that hairpin generation originates from the interaction between the primary shear layers rolling up along the free edges and the secondary corner vortices trapped within the separation bubbles. As the flow approaches the bifurcation point, infinitesimal spanwise perturbations amplify through a convective instability, leading to localized vortex pairing. This pairing process induces a spanwise redistribution of vorticity, which ultimately folds into the characteristic arch-like topology. Proper orthogonal decomposition further isolates the dominant modal contributions governing the transient growth phase. The proposed mechanism elucidates how geometric confinement and wall-induced blockage modulate the vortex evolution, offering a refined understanding of transitional bluff-body wakes. These insights provide a framework for passive flow control strategies targeting periodic loading suppression in ducted configurations.

title: Articulatory Representation Learning Via Joint Factor Analysis and Neural Matrix Factorization
text_ai: Articulatory representation learning is the fundamental research in modeling neural speech production system. Our previous work has established a deep paradigm to decompose the articulatory kinematics data into gestures, which explicitly model the phonological and linguistic structure encoded with human speech production mechanism, and corresponding gestural scores. Building upon this foundation, we introduce a novel framework that integrates joint factor analysis with neural matrix factorization to simultaneously learn latent articulatory representations and optimize reconstruction fidelity. By coupling linear dimensionality reduction with nonlinear deep embeddings, our approach captures both global kinematic covariations and fine-grained temporal dynamics inherent in articulator movements. We evaluate the proposed model on three public articulatory datasets, demonstrating superior gesture segmentation accuracy and enhanced cross-speaker generalization compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Specifically, the hybrid architecture reduces reconstruction error by 18.4% while preserving physiologically plausible gesture timing. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that the synergistic interaction between probabilistic factor structures and adaptive neural weights yields more interpretable gestural codes without compromising predictive performance. These findings advance computational models of speech motor control and provide a robust, scalable pipeline for downstream applications in speech synthesis, clinical assessment, and neuroprosthetic decoding systems.

title: Active Feature Acquisition with Supervised Matrix Completion
text_ai: Feature missing is a serious problem in many applications, which may lead to low quality of training data and further significantly degrade the learning performance. While feature acquisition usually involves special devices or complex process, it is expensive to acquire all feature values for the whole dataset. To address this limitation, we introduce an active feature acquisition framework that strategically identifies the most informative missing entries through supervised matrix completion. By incorporating label signals directly into the factorization objective, our approach simultaneously recovers latent feature dependencies and optimizes a cost-aware sampling policy. We formalize the selection process as a bi-level optimization problem and develop a scalable coordinate-descent solver that guarantees monotonic improvement at each iteration. Rigorous theoretical analysis provides generalization bounds and sample complexity guarantees under standard incoherence conditions. Empirical evaluations across diverse real-world benchmarks reveal that our method consistently outperforms heuristic and probabilistic alternatives, achieving comparable predictive accuracy while reducing measurement expenditures by over fifty-five percent. These results establish supervised matrix completion as a principled foundation for economical feature procurement in large-scale predictive modeling. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that explicit supervision significantly enhances recovery fidelity, particularly under high missingness rates where traditional unsupervised imputation fails.

title: Comparison of space weathering spectral changes induced by solar wind and micrometeoroid impacts using ion- and femtosecond-laser-irradiated olivine and pyroxene
text_ai: Space weathering is a process that changes the surface of airless planetary bodies. Prime space weathering agents are solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes alter planetary reflectance spectra and often modify their compositional diagnostic features. To disentangle their distinct spectral signatures, we experimentally simulated solar wind implantation via low-energy H⁺ and He⁺ ion irradiation, while micrometeoroid-like vapor deposition and melting were replicated using high-fluence femtosecond laser pulses on synthetic olivine and Mg-rich pyroxene powders. Reflectance spectroscopy and UV–Vis–NIR measurements reveal divergent alteration pathways: ion implantation induces gradual spectral reddening and shallow band weakening driven by amorphization and nanophase metallic iron (npFe⁰) nucleation at grain boundaries, whereas fs-laser treatment produces abrupt spectral darkening, pronounced band depression, and extensive melt-vapor condensation films. Mineral-specific responses highlight olivine’s greater susceptibility to structural collapse compared to pyroxene’s retention of silicate framework order under identical dosages. Quantitative inversion of optical constants demonstrates that ion-driven changes primarily affect the outermost 50–100 nm, preserving bulk mineralogical integrity, while laser-induced modification penetrates deeper, generating heterogeneous submicron crystallites embedded in glassy matrices. The resulting spectral slopes and absorption band centers shift nonlinearly with fluence, highlighting threshold-dependent phase transformations unique to each agent. Transmission electron microscopy corroborates these optical trends, revealing distinct defect architectures and particle morphologies that govern wavelength-dependent scattering efficiency and thermal relaxation dynamics. By directly comparing these end-member processing regimes, we establish empirical scaling relationships between irradiation dose, npFe⁰ size distribution, and continuum-normalized band area ratios. These findings refine our ability to deconvolve overlapping space weathering effects in remote sensing datasets, improve chronological models of regolith maturation, and constrain the relative contributions of atomic sputtering versus hypervelocity impact gardening across diverse regolith types.

title: Celestial $w_{1+\infty}$ Symmetries from Twistor Space
text_ai: We explain how twistor theory represents the self-dual sector of four dimensional gravity in terms of the loop group of Poisson diffeomorphisms of the plane via Penrose's non-linear graviton construction. The symmetries of the self-dual sector are generated by the corresponding loop algebra $Lw_{1+\infty}$ of the algebra $w_{1+\infty}$ of these Poisson diffeomorphisms. We demonstrate that the action of this infinite-dimensional symmetry algebra on the asymptotic phase space induces a corresponding tower of conformally soft gravitons on the celestial sphere. By explicitly constructing the twistorial representatives of these modes, we establish a direct dictionary between the loop algebra generators and celestial conformal primary operators. This correspondence reveals that the full $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetry governs the analytic structure of tree-level scattering amplitudes, enforcing non-trivial Ward identities that constrain the celestial operator product expansion and radiative modes. Furthermore, we show how the underlying Poisson bracket structure on twistor space precisely reproduces the commutation relations of the celestial stress-energy tensor and its higher-spin generalizations. These results provide a rigorous geometric foundation for celestial holography, suggesting that the exact symmetry group of asymptotically flat spacetimes emerges intrinsically from the complex geometry of twistor space rather than as an asymptotic boundary artifact.

title: Evaluation of nerve capture using classical landmarks for genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation: 3D cadaveric study.
text_ai: Radiofrequency (RF) denervation of the superolateral genicular nerve (SLGN), superomedial genicular nerve (SMGN) and inferomedial genicular nerve (IMGN) is commonly used to manage chronic knee joint pain. However, knowledge of articular branches captured, using classical landmarking techniques, remains unclear. This three-dimensional cadaveric study evaluated anatomical targeting accuracy using established surface landmark protocols. High-resolution computed tomography scans of twelve human lower extremities were reconstructed to map the precise courses of the SLGN, SMGN, and IMGN relative to bony prominences and fascial planes. Virtual needle trajectories were simulated following standard landmark-based insertion techniques, and spatial relationships between electrode tips and target nerves were quantified. Bland-Altman analysis confirmed acceptable interobserver agreement (ICC = 0.89). Classical landmarking demonstrated substantial deviation from actual nerve pathways, with mean radial displacement exceeding 6.2 ± 1.8 mm across all target sites. Only 38.5% of simulated deployments achieved optimal contact with intended articular branches. Interindividual morphological differences, particularly regarding tibial tuberosity prominence and suprapatellar plica configuration, significantly compromised prediction reliability. Surrounding adipose tissue layers further obscured direct nerve-electrode coupling during theoretical ablation. Geometric modeling revealed that traditional perpendicular insertion angles frequently intersect adjacent cutaneous branches. These findings indicate that conventional surface-marking approaches yield inconsistent anatomical localization and suboptimal neural engagement. Incorporating real-time fluoroscopic guidance or ultrasound augmentation may improve targeting precision. Future clinical protocols should prioritize image-assisted verification to enhance therapeutic outcomes and minimize non-target thermal injury in patients undergoing genicular radiofrequency neurotomy for refractory osteoarthritic pain.

title: Trainable Weight Averaging: Accelerating Training and Improving Generalization
text_ai: Weight averaging is a widely used technique for accelerating training and improving the generalization of deep neural networks (DNNs). While existing approaches like stochastic weight averaging (SWA) rely on pre-set weighting schemes, they can be suboptimal when handling diverse weights. To address this limitation, we propose Trainable Weight Averaging (TWA), a novel framework that dynamically optimizes averaging coefficients through gradient-based learning rather than relying on heuristic schedules. By treating the mixing weights as trainable parameters integrated directly into the optimization trajectory, TWA adaptively balances historical model states according to their current predictive utility and curvature properties. This formulation enables simultaneous acceleration of convergence and refinement of the implicit regularization effect, yielding flatter minima without additional hyperparameter tuning. Extensive experiments across convolutional architectures, vision transformers, and language models demonstrate that TWA consistently outperforms fixed-scheme counterparts, reducing wall-clock training time by up to 35% while achieving state-of-the-art test accuracy under identical computational budgets. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that the learned weighting mechanism generalizes across different network depths and data distributions. Our findings establish trainable coefficient adaptation as a practical and theoretically grounded alternative to static ensemble strategies, offering a straightforward plug-in enhancement for modern deep learning pipelines.

title: Adaptive sports for promoting physical activity in community-dwelling adults with stroke: A feasibility study.
text_ai: Despite proven health benefits of regular participation in physical activities (PA), adults with stroke fail to achieve recommended levels of PA. Sports being an enjoyable activity is more likely to encourage participation. This feasibility study evaluated the practicality, safety, and preliminary efficacy of a structured adaptive sports program designed to enhance PA engagement among this population. Twelve community-dwelling adults (mean age = 68.4 years; median time since stroke = 36 months) with mild-to-moderate motor impairments were recruited through local rehabilitation networks and patient advocacy groups. Participants engaged in twice-weekly, supervised adaptive sports sessions (tennis, badminton, and cycling) over eight weeks. Feasibility was assessed via recruitment rates, retention, session attendance, adverse events, and protocol fidelity. Acceptability was measured using post-intervention surveys and semi-structured interviews. Preliminary efficacy examined changes in moderate-to-vigorous PA (MVPA), functional mobility, and self-efficacy using accelerometry, timed up-and-go, and the Physical Activity Self-Efficacy Scale, respectively. Recruitment achieved 85% of target enrollment within four weeks, with a 92% retention rate. Average session attendance was 7.8/8 (97.5%), and no serious adverse events occurred. Qualitative feedback indicated high enjoyment, social integration, and perceived relevance to daily functioning. Quantitatively, participants increased mean daily MVPA by 34 minutes (SD = 12.4), demonstrated improved TUG performance (−1.8 seconds, p = .04), and reported enhanced PA self-efficacy (Δ = +14.2 points). Adaptive sports represent a highly acceptable and feasible modality for increasing PA in community-dwelling adults with stroke. These results strongly support conducting a definitive randomized controlled trial to assess sustained clinical, psychological, and functional impacts.

title: On channel sounding with switched arrays in fast time-varying channels
text_ai: Time-division multiplexed (TDM) channel sounders, in which a single RF chain is connected sequentially via an electronic switch to different elements of an array, are widely used for the measurement of double-directional/MIMO propagation channels. This paper investigates the impact of array switching patterns on the accuracy of parameter estimation of multipath components (MPC) for a time-division multiplexed (TDM) channel sounder. We develop a comprehensive analytical framework that characterizes the relationship between switching sequence design, Doppler spread, and angular-Doppler resolution limits. Modeling the rapidly evolving channel as a sparse delay-Doppler-angle structure, we derive closed-form Cramér-Rao lower bounds for direction-of-arrival, direction-of-departure, and Doppler estimates. Extensive simulations and over-the-air measurements at 28 GHz reveal that periodic switching induces severe spectral aliasing under high mobility, whereas optimized pseudo-random sequences substantially reduce estimation bias and variance. Consequently, we introduce a dynamic switching protocol that adaptively redistributes sampling intervals according to instantaneous Doppler statistics, effectively decoupling spatial scanning from temporal undersampling. This methodology consistently maintains full angular resolution while accommodating rapid channel fluctuations inherent to vehicular and aerial platforms. The results establish practical design guidelines for next-generation TDM sounders, facilitating reliable MIMO channel modeling for emerging high-mobility 6G deployments.

title: Tetrahedral framework nucleic acids promote scarless healing of cutaneous wounds via the AKT-signaling pathway.
text_ai: While the skin is considered the first line of defense in the human body, there are some vulnerabilities that render it susceptible to certain threats, which is an issue that is recognized by both patients and doctors. Cutaneous wound healing is a series of complex processes that involve many types of cells, such as fibroblasts and keratinocytes. However, conventional therapeutic strategies frequently culminate in pathological fibrosis and suboptimal tissue regeneration. To address this limitation, tetrahedral framework nucleic acids (TFNAs), characterized by superior structural stability and efficient cellular uptake, were evaluated for their regenerative capacity. Herein, we demonstrate that topical TFNA administration significantly accelerates cutaneous wound closure in murine full-thickness excision models. Mechanistic analyses reveal that TFNAs robustly activate the AKT signaling cascade, thereby enhancing fibroblast proliferation and migration while suppressing pro-inflammatory cytokine release. Transcriptomic profiling further confirms TFNA-mediated upregulation of AKT downstream effectors critical for re-epithelialization and neovascularization. Histomorphometric evaluation indicates markedly organized collagen deposition and attenuated inflammatory infiltration, yielding regenerated epidermis indistinguishable from native tissue. Collectively, these data establish TFNAs as a precision biomaterial that harnesses AKT-dependent modulation to orchestrate optimal extracellular matrix remodeling, providing a novel therapeutic paradigm for achieving scarless cutaneous wound repair.

title: Discovery and characterisation of detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries in the WFCAM Transit Survey
text_ai: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag and provide a detailed characterisation of three of them, using high-precision infrared light curves from the WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Such systems provide the most accurate and model-independent method for measuring the fundamental parameters of these poorly understood yet numerous stars, which currently lack sufficient observations to precisely calibrate stellar evolution models. Photometric analysis was performed using Wilson–Devinney iterations constrained by multi-band WTS passbands, supplemented by radial velocity measurements for two systems to break degeneracies. The resulting dynamical masses and radii span 0.12–0.25 M☉ and 0.14–0.28 R☉, with derived effective temperatures ranging from 3100 to 3900 K. When compared against modern isochrone predictions, our empirical points reveal systematic radius inflation of approximately five to eight per cent relative to standard zero-age main sequence calculations, consistent with magnetic activity-induced suppression of convective energy transport. Orbital solutions indicate near-circular configurations, confirming tidal circularisation has proceeded efficiently at these short periods below twelve days. Furthermore, one system exhibits a marginally eccentric orbit that may trace recent dynamical interactions or unresolved triplet architecture. These precision benchmarks establish a robust observational framework for testing low-mass stellar physics under varying metallicity and age conditions. By anchoring theoretical tracks to empirically verified mass–radius relations, this work constrains opacity treatments and equation-of-state assumptions critical for substellar evolutionary pathways. The demonstrated efficacy of infrared transit photometry underscores WTS as a productive pipeline for identifying rare compact binaries, paving the way for targeted follow-up campaigns with JWST and next-generation ground-based facilities. Ultimately, these characterised systems will serve as primary calibrators for refining population synthesis models and interpreting large-scale time-domain surveys.

title: Cycle-SUM: Cycle-consistent Adversarial LSTM Networks for Unsupervised Video Summarization
text_ai: In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised video summarization model that requires no manual annotation. The proposed model termed Cycle-SUM adopts a new cycle-consistent adversarial LSTM architecture that can effectively maximize the information preserving and compactness of the summary video. It consists of a frame selector and a cycle-consistent learning based evaluator. During training, the frame selector iteratively proposes high-potential subsequences, which are subsequently refined by the evaluator through a min-max game. To guarantee semantic fidelity, we impose a bidirectional reconstruction penalty that maps extracted features back to the original pixel space, thereby mitigating critical information loss. This is complemented by a diversity-aware regularization term that explicitly penalizes redundant selections, ensuring comprehensive temporal coverage. Extensive evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over contemporary baselines across multiple automated metrics. Quantitative results indicate superior performance in both precision and recall, while qualitative assessments highlight enhanced visual coherence and narrative flow. Ablation studies further confirm that the cycle-consistency mechanism substantially boosts summary stability across heterogeneous video lengths. Ultimately, this research establishes a highly effective, annotation-free paradigm for content distillation, enabling practical deployment in large-scale video analytics pipelines.

title: Neural response to modulating the probability that actions of self or other result in auditory tones: A parametric fMRI study into causal ambiguity.
text_ai: In normal circumstances we can easily distinguish between changes to the external world brought about by our own actions from those with external causes. However, in certain contexts our sense of ownership and agency over acts is not so clear. To investigate the neural correlates of this phenomenon, we employed a parametric fMRI design where participants performed button presses that probabilistically triggered auditory tones. We constructed a factorial paradigm crossing self versus other action labels with varying conditional probabilities to systematically manipulate the action-to-tone contingency. This manipulation generated graded levels of causal ambiguity regarding whether the resulting sound originated from self-generated movement or an external agent. Whole-brain analysis revealed that increased causal uncertainty progressively engaged a fronto-parietal network, including the right temporoparietal junction (rTPJ), dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), and inferior frontal gyrus (IFG). Parametric modulation analyses demonstrated linear increases in BOLD signal within these regions as the subjective probability of self-agency decreased. Crucially, these parametric responses remained robust after controlling for motion artifacts and were spatially distinct from primary auditory cortex activation. Notably, functional connectivity between the rTPJ and premotor cortices was significantly enhanced under high-ambiguity conditions, suggesting adaptive recalibration of sensorimotor predictions. These findings delineate the dynamic neural architecture supporting agency attribution under uncertain contingencies. By isolating the parametric effects of causal ambiguity, we identify a distributed cortical system that continuously weights proprioceptive evidence against external feedback to maintain a coherent sense of self-initiated action. This framework has implications for understanding disorders of agency, such as schizophrenia, where pathological causal inference may underlie delusions of control.

title: Simultaneous Segmentation and Recognition: Towards more accurate Ego Gesture Recognition
text_ai: Ego hand gestures can be used as an interface in AR and VR environments. While the context of an image is important for tasks like scene understanding, object recognition, image caption generation and activity recognition, it plays a minimal role in ego hand gesture recognition. Current approaches often treat gesture classification as a purely contextual problem, inadvertently incorporating irrelevant background features that degrade generalization across varying environments. To address this limitation, we introduce a dual-branch framework that concurrently performs precise hand segmentation and fine-grained gesture recognition. By explicitly decoupling spatial foreground localization from semantic classification, our model learns environment-invariant representations focused exclusively on salient articulatory cues. The architecture employs a shared encoder with task-specific decoders, optimized through a unified loss function balancing boundary precision and categorical accuracy. Extensive experiments on standard ego-gesture benchmarks demonstrate that simultaneous modeling yields significant improvements in both segmentation fidelity and recognition accuracy, outperforming sequential and single-task baselines by notable margins. Ablation studies further validate the complementary benefits of joint training, revealing that mutual supervision enhances feature discriminability while suppressing spurious contextual correlations. These findings establish a robust paradigm for immersive interaction systems, offering a scalable pathway toward reliable gesture interfaces.

title: The Comparative Study of Cervical Shear Wave Elastography Between Twin and Singleton Pregnancy.
text_ai: To compare the cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) by using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women. This was a prospective cohort study involving the twin and singleton pregnant women who attended the antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok, Thailand. Eligible participants aged 18–40 years with uncomplicated pregnancies were enrolled. Exclusions comprised prior cervical intervention, obstetric history of preterm birth, or uterine anomalies. One hundred twenty singleton and eighty-five dichorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancies were recruited between 20 and 36 weeks’ gestation. Cervical SWE assessments utilized a standardized transvaginal protocol, recording three consecutive Young’s modulus values at the internal os. Mean tissue stiffness (kPa) was derived per participant. Baseline demographics and clinical parameters were documented. Group comparisons employed independent t-tests or Mann–Whitney U analyses for continuous variables, alongside Chi-square tests for categorical data. Statistical significance was defined at p < 0.05 using SPSS v26.0. Scanning gestational ages were comparable across cohorts (p = 0.42). Mean cervical stiffness was significantly elevated in twins versus singletons (14.8 ± 3.2 kPa vs. 9.4 ± 2.1 kPa; p < 0.001). Multivariate adjustment confirmed this association (adjusted mean difference: 4.9 kPa; 95% CI: 3.1–6.7; p < 0.001). Elasticity declined with advancing gestation in both groups, though the degradation trajectory was steeper among twins. No SWE metrics correlated with adverse perinatal endpoints during follow-up. Twin gestations exhibit markedly increased cervical stiffness compared to singleton counterparts via TVS-SWE. These biomechanical disparities likely indicate divergent cervical remodeling dynamics in multifetal pregnancies, implying that singleton-derived elastographic cutoffs may inadequately capture preterm labor risk in twins. Future multicenter longitudinal studies should validate gestation-specific reference ranges to optimize clinical surveillance protocols and refine risk stratification algorithms.

title: Xiaoyao Pills Ameliorate Depression-like Behaviors and Oxidative Stress Induced by Olfactory Bulbectomy in Rats via the Activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF Signaling Pathway.
text_ai: Numerous studies have revealed that oxidative stress is closely associated with the occurrence and development of depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW) are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia and are frequently used for treating anxiety and depression by smoothing the liver, strengthening the spleen, and nourishing the blood. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic efficacy of XYW on OBX-induced depressive phenotypes and elucidated the underlying molecular mechanisms. Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats underwent bilateral olfactory bulbectomy or sham surgery. Following a two-week recovery period, OBX rats were randomly assigned to receive either vehicle, fluoxetine hydrochloride (positive control), or escalating doses of XYW extract for four weeks. Behavioral assessments, including the forced swimming test (FST), tail suspension test (TST), and open field test (OFT), were conducted to evaluate depressive- and anxiety-like behaviors. Hippocampal tissue was subsequently harvested for histopathological examination, measurement of oxidative stress biomarkers (malondialdehyde, superoxide dismutase, glutathione peroxidase), and Western blot analysis of key proteins in the PI3K/AKT/Nfe2l2/Bdnf cascade. XYW treatment significantly attenuated OBX-induced immobility in the FST and TST while restoring locomotor activity in the OFT. Biochemically, XYW administration markedly reduced hippocampal malondialdehyde levels and restored antioxidant enzyme activities to near-normal ranges. At the molecular level, XYW upregulated the phosphorylation of PIK3CA and AKT1, enhanced nuclear translocation of NFE2L2, and subsequently increased BDNF expression. These effects were comparable to those observed with fluoxetine treatment. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that XYW exerts potent antidepressant-like effects in the OBX rat model by mitigating hippocampal oxidative damage through the targeted activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF signaling axis. This mechanistic insight provides a robust preclinical foundation for the clinical translation of XYW as a multi-target therapeutic strategy for depression.

title: New interventions to treat chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
text_ai: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) can be defined as a type of precapillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) resulting from incomplete resolution of pulmonary embolism. Symptoms are exertional breathlessness and most patients come to a cardiologist's attention with a dilated right heart on echocardiography. Historically, pulmonary endarterectomy has served as the definitive therapeutic modality; however, a substantial proportion of individuals remain ineligible due to distal vascular involvement or prohibitive surgical risk. Consequently, balloon pulmonary angioplasty has emerged as a pivotal alternative, demonstrating marked improvements in mean pulmonary arterial pressure and exercise capacity through sequential mechanical disruption of organized thromboembolic material. Concurrently, pharmacological strategies targeting endothelin receptor pathways, soluble guanylate cyclase stimulation, and prostacyclin signaling have been increasingly integrated into management algorithms, particularly for patients with persistent or recurrent disease post-intervention. Contemporary evidence supports these emerging modalities, emphasizing advancements in catheter-based techniques, next-generation vasodilator regimens, and personalized treatment stratification guided by right ventricular remodeling metrics. Hemodynamic parameters consistently reveal sustained reductions in pulmonary vascular resistance alongside enhanced six-minute walk distances, although long-term survival data remain limited. Safety profiles indicate acceptable complication rates when performed at specialized centers, though procedural optimization and standardized patient selection criteria require further validation through multicenter randomized trials. Ultimately, the integration of minimally invasive endovascular approaches with refined medical therapy represents a paradigm shift in CTEPH management, offering viable salvage options for previously untreatable populations. Future research must prioritize prospective comparative effectiveness studies to establish hierarchical treatment algorithms that optimize resource allocation while mitigating clinical disease progression.

title: Modified Lagrangian Formulation of Gear Tooth Crack Analysis using Combined Approach of Variable Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Time Synchronous Averaging (TSA)
text_ai: This paper discusses the possible observation of an integrated gear tooth crack analysis procedure that employs the combined approach of variable mode decomposition (VMD) and time synchronous averaging (TSA) based on the coupled electromechanical gearbox (CEMG) system. This paper also incorporates the modified Lagrangian formulation to model the CEMG system by considering Rayleigh's dissipative potential. The proposed framework synergistically couples VMD for adaptive signal decomposition with TSA to isolate periodic fault signatures from complex operational noise. Within the modified Lagrangian structure, generalized coordinates are augmented to capture torsional-electrical coupling dynamics, while Rayleigh’s dissipation function explicitly accounts for frictional and structural damping mechanisms inherent to degraded mesh interfaces. Numerical simulations validate the model’s capacity to replicate amplitude-modulated vibration responses under varying load conditions, demonstrating enhanced sensitivity to incipient tooth fractures. Experimental validation utilizing accelerated life test data confirms that the VMD-TSA hybridization effectively suppresses background interference, yielding superior signal-to-noise ratios compared to conventional spectral techniques. Quantitative metrics reveal a measurable phase shift and energy redistribution in the decomposed intrinsic mode functions correlating directly with progressive crack propagation depths. Furthermore, the integration of electromechanical feedback loops within the Lagrangian framework enables real-time monitoring of stiffness degradation without requiring external excitation sources. These findings establish a robust diagnostic protocol capable of early-stage defect identification in industrial drive systems, offering significant advantages for predictive maintenance strategies. The proposed methodology’s computational efficiency and numerical stability underscore its practical applicability across diverse rotating machinery configurations, bridging theoretical dynamical modeling with advanced signal processing techniques for reliable condition assessment and fault prognostics.

title: Is the faint young Sun problem for Earth solved?
text_ai: Stellar evolution models predict that the solar luminosity was lower in the past, typically 20-25 % lower during the Archean (3.8-2.5 Ga). Despite the fainter Sun, there is strong evidence for the presence of liquid water on Earth's surface at that time. This thermal paradox has driven research into atmospheric compositions and feedback mechanisms capable of maintaining liquid water under reduced insolation. Proposed resolutions predominantly invoke elevated carbon dioxide, methane, and molecular hydrogen to enhance radiative forcing, alongside reduced surface albedo or diminished stratospheric clouds. Radiative-convective modeling and Neoarchean paleosol constraints have narrowed permissible gas partial pressures, though uncertainties persist regarding prebiotic methane budgets and biosphere-atmosphere coupling. We evaluate these proposals against observational datasets and climate simulations. Although elevated CO₂ levels are thermodynamically viable, they contradict carbonate-silicate weathering indicators unless ancient oceans exhibited anomalously low pH. Methane-dominated atmospheres encounter severe photochemical loss rates, demanding exotic surface catalysts or attenuated solar ultraviolet output. No isolated mechanism adequately reconciles the energy deficit; instead, a synergistic interplay of modest greenhouse amplification, modified atmospheric dynamics, and shifting surface characteristics probably preserved Archean warmth. Accordingly, we assert that the faint young Sun problem remains incompletely solved, requiring unified biogeochemical-climate approaches to align with the empirical record.

title: Diversifying Knowledge Enhancement of Biomedical Language Models using Adapter Modules and Knowledge Graphs
text_ai: Recent advances in natural language processing (NLP) owe their success to pre-training language models on large amounts of unstructured data. Still, there is an increasing effort to combine the unstructured nature of LMs with structured knowledge and reasoning. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel framework integrating parameter-efficient adapter modules with biomedical knowledge graphs to systematically diversify model expertise across clinical and molecular domains. Rather than relying on monolithic fine-tuning, our approach injects graph-structured relational priors into frozen transformer weights via lightweight, task-specific adapters. These components are dynamically routed based on entity type and contextual uncertainty, enabling modular knowledge acquisition without catastrophic forgetting. We evaluate the method on three downstream tasks: relation extraction, drug-target interaction prediction, and clinical concept normalization. Results demonstrate consistent improvements over baseline LMs and full-parameter fine-tuning, yielding average F1 gains of 4.7% and 6.2%, respectively. Ablation studies further confirm that adapter diversification significantly enhances out-of-distribution generalization while reducing computational overhead by 89%. By decoupling structural reasoning from parametric memory, this framework establishes a scalable paradigm for continuously updating biomedical representations. Ultimately, our findings highlight how hybrid architectures can effectively bridge symbolic knowledge and statistical learning, providing a reproducible blueprint for robust clinical AI systems.

title: REPOSE: Distributed Top-k Trajectory Similarity Search with Local Reference Point Tries
text_ai: Trajectory similarity computation is a fundamental component in a variety of real-world applications, such as ridesharing, road planning, and transportation optimization. Recent advances in mobile devices have enabled an unprecedented increase in the amount of available trajectory data such that efficient query processing can no longer be supported by a single machine. To address this scalability bottleneck, we introduce REPOSE, a distributed framework designed for efficient top-k trajectory similarity search across massive spatio-temporal datasets. REPOSE utilizes a hierarchical indexing architecture grounded in local reference point tries, which recursively partitions trajectories according to spatial proximity and temporal alignment while drastically reducing inter-node communication. By dynamically routing subtrajectory fragments across cluster nodes and integrating adaptive distance pruning, our approach significantly lowers both computational latency and bandwidth consumption. Comprehensive evaluations on real-world GPS traces demonstrate that REPOSE yields up to 3.2× speedup over leading centralized methods, while exhibiting near-linear scalability relative to dataset volume and cluster size. These findings position REPOSE as a practical, high-performance engine for latency-critical location-based analytics.

title: SL-YOLO: A Stronger and Lighter Drone Target Detection Model
text_ai: Detecting small objects in complex scenes, such as those captured by drones, is a daunting challenge due to the difficulty in capturing the complex features of small targets. While the YOLO family has achieved great success in large target detection, its performance is less than satisfactory when faced with small targets. To address these limitations, we propose SL-YOLO, a novel framework specifically engineered for aerial surveillance applications. First, we integrate a multi-scale feature aggregation module that enhances cross-layer information flow, thereby preserving fine-grained spatial details crucial for miniature object localization. Second, a lightweight channel attention mechanism is embedded within the backbone to suppress background noise while amplifying salient target responses without introducing substantial computational overhead. Furthermore, we redesign the neck architecture with an optimized path aggregation network to accelerate gradient propagation and reduce parameter redundancy. Extensive experiments on two benchmark UAV datasets demonstrate that SL-YOLO achieves a mean average precision of 41.3%, outperforming state-of-the-art variants by up to 3.8% while reducing model parameters by 32% and improving inference speed by 27%. These results validate the efficacy of our structural optimizations, establishing SL-YOLO as a robust solution for real-time, resource-constrained aerial monitoring systems.

title: Simplified Muscle-Suspension Lower Blepharoplasty by Orbicularis Hitch.
text_ai: The suspension of orbicularis oculi during lower blepharoplasty presents a logical surgical addition for further support of the lid, as well as further improvement to its contour profile. It has traditionally been performed as an extension of the skin-muscle flap procedure, but more recently, and aggressively, as a muscle strap-flap separated from the orbicularis sheet by myotomy. This article introduces the orbicularis hitch technique, a streamlined alternative that preserves fascial continuity while achieving comparable or superior structural reinforcement. By utilizing targeted suturing anchors rather than extensive tissue division, the procedure minimizes dissection trauma and reduces postoperative edema and ecchymosis. A retrospective analysis of 142 consecutive patients undergoing primary lower blepharoplasty between 2021 and 2023 was conducted to evaluate safety, functional stability, and aesthetic outcomes. Mean follow-up duration was 18.4 months. Clinical assessments demonstrated significant reduction in lower eyelid laxity, with 96.4% of subjects exhibiting maintained lid-cheek junction definition at final evaluation. Complication rates remained low, including no instances of ectropion, scleral show, or persistent orbital hollowing. Patients reported accelerated visual recovery and high satisfaction regarding natural contour restoration. Compared to conventional strap-flap modifications, the orbicularis hitch requires fewer operative steps, eliminates the need for intramuscular myotomy, and decreases reliance on fat repositioning alone for volume management. These findings indicate that the simplified suspension method offers a reproducible, tissue-preserving strategy that optimizes both anatomical support and aesthetic harmony. Consequently, this technique represents a viable standard of care for surgeons seeking predictable, durable results with minimized perioperative morbidity in contemporary lower eyelid rejuvenation across diverse facial morphologies.

title: VIVID: A Novel Approach to Remediation Prioritization in Static Application Security Testing (SAST)
text_ai: Static Application Security Testing (SAST) enables organizations to detect vulnerabilities in code early; however, major SAST platforms do not include visual aids and present little insight on correlations between tainted data chains. To address these limitations, we introduce VIVID, a novel framework that integrates interactive graph-based visualization with conventional static analysis pipelines to reconstruct and prioritize tainted data flows. By explicitly mapping propagation paths across function boundaries, VIVID reveals latent correlations among seemingly isolated findings, enabling developers to assess contextual risk rather than relying on isolated severity scores. The system employs a multi-dimensional scoring model that weights exploitability, attack surface exposure, and downstream impact, dynamically ranking vulnerabilities according to their actual threat posture. We evaluated VIVID against three industry-standard SAST engines using a benchmark suite of 412 applications containing 1,847 confirmed vulnerabilities. Results demonstrate a 34% reduction in triage time and a 28% decrease in misprioritized alerts compared to baseline toolchains. Furthermore, user studies indicate significantly improved developer comprehension when utilizing VIVID’s visual correlation maps during remediation planning. By transforming opaque scan outputs into actionable, context-aware threat narratives, VIVID bridges the critical gap between automated vulnerability detection and efficient security operations, offering a scalable pathway toward proactive application hardening.

title: VasTSD: Learning 3D Vascular Tree-state Space Diffusion Model for Angiography Synthesis
text_ai: Angiography imaging is a medical imaging technique that enhances the visibility of blood vessels within the body by using contrast agents. Angiographic images can effectively assist in the diagnosis of vascular diseases. However, contrast agents may bring extra radiation exposure which is harmful to patients with health risks. To mitigate these adverse effects while preserving diagnostic fidelity, we propose VasTSD, a novel 3D vascular tree-state space diffusion model for non-invasive angiography synthesis. Unlike conventional generative approaches that operate directly on volumetric voxels, VasTSD explicitly encodes the topological and geometric priors of vascular networks within a unified tree-state space. By integrating a hierarchical diffusion process conditioned on sparse anatomical landmarks and hemodynamic features, our framework iteratively denoises implicit vessel representations to reconstruct high-fidelity, contrast-free angiographic volumes. Extensive experiments on clinical datasets demonstrate that VasTSD achieves state-of-the-art quantitative performance across structural similarity, peak signal-to-noise ratio, and vascular continuity metrics, significantly outperforming baseline GAN and unconditional diffusion architectures. Furthermore, downstream segmentation tasks trained on synthesized data yield diagnostic accuracy comparable to models utilizing real contrast-enhanced scans. These findings establish VasTSD as a robust, clinically viable solution for radiation-free vascular imaging, enabling safer interventional planning and reducing patient risk.

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
text_ai: Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs) by encouraging step by step thinking. However, CoT-based methods depend on intermediate reasoning steps, which limits scalability and generalization. Recent work explores recursive reasoning, where LLMs reuse internal layers across iterations to refine latent representations without explicit CoT supervision. To address these limitations, we introduce SCOUT (Sequential Contextual Optimization via Unified Thinking), a framework that integrates dynamic flow-based chain-of-thought generation with iterative latent refinement. Unlike conventional approaches, SCOUT employs a lightweight routing module that adaptively directs task-specific gradients through residual connections, enabling continuous thought propagation across model depths. This flow mechanism preserves explicit reasoning traces while leveraging recursive updates to stabilize representation learning. We train SCOUT using a hierarchical contrastive objective that aligns generated thought trajectories with gold-standard solutions, effectively distilling multi-step logic into compact parameter updates. During inference, the model dynamically adjusts its computational budget by selectively activating deeper layers only when predictive uncertainty exceeds predefined thresholds. Extensive evaluations on mathematical reasoning, symbolic manipulation, and logical deduction benchmarks demonstrate that SCOUT outperforms standard CoT and recursive baselines by up to 14.2% accuracy, while reducing inference latency by 38%. Experiments validate the routing mechanism’s role in sustaining multi-step consistency. The method exhibits strong zero-shot transfer capabilities across domains lacking domain-specific fine-tuning. By unifying explicit trace generation with implicit recursive refinement, SCOUT establishes a scalable paradigm for reasoning enhancement that maintains interpretability without compromising efficiency. Our findings suggest that structured flow dynamics offer a promising direction for next-generation reasoning architectures.

title: A GPU-accelerated viewer for HEALPix maps
text_ai: HEALPix by G\'orski et. al. (2005) is de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data storage and analysis, and is widely used in current and upcoming CMB experiments. Almost all the datasets in Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis (LAMBDA) use HEALPix as a format of choice. Despite its ubiquity, interactive visualization of high-resolution HEALPix maps remains computationally prohibitive on conventional central processing units, particularly when handling multi-terabyte datasets from next-generation surveys. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a novel GPU-accelerated rendering engine specifically optimized for hierarchical equal-area iso-latitude pixelization schemes. Our implementation leverages massive parallelism through a custom compute shader pipeline that directly processes nested and ring-formatted HEALPix indices without intermediate rasterization steps. By implementing dynamic level-of-detail culling and zero-copy memory architectures, the viewer minimizes host-device transfer overhead while maintaining sub-pixel precision across azimuthal equidistant, Mollweide, and orthographic projections. We further integrate an adaptive color-mapping algorithm that dynamically scales statistical displays based on local variance estimates, ensuring optimal contrast preservation for both temperature and polarization components. Benchmarking against state-of-the-art CPU-based astronomical visualization frameworks demonstrates a consistent 15–40× throughput improvement, enabling real-time interaction with Nside=8192 maps at 60 frames per second on mid-range workstation GPUs. The software suite provides standardized command-line interfaces for automated batch processing alongside seamless integration with Python and C++ analysis environments via shared-memory bindings. Validation through representative cosmological workflows confirms robust performance during polarization field decomposition, beam convolution diagnostics, and cross-correlation mask generation for Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 precursor campaigns. By eliminating legacy rendering constraints, this architecture substantially lowers the computational threshold for rapid data interrogation, thereby streamlining hypothesis testing and quality assurance protocols across the broader cosmological research community.
