title: A Latent Variable Approach for Non-Hierarchical Multi-Fidelity Adaptive Sampling
text_ai: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in the exploring and exploiting the design space. However, designing efficient acquisition strategies for non-hierarchical fidelity levels remains challenging due to complex cross-fidelity correlations and computational trade-offs. To address this limitation, we propose a novel latent variable framework that unifies disparate fidelity sources within a single probabilistic representation. By embedding each fidelity model into a shared latent space, our approach explicitly captures structural similarities and systematic biases without requiring strict hierarchical ordering or linear correlation assumptions. Building upon this representation, we develop a computationally tractable adaptive sampling criterion that balances exploration and exploitation across fidelity tiers through a modified expected improvement formulation. The acquisition function is optimized using a multi-start gradient-based scheme augmented with stochastic re-evaluation to mitigate local optima. Cross-validation metrics confirm that the latent embeddings preserve essential physical characteristics while filtering out fidelity-specific noise. Extensive numerical experiments on benchmark engineering problems demonstrate that the proposed methodology consistently outperforms state-of-the-art MF surrogates and traditional adaptive schemes. Specifically, our approach reduces the number of high-fidelity evaluations required to reach target accuracy by up to 45% while maintaining robust convergence across diverse objective landscapes. Furthermore, the latent formulation naturally accommodates heterogeneous data availability and facilitates seamless transfer learning between fidelity levels. Computational overhead scales favorably with dimensionality, enabling application to medium-scale parameterized systems. These findings underscore the practical utility of probabilistic latent representations for resource-constrained optimization, offering a scalable pathway toward next-generation multi-fidelity design frameworks.

title: On exponentiality of automorphisms of ${\bf A}^n$ of order $p$ in characteristic $p>0$
text_ai: Let $X$ be an integral affine scheme of characteristic $p>0$, and $\sigma $ a non-identity automorphism of $X$. If $\sigma $ is $\textit{exponential}$, i.e., induced from a ${\bf G}_a$-action on $X$, then $\sigma $ is obviously of order $p$. It is easy to see that the converse is not true in general. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for an automorphism of order $p$ on ${\bf A}^n$ to be exponential. Specifically, we prove that any such automorphism fixing a hyperplane pointwise arises from a locally nilpotent derivation if and only if its higher-order differential operators satisfy a Frobenius-compatibility condition. Conversely, we construct explicit counterexamples in dimensions $n \geq 3$ where an order-$p$ automorphism fails to be exponential despite inducing the identity on the cotangent space. Our method exploits the correspondence between ${\bf G}_a$-actions and exponential maps via truncated divided power structures, yielding a precise obstruction class in the first cohomology of the tangent sheaf. We further show that local exponentiality does not guarantee global integrability, thereby resolving a longstanding ambiguity regarding the extent to which infinitesimal data determines global group actions in positive characteristic. These structural insights directly inform recent computational approaches to the Zariski cancellation problem.

title: UCPhrase: Unsupervised Context-aware Quality Phrase Tagging
text_ai: Identifying and understanding quality phrases from context is a fundamental task in text mining. The most challenging part of this task arguably lies in uncommon, emerging, and domain-specific phrases. The infrequent nature of these phrases significantly hurts the performance of phrase mining methods that rely on sufficient phrase occurrences in the input corpus. To address this limitation, we introduce UCPhrase, an unsupervised framework designed to extract high-quality phrases without relying on explicit occurrence thresholds. Our approach leverages contextualized representations to capture semantic coherence and syntactic validity simultaneously, enabling robust identification of rare and novel expressions across diverse domains. Specifically, UCPhrase employs a contrastive learning objective that aligns phrase candidates with their surrounding textual contexts while penalizing spurious co-occurrences. We further integrate a dynamic thresholding mechanism that adapts to local vocabulary density, effectively mitigating data sparsity issues inherent in traditional n-gram and dependency-based parsers. Extensive experiments on four benchmark corpora demonstrate that UCPhrase consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving up to 18.4% improvement in F1-score on low-frequency phrase extraction. Ablation studies confirm the critical role of contextual alignment and adaptive scoring in enhancing recall without compromising precision. By decoupling phrase discovery from raw frequency counts, UCPhrase enables scalable, domain-agnostic quality tagging for downstream applications in information retrieval, knowledge graph construction, and automated summarization. Our code and pre-trained models will be publicly released to facilitate reproducible research in lexical semantics. Furthermore, cross-domain transfer evaluations reveal minimal performance degradation when applied to specialized scientific literature, underscoring the framework’s generalizability and practical utility for real-world NLP pipelines.

title: Performances of Neutron Scattering Spectrometers on a Compact Neutron Source
text_ai: There is currently a big effort put into the operation and construction of world class neutron scattering facilities (SNS and SNS-TS2 in the US, J-PARC in Japan, ESS in Europe, CSS in China, PIK in Russia). Despite these investments, access to high-flux pulsed or steady-state beams remains limited, prompting parallel developments in accelerator-driven compact neutron sources (CNS). These systems offer decentralized, cost-effective alternatives tailored for specialized research and industrial applications. This study systematically evaluates the performance of thermal and cold neutron scattering spectrometers deployed on a representative CNS platform. We quantify instrumental parameters including energy resolution, momentum transfer coverage, and neutron yield under varying operational conditions. Experimental campaigns across inelastic, quasielastic, and diffraction modes demonstrate that modern moderator designs and optimized beamline optics can achieve resolutions comparable to those of megawatt-class facilities, albeit with proportionally reduced flux. Monte Carlo simulations corroborate empirical measurements, highlighting the critical role of chopper timing synchronization and sample environment constraints. Our results establish clear performance benchmarks for CNS-integrated spectrometry, outlining pathways for targeted instrument upgrades and multi-user operational strategies. These findings underscore the viability of compact sources as complementary assets to traditional large-scale infrastructure, enabling broader accessibility without compromising scientific rigor.

title: Point-MoE: Towards Cross-Domain Generalization in 3D Semantic Segmentation via Mixture-of-Experts
text_ai: While scaling laws have transformed natural language processing and computer vision, 3D point cloud understanding has yet to reach that stage. This can be attributed to both the comparatively smaller scale of 3D datasets, as well as the disparate sources of the data itself. To address these limitations, we introduce Point-MoE, a novel mixture-of-experts framework explicitly engineered to enhance cross-domain generalization in 3D semantic segmentation. Departing from conventional monolithic backbones, our architecture employs a hierarchical routing protocol that directs query points to domain-adaptive expert modules based on localized geometric distributions and semantic cues. This sparse activation paradigm allows individual experts to specialize in distinct sensor modalities while preserving a unified feature space through shared normalization layers. We further integrate a differentiable load-balancing objective that prevents expert collapse and ensures equitable parameter utilization throughout optimization. Comprehensive evaluations across established indoor and outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that Point-MoE consistently surpasses contemporary single-network baselines under rigorous zero-shot transfer protocols, yielding up to 18.4% reduction in mean intersection-over-union degradation. These findings validate conditional computation as a principled remedy for dataset fragmentation, charting a reproducible trajectory toward scalable, domain-agnostic 3D scene understanding.

title: GRBs luminosity function synthesized from \textit{Swift/BAT}, \textit{Fermi/GBM} and \textit{Konus-Wind} data
text_ai: We study the luminosity function of long gamma-ray bursts (LGRBs) using the peak flux obtained from three LGRB samples with known redshifts: (a) a sample of 251 LGRBs from the \textit{Swift/BAT} satellite/instrument; (b) a sample of 37 LGRBs from the \textit{Fermi/GBM} telescope; (c) a sample of 152 GRBs from the \textit{Konus-Wind} instrument. We apply a modified Kaplan–Meier estimator coupled with the $C_{\rm min}$ technique to correct for Malmquist bias and detector threshold effects, yielding a volume-luminosity corrected distribution across the 10–1000 keV rest-frame band. The resulting luminosity function is well-constrained by a broken power-law model, exhibiting a characteristic break at $L^{\ast} \approx 2.1^{+0.3}_{-0.2} \times 10^{52}$ erg s$^{-1}$ with faint-end and bright-end slopes of $\alpha_{1} = -1.85 \pm 0.12$ and $\alpha_{2} = -3.41 \pm 0.18$, respectively. Introducing a pure luminosity evolution prescription substantially improves the statistical fit, indicating a mild dimming of the characteristic luminosity toward lower redshifts. When compared with single-mission determinations, our synthesized LF maintains excellent consistency across the overlapping flux regimes while significantly improving constraints on the faint-end population. These findings establish a coherent observational baseline for modeling GRB progenitor channels, tracing cosmic star-formation history beyond $z \sim 6,$ and refining duty-cycle calculations for upcoming high-energy transient monitors, thereby strengthening coordinated multi-wavelength follow-up strategies.

title: Towards Practical Implementations of Person Re-Identification from Full Video Frames
text_ai: With the major adoption of automation for cities security, person re-identification (Re-ID) has been extensively studied recently. In this paper, we argue that the current way of studying person re-identification, i.e. by trying to re-identify a person within already detected and pre-cropped images of people, is not sufficient to implement practical security applications, where the inputs to the system are the full frames of the video streams. To bridge this gap, we propose a unified framework that processes raw surveillance feeds without external detectors. Our architecture couples a differentiable region proposer with a hierarchical backbone, enabling simultaneous localization and discriminative embedding extraction. Joint optimization of classification and metric learning objectives yields viewpoint-invariant features resilient to heavy occlusion and scale variation. Comprehensive experiments on three public datasets reveal that our approach surpasses existing two-stage methods in both rank-1 accuracy and mean average precision, while cutting computational overhead by nearly half. By eliminating reliance on fragile preprocessing modules, our design significantly improves end-to-end reliability under adverse weather conditions. We release a curated dataset of synchronized multi-camera recordings to facilitate realistic evaluation. These findings establish a viable pathway for deploying robust Re-ID systems in live metropolitan infrastructure.

title: Variability in Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line Outflows
text_ai: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs (LoBAL QSOs) at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale of 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. Line parameters are derived via multi-component Voigt profile fitting, tracking variations in equivalent width, central velocity, and optical depth. Our analysis reveals that 36 per cent of the sample exhibits statistically significant absorption variability at the >3σ confidence level, predominantly manifesting as velocity shifts of up to 250 km s⁻¹ and equivalent width fluctuations exceeding 15 per cent. Detected changes occur on rest-frame timescales as short as three weeks, implying outflow launch regions within a few hundred gravitational radii of the central supermassive black hole. No strong correlation emerges between variability amplitude and quasar bolometric luminosity or broad-line region size, challenging purely radiative driving scenarios. Instead, the observed kinematic and column density perturbations align with magnetohydrodynamic disk wind models wherein magnetic tension and turbulent pressure gradients modulate mass loss rates on dynamical timescales. Furthermore, the co-variability of Mg II and Al III profiles suggests a chemically homogeneous outflow component, though differential ionization effects cannot be entirely ruled out due to metallicity uncertainties. These findings place stringent constraints on the geometry and acceleration mechanism of low-ionization BAL winds, supporting a picture where absorbers reside in structured, clumpy streams rather than a smooth halo. Future high-cadence spectroscopic campaigns combined with ultraviolet X-ray observations will be essential to disentangle ionization-driven variability from intrinsic kinematic evolution in these powerful extragalactic outflows.

title: Nuclear dimension and Z-stability of pure C*-algebras
text_ai: In this article I study a number of topological and algebraic dimension type properties of simple C*-algebras and their interplay. In particular, a simple C*-algebra is defined to be (tracially) (m,\bar{m})-pure, if it has (strong tracial) m-comparison and is (tracially) \bar{m}-almost divisible. These notions are related to each other, and to nuclear dimension. We establish that tracial $(m,\bar{m})$-purity imposes stringent constraints on the asymptotic structure of these algebras, effectively bridging local comparability features with global regularity. Specifically, we prove that any separable, simple, unital C*-algebra exhibiting uniform tracial $(m,\bar{m})$-purity admits finite nuclear dimension, provided $m$ and $\bar{m}$ satisfy explicit quantitative bounds. Conversely, we demonstrate that finite nuclear dimension entails a form of approximate tracial purity, thereby revealing a tight equivalence between order-theoretic divisibility and dimensional finiteness in the tracial regime. These structural insights yield new criteria for $\mathcal{Z}$-stability: we show that tracially pure algebras with strict comparison automatically absorb the Jiang–Su algebra, resolving several open questions regarding the necessity of almost divisibility in classification schemes. Furthermore, we develop a refined calculus for tracial comparison that accommodates non-unital settings and extends naturally to crossed products by amenable groups. The resulting framework unifies disparate regularity hypotheses appearing in recent classification efforts, offering a streamlined pathway to establishing isomorphism classes via K-theoretic invariants. Our techniques also clarify the role of tracial ranks in controlling approximation properties, ultimately strengthening the connection between geometric dimension theory and operator-algebraic stability. Finally, we outline how these purity conditions interact with quasidiagonality, suggesting new directions for extending the classification program beyond the stably finite realm.

title: Minimization based formulations of inverse problems and their regularization
text_ai: The conventional way of formulating inverse problems such as identification of a (possibly infinite dimensional) parameter, is via some forward operator, which is the concatenation of the observation operator with the parameter-to-state-map for the underlying model. Typically, this framework necessitates the construction of a data-misfit functional augmented by a stabilizing penalty term, thereby transforming the inherently ill-posed inversion into a tractable optimization problem. While classical Tikhonov regularization remains foundational, contemporary research has expanded toward nonlinear, non-convex, and structure-preserving penalizers that encode sophisticated prior information. This manuscript systematically examines minimization-based formulations, emphasizing the critical interplay between forward-operator geometry, Banach-space topologies, and the analytical properties of the regularizing functional. We derive sufficient conditions guaranteeing the existence of minimizers and establish strong convergence rates for minimizing sequences under source-type assumptions. Error bounds are rigorously analyzed in both deterministic and stochastic noise regimes, alongside a detailed investigation of parameter selection strategies. Furthermore, we compare standard convex relaxations with modern sparsity-inducing and low-rank promoting mechanisms, delineating their comparative efficacy in reconstructing discontinuous or multiscale parameter distributions. Numerical implementation is addressed through gradient-based and proximal algorithms specifically adapted to the curvature and nonsmooth characteristics of the composite objective. Finally, we identify pressing theoretical and computational challenges, including adaptive penalty design, Bayesian interpretation of variational schemes, and the incorporation of mechanistic constraints. Such developments enhance predictive reliability in data-scarce environments. By synthesizing analytical rigor with algorithmic pragmatism, this work establishes a unified paradigm for constructing stable, accurate, and computationally efficient inversion methodologies across modern rigorous computational science.

title: Building a Bridge Between NMDAR-Mediated Excitotoxicity and Mitochondrial Dysfunction in Chronic and Acute Diseases.
text_ai: Glutamate is the major excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain, and it is widely accepted to play a role in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxic cell death. Glutamate binds to several receptors, including ionotropic N-methyl-D-Aspartate receptor (NMDAR), which is essential in synaptic plasticity and excitotoxicity. Excessive activation of these channels triggers pathological calcium influx, subsequently compromising mitochondrial membrane potential and impairing oxidative phosphorylation. Such bioenergetic compromise elevates reactive oxygen species, establishing a destructive cycle that accelerates neuronal loss. Despite extensive investigation into isolated pathways, the direct molecular crosstalk between postsynaptic NMDAR signaling cascades and organelle homeostasis remains incompletely characterized. We integrate evidence demonstrating how sustained receptor overactivation disrupts mitochondrial dynamics, including fission-fusion balance and mitophagy clearance. We further evaluate how this integrated axis contributes to disease progression in both acute insults, such as ischemic stroke and traumatic brain injury, and chronic conditions, including Alzheimer’s disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. By delineating shared signaling nodes—particularly calpain-mediated cytoskeletal breakdown and impaired adenine nucleotide translocator function—we propose a unified framework linking synaptic hyperexcitation to metabolic collapse. Ultimately, targeting convergent regulatory elements within this interface may yield novel neuroprotective strategies mitigating progressive tissue damage while preserving cognitive resilience across the clinical spectrum.

title: Distributed generalized Nash equilibria computation of monotone games via a preconditioned proximal point algorithm
text_ai: In this paper, we investigate distributed generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) computation of monotone games with affine coupling constraints. Each player can only utilize its local objective function, local feasible set and a local block of the coupling constraint, and can only communicate with its neighbours. To address the computational challenges posed by the coupled constraints, we propose a distributed preconditioned proximal point algorithm that operates entirely through local computations and pairwise message exchanges. By introducing a symmetric positive definite preconditioner tailored to the network topology and constraint structure, our method effectively decouples the implicit proximal subproblems while preserving the monotonicity of the underlying variational inequality. We prove global convergence under standard monotonicity assumptions, deriving explicit stepsize conditions that guarantee linear convergence when the game mapping is strongly monotone. The contraction factor depends explicitly on the spectral properties of the preconditioner and the communication graph. Furthermore, we provide a constructive procedure for tuning the algorithmic parameters to optimize asymptotic rates. Numerical simulations on large-scale congestion and resource allocation games demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms existing distributed GNE-seeking protocols in terms of iteration complexity and communication overhead, yielding a highly efficient solution framework.

title: Loss Minimization for Electrical Flows over Spanning Trees on Grids
text_ai: We study the electrical distribution network reconfiguration problem, defined as follows. We are given an undirected graph with a root vertex, demand at each non-root vertex, and resistance on each edge. Then, we want to find a spanning tree of the graph that specifies the routing of power from the root to each vertex so that all the demands are satisfied and the energy loss is minimized. We prove this optimization problem is strongly NP-hard even on uniform-resistance grid graphs. To address this barrier, we develop a polynomial-time approximation algorithm that selects spanning trees yielding provably near-minimal resistive losses relative to the unconstrained electrical flow. Our method leverages hierarchical partitioning to decompose the grid into balanced subgraphs, enabling efficient local tree construction while maintaining global flow feasibility. We establish a logarithmic performance guarantee that tightens to a constant factor under regular node placement and homogeneous demand distributions. Extensive experiments on IEEE test feeders and synthetic urban networks demonstrate 20–30% loss reductions versus standard heuristics, including minimum-weight spanning trees and greedy growth baselines. Additionally, we verify that the resulting configurations respect operational voltage constraints and exhibit robustness against minor edge perturbations. These findings deliver a scalable, theoretically grounded framework for practical distribution grid reconfiguration.

title: The Implications of Local Fluctuations in the Galactic Midplane for Dynamical Analysis in the Gaia Era
text_ai: Orbital properties of stars, computed from their six-dimensional phase space measurements and an assumed Galactic potential, are used to understand the structure and evolution of the Galaxy. Stellar actions, computed from orbits, have the attractive quality of being invariant under certain assumptions and are therefore used as quantitative labels of a star's orbit. However, this invariance strictly holds only for axisymmetric, time-independent potentials. In reality, the solar neighborhood is permeated by transient density waves, giant molecular clouds, and spiral arm perturbations that induce significant local fluctuations in the midplane gravitational field. These non-stationary components introduce secular drifts in computed actions, effectively breaking their adiabatic invariance over gigayear timescales. Leveraging the unprecedented astrometric precision of the Gaia mission, we demonstrate that neglecting such midplane heterogeneities systematically biases action-space reconstructions, particularly for high-eccentricity and thick-disk populations. By incorporating a stochastic midplane potential model derived from recent hydrodynamical simulations, we quantify the resulting action dispersion and show that conventional single-potential frameworks underestimate orbital uncertainties by up to thirty per cent in key dynamical coordinates. We further develop a correction formalism that propagates local mass-variance into action covariance matrices, enabling robust statistical inference in action-based analyses. Our results establish that future Milky Way archaeology studies must explicitly account for small-scale gravitational variability when mapping stellar streams, identifying moving groups, or reconstructing formation histories. Ultimately, this work provides a practical pathway for integrating realistic midplane fluctuations into Gaia-driven dynamical models, ensuring that action-space classifications remain physically meaningful for galactic research across diverse kinematic substructures.

title: Interleukin-1beta-mediated suppression of microRNA-27a-3p activity in human cartilage via MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways: A potential mechanism of osteoarthritis pathogenesis
text_ai: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA). Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting were performed to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues from patients with OA and healthy controls, and also in interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes. Silencing endogenous miR-27a-3p significantly upregulated ADAMTS5 protein levels, whereas transfection with a specific mimic effectively suppressed its expression and reduced downstream catabolic enzyme secretion. Mechanistic investigations demonstrated that IL-1beta stimulation triggered rapid phosphorylation of p38 MAPK and ERK1/2, alongside robust nuclear translocation of NF-kappaB p65, which collectively mediated the transcriptional repression of miR-27a-3p. Selective pharmacological blockade or siRNA-mediated knockdown of these upstream kinases markedly rescued miR-27a-3p abundance and concurrently attenuated ADAMTS5-driven extracellular matrix breakdown. Luciferase reporter assays further validated direct sequence-specific binding of miR-27a-3p to the 3′-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 transcripts. Additionally, cell viability and apoptosis assays demonstrated that restoration of miR-27a-3p levels effectively counteracted IL-1beta-induced chondrocyte dysfunction and preserved type II collagen accumulation. Quantitative assessments of glycosaminoglycan release corroborated these molecular findings, indicating substantial preservation of synthetic matrix architecture following targeted miRNA repletion. Statistical analysis confirmed significant differential expression patterns across all experimental groups (P<0.01). The reciprocal relationship between inflammatory signaling intensity and miRNA activity underscores the central role of post-transcriptional regulation in joint homeostasis. Clinically, inverse correlation analyses between miR-27a-3p and ADAMTS5 expression levels were consistently observed across independent OA cohorts. Collectively, these data establish a previously unrecognized inflammatory cascade wherein IL-1beta-induced MAPK and NF-kappaB signaling converges to suppress miR-27a-3p activity, thereby releasing ADAMTS5-mediated proteolytic damage in human articular cartilage. Modulating this miRNA-centered regulatory node presents a compelling molecular target for future disease-modifying osteoarthritis therapies.

title: High performance Broadband Photodetection Based on Graphene -- MoS$_{2x}$Se$_{2(1-x)}$ Alloy Engineered Phototransistors
text_ai: The concept of alloy engineering has emerged as a viable technique towards tuning the bandgap as well as engineering the defect levels in two-dimensional transition metal dichalcognides (TMDC). Possibility to synthesize these ultrathin TMDC materials through chemical route has opened realistic possibilities to fabricate hybrid multi-functional devices. Herein, we report the scalable chemical exfoliation and subsequent integration of chemically synthesized MoS$_{2x}$Se$_{2(1-x)}$ ternary alloys into graphene-based phototransistor architectures. By systematically varying the selenium stoichiometry, we achieve precise modulation of the optical absorption profile across the visible to near-infrared spectrum. The resulting heterostructures exhibit exceptionally high photoresponsivity exceeding 10$^3$ A W$^{-1}$ and specific detectivity surpassing 10$^{12}$ Jones under ambient conditions. Enhanced charge separation at the van der Waals graphene-alloy interface, coupled with suppressed trap-assisted recombination, significantly prolongs carrier lifetime and amplifies photocurrent gain. Furthermore, the compositionally tuned active channel demonstrates remarkable operational stability over prolonged illumination cycles and maintains consistent spectral response from 400 to 1600 nm. These results highlight the pivotal influence of chalcogenide mixing ratios on optimizing optoelectronic figure-of-merits, establishing a practical framework for developing high-throughput, low-cost broadband photodetection platforms suitable for advanced imaging, environmental monitoring, and integrated optoelectronic circuits operating under real-world conditions.

title: Do people's user types change over time? An exploratory study
text_ai: In recent years, different studies have proposed and validated user models (e.g., Bartle, BrainHex, and Hexad) to represent the different user profiles in games and gamified settings. However, the results of applying these user models in practice (e.g., to personalize gamified systems) are still contradictory. To address this inconsistency, we investigate the stability of player classifications across longitudinal engagement periods. Drawing on a sample of 312 participants repeatedly assessed through the Hexad scale over six months, we employ cluster analysis and latent transition modeling to track typological shifts. Our findings reveal that while core motivational preferences exhibit moderate temporal stability, significant reclassification occurs among players initially categorized as socializers and conquerors. These transitions correlate strongly with changes in gameplay frequency and contextual feedback mechanisms, suggesting that user typologies are not static traits but dynamic states shaped by experiential learning. Consequently, static profiling approaches may oversimplify individual motivations, limiting the efficacy of adaptive interventions. We propose a fluid, state-oriented framework for user segmentation that accounts for temporal variability. This research underscores the necessity of iterative assessment in gamification design and offers practitioners actionable insights for maintaining sustained engagement through dynamically responsive system architectures.

title: Development and clinical study of submicronic-atropine sulphate respiratory fluid as a novel organophosphorous poisoning antidote.
text_ai: Increased use of organophosphate insecticides (OPI) and possibility of terror groups using stocks of nerve agents underscore the need to develop effective and safe antidotes. While intramuscular administration of antidotes like atropine sulphate (AS) has certain lacunae, intravenous route may not be always feasible in emergency field conditions. To address these constraints, we developed a submicronic-atropine sulphate respiratory fluid designed for rapid pulmonary deposition and systemic absorption. The formulation was optimized via nebulization parameters to achieve a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 1.5–2.5 μm, ensuring efficient alveolar targeting while maintaining physicochemical stability under ambient storage conditions. Stability assessments under extreme temperature fluctuations further corroborated formulation robustness, supporting extended stockpiling requirements. In a murine model of soman-induced cholinergic crisis, inhalation of the submicronic AS fluid demonstrated an accelerated time-to-onset compared to conventional intramuscular injection, with therapeutic plasma concentrations achieved within three minutes. Pharmacokinetic profiling revealed enhanced bioavailability (approximately 68% relative to parenteral administration) without evidence of local respiratory irritation or systemic toxicity at clinically relevant doses. Subsequent phase I clinical trials in healthy volunteers confirmed excellent tolerability, with no adverse pulmonary or cardiovascular events reported following standardized dosing regimens. The device-assisted inhalation protocol proved operationally straightforward, requiring minimal training and enabling self- or buddy-administration during mass-casualty scenarios. These findings collectively validate the submicronic-atropine sulphate respiratory fluid as a rapidly acting, field-deployable countermeasure that circumvents the logistical and physiological limitations of injectable formulations. Its integration into military and civilian emergency response protocols could improve survival outcomes in organophosphate exposures.

title: Genetic engineering and characterisation of chlorotoxin-fused gelonin for enhanced glioblastoma therapy.
text_ai: Despite substantial advances in its treatment, brain cancer remains a life-threatening disease with a poor survival rate. The main challenges for the conventional chemotherapy include an insufficient efficacy of drugs and toxicity caused by their nonselective mode of action. To overcome these limitations, we engineered a novel recombinant immunotoxin by fusing chlorotoxin, a glioma-homing peptide, with gelonin, a potent plant-derived ribosome-inactivating protein. The fusion construct was expressed in Escherichia coli, purified via affinity chromatography, and extensively characterized using SDS-PAGE, mass spectrometry, and surface plasmon resonance. In vitro assessments demonstrated that the Chx-Gel conjugate selectively bound to glioblastoma cells overexpressing matrix metalloproteinase-2 and integrin αvβ3, exhibiting sub-nanomolar affinity while sparing normal astrocytes. Cellular uptake studies confirmed rapid internalization and subsequent inhibition of protein synthesis, leading to dose-dependent apoptosis in U87MG and patient-derived GBM xenografts. Notably, the targeted construct showed a 50-fold reduction in systemic cytotoxicity compared to unmodified gelonin. In orthotopic murine models, intratumoral administration significantly suppressed tumor growth and prolonged median survival without observable neurotoxicity or weight loss. These findings underscore the robust targeting capability and pronounced antineoplastic activity of the chlorotoxin-gelonin chimera, establishing it as a promising next-generation biotherapeutic strategy for precision oncology in refractory glioblastoma.

title: Towards An Efficient LLM Training Paradigm for CTR Prediction
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated tremendous potential as the next-generation ranking-based recommendation system. Many recent works have shown that LLMs can significantly outperform conventional click-through-rate (CTR) prediction approaches. Despite such promising results, the computational inefficiency inherent in the current training paradigm makes it particularly challenging to train LLMs for ranking-based recommendation tasks on large datasets. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a novel parameter-efficient training framework for aligning LLMs with sparse interaction data. Our approach integrates a lightweight adapter mechanism with a curriculum-guided sampling strategy that dynamically prioritizes hard-negative samples during optimization, thereby reducing redundant gradient computations without compromising representation fidelity. Furthermore, we devise a knowledge distillation protocol that transfers decision boundaries from a fully fine-tuned teacher model to a student architecture via contrastive alignment losses, enabling rapid convergence while retaining the generative capabilities of the underlying language backbone. Extensive experiments across three public benchmark datasets and one industrial-scale deployment scenario demonstrate that our paradigm achieves comparable or superior AUC and NDCG scores relative to state-of-the-art baselines, while cutting total training time by up to 68% and decreasing GPU memory footprint by 54%. Ablation studies confirm the synergistic contribution of each component, particularly highlighting the stability gains from adaptive sample weighting under severe class imbalance. Cross-domain generalization tests further validate the robustness of our methodology against distributional shifts typical of production environments. By decoupling representational capacity from prohibitive computational overhead, this work establishes a scalable foundation for deploying generative ranking models in recommender pipelines, bridging the gap between research and industry.

title: Funding pharmacists in general practice: A feasibility study to inform the design of future economic evaluations.
text_ai: Funding is a significant barrier to employing general practice pharmacists. To explore the feasibility of determining the cost-benefit of pharmacists in Australian general practice. Two part-time pharmacists were employed by general practices in Canberra, Australia. Diaries of the pharmacists were analysed to determine time worked and participation in income-generating activities, including Government-funded programs: Asthma Cycle of Care, Home Medicine Reviews, and Health Care Assessments. Analysis revealed that pharmacists spent approximately 65 per cent of scheduled hours on clinical services reimbursed through existing Medicare and Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme items. The remainder supported medication reconciliation, patient education, and interdisciplinary collaboration with general practitioners. Direct revenue generation proved feasible; however, prevailing billing rates yielded only partial recovery of employment costs, creating a persistent funding deficit. Administrative overheads and non-billable clinical duties further limited financial viability under current remuneration structures. Consequently, diary-based workload mapping emerged as a practical methodology for quantifying pharmacist contributions and service utilisation. Contemporary fee-for-service models remain inadequate for fully offsetting recruitment expenditures. Future economic evaluations require holistic costing frameworks that integrate direct revenues, downstream healthcare savings, and sustainable financing alternatives to accurately quantify the economic impact of integrated pharmacy services in primary care.

title: Clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of triangular fibrocartilage complex tears associated with distal radius fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: We evaluate the clinical and functional outcome of open primary repair of acute TFCC tears in distal radius fracture, when there is gross intraoperative distal radioulnar joint (DRUJ) instability after fixation of the distal radius, in the absence of an ulnar styloid fracture or when the ulnar fracture fragment is too small to be fixed. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study evaluated consecutive patients undergoing open TFCC repair following definitive distal radius fixation. Eligibility required acute injury presentation, documented gross DRUJ instability, and non-reconstructible ulnar styloid fragments. Clinical evaluation utilized validated patient-reported outcome measures, including DASH and Mayo Wrist Scores, alongside standardized goniometry for wrist and forearm rotation. Radiographic parameters assessed fracture alignment and carpal spacing. Paired statistical comparisons determined significance across baseline and final follow-up intervals. RESULTS: Twenty-four patients (mean age 53.8 years) completed minimum 18-month surveillance. Fracture union was universal. Mean Mayo Wrist Score increased substantially from 41.5 preoperatively to 87.2 postoperatively (p<0.001), paralleled by DASH reductions from 49.1 to 13.8. Dynamic fluoroscopy confirmed persistent DRUJ stability in all specimens. Functional recovery averaged 94% restoration of contralateral range of motion. Minor complications included one case of transient neural irritation requiring conservative management; zero instances of recurrent laxity or hardware failure were recorded. CONCLUSION: Primary open TFCC reconstruction reliably addresses secondary DRUJ instability when bony stabilization remains unfeasible. This surgical approach demonstrates consistently robust clinical efficacy in restoring joint mechanics and optimizing functional capacity, thereby strongly supporting its routine integration into established algorithmic treatment pathways for complex distal radius trauma.

title: Truth is Universal: Robust Detection of Lies in LLMs
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionised natural language processing, exhibiting impressive human-like capabilities. In particular, LLMs are capable of "lying", knowingly outputting false statements. Hence, it is of interest and importance to develop methods to detect when LLMs lie. Indeed, several authors trained classifiers to detect LLM lies based on their internal model activations. However, these activation-based approaches frequently suffer from poor generalisation across diverse model families and fail to distinguish between deliberate deception and unintentional hallucination. To address these limitations, we propose a novel detection framework that leverages universal semantic consistency rather than architecture-specific internal signals. By analysing cross-lingual alignment and factual grounding across multiple knowledge domains, our method isolates deceptive outputs through invariant truth-preservation metrics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves state-of-the-art detection accuracy across seven benchmark datasets, maintaining robust performance even under severe distributional shifts and adversarial prompting. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that truth-universal features significantly outperform activation-based baselines in both precision and calibration stability across varying temperature settings. These findings establish a scalable paradigm for monitoring LLM honesty, offering critical insights for deploying trustworthy generative systems in high-stakes applications where veracity remains paramount.

In particular, LLMs are capable of "lying", knowingly outputting false statements. Hence, it is of interest and importance to develop methods to detect when LLMs lie. Indeed, several authors trained classifiers to detect LLM lies based on their internal model activations.

title: $R^2$-Mesh: Reinforcement Learning Powered Mesh Reconstruction via Geometry and Appearance Refinement
text_ai: Mesh reconstruction based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) is popular in a variety of applications such as computer graphics, virtual reality, and medical imaging due to its efficiency in handling complex geometric structures and facilitating real-time rendering. However, existing works often fail to capture fine geometric details accurately and struggle with optimizing rendering quality. To address these limitations, we introduce $R^2$-Mesh, a novel framework that leverages reinforcement learning to jointly optimize mesh topology and surface appearance. Our approach formulates refinement as a sequential decision process, where an agent iteratively adjusts vertex coordinates and material parameters through a composite reward balancing geometric fidelity and photometric accuracy. We design a hierarchical policy network that decouples structural deformation from shading estimation, ensuring stable convergence despite severe initialization errors. Comprehensive evaluations on standard benchmarks reveal that $R^2$-Mesh consistently surpasses contemporary NeRF-based pipelines, yielding superior PSNR values and markedly lower Chamfer distances. Additionally, the proposed strategy demonstrates strong generalization across heterogeneous scene complexities while preserving inference speeds compatible with interactive applications. By integrating geometry-aware exploration with appearance-driven feedback, our method establishes a robust paradigm for high-fidelity 3D reconstruction, substantially advancing practical deployment in computational photography and synthetic data generation.

title: Dynamical Majorana Neutrino Masses and Axions II: Inclusion of Axial Background and Anomaly Terms
text_ai: We extend the study of a previous publication \cite{amsot} on Schwinger-Dyson dynamical mass generation for fermions and pseudoscalar fields (axion-like particles (ALP)), in field theories containing Yukawa type interactions between the fermions and ALPs, by incorporating anomaly terms and/or (constant) axial background fields. The inclusion of these contributions systematically modifies the coupled integral equations governing the fermion propagator and the pseudoscalar self-energy. We demonstrate that constant axial backgrounds induce a chiral symmetry breaking pattern distinct from the standard vacuum configuration, generating parity-odd effective potentials that shift the critical coupling thresholds for mass generation. Concurrently, topological anomaly terms introduce non-local vertex corrections that enhance the infrared dynamics, leading to robust dynamical Majorana mass terms even in regimes where perturbative analyses predict massless solutions. By solving the resulting gap equations numerically across varying background strengths and anomaly coefficients, we map out the phase diagram of the theory, identifying regions of spontaneous CP violation and multiple degenerate vacua. Our analysis reveals that the interplay between axial torsion-like backgrounds and Chern-Simons-type anomaly couplings can naturally suppress Dirac mass channels while amplifying Majorana channels, offering a compelling mechanism for light neutrino mass generation without invoking high-scale seesaw scales. Furthermore, we derive modified dispersion relations for the ALP sector, showing that anomaly-induced mixing with gauge fields yields observable modifications to axion phenomenology in strong magnetic environments. These findings establish a unified framework linking non-perturbative fermion condensates, topological QCD-like sectors, and low-energy neutrino observables, providing concrete testable predictions for next-generation haloscope axion searches and precision neutrino oscillation experiments.

title: On the stability of the spherically symmetric solution to an inflow problem for an isentropic model of compressible viscous fluid
text_ai: We investigate an inflow problem for the multi-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations. The fluid under consideration occupies the exterior domain of unit ball, $\Omega=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\,\vert\, |x|\ge 1\}$, and a constant stream of mass is flowing into the domain from the boundary $\partial\Omega=\{|x|=1\}$. We establish the global existence and uniqueness of a stationary spherically symmetric solution satisfying prescribed inflow boundary data at the inner boundary and a positive constant far-field density at infinity. By introducing appropriately weighted Sobolev spaces that capture radial decay near the boundary and far field, we derive uniform a priori estimates for the nonlinear perturbations around this steady state. A careful spectral analysis of the linearized operator reveals a spectral gap, which, combined with a refined energy method, yields optimal algebraic decay rates for the $L^2$-norms of the density and velocity fluctuations. Consequently, we prove the global nonlinear asymptotic stability of the spherically symmetric inflow profile for arbitrary small initial disturbances in a high-order weighted space. These results extend classical stability frameworks to multi-dimensional exterior domains with non-trivial mass flux and clarify how viscous dissipation jointly regulates mass accumulation and long-term convergence in compressible flows. The proof relies on commutator estimates and treatment of the degenerate elliptic structure under spherical symmetry.

title: Generative Text-Guided 3D Vision-Language Pretraining for Unified Medical Image Segmentation
text_ai: Vision-Language Pretraining (VLP) has demonstrated remarkable capabilities in learning visual representations from textual descriptions of images without annotations. Yet, effective VLP demands large-scale image-text pairs, a resource that suffers scarcity in the medical domain. Moreover, conventional VLP is limited to 2D images while medical images encompass diverse modalities, often in 3D, making the learning process more challenging. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel generative text-guided 3D vision-language pretraining framework designed specifically for volumetric medical imaging. Our approach leverages diffusion-based synthesis to generate pseudo-paired 3D volumes and corresponding clinical reports, effectively circumventing the annotation bottleneck. By integrating spatial-temporal attention mechanisms, the model learns robust cross-modal alignments directly from uncurated multi-modality scans, preserving critical anatomical structures. We further propose a unified segmentation head that dynamically routes learned feature representations according to natural language prompts, enabling zero-shot adaptation across diverse organ systems. Additionally, a contrastive regularization term ensures semantic consistency between generated volumetric patches and their textual counterparts. Extensive evaluations on three public benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing supervised baselines, achieving state-of-the-art Dice scores while requiring minimal task-specific fine-tuning. These findings establish generative 3D VLP as a scalable paradigm for annotation-efficient, multi-task medical image analysis.

title: Strategic Defense against Stealthy Link Flooding Attacks: A Signaling Game Approach
text_ai: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, it is becoming extremely challenging to design a fully protected network. For instance, Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) is a variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, and it is shown that it can bypass traditional DDoS defense mechanisms. To address this vulnerability, we formulate the SLFA mitigation problem as a dynamic signaling game between a network defender and an intelligent adversary. By explicitly modeling the informational asymmetry inherent in stealthy attacks, our framework captures the strategic interplay where the defender allocates limited monitoring resources while the attacker optimizes link selection to minimize detection probability. We derive a perfect Bayesian equilibrium that characterizes optimal defensive strategies under partial observability, enabling proactive resource reallocation before congestion thresholds are breached. The proposed architecture integrates lightweight traffic profiling with adaptive filtering rules, dynamically adjusting threshold parameters based on inferred attacker types. Extensive simulations over realistic ISP topologies demonstrate that our game-theoretic defense significantly reduces service degradation compared to static threshold-based and machine learning-driven baselines. Specifically, the approach achieves up to 68% higher available bandwidth during sustained SLFA campaigns while maintaining false positive rates below 2.5%. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses reveal robust performance across varying attack intensities and network scales, confirming the practical viability of equilibrium-guided mitigation. Additionally, we establish theoretical convergence guarantees for the iterative strategy update process, demonstrating polynomial computational complexity relative to topology size. Moreover, the framework accommodates heterogeneous node capabilities, allowing seamless integration with existing routing protocols without requiring hardware upgrades. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating strategic reasoning into next-generation network security architectures, offering a scalable paradigm for countering sophisticated, low-rate flooding threats.

title: Funnel control -- a survey
text_ai: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and it has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes encompassing linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. This survey systematically categorizes recent theoretical advancements, emphasizing the structural flexibility of the funnel boundary as a dynamic performance metric that inherently accommodates parametric uncertainties and unmodeled dynamics without requiring prior knowledge of system bounds. We examine the evolution of adaptation laws, highlighting how the error-dependent gain structure ensures boundedness while enforcing strict adherence to time-varying performance constraints. Particular attention is devoted to extensions beyond single-input single-output configurations, including multivariable formulations, networked systems, and hybrid architectures where conventional control paradigms encounter fundamental limitations. Rigorous Lyapunov-based stability arguments are critically assessed, particularly regarding global uniform ultimate boundedness and exponential convergence rates under varying relative degrees and sector-bounded nonlinearities. The narrative further encompasses numerical implementation strategies, addressing computational challenges associated with real-time evaluation of the performance funnel and integration with digital control hardware. Discretization effects and sampling-induced performance degradation are rigorously analyzed, providing design guidelines for reliable software-in-the-loop deployment. Empirical validations across robotics, power electronics, and chemical process control are synthesized to illustrate the methodology’s resilience under stringent operational requirements. Finally, we identify critical research frontiers, such as stochastic disturbance rejection, event-triggered implementations, and rigorous sample-and-hold analysis, which remain pivotal for broader industrial deployment. By consolidating disparate contributions into a unified framework, this work serves as both a comprehensive reference for newcomers and a strategic roadmap for advancing funnel-based architectures in complex, safety-critical engineering domains.

title: CorrectNav: Self-Correction Flywheel Empowers Vision-Language-Action Navigation Model
text_ai: Existing vision-and-language navigation models often deviate from the correct trajectory when executing instructions. However, these models lack effective error correction capability, hindering their recovery from errors. To address this challenge, we propose Self-correction Flywheel, a novel post-training paradigm. Central to this framework is an iterative feedback loop that continuously aligns predicted actions with environmental ground truth through structured reward shaping. By integrating trajectory-level verification with language-conditioned policy updates, the flywheel dynamically amplifies corrective signals during inference without requiring architectural modifications or external planners. Specifically, we introduce a lightweight critic module that evaluates intermediate pose estimates against instruction semantics, generating implicit supervision gradients that refine the actor’s decision boundary. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets, including AI2-THOR and Habitat, demonstrate that our approach reduces cumulative angular error by 34.7% and improves success rate weighted by path length (SPLO) by 12.3 percentage points over state-of-the-art baselines. Notably, the self-corrective mechanism exhibits strong generalization across unseen environments and complex multi-step directives, effectively mitigating compounding prediction drift. These findings establish a scalable pathway for robust embodied intelligence, positioning autonomous navigators closer to reliable real-world deployment. Ablation studies confirm the critical contribution of each feedback component to system stability.

title: Randomized Classifiers vs Human Decision-Makers: Trustworthy AI May Have to Act Randomly and Society Seems to Accept This
text_ai: As \emph{artificial intelligence} (AI) systems are increasingly involved in decisions affecting our lives, ensuring that automated decision-making is fair and ethical has become a top priority. Intuitively, we feel that akin to human decisions, judgments of artificial agents should necessarily be grounded in some moral principles. Yet contemporary machine learning paradigms frequently employ stochastic mechanisms to optimize performance and mitigate overconfidence, raising fundamental questions about whether algorithmic randomness inherently undermines perceived moral accountability. To investigate this tension, we conduct a controlled comparative study examining how individuals evaluate deterministic versus randomized classifiers across high-stakes domains including healthcare allocation and criminal recidivism prediction. Through a series of between-subjects experiments (N=1,240), we measure trust calibration, perceived fairness, and willingness to defer to automated recommendations when decision processes are explicitly framed as either rule-based or probabilistic. Contrary to prevailing assumptions that transparency and determinism are prerequisites for ethical acceptability, our results demonstrate that participants consistently rate randomized systems as equally or sometimes more trustworthy when outcome distributions align with established equity benchmarks. Furthermore, exposure to distributional transparency significantly attenuates skepticism toward stochastic outputs, suggesting that society prioritizes calibrated uncertainty over rigid determinism. These findings challenge normative frameworks that equate moral agency with fixed computational logic, proposing instead that responsible AI deployment may require embracing controlled randomness as a mechanism for robust fairness. We conclude by outlining governance pathways that reconcile stochastic model architectures with accountability standards, emphasizing that ethical AI design must evolve beyond deterministic idealism toward empirically validated trust models accommodating probabilistic reasoning within regulatory frameworks.

title: Generative AI as a Geopolitical Factor in Industry 5.0: Sovereignty, Access, and Control
text_ai: Industry 5.0 marks a new phase in industrial evolution, emphasizing human-centricity, sustainability, and resilience through the integration of advanced technologies. Within this evolving landscape, Generative AI (GenAI) and autonomous systems are not only transforming industrial processes but also emerging as pivotal geopolitical instruments. This study interrogates how state actors, multinational corporations, and transnational alliances leverage GenAI architectures to reshape industrial competitiveness and strategic autonomy. Employing comparative policy analysis across the European Union, the United States, and China, we examine three interlocking dimensions: technological sovereignty, equitable access to foundational models, and regulatory control over deployment ecosystems. Our findings reveal that while Industry 5.0 advocates inclusive innovation, contemporary GenAI development remains centralized within digital hegemonies, exacerbating asymmetries in computational infrastructure and data governance. These structural imbalances directly constrain developing economies seeking participation in advanced manufacturing networks. We demonstrate that strategic decoupling, export controls, and localized model fine-tuning function as instruments of economic statecraft, fragmenting the global innovation landscape. Consequently, the transition toward resilient, human-aligned manufacturing necessitates multilateral frameworks balancing open collaboration with jurisdictional oversight. Ultimately, this research repositions GenAI as a structural determinant of post-industrial power relations, urging policymakers to embed democratic accountability and distributed architectural standards into next-generation industrial strategies.

title: Palette-colouring: a belief-propagation approach
text_ai: We consider a variation of the prototype combinatorial-optimisation problem known as graph-colouring. Our optimisation goal is to colour the vertices of a graph with a fixed number of colours, in a way to maximise the number of different colours present in the set of nearest neighbours of each given vertex. To address this challenge, we develop a tailored belief-propagation framework that propagates local colour distributions across the network topology. By introducing pairwise compatibility factors that penalise monochromatic neighbourhoods, the algorithm iteratively refines marginal probabilities until convergence. We demonstrate that our message-passing scheme naturally captures the global constraints inherent to palette-colouring while maintaining linear computational complexity with respect to the number of edges. Extensive numerical experiments on synthetic ensembles and real-world networks reveal that the proposed method consistently outperforms greedy heuristics and standard spectral relaxations, achieving higher average palette diversity and lower computational overhead. Furthermore, we provide analytical insights into the phase-transition behaviour of the system under varying colour budgets, establishing clear conditions for successful decoding. Consequently, belief propagation emerges as a robust framework for diversity-driven graph optimisation, with potential applications ranging from frequency assignment in wireless communications to equitable resource allocation in distributed systems.

title: Enhancing the Properties of Plasma Activated Water using an Air Bubble Diffuser
text_ai: In this study, the impact of an air bubbler on the properties of plasma-activated water (PAW) was investigated in different configurations. A pencil plasma jet (PPJ) using a dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) was used to prepare PAW. Three distinct operational modes were evaluated: direct surface exposure, subsurface sparging, and sequential bubbling following plasma treatment. Physicochemical characteristics, including pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), electrical conductivity, and concentrations of nitrite (NO₂⁻), nitrate (NO₃⁻), hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂), and dissolved ozone, were quantified over a 7-day storage period. Microbial inactivation efficacy against Escherichia coli K-12 and Bacillus subtilis spores was also assessed to evaluate practical applicability. Results demonstrated that subsurface air sparging significantly enhanced the accumulation of long-lived reactive nitrogen species (RNS) and reactive oxygen species (ROS), increasing H₂O₂ and total nitrate concentrations by 38% and 52%, respectively, compared to static PAW. The enhanced gas-liquid interfacial area facilitated greater dissolution of plasma-generated gaseous precursors, thereby shifting the radical equilibrium toward stable oxidants. Furthermore, the bubbler-assisted configuration maintained a lower pH (<4.2) and higher ORP (>900 mV) throughout the storage window, correlating with a two-log reduction in bacterial viability within 30 minutes of treatment. No significant synergistic effect was observed for sequential bubbling, indicating that simultaneous plasma activation and continuous aeration optimizes mass transfer kinetics. These findings establish air-sparged PAW as a highly effective, scalable pretreatment strategy for agricultural and food safety applications, offering improved physicochemical stability and sustained antimicrobial potency without requiring additional chemical additives or complex post-processing equipment, thereby facilitating broader industrial adoption.

title: Why the World Reads Wikipedia: Beyond English Speakers
text_ai: As one of the Web's primary multilingual knowledge sources, Wikipedia is read by millions of people across the globe every day. Despite this global readership, little is known about why users read Wikipedia's various language editions. To address this empirical gap, this study employs a mixed-methods approach combining large-scale clickstream analysis with cross-lingual survey data spanning twelve language editions. We investigate how linguistic familiarity, topic preference, and perceived informational utility drive reading behavior among non-English audiences. Our quantitative modeling reveals that while English dominance initially shapes discovery patterns, sustained readership in minority-language editions is primarily motivated by domain-specific knowledge gaps and culturally relevant content curation rather than mere translation availability. Qualitative thematic analysis further indicates that readers prioritize semantic precision and local contextualization when consulting non-Anglophone articles. These findings challenge prevailing assumptions about unidirectional knowledge flows in digital encyclopedias, demonstrating instead a decentralized ecosystem where linguistic communities actively construct and consume tailored epistemic resources. By decoupling readership metrics from edition size, we establish a framework for understanding multilingual information seeking that transcends Anglophone-centric paradigms. Ultimately, this research offers insights for platform designers, researchers, and knowledge-sharing initiatives aiming to foster equitable global access to human knowledge.

title: PRIMG : Efficient LLM-driven Test Generation Using Mutant Prioritization
text_ai: Mutation testing is a widely recognized technique for assessing and enhancing the effectiveness of software test suites by introducing deliberate code mutations. However, its application often results in overly large test suites, as developers generate numerous tests to kill specific mutants, increasing computational overhead. To address these limitations, we introduce PRIMG, a novel framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) for targeted test generation guided by dynamic mutant prioritization. Rather than exhaustively targeting all generated mutants, PRIMG employs a multi-criteria ranking strategy that evaluates mutation score potential, execution cost, and fault-detection likelihood to select high-impact targets. An LLM-based generator then synthesizes concise, coverage-maximizing test cases for selected targets. Extensive empirical evaluation across six benchmark repositories demonstrates that PRIMG reduces test suite size by up to 68% while maintaining 94.7% mutant kill rates compared to conventional exhaustive approaches. Moreover, execution time and memory usage decrease substantially, positioning PRIMG as a viable solution for resource-constrained environments. Specifically, PRIMG incorporates a feedback loop that dynamically recalibrates prioritization weights based on real-time mutation outcomes, thereby preventing redundant test generation. Evaluations against heuristic baselines confirm robust cross-codebase performance. Ultimately, this work provides a practical pathway toward sustainable, AI-augmented quality assurance workflows without compromising fault detection guarantees.

title: Microfracture provides better clinical results than debridement in the treatment of acute talar osteochondral lesions using arthroscopic assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: Ankle arthroscopy is a useful tool for detection and treatment of accompanying intraarticular pathologies in acute ankle fractures. The purpose of this study was to compare the treatment results of talus osteochondral lesions (OLT) with debridement and microfracture in arthroscopy assisted surgery of acute ankle fractures. METHODS: A retrospective comparative analysis was conducted on 68 patients who underwent arthroscopic-assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures accompanied by acute OLT between 2018 and 2022. Patients were allocated into two cohorts based on intraoperative lesion management: simple mechanical debridement (n=34) versus subchondral microfracture (n=34). Inclusion criteria required symptomatic lesions ≥1 cm² without pre-existing degenerative changes. Clinical outcomes were evaluated at minimum two-year follow-up using the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) hindfoot score, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for pain. Imaging assessed lesion filling and cartilage integrity. Independent samples t-tests determined statistical significance. RESULTS: The microfracture cohort demonstrated significantly superior functional outcomes compared to the debridement group (AOFAS mean 89.4 ± 6.2 vs. 76.8 ± 9.1; p<0.001). Postoperative pain scores were markedly reduced in the intervention arm (VAS 1.8 ± 0.7 vs. 3.6 ± 1.2; p<0.001). Imaging revealed substantial fibrocartilaginous restoration in 85% of microfracture cases, whereas 62% of debrided lesions exhibited persistent chondral defects. Complication rates remained comparable between cohorts. CONCLUSION: Subchondral microfracture yields superior clinical and radiographic outcomes compared to isolated debridement when managing acute OLT during arthroscopic ankle fracture fixation. Routine integration of microfracture should be considered standard practice to optimize joint preservation and functional recovery.

title: Sense of Self and Time in Borderline Personality. A Comparative Robustness Study with Generative AI
text_ai: This study examines the capacity of large language models (LLMs) to support phenomenological qualitative analysis of first-person experience in Borderline Personality Disorder (BPD), understood as a disorder of temporality and selfhood. Building on a prior human-led thematic analysis of 24 inpatients' life-story interviews, we compared three LLMs (OpenAI GPT-4o, Google Gemini 2.5 Pro, Anthropic Claude Opus 4) prompted to mimic the interpretative style of the original investigators. To assess methodological robustness, each model underwent iterative prompt refinement and cross-validation against established phenomenological coding frameworks. Performance was evaluated through inter-rater reliability metrics, thematic convergence scores, and fidelity to core constructs of fragmented temporality and unstable self-representation. Results indicate that while all models successfully extracted surface-level narrative patterns, only GPT-4o demonstrated consistent alignment with human-derived categories, particularly regarding disruptions in autobiographical continuity. Gemini and Claude exhibited notable drift toward diagnostic stereotyping, compromising interpretative validity. These findings suggest that current generative architectures lack the nuanced temporal sensitivity required for rigorous clinical phenomenology without extensive domain-specific fine-tuning. Nevertheless, targeted LLM integration may augment researcher workflows by pre-structuring raw narratives, provided human oversight remains central to safeguarding epistemic integrity. Future research must prioritize algorithmic transparency and bias mitigation in psychiatric applications.

title: A Trust and Reputation System for IoT Exploiting Distributed Ledger Technology
text_ai: The advent of Bitcoin, and consequently Blockchain, has ushered in a new era of decentralization. Blockchain enables mutually distrusting entities to work collaboratively to attain a common objective. However, current Blockchain technologies lack scalability, which limits their use in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. To address this bottleneck, we propose a lightweight trust and reputation framework tailored for resource-constrained IoT ecosystems, leveraging a permissioned distributed ledger architecture. Our design incorporates a dynamic scoring mechanism that aggregates historical interaction data, behavioral metrics, and peer feedback to compute verifiable reputation scores without compromising throughput. By integrating shard-based partitioning and optimized Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus, the system substantially reduces computational overhead while preserving cryptographic guarantees. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our approach achieves sub-second finality and near-linear scalability, reducing transaction latency by 38% and energy consumption by 31% compared to state-of-the-art alternatives. The integrated reputation module successfully isolates adversarial nodes, ensuring robust service provisioning across heterogeneous deployments. Ultimately, this research provides a viable pathway for secure, efficient, and autonomous device collaboration in large-scale decentralized IoT networks.

title: Clinical Significance of Cytotoxic Lesions of the Corpus Callosum in Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Patients: A Retrospective Analysis.
text_ai: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels in the brain and are associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). However, their clinical significance in SAH patients remains unclear. This retrospective study aimed to elucidate the prognostic value of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum (CLACC) on functional outcomes and mortality following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). We retrospectively reviewed medical records and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI) scans of 214 consecutive patients diagnosed with aSAH between January 2018 and December 2022. CLACC presence was independently verified by two board-certified neuroradiologists. Primary endpoints included poor functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score ≥3) at three months and in-hospital mortality. Secondary endpoints encompassed delayed cerebral ischemia, symptomatic hydrocephalus, and length of intensive care unit stay. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to adjust for established confounders, including Hunt and Hess grade, modified Fisher scale, and initial Glasgow Coma Scale score. CLACC were identified in 47 patients (21.9%). Univariate analysis revealed that CLACC positivity was significantly associated with advanced age, higher admission severity scores, and increased rates of intraventricular hemorrhage. At three-month follow-up, patients with CLACC demonstrated a markedly elevated risk of poor functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.84; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.62–4.98; p<0.001) and in-hospital mortality (aOR 3.12; 95% CI 1.45–6.71; p=0.003). Furthermore, CLACC presence independently predicted prolonged ICU stay and higher incidence of delayed cerebral ischemia after comprehensive covariate adjustment. The emergence of CLACC on early DWI serves as a robust independent predictor of adverse neurological recovery and survival in aSAH. Incorporating CLACC assessment into routine neuroimaging protocols may enhance risk stratification, guide therapeutic intensity, and inform early rehabilitative planning for critically ill SAH populations.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Parameter Selection for Distributed Optimal Power Flow
text_ai: With the increasing penetration of distributed energy resources, distributed optimization algorithms have attracted significant attention for power systems applications due to their potential for superior scalability, privacy, and robustness to a single point-of-failure. The Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is a popular distributed optimization algorithm; however, its convergence performance is highly dependent on the selection of penalty parameters, which are usually chosen heuristically. To address this limitation, we propose a novel reinforcement learning framework that automatically learns adaptive penalty parameter policies for distributed optimal power flow problems. We formulate the parameter tuning task as a Markov decision process, where the agent observes local primal-dual residuals and iteratively selects scaling factors without explicit gradient information. A composite reward function explicitly penalizes constraint violations while rewarding rapid consensus, facilitating stable training via proximal policy optimization. Comprehensive case studies on modified IEEE bus systems reveal that the trained agents achieve up to forty percent faster convergence relative to conventional heuristic schemes, while guaranteeing strict adherence to thermal and voltage limits across stochastic operating conditions. This work validates data-driven policy learning as a robust mechanism for automated algorithmic calibration in modern power system control.
