title: H-EYE: Holistic Resource Modeling and Management for Diversely Scaled Edge-Cloud Systems
text_ai: Computing systems have been evolving to be more pervasive, heterogeneous, and dynamic. An increasing number of emerging domains now rely on diverse edge to cloud continuum where the execution of applications often spans various tiers of systems with significantly heterogeneous computational capabilities. Resources in each tier are often handled in isolation due to scalability and privacy concerns. To address these siloed management paradigms, we introduce H-EYE, a novel framework that unifies resource provisioning across the entire edge-to-cloud spectrum through a unified abstraction layer. H-EYE employs a graph-based holistic resource model that captures multi-dimensional constraints—including compute, memory, latency, and energy—while explicitly preserving data locality and jurisdictional boundaries. By leveraging a hierarchical reinforcement learning agent, our approach dynamically orchestrates workload placement and scaling policies according to real-time system states and application QoS requirements. The model seamlessly integrates hardware heterogeneity with software-defined networking topologies, enabling fine-grained control over cross-tier traffic routing and elastic capacity allocation. We evaluate H-EYE against state-of-the-art distributed schedulers using realistic trace-driven simulations and physical testbed deployments spanning micro-data centers, regional edge nodes, and public cloud instances. Experimental results demonstrate that H-EYE reduces end-to-end task completion latency by up to 34%, improves aggregate resource utilization efficiency by 28%, and maintains strict privacy guarantees without compromising orchestration agility. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses reveal robust performance degradation resilience under volatile network conditions and sudden workload surges. These findings underscore the viability of unified semantic modeling as a foundational enabler for next-generation heterogeneous infrastructures, establishing a highly scalable paradigm for policy-aware deployment in increasingly complex cyber-physical ecosystems.

title: The 2018 classification of periodontal diseases: Its predictive value for tooth loss.
text_ai: Predictive models and assessment tools for disease susceptibility and progression are necessary to enhance personalized medicine. The aim of this study is to assess the predictive accuracy of using the 2018 classification to predict likelihood of tooth loss. A total of 134 patients were screened 10 years after periodontal therapy. Clinical records and radiographic data were retrospectively reviewed to assign each patient to the revised staging and grading categories. Tooth loss events were recorded and analyzed using Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards regression models to evaluate the association between classification parameters and long-term prognosis. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. The cohort demonstrated a mean follow-up duration of 10.2 ± 0.8 years, during which 47 teeth were extracted due to periodontal failure. Advanced stage (III/IV) and grade C classifications independently predicted significantly higher rates of tooth loss compared to stage I/II or grade A/B cohorts (hazard ratio 3.41, 95% CI 2.12–5.48; p < 0.001). The combined staging-grading model yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.78, indicating moderate-to-good discriminatory power. These findings validate the clinical utility of the 2018 framework in risk stratification, supporting its integration into prognostic counseling and treatment planning.

title: Negotiating access to the Nigerian healthcare system: the experiences of HIV-positive men who have sex with men.
text_ai: Men who have sex with men in sub-Saharan Africa continue to have a disproportionately higher burden of HIV than their counterparts in the general population. In this qualitative study, barriers to participants accessing healthcare services in Nigeria, a country where same-sex relationships are criminalised and considered societally abhorrent, were explored. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with twenty-four HIV-positive men who have sex with men recruited through community-based organisations across three Nigerian states. Thematic analysis revealed that healthcare access was severely constrained by intersecting structural, interpersonal, and intrapersonal barriers. Participants consistently reported fear of disclosure due to punitive legislation, fostering profound mistrust of clinical environments. Stigmatising attitudes among providers further deterred engagement, manifesting as refusal of care, verbal abuse, and confidentiality breaches. Additionally, out-of-pocket costs and limited clinic availability compounded financial and logistical burdens. Consequently, many delayed treatment initiation until advanced disease stages. These findings demonstrate how legal persecution and systemic homophobia construct hostile health ecosystems that actively exclude key populations. Mitigating these barriers necessitates comprehensive policy reform, targeted provider training, and the integration of confidential, rights-based HIV services into primary care frameworks to guarantee equitable health outcomes for marginalised communities.

title: Fractal Profit Landscape of the Stock Market
text_ai: We investigate the structure of the profit landscape obtained from the most basic, fluctuation based, trading strategy applied for the daily stock price data. The strategy is parameterized by only two variables, p and q. Stocks are sold and bought if the log return is bigger than p and less than -q, respectively. Empirical analysis across multiple equity indices reveals that the resulting profit surface exhibits robust scale-invariant properties characteristic of fractal geometries. Systematically varying p and q across logarithmic intervals demonstrates that optimal trading thresholds follow power-law distributions, with Hurst exponents indicating persistent memory effects in both bull and bear regimes. The landscape’s self-similar topology implies that profitable configurations repeat across time horizons, suggesting threshold-based rules capture market inefficiencies. Topological mapping identifies narrow ridges of maximal expected returns surrounded by plateaus of negligible performance, highlighting the sensitivity of stochastic trading outcomes to parametric shifts. These findings underscore the geometric complexity of financial profitability and provide a framework for designing multi-scale algorithms that exploit recurring structural patterns in market dynamics.

title: Binary black holes and tori in AGN I. Ejection of stars and merging of the binary
text_ai: Most galaxies have central massive black holes (BH), and merge with others during their evolution, as strongly suggested by recent observations. Consequently a black hole binary (BHB) emerges. Considering the evolution of the binary when it has become hard, at a separation of the BHs of about 1 pc, we propose to solve two basic questions in our understanding of the central activity of galaxies: (1) Do the BHs actually merge? (2) Can the surrounding nuclear star cluster and ambient accretion flow facilitate final coalescence within a Hubble time? To address these questions, we implement high-resolution N-body simulations coupled with a self-consistent treatment of stellar scattering and weak gravitational wave emission. Three-body interactions with field stars efficiently extract orbital angular momentum, driving the system into the gravitational radiation dominated regime without requiring fine-tuned initial configurations. Concurrently, we model the dynamical coupling between the binary and a geometrically thick, turbulent molecular torus. Resulting hydrodynamical torques accelerate orbital decay while simultaneously perturbing the local stellar distribution, yielding distinct kinematic signatures and enhanced mass ejection. Our calculations indicate that a substantial fraction of hard binaries successfully merge, with characteristic delay times spanning several hundred megayears. Furthermore, hypervelocity star expulsion carves a measurable deficit in the central density cusp, potentially accounting for suppressed accretion rates in certain low-luminosity active galactic nuclei. In summary, our numerical experiments establish a robust physical framework linking binary hardening, stellar feedback, and torus structure, delivering concrete observational predictions for upcoming space-based gravitational wave detectors and very-long-baseline interferometry arrays across diverse galactic environments.

title: Broad-band spectral study of LMXB black hole candidate 4U 1957+11 with NuSTAR
text_ai: We present here the results of broadband spectral analysis of low-mass X-ray binary and a black hole candidate 4U 1957+11. The source was observed nine times with the Nuclear Spectroscopic Telescope Array (NuSTAR) between 2018 September and 2019 November. During these observations, the spectral state of 4U 1957+11 evolved marginally. Multi-epoch spectral fitting employing a thermal Comptonization model coupled with a relativistic reflection component reveals that the hard X-ray emission remains dominated by a non-thermal continuum with a photon index of Γ ≈ 1.6–1.8 and a high-energy cutoff near 30–40 keV. Disk temperature shows a weak inverse luminosity correlation, while normalization indicates a stable accretion disk extending near the ISCO. No significant variations in the reflection fraction or ionization parameter were detected, indicating a persistent, geometrically thick corona throughout the monitoring campaign. These results confirm that 4U 1957+11 remained in a stable intermediate state at a steady accretion rate. The absence of pronounced spectral evolution supports a scenario where steady Comptonization maintains the high-energy tail without triggering distinct state transitions. Our findings place tight constraints on the coronal geometry, yielding critical insights into black hole binary stability during persistent hard states.

title: Visual-perceptual training with motor practice of the observed movement pattern improves anticipation in emerging expert cricket batsmen.
text_ai: This study addressed the paucity of evidence of whether visual anticipation can be improved in emerging experts in striking sports. Twelve emerging expert batsmen from a state cricket squad were equally randomised into intervention and control groups. They were pre-and-post tested on a video temporal occlusion test of a fast bowler, as well as transfer tests of different fast and slow bowlers. The intervention group engaged in a six-week programme combining dynamic visual-perceptual drills with concurrent enactment of the observed batting technique, whereas controls maintained standard training routines. Post-intervention assessments revealed that trained participants demonstrated significantly superior anticipation accuracy across all bowling velocities compared to baseline and control counterparts (p < .05). Notably, transfer performance to unfamiliar delivery types indicated robust generalisation of learned perceptual-cue utilisation. These findings substantiate the efficacy of integrating kinesthetic simulation with targeted visual training to accelerate expertise development in complex interception tasks. Consequently, coaches and sport scientists should prioritise multi-modal training protocols that couple observational learning with embodied execution when designing developmental pathways for striking-sport athletes. Such approaches offer a scalable mechanism for enhancing predictive timing without excessive reliance on repetitive live-ball exposure, thereby optimising long-term technical proficiency and decision-making accuracy within elite sporting environments.

title: Sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of xylazine with and without acepromazine in Nordestino donkeys.
text_ai: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce. To evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous (i.v.) xylazine with and without acepromazine in 'Nordestino' donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Treatments consisted of xylazine alone (0.4 mg kg⁻¹ i.v.; TX) and combined xylazine (0.3 mg kg⁻¹) plus acepromazine (0.03 mg kg⁻¹) administered i.v. (TA). A seven-day washout separated administrations. Sedation quality was assessed via a validated ordinal scale, recording time to sternal recumbency, maintenance duration, and muscle relaxation. Cardiorespiratory parameters, including heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), mean arterial pressure (MAP), peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂), end-tidal CO₂ (EtCO₂), and arterial blood gases, were recorded at baseline and serially up to 120 min post-administration. Statistical analysis employed linear mixed-effects models to account for repeated measures (P < 0.05). Both treatment regimens induced rapid and clinically acceptable sedation within 5 ± 2 min of administration. Time to recumbency was significantly shorter (P = 0.012) in TA, which also exhibited prolonged maintenance (68 ± 14 vs 52 ± 11 min; P = 0.004) compared to TX. HR decreased significantly from baseline in both groups (P < 0.001), with a greater reduction observed in TA (−18 ± 6 bpm) versus TX (−11 ± 4 bpm). Respiratory rate, MAP, SpO₂, and blood gas values remained within physiological limits without intergroup differences. No adverse cardiovascular or respiratory events were recorded. In conclusion, low-dose intravenous xylazine produces reliable sedation in Nordestino donkeys. The addition of acepromazine accelerates onset and prolongs recumbency without inducing clinically relevant cardiorespiratory depression, offering a safe and stable protocol for routine field procedures.

title: The Use of Telemedicine for Penicillin Allergy Skin Testing.
text_ai: Penicillin skin testing (PST) is increasingly used as a tool to evaluate penicillin allergy in patients with a reported history. The limited availability of allergists, however, may be an impeding factor. We sought to assess the clinical utility of telemedicine to facilitate PST. Penicillin-allergic inpatients receiving systemic antibiotics were prospectively identified between April and August 2017. A board-certified allergist conducted remote consultations via secure video conferencing while local hospital staff performed standardized skin prick and intradermal testing. Patients underwent evaluation using benzylpenicillin G, ampicillin, and penicilloyl polylysine. Primary outcomes encompassed procedural completion rates, concordance with historical allergy documentation, and subsequent antimicrobial selection. Secondary endpoints tracked procedural safety and adverse event frequency. Among 42 eligible participants, 38 successfully completed the tele-guided workflow. Diagnostic results identified true IgE-mediated sensitization in 11 individuals (26.2%), whereas 27 exhibited negative cutaneous responses, permitting formal de-labeling. No severe hypersensitivity reactions occurred; merely two transient erythematous sites necessitated topical corticosteroid application. Post-testing, 96% of successfully de-labeled patients transitioned from broad-spectrum empiric regimens to targeted narrow-spectrum agents within three days. These findings support widespread implementation of hybrid care pathways to maximize resource utilization. Telemedicine-facilitated PST demonstrated robust feasibility, safety, and diagnostic accuracy mirroring conventional in-person assessments. By enabling real-time specialist supervision across institutional boundaries, this framework directly mitigates geographic constraints and specialist shortages inherent to contemporary allergy care. Embedding such virtual models within institutional antimicrobial stewardship initiatives presents a highly viable strategy to enhance prescription precision, curtail unnecessary expenditures, and ultimately refine long-term clinical trajectories for patients burdened by falsely attributed drug allergies.

title: 3D morphological analysis of spiral intestine morphogenesis in the little skate, Leucoraja erinacea.
text_ai: The evolution of organ asymmetries is less explored than the field of organ morphology and coiling. The digestive tract of elasmobranchs provides a fascinating model for studying the evolution of morphological asymmetries. Unique to elasmobranchs and all basal fishes is the spiral intestine, which may represent an intermediate morphology in evolution from the straight gut of lamprey to the elongated coils of higher vertebrates. Here, we present a high-resolution three-dimensional morphological analysis of spiral intestine development in the little skate (*Leucoraja erinacea*). Utilizing micro-computed tomography and computational volumetric reconstruction, we quantified spatial growth gradients, tissue strain distributions, and helical pitch variations across embryonic staging. Results indicate that intestinal coiling initiates via localized differential proliferation along the dorsal mesentery, generating torsional forces that establish left-handed chirality. Biomechanical modeling further demonstrates that intrinsic stiffness gradients, regulated by extracellular matrix remodeling, are sufficient to produce the observed helical architecture without external constraints. These data establish a quantitative framework linking cellular proliferation patterns to macroscopic organ topology. By integrating morphometric precision with biophysical simulation, this work elucidates how conserved developmental mechanisms are co-opted to generate three-dimensional asymmetries. Ultimately, the elasmobranch spiral intestine bridges ancestral and derived states, revealing mechanical principles governing vertebrate gastrointestinal morphogenesis.

title: WhisperFuzz: White-Box Fuzzing for Detecting and Locating Timing Vulnerabilities in Processors
text_ai: Timing vulnerabilities in processors have emerged as a potent threat. As processors are the foundation of any computing system, identifying these flaws is imperative. Recently fuzzing techniques, traditionally used for detecting software vulnerabilities, have shown promising results for uncovering vulnerabilities in large-scale hardware designs, such as processors. However, existing hardware fuzzers predominantly rely on black-box methodologies, which severely limit their ability to navigate complex state spaces and precisely pinpoint temporal race conditions within critical paths. To address this limitation, we introduce WhisperFuzz, a novel white-box fuzzing framework specifically engineered to detect and localize timing vulnerabilities in processor microarchitectures. WhisperFuzz integrates dynamic symbolic execution with cycle-accurate RTL simulation to generate targeted input sequences that maximally explore control-flow divergence and data-dependent scheduling hazards. By maintaining a comprehensive coverage map of pipeline stages and forwarding networks, our framework employs a timing-aware mutation strategy that systematically perturbs operand dependencies to trigger metastability and setup/hold violations. We evaluate WhisperFuzz across five commercial and open-source processor cores, achieving a 3.2× improvement in vulnerability discovery rate compared to state-of-the-art grey-box alternatives. Furthermore, our analysis demonstrates high localization accuracy, successfully isolating root-cause logic gates responsible for 94% of identified timing faults without manual trace inspection. These findings establish WhisperFuzz as a scalable verification paradigm, offering hardware designers a rigorous, automated mechanism to mitigate side-channel and reliability risks inherent in modern computational architectures while significantly reducing post-silicon validation cycles.

title: Illustrating the Applicability of IRT to Implementation Science: Examining an Instrument of Therapist Attitudes.
text_ai: Pragmatic instruments with psychometric support are important to advance dissemination and implementation (D&I) research, but few well-researched D&I instruments exist. Item response theory (IRT), an approach that is underutilized in D&I, can help with the development of actionable and brief instruments. This study demonstrates IRT’s utility by evaluating the Evidence-Based Practice Attitude Scale (EBPAS) using data from 842 community mental health clinicians. We applied graded response models to examine item-level information, threshold parameters, and scale precision across the attitudinal continuum. Results revealed substantial differential item functioning across experience levels, with four items providing maximal measurement information at extreme attitudinal poles. The Discovery subscale demonstrated strong discrimination, whereas the Penalization subscale exhibited restricted variance among veteran providers. These findings illustrate how IRT enables rigorous item reduction while preserving construct validity, ultimately yielding a condensed 10-item instrument that maintains high reliability and predictive accuracy for implementation metrics. Integrating IRT into D&I methodology allows investigators to generate efficient, clinically feasible measures tailored to specific workforce populations. Consequently, this application offers a scalable framework for optimizing attitude assessment, thereby improving fidelity monitoring and strengthening the methodological rigor of future dissemination and implementation trials.

title: A probabilistic reduced-order modeling framework for patient-specific cardio-mechanical analysis
text_ai: Cardio-mechanical models can be used to support clinical decision-making. Unfortunately, the substantial computational effort involved in many cardiac models hinders their application in the clinic, despite the fact that they may provide valuable information. In this work, we present a probabilistic reduced-order modeling (ROM) framework to dramatically reduce the computational effort of such models while providing a credibility interval. The framework leverages proper orthogonal decomposition coupled with stochastic collocation to construct a low-dimensional surrogate capturing the essential dynamics of ventricular deformation and pressure-volume relationships. By projecting the governing finite element equations onto a learned manifold and propagating patient-specific parameter uncertainties through Gaussian processes, the approach yields rapid predictions alongside rigorous credibility bounds. We validate the methodology against high-fidelity subject-specific simulations across five distinct anatomical configurations representing varying degrees of pathological remodeling. The probabilistic ROM achieves speedups exceeding two orders of magnitude relative to full-order solvers, while maintaining mean absolute errors below 4% for peak pressures and regional strain metrics. Furthermore, the constructed credibility intervals consistently encompass ground-truth solutions, demonstrating robust uncertainty quantification even under significant parameter variation. Cross-validation experiments further confirm the model’s generalizability across unseen hemodynamic regimes, ensuring reliable extrapolation during dynamic loading conditions. These findings establish that probability-aware dimensionality reduction can effectively bridge the gap between computationally intensive biomechanical simulation and real-time clinical workflows. By enabling fast, uncertainty-quantified patient-specific assessments, the proposed framework offers a viable pathway for integrating detailed cardio-mechanical insights into routine diagnostic planning, surgical rehearsal, and therapeutic optimization.

title: Energy Gap from Step Structure of the Analytically Inverted Non-Additive Kinetic Potential
text_ai: The bandgap constitutes a challenging problem in density functional theory (DFT) methodologies. It is known that the energy gap values calculated by common DFT approaches are underestimated. The bandgap was also found to be related to the derivative discontinuity (DD) of the exchange-correlation potential in the Kohn-Sham formulation of DFT. To address this deficiency, we investigate the precise manifestation of the derivative discontinuity through the spatially localized step features inherent in the exact non-additive kinetic potential. Through analytical inversion of high-fidelity reference densities, we reconstruct the constituent components of the Kohn–Sham potential and demonstrate that the magnitude of the interfragment potential step directly governs the fundamental bandgap. Our analysis reveals that the traditionally neglected kinetic contribution accounts for a substantial fraction of the total derivative discontinuity, thereby resolving a long-standing discrepancy in conventional semilocal approximations. Systematic evaluation across diverse chemical environments confirms that incorporating this step structure yields bandgap predictions that align closely with experimental measurements and many-body perturbation theory results. Furthermore, we establish a rigorous mathematical relationship linking the asymptotic behavior of the non-additive kinetic potential to the integer-valued change in particle number required by the exact theory. These findings provide a clear pathway for developing improved approximate functionals that explicitly encode step-like corrections, ultimately enabling accurate and computationally efficient electronic structure calculations for extended systems and heterogeneous materials without resorting to costly hybrid or GW methodologies.

title: Discovering momentum-dependent magnon spin texture in insulating antiferromagnets: Role of the Kitaev interaction
text_ai: We theoretically show that the Kitaev interaction generates a novel class of spin texture in the excitation spectrum of the antiferromagnetic insulator found in the Kitaev-Heisenberg-$\Gamma$ model. In conducting electronic systems, there is a series of vortex type of spin texture along the Fermi surface induced by Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. Here, we demonstrate that a topologically analogous momentum-dependent magnon spin texture emerges in the complete absence of itinerant charge carriers. Through rigorous linear spin-wave theory applied to the Kitaev-Heisenberg-$\Gamma$ Hamiltonian, we identify that the interplay between bond-directional Kitaev exchange and off-diagonal symmetric $\Gamma$ interactions explicitly breaks translational and point-group symmetries in reciprocal space. This symmetry reduction enforces a non-collinear, winding spin configuration across the magnon dispersion branches, which is fundamentally characterized by a momentum-resolved spin expectation value exhibiting vortex-like circulation around high-symmetry points across the entire Brillouin zone. Consequently, the resulting texture imparts a finite geometric phase to propagating magnons, yielding a substantial and tunable intrinsic contribution to the thermal Hall conductivity and spin Seebeck coefficient. We quantitatively map the parameter regime where these magnonic vortices dominate over conventional Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya contributions, demonstrating their clear experimental distinguishability through polarization-resolved inelastic neutron scattering. Our analytical framework remains valid under finite temperature corrections, confirming the robustness of the predicted phenomena up to the Néel temperature. These results establish a direct correspondence between fermionic spin-momentum locking and bosonic magnon textures, providing a foundational mechanism for engineering dissipationless heat transport in frustrated quantum magnets.

title: Two-scale momentum theory for time-dependent modelling of large wind farms
text_ai: This paper presents a theory based on the law of momentum conservation to define and help analyse the problem of large wind farm aerodynamics. Traditional single-scale actuator disk models fail to capture the complex interplay between individual turbine wakes and the evolving atmospheric boundary layer over extended operational periods. To address this limitation, we develop a hierarchical framework that couples near-wake dynamics with far-field flow adjustments through distinct spatial and temporal scales. The proposed formulation introduces a time-resolved momentum sink distribution evolving according to local shear profiles and turbulence intensity, while simultaneously enforcing global mass and momentum balance across the farm footprint. By decomposing the governing equations into fast-varying rotor-level perturbations and slow-evolving macro-scale flow corrections, the model achieves computational tractability without sacrificing physical fidelity. We validate the theoretical predictions against high-fidelity large-eddy simulations and field measurements from offshore installations under varying wind directions and stability conditions. Results demonstrate that the two-scale approach accurately reproduces transient power deficits, wake meandering statistics, and recovery lengths beyond twenty rotor diameters downstream. Furthermore, the methodology reveals feedback mechanisms wherein collective farm-induced drag modulates the low-level jet structure, altering energy yield estimates by up to twelve percent compared to steady-state approximations. These findings establish a robust foundation for next-generation layout optimization algorithms and grid-integration strategies requiring dynamic performance forecasting. Ultimately, the presented theory bridges the gap between simplified engineering tools and computationally prohibitive numerical weather prediction systems, enabling efficient simulation of utility-scale renewable infrastructure under realistic meteorological forcing.

title: A tutorial on individualized treatment effect prediction from randomized trials with a binary endpoint
text_ai: Randomized trials typically estimate average relative treatment effects, but decisions on the benefit of a treatment are possibly better informed by more individualized predictions of the absolute treatment effect. In case of a binary outcome, these predictions of absolute individualized treatment effect require knowledge of the individual's risk without treatment and incorporation of a possibly differential treatment effect (i.e. baseline-risk-dependent effects). Estimating such individualized absolute effects demands careful consideration of model specification, particularly regarding the functional form of covariate–outcome and covariate–treatment interactions. This tutorial provides a comprehensive yet accessible framework for predicting absolute individualized treatment effects in randomized controlled trials with binary endpoints. We first outline the conceptual distinction between relative and absolute effect measures, emphasizing why clinical decision-making benefits from risk-stratified predictions. We then review established statistical approaches, including parametric modeling, machine learning algorithms, and doubly robust estimators, detailing their underlying assumptions, strengths, and limitations. Practical guidance on model building, cross-validation, calibration assessment, and uncertainty quantification is provided alongside reproducible code implementations in R. Through two illustrative applications using published trial data, we demonstrate how to translate estimated effects into clinically interpretable metrics, such as number needed to treat. Finally, we discuss common pitfalls, including overfitting, transportability concerns, and the misinterpretation of predictive accuracy metrics. By bridging methodological theory with applied practice, this tutorial equips researchers and clinicians with the tools necessary to harness individualized treatment effect estimation for precision medicine initiatives. These resources collectively facilitate transparent reporting and reproducibility in future clinical research.

title: Twin-width and types
text_ai: We study problems connected to first-order logic in graphs of bounded twin-width. Inspired by the approach of Bonnet et al. [FOCS 2020], we introduce a robust methodology of local types and describe their behavior in contraction sequences -- the decomposition notion underlying twin-width. Specifically, we formalize how local types evolve when red edges are contracted, proving that the induced partition of vertex pairs stabilizes after a number of steps bounded by a function of the twin-width. This stabilization enables us to compute a canonical representation of each type directly from the contraction sequence without explicit backtracking. Leveraging this representation, we establish that logical equivalence coincides with indistinguishability via a finite set of atomic formulas, thereby yielding a fixed-parameter tractable model-checking algorithm parameterized solely by the formula size and the twin-width. Our construction improves upon prior doubly exponential dependencies by exploiting the hierarchical nature of the decomposition. Moreover, we prove closure properties for local types under standard graph operations, which facilitates compositional reasoning across complex graph families. The resulting framework circumvents heavy model-theoretic machinery, offering a self-contained combinatorial proof that aligns naturally with algorithmic design patterns in modern graph decomposition theory. As immediate applications, we derive tight upper bounds for counting homomorphisms and extend known transfer principles to a wider spectrum of first-order properties. Finally, we discuss how our type-tracking mechanism integrates seamlessly with existing twin-width computation pipelines, paving the way for practical implementations and further generalizations to dynamic graph settings.

title: TractoSCR: A Novel Supervised Contrastive Regression Framework for Prediction of Neurocognitive Measures Using Multi-Site Harmonized Diffusion MRI Tractography
text_ai: Neuroimaging-based prediction of neurocognitive measures is valuable for studying how the brain's structure relates to cognitive function. However, the accuracy of prediction using popular linear regression models is relatively low. We propose a novel deep regression method, namely TractoSCR, that allows full supervision for contrastive learning in regression tasks using diffusion MRI tractography. TractoSCR integrates a graph convolutional network with a supervised contrastive loss, aligning subject-wise tract profiles with continuous neurocognitive scores during training. By simultaneously maximizing similarity between samples with proximate cognitive values and minimizing overlap across dissimilar targets, the framework captures nuanced structure-function mappings that standard mean-squared error optimization overlooks. To address site-specific acquisition variability, tractograms undergo ComBat harmonization before network input, ensuring robust cross-cohort generalizability. Evaluated on a pooled dataset spanning three independent cohorts (N=1,248), TractoSCR consistently outperformed conventional ridge regression, support vector machines, and unsupervised contrastive baselines. It achieved Pearson correlation coefficients ranging from 0.52 to 0.68 across executive function, processing speed, and memory domains, representing absolute improvements of 11% to 24% over existing linear benchmarks. Ablation studies confirm that the supervised contrastive objective substantially enhances feature discriminability without introducing overfitting. These findings demonstrate that aligning representation learning directly with regression targets via contrastive objectives significantly advances the predictive utility of structural connectomics. Consequently, TractoSCR provides a scalable, harmonized pipeline for translational neuroimaging research and holds promise for early biomarker discovery in neurodegenerative populations.
prefix: Neuroimaging-based prediction of neurocognitive measures is valuable for studying how the brain's structure relates to cognitive function. However, the accuracy of prediction using popular linear regression models is relatively low. We propose a novel deep regression method, namely TractoSCR, that allows full supervision for contrastive learning in regression tasks using diffusion MRI tractography.

title: Character-based Neural Machine Translation
text_ai: We introduce a neural machine translation model that views the input and output sentences as sequences of characters rather than words. Since word-level information provides a crucial source of bias, our input model composes representations of character sequences into representations of words (as determined by whitespace boundaries), and then these are translated using a joint attention/translation model. Empirical evaluations on standard English-German and French-English benchmarks demonstrate that this character-aware architecture consistently surpasses conventional subword-based systems, particularly in low-resource settings. By explicitly modeling morphological variations through fine-grained character units, the framework substantially reduces out-of-vocabulary errors while maintaining training stability. Furthermore, shared character embeddings facilitate effective cross-lingual representation learning, enabling robust zero-shot translation between unseen language pairs. Ablation studies confirm that compositional hierarchies significantly improve gradient propagation during optimization. Collectively, these results underscore the necessity of abandoning rigid lexical segmentation, establishing character-level compositionality as a foundational component for scalable machine translation across diverse linguistic domains.

title: Third-order analysis of pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann model for multiphase flow
text_ai: In this work, a third-order Chapman-Enskog analysis of the multiple-relaxation-time (MRT) pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann (LB) model for multiphase flow is performed for the first time. The leading terms on the interaction force, consisting of an anisotropic and an isotropic term, are successfully identified in the third-order macroscopic equation recovered by the lattice Boltzmann equation (LBE), and then new mathematical insights into the pseudopotential LB model are provided. Specifically, the anisotropic contribution is rigorously traced to incomplete rotational symmetry in the discrete velocity manifold, whereas the isotropic component manifests as a spurious modification to the equilibrium pressure tensor. By analytically decoupling these terms, we formulate targeted correction protocols that neutralize nonphysical capillary waves while preserving the prescribed interfacial thickness. Moreover, the third-order expansion elucidates the intricate coupling between the interaction potential gradient and the MRT collision matrix, demonstrating that strategic eigenvalue tuning can selectively dampen numerical oscillations without compromising macroscopic hydrodynamic consistency. Comprehensive benchmark tests involving static droplet equilibria and spinodal decomposition dynamics quantitatively validate these theoretical predictions, yielding substantial suppression of residual spurious velocities relative to conventional single-relaxation-time formulations. These results underscore the necessity of higher-order moment matching in lattice design and offer a direct route to mitigating thermodynamic inconsistencies at elevated density ratios. Consequently, this investigation establishes a comprehensive diagnostic framework for resolving inherent discretization artifacts in pseudopotential lattice Boltzmann schemes, ultimately providing practitioners with actionable guidelines for optimizing numerical stability and accuracy in complex interfacial flow simulations.

title: Performance evaluation of a new route optimization technique for mobile IP
text_ai: Mobile ip (mip) is an internet protocol that allows mobile nodes to have continuous network connectivity to the internet without changing their ip addresses while moving to other networks. The packets sent from correspondent node (cn) to a mobile node (mn) go first through the mobile node's home agent (ha), then the ha tunnels them to the mn's foreign network. This indirect forwarding mechanism, however, introduces substantial triangle routing inefficiencies, resulting in elevated end-to-end latency, excessive bandwidth consumption, and degraded quality of service during handoffs. To address these limitations, this study proposes an enhanced route optimization scheme that dynamically establishes direct communication pathways between the CN and MN while maintaining seamless mobility management. The proposed architecture leverages localized binding updates and predictive location tracking to minimize control-plane signaling and eliminate redundant tunneling operations. Performance was rigorously evaluated using NS-3-based simulations under varying mobility patterns, network densities, and packet arrival rates. Comparative analysis against baseline MIP and IETF-standard route optimization protocols demonstrates that the novel approach consistently reduces average handoff latency by 34.7%, decreases packet loss during transition phases by 28.3%, and improves overall throughput by 22.1% under high-mobility conditions. Furthermore, control message overhead is significantly curtailed, thereby enhancing scalability for dense cellular deployments. These findings validate the efficacy of the optimized routing framework in supporting real-time multimedia services and resource-constrained IoT environments. Consequently, the presented methodology offers a robust and backward-compatible upgrade path for legacy infrastructure while actively advancing next-generation mobile networking standards globally.

title: Development and Validation of a Scale for Measuring Instructors' Attitudes toward Concept-Based or Reform-Oriented Teaching of Introductory Statistics in the Health and Behavioral Sciences
text_ai: Despite more than a decade of reform efforts, students continue to experience difficulty understanding and applying statistical concepts. The predominant focus of reform has been on content, pedagogy, technology and assessment, with little attention to instructor characteristics. However, there is strong theoretical and empirical evidence that instructors' attitudes impact the quality of teaching and learning. To address this critical gap, we developed and validated the Attitudes toward Concept-Based Statistics Instruction (ACSI) scale. Employing a sequential mixed-methods design, initial item generation drew upon extant literature and cognitive interviews with fifteen health science faculty members to ensure domain relevance. Psychometric evaluation proceeded through exploratory factor analysis (N = 203) followed by confirmatory factor analysis on an independent cohort (N = 512). Results supported a refined four-factor model capturing epistemological beliefs, perceived implementation viability, disciplinary congruence, and resistance to traditional algorithmic approaches. Reliability estimates demonstrated strong internal consistency (Cronbach’s α ranging from .82 to .91), while convergent validity was confirmed through positive associations with documented adoption of inquiry-based curricula and peer-reviewed teaching portfolios. Notably, structural equation modeling indicated that reform-aligned attitudes mediated the relationship between professional development participation and classroom practice shifts. These findings underscore the necessity of addressing affective dimensions alongside technical training. The ACSI scale provides educators with a rigorous diagnostic instrument to identify attitudinal constraints and tailor faculty support mechanisms. Ultimately, integrating attitude measurement into reform frameworks promises sustainable, context-sensitive enhancements to statistical literacy across health and behavioral disciplines.

title: The Community In-reach Rehabilitation and Care Transition (CIRACT) clinical and cost-effectiveness randomisation controlled trial in older people admitted to hospital as an acute medical emergency.
text_ai: To compare the clinical and cost-effectiveness of a Community In-reach Rehabilitation and Care Transition (CIRACT) service with the traditional hospital-based rehabilitation (THB-Rehab) service. Pragmatic randomised controlled trial with an integral health economic study. Large UK teaching hospital, with community follow-up. Frail older people aged 70 years and older admitted to hospital as an acute medical emergency. Participants were randomly allocated (1:1) via computer-generated sequence to receive either CIRACT or THB-Rehab. The CIRACT intervention delivered multidisciplinary rehabilitation, care coordination, and discharge planning directly within the acute ward, bridging seamlessly into community-based support. Primary outcomes included functional independence measured by the Modified Rankin Scale at three months and direct healthcare costs. Secondary outcomes encompassed quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), unplanned readmissions, mortality, and patient-reported experience measures. Data were analysed on an intention-to-treat basis using mixed-effects regression models adjusted for baseline covariates, with cost-effectiveness evaluated through incremental cost-effectiveness ratios and acceptability curves. At three-month follow-up, 842 participants completed outcome assessments. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed for functional independence (adjusted odds ratio 1.12, 95% CI 0.89 to 1.41; p=0.34) or quality of life. However, CIRACT significantly reduced mean direct healthcare costs (£1,840 vs £2,310 per patient; difference -£470, 95% CI -£890 to -£50; p=0.03). Unplanned readmission rates and mortality did not differ substantially between arms. The CIRACT model demonstrates comparable clinical effectiveness to standard ward-based rehabilitation while generating modest economic savings. Implementation within acute trusts warrants consideration as a viable pathway to optimise resource utilisation without compromising patient outcomes during critical care transitions.

title: Effectiveness of Bone Conduction Stimulation Applied Directly to the Otic Capsule Measured at Promontory: Assessment in Cadavers.
text_ai: The aims of this study included: (a) to develop a method of direct acoustic bone conduction (BC) stimulation applied directly to the otic capsule, (b) to investigate the effect of different stimulation sites on the promontory displacement amplitude, and (c) to find the best stimulation site (among 2 located directly on the otic capsule and 1 standard site approved for clinical use) that provides the greatest transmission of vibratory energy. Six fresh-frozen human temporal bone specimens were utilized. A custom-built transducer was positioned at two anatomically defined loci on the otic capsule and one reference site consistent with current clinical protocols. Vibratory responses at the cochlear promontory were quantified using laser Doppler vibrometry across a frequency range of 250 Hz to 8000 Hz. Stimulation directly applied to the otic capsule yielded significantly higher promontory displacement amplitudes compared to the standard clinical site (p < 0.01). Among the two otic capsule locations, the posterior-superior quadrant demonstrated peak energy transmission, particularly between 1000 Hz and 4000 Hz, where displacement magnitudes exceeded those of the conventional approach by an average of 6.2 dB. Statistical analysis confirmed a strong positive correlation between proximity to the otic capsule’s thinnest bony regions and signal attenuation reduction. These findings demonstrate that direct otic capsule stimulation substantially enhances vibratory energy transfer to the cochlea relative to established clinical paradigms. Optimizing transducer placement at the posterior-superior otic capsule may inform next-generation implantable bone conduction devices, potentially improving audiological outcomes for patients with conductive or mixed hearing loss.

title: A natural killer T-cell subset that protects against airway hyperreactivity.
text_ai: Infection of suckling mice with influenza virus expands a CD4 - CD8 - double-negative (DN) natural killer T (NKT) cell subpopulation that protects the mice as adults against allergen-induced airway hyperreactivity (AHR). However, this NKT cell subset has not been characterized, and the underlying mechanisms of protection remain unknown. Here, we demonstrate that these neonatally expanded DN-NKT cells acquire a stable regulatory phenotype characterized by high expression of interleukin-10 (IL-10) and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), while remaining unresponsive to classical lipid antigens presented by CD1d. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of transcription factors associated with tissue residency and immune suppression, including Il10, Tgfb1, and Prdm1. Single-cell RNA sequencing further delineated distinct metabolic pathways favoring oxidative phosphorylation, supporting sustained cytokine production during homeostatic conditions. Functionally, adoptive transfer of these DN-NKT cells into adult recipients prior to ovalbumin sensitization and challenge significantly attenuated eosinophilic inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and bronchoconstriction. Mechanistic studies indicated that DN-NKT-derived IL-10 directly acted upon alveolar macrophages to promote efferocytosis and limit pro-inflammatory cytokine release, thereby disrupting the Th2-skewed microenvironment essential for AHR development. Furthermore, neutralization of IL-10 or depletion of macrophages abrogated the protective effect, confirming the necessity of this cellular axis. These findings define a previously unrecognized DN-NKT cell lineage with potent anti-inflammatory capacity and establish IL-10-dependent macrophage modulation as a critical pathway by which early-life viral exposure confers long-term resilience against allergic airway disease. This work provides a novel framework for understanding developmental immune programming and highlights potential targets for asthma prophylaxis.

title: Lateral brow lift: A multi-point suture fixation technique
text_ai: Background Descent of the lateral aspect of the brow is one of the earliest signs of aging. The purpose of this study was to describe an open surgical technique for lateral brow lifts, with the goal of achieving reliable, predictable, and long-lasting results. The procedure utilizes a temporal hairline incision with subperiosteal dissection to expose the lateral orbital rim and deep temporal fascia. Three strategic anchor points are established using permanent, non-absorbable sutures: the lateral canthal tendon region, the temporal fascia, and the superior periosteum. This multi-point configuration distributes tension evenly while preserving the frontal branch of the facial nerve. We retrospectively reviewed 42 consecutive patients undergoing unilateral or bilateral lateral brow lifts over a two-year period. Preoperative and postoperative standardized photographs were analyzed using digital caliper measurements to quantify vertical brow elevation. Complications, revision rates, and patient-reported satisfaction were documented during a minimum 18-month follow-up. Mean vertical brow elevation measured 6.8 ± 1.4 mm at final assessment. All patients maintained ≥70% of initial correction without positional drift. Minor transient periorbital numbness resolved within three months in four cases; no hematomas, infections, or suture extrusions occurred. Overall patient satisfaction reached 94%, with 88% reporting sustained aesthetic improvement beyond one year. Distributing elevating forces across multiple anatomical anchors minimizes tissue tearing and suture pull-through. This technique achieves durable lateral brow repositioning with a favorable safety profile, offering a refined alternative for targeted upper facial rejuvenation.

title: On the thermal sunset diagram for scalar field theories
text_ai: We study the so-called `` sunset diagram'', which is one of two-loop self-energy diagrams, for scalar field theories at finite temperature. For this purpose, we first find the complete expression of the bubble diagram, the one-loop subdiagram of the sunset diagram, for arbitrary momentum. Building upon this foundation, we systematically evaluate the full two-loop thermal integral by employing analytic continuation and contour deformation techniques to perform the Matsubara frequency summations. The resulting closed-form expression is formulated in terms of generalized polylogarithms and Bose-Einstein distribution functions, remaining valid across the entire kinematic regime. We carefully isolate the infrared-sensitive contributions originating from soft modes and demonstrate their systematic modification of the naive high-temperature expansion. By cross-referencing our analytic derivations with independent numerical quadratures, we verify the internal consistency of the perturbative scheme at next-to-leading order. Furthermore, we extract the thermal mass shift and characterize its functional dependence on external spatial momentum and temperature scales. Our analysis reveals a subtle interplay between ultraviolet renormalization procedures and infrared screening mechanisms, necessitating a consistent resummation strategy near phase boundaries. We explicitly compute the divergent counterterms required to cancel ultraviolet poles and show that the remaining finite parts exhibit universal scaling behavior. Comparison with earlier approximate treatments confirms that our exact formulation resolves longstanding discrepancies in the perturbative series. The established computational framework delivers precise two-loop thermal corrections for interacting scalar models and establishes a rigorous foundation for subsequent investigations of transport phenomena and early-universe thermodynamics.

title: Discontinuous Galerkin Methods for Hypersonic Flows
text_ai: In recent years, high-order discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods have emerged as an attractive approach for numerical simulations of compressible flows. This paper presents an overview of the recent development of DG methods for compressible flows with particular focus on hypersononic flows. First, we survey state-of-the-art DG methods for computational fluid dynamics. Special attention is devoted to the inherent numerical challenges associated with hypersonic regimes, including strong shock waves, thin boundary layers, and high-temperature gas effects. To address these difficulties, we examine advanced stabilization techniques such as artificial viscosity, slope limiters, and hybrid DG/finite-volume formulations that ensure robust shock capturing without compromising high-order accuracy in smooth regions. The discussion extends to efficient time-integration strategies and adaptive mesh refinement frameworks tailored for unsteady hypersonic aerothermodynamics. Furthermore, we introduce a newly developed entropy-stable flux discretization coupled with a dynamic subcell limiting procedure, which significantly enhances solution fidelity while maintaining strict conservation properties. Comprehensive numerical experiments are presented across test cases, including supersonic flow over a flat plate, double-wedge configurations, and blunt-body reentry scenarios at Mach numbers exceeding five. Results demonstrate superior resolution of contact discontinuities and thermal gradients compared to traditional low-order schemes, alongside favorable scaling on computing architectures. Additionally, RANS-based turbulence closures are integrated to resolve critical viscous-inviscid coupling mechanisms within boundary layers. These findings underscore the transformative potential of high-order DG methodologies for hypersonic vehicle design and atmospheric entry analysis.

title: The susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model: New developments
text_ai: We have made substantial advances in elucidating the properties of the susceptibility of the square lattice Ising model. We discuss its analyticity properties, certain closed form expressions for subsets of the coefficients, and give an algorithm of complexity O(N^6) to determine its first N coefficients. Building upon these computational tools, we derive exact nonlinear differential equations satisfied by the susceptibility, revealing connections to Calabi–Yau manifolds and modular forms. By analyzing the singularity structure near the critical temperature, we extract precise asymptotic expansions that confirm formulated conjectures regarding crossover scaling functions and correction-to-scaling exponents. Furthermore, we extend the coefficient extraction framework to two-point correlation functions, demonstrating that similar algebraic structures govern their high-temperature series. These results not only streamline numerical investigations across related lattice systems but also provide rigorous analytical benchmarks for renormalization group analyses. Our findings underscore the enduring richness of integrable models and suggest novel pathways for tackling non-integrable generalizations through symbolic computation.

title: The orbital structure of a tidally induced bar
text_ai: Orbits are the key building blocks of any density distribution and their study helps us understand the kinematical structure and the evolution of galaxies. Here we investigate orbits in a tidally induced bar of a dwarf galaxy, using an $N$-body simulation of an initially disky dwarf galaxy orbiting a Milky Way-like host. We employ a frequency-map analysis technique to classify orbital families within the evolving potential, distinguishing between regular box orbits that sustain the bar’s elongation and chaotic trajectories that facilitate angular momentum exchange with the halo. Our results reveal that tidal forcing significantly alters the resonance landscape, suppressing high-order commensurabilities while enhancing low-order resonances that trap stellar streams near the corotation radius. The dominant orbital support shifts from purely regular x1-type orbits during the initial bar growth phase to a mixed population where tidally driven chaotic orbits contribute up to thirty percent of the mass budget in the inner regions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the outer disk responds through a network of overlapping secular resonances, generating non-axisymmetric perturbations that mimic spiral arm kinematics without requiring self-gravity instability. These findings underscore the critical role of external tidal fields in reshaping phase-space architectures, providing a mechanistic link between environmental harassment and the morphological transformation of low-mass systems. By quantifying the orbital contributions to bar strength and lifetime, this work offers a refined framework for interpreting integral-field spectroscopy of satellite galaxies and constrains the viability of isolated bar models in cosmological contexts.

title: Prospects for constraining the spin of the massive black hole at the Galactic center via the relativistic motion of a surrounding star
text_ai: In this paper, we investigate the quality of constraining the spin of the massive black hole (MBH) at the Galactic center (GC) by using full general relativistic simulations of the motion of a surrounding star. We model test-particle trajectories in the Kerr metric, incorporating frame-dragging effects, gravitational redshift, and light-bending corrections to generate synthetic astrometric and spectroscopic observables. By varying the dimensionless spin parameter $a_* \in [0, 0.998]$ and initial orbital configurations, we assess the recoverability of the spin through Markov Chain Monte Carlo fitting against mock data sets mimicking next-generation interferometric observations. Our results demonstrate that the relativistic periapsis shift and Lense–Thirring precession imprint distinct signatures on the orbital plane orientation and argument of periapsis evolution. For stars with semi-major axes $a \lesssim 1000\,\mathrm{AU}$ and eccentricities $e > 0.8$, a spin constraint at the $1\sigma$ level of $\Delta a_* \approx 0.1$ is achievable within a five-year observational baseline, provided positional uncertainties remain below $50\,\mu\mathrm{as}$. We identify a mild degeneracy between spin and the distance to the Galactic center, which can be systematically broken by combining relative astrometry with independent trigonometric parallax measurements. Furthermore, we show that incorporating higher-order post-Newtonian corrections significantly improves constraint stability for highly inclined orbits and reduces systematic biases in the recovered inclination angle. These findings establish a robust observational pathway toward measuring the MBH spin using currently operational instruments, underscoring the scientific return of sustained monitoring of high-eccentricity S-stars. Ultimately, this framework offers a predictive tool for optimizing observation strategies and interpreting forthcoming high-precision stellar dynamics data within the regime of strong-field general relativity.

title: Patient Insurance Status Is Associated With Care Received After Transfer Among Pediatric Patients in the Emergency Department.
text_ai: To determine whether frequency of interfacility transfer varied by insurance status among pediatric emergency department (ED) patients. Secondarily, we tested for an association between insurance status and odds of transfer with discharge from the second ED without observation or admission. We used the 2016 New York State ED and Inpatient Databases to identify all patients <18 years. We restricted the cohort to patients presenting to nonchildren’s hospitals who subsequently visited another facility within 72 hours. Insurance categories included private, public (Medicaid/CHIP), uninsured, and self-pay. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, clinical severity indices, primary diagnosis category, hospital size, teaching status, and geographic region were constructed to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 1,247,832 pediatric ED encounters, 89,412 (7.2%) qualified as transfers. Uninsured children exhibited significantly elevated odds of interfacility transfer relative to privately insured peers (aOR 1.34, 95% CI 1.28–1.40), whereas Medicaid recipients demonstrated statistically similar rates (aOR 1.02, 95% CI 0.99–1.05). Regarding secondary outcomes, publicly insured and uninsured youth were markedly less likely to receive direct discharge from the receiving ED following transfer (private: reference; Medicaid: aOR 0.78, 95% CI 0.75–0.81; uninsured: aOR 0.69, 95% CI 0.64–0.74; both p<0.001), reflecting increased reliance on observation units or inpatient admission. These findings demonstrate that insurance type independently predicts both transfer utilization and post-transfer disposition. Systematic disparities in care navigation and resource allocation across payer categories underscore the need for standardized triage protocols and policy interventions to mitigate inequitable treatment pathways in pediatric emergency medicine.

title: MOSEv2: A More Challenging Dataset for Video Object Segmentation in Complex Scenes
text_ai: Video object segmentation (VOS) aims to segment specified target objects throughout a video. Although state-of-the-art methods have achieved impressive performance (e.g., 90+% J&F) on existing benchmarks such as DAVIS and YouTube-VOS, these datasets primarily contain salient, dominant, and isolated objects, limiting their generalization to real-world scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce MOSEv2, a meticulously curated benchmark comprising 1,250 high-resolution videos featuring densely populated, dynamically changing environments. Unlike prior collections, MOSEv2 emphasizes severe inter-object occlusions, highly textured backgrounds, rapid camera motions, and ambiguous object boundaries that closely mimic uncontrolled real-world conditions. We construct the dataset through a hybrid pipeline combining expert annotation with rigorous quality control, ensuring precise pixel-level masks across all frames while preserving natural motion trajectories. Comprehensive evaluations reveal that leading VOS architectures experience substantial performance degradation on MOSEv2, with J&F scores dropping by up to 28% relative to standard benchmarks. These findings underscore the critical gap between controlled laboratory conditions and operational deployment requirements. Cross-dataset generalization tests further confirm that models pretrained solely on conventional collections fail to transfer effectively without targeted fine-tuning. Furthermore, we provide extensive ablation studies analyzing failure modes related to temporal consistency, background suppression, and instance discrimination under heavy clutter. By establishing a standardized protocol for evaluating robustness in intricate visual settings, MOSEv2 serves as a demanding yet reproducible testbed for advancing next-generation segmentation models. We release comprehensive annotations, baseline implementations, and evaluation protocols to foster community-driven progress toward generalizable video understanding systems.

title: The Quest for Omnioculars: Embedded Visualization for Augmenting Basketball Game Viewing Experiences
text_ai: Sports game data is becoming increasingly complex, often consisting of multivariate data such as player performance stats, historical team records, and athletes' positional tracking information. While numerous visual analytics systems have been developed for sports analysts to derive insights, few tools target fans to improve their understanding and engagement of sports data during live games. To bridge this participatory gap, we introduce Omnioculars, a novel embedded visualization framework designed specifically for second-screen mobile applications during live basketball broadcasts. Our approach leverages spatial anchoring and context-aware rendering to overlay real-time statistical overlays directly onto the broadcast feed, minimizing cognitive load while preserving narrative immersion. We detail the system architecture, which integrates low-latency data pipelines with adaptive UI components that respond to game state transitions and viewer interaction patterns. A controlled user study involving 48 novice and experienced basketball spectators was conducted to evaluate usability, comprehension, and entertainment value. Quantitative metrics indicate a 34% improvement in tactical understanding and a significant increase in sustained attention compared to conventional static dashboards. Qualitative feedback highlights the efficacy of non-intrusive, gaze-contingent displays in fostering deeper analytical engagement without disrupting the primary viewing experience. These findings demonstrate the viability of contextually embedded visualizations as a scalable medium for democratizing sports analytics. Ultimately, Omnioculars establishes a foundational paradigm for designing spectator-centric augmented interfaces that transform passive consumption into interactive, data-informed appreciation of athletic performance.

title: Unraveling the emergence of quantum state designs in systems with symmetry
text_ai: Quantum state designs, by enabling an efficient sampling of random quantum states, play a quintessential role in devising and benchmarking various quantum protocols with broad applications ranging from circuit designs to black hole physics. Symmetries, on the other hand, are expected to reduce the randomness of a state. Here, we resolve this apparent tension by demonstrating that approximate unitary designs naturally emerge within symmetry-constrained Hilbert spaces through generic dynamical evolution. We establish rigorous bounds on the convergence rate of symmetry-respecting circuits to t-designs, revealing that the requisite depth scales logarithmically with system size but exhibits a universal dependence on the dimension of the invariant subspaces. By analyzing both local and non-local conserved charges, we show that symmetry-induced constraints merely partition the ensemble into independent sectors, each of which independently approaches the desired statistical properties. Our analytical framework, supported by numerical simulations across spin chains and lattice gauge models, identifies a sharp transition in design efficiency governed by the interplay between scrambling dynamics and topological order. Crucially, we demonstrate that even weak symmetry breaking suffices to restore full design properties at asymptotic timescales. Furthermore, we derive closed-form expressions for the frame potential decay, confirming that sector-wise decorrelation dominates the approach to the Haar measure. These results provide a unifying perspective on randomized benchmarking, thermalization, and holographic duality in constrained quantum systems, establishing symmetry-preserving architectures as viable platforms for fault-tolerant quantum simulation and complexity-driven protocol verification under physically realistic conditions.

title: Treatment of pediatric vesicoureteral reflux using endoscopic injection of hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel: intermediate-term experience by a single surgeon
text_ai: OBJECTIVES: Endoscopic injection of non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel is an increasingly recognized treatment option for vesicoureteral reflux. The procedure is minor compared with open surgery and, when successful, avoids the need for long-term antibiotic prophylaxis. We present data from 3 years of using non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel to treat children with vesicoureteral reflux. METHODS: A retrospective review evaluated consecutive pediatric patients treated between January 2019 and December 2021. Inclusion required preoperative voiding cystourethrography confirming grades II–V reflux. All procedures utilized standardized subureteral injection techniques under general anesthesia. Imaging was obtained at 6 months or earlier if indicated. Success required complete radiographic resolution without recurrent febrile urinary tract infection. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated cumulative success across reflux grades. RESULTS: One hundred twelve ureters in 78 patients met criteria, with a mean injection age of 4.2 years. Preoperative grading comprised grade II (n=38), III (n=41), IV (n=24), and V (n=9). Technical success was achieved in 104 ureters (92.9%). At 24-month median follow-up, clinical success was observed in 89 ureters (79.5%). Higher-grade reflux exhibited reduced cure rates, notably grade V (55.6%). Minor transient hematuria occurred in six patients; zero major complications or conversions were recorded. CONCLUSIONS: Subureteral injection of hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel provides a safe, minimally invasive intervention with durable intermediate-term efficacy, especially for low- to mid-grade reflux. Appropriate patient selection effectively eliminates reflux and obviates prolonged antibiotic therapy, establishing this modality as a preferred endoscopic alternative prior to definitive ureteral reimplantation.

The procedure is minor compared with open surgery and, when successful, avoids the need for long-term antibiotic prophylaxis. We present data from 3 years of using non-animal-stabilized hyaluronic acid/dextranomer gel to treat children with vesicoureteral reflux.

title: Moist convection is most vigorous at intermediate atmospheric humidity
text_ai: In Earth's current climate, moist convective updraft speeds increase with surface warming. This trend suggests that very vigorous convection might be the norm in extremely hot and humid atmospheres, such as those undergoing a runaway greenhouse transition. To resolve this apparent paradox, we employ three-dimensional cloud-resolving simulations spanning a wide range of surface temperatures and water vapor contents. Contrary to linear extrapolations from present-day conditions, our results demonstrate that convective intensity exhibits a pronounced non-monotonic dependence on near-surface humidity. Peak updraft velocities and available potential energy occur at intermediate moisture levels, declining substantially under both arid and saturated conditions. This suppression in extremely humid regimes arises from a fundamental trade-off: while enhanced latent heat release strengthens buoyancy, simultaneously elevated water vapor concentrations dramatically increase longwave optical depth, which stabilizes the lower troposphere and enhances radiative cooling aloft. The resulting reduction in convective available potential energy counteracts the thermodynamic boost from additional condensation. We confirm this mechanism through idealized single-column experiments isolating radiative-dynamic feedbacks. This humidity-dependent modulation persists across varying gravitational accelerations and stellar irradiance levels, indicating its robustness for terrestrial planets across diverse climatic states. These findings revise prevailing assumptions about convective efficiency in super-Earths and early Mars analogs, suggesting that runaway greenhouse transitions may be characterized by episodic, rather than continuously intensifying, convective overturning. Consequently, parameterizations of deep convection in global circulation models must explicitly account for non-linear humidity dependencies to accurately project extreme climate scenarios and interpret atmospheric dynamics beyond Earth.

title: Impact of QCD jets and heavy-quark production in cosmic-ray proton atmospheric showers up to 10$^{20}$ eV
text_ai: The PYTHIA 6 Monte Carlo (MC) event generator, commonly used in collider physics, is interfaced for the first time with a fast transport simulation of a hydrogen atmosphere, with the same density as air, in order to study the properties of extended atmospheric showers (EAS) produced by cosmic ray protons with energies E$_{CR}\approx 10^{14}$--$10^{20}$ eV. We quantify the influence of perturbative QCD jet fragmentation and open heavy-flavor channels on longitudinal shower development and transverse lateral distributions. By varying the strong coupling constant $\alpha_s$ and implementing next-to-leading-order matrix elements for charm and bottom production, we demonstrate that enhanced heavy-quark yields significantly modify the hadronic energy fraction reaching the electromagnetic cascade. This results in a measurable shift in the depth of shower maximum ($X_{\rm max}$) and an increased muon multiplicity at ground level. Our simulations reveal that standard parametrizations underestimate the hadronic core intensity above $10^{18}$ eV, leading to discrepancies in reconstructed primary energy scales. The modified parton distribution functions and improved hadronization schemes reduce extrapolation uncertainties beyond LHC kinematic limits. Consequently, these corrections are critical for interpreting data from current and future fluorescence detectors, addressing the muon deficit puzzle. We provide parameterized correction factors for standard hadronic interaction models, enabling accurate reconstruction of ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray spectra and composition analyses. Validation against benchmark datasets confirms consistency within systematic uncertainties. This establishes a framework for integrating collider-derived QCD constraints into astroparticle phenomenology.

title: Successful intra-class switching among IL-17 antagonists: a multicentre, multinational, retrospective study.
text_ai: IL-17 blockers are among the newer anti-psoriatic treatment options and little is known about the interclass switching. We have thus initiated a multi-center, multi-national, retrospective study to assess the treatment response of patients who were switched from one IL-17 blocker to another. Data were extracted from electronic health records across twelve tertiary care centers spanning five European countries between 2018 and 2023. Eligible adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis transitioning between secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab, or brodalumab were enrolled. Primary endpoints evaluated changes in Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI) at weeks 12 and 16 post-transition. Secondary measures monitored adverse events, drug survival, and concurrent systemic immunosuppressant use. A cohort of 287 patients satisfied inclusion criteria (median age 51 years). At week 12, 76.3% achieved PASI 75 and 61.8% reached PASI 90, yielding significant DLQI reductions from 10 to 2 points (p<0.001). Twelve-month persistence remained high at 79.4%, with adverse event incidence mirroring initial induction profiles. Multivariate regression identified baseline PASI 100 status and shorter prior antagonist exposure as independent predictors of sustained remission. Adjustments for confounding variables confirmed these associations remained statistically significant after propensity score matching. In conclusion, intra-class switching between IL-17 antagonists preserves clinical efficacy and safety in routine practice. Clinicians may confidently employ biologic rotation strategies to overcome secondary failure while maintaining optimal cutaneous clearance and quality-of-life improvements.
