title: Histologic Findings of a Human Immature Revascularized/Regenerated Tooth with Symptomatic Irreversible Pulpitis.
text_ai: Pulp revascularization/regeneration in immature permanent teeth with necrotic pulp and/or apical periodontitis is an effective approach for inducing root maturation. Previous histologic studies showed cementoid/osteoid tissue and/or periodontal ligament-like tissue formed within the root canals. This case report describes the histologic findings of a human symptomatic irreversible pulpitis immature permanent tooth with most of the pulp removed after a revascularization/regeneration procedure. Microscopic examination revealed a heterogeneous tissue matrix characterized by abundant vascular channels, loosely arranged fibroblasts, and scattered inflammatory cell aggregates predominantly comprising lymphocytes and macrophages. Notably, irregular predentin deposits and well-organized dentin bridges formed adjacent to the remaining radicular pulp space, indicating active hard tissue synthesis. Odontoblast-like cells aligned along these matrices, while focal chronic inflammation persisted near the coronal resection margin. Immunohistochemical analysis demonstrated positive expression of nestin, collagen type I, and osteocalcin, confirming mesenchymal stem cell differentiation toward odontogenic and osteogenic lineages. Clinically, symptom resolution occurred within three months, accompanied by significant continuous root lengthening and canal wall thickening on serial radiographs. These histomorphological observations indicate that despite preoperative symptomatic irreversible pulpitis, partial pulp preservation combined with biologically induced revascularization successfully stimulates reparative dentinogenesis and maintains viable pulpal architecture. Conservative access techniques that minimize tissue removal may therefore enhance regenerative efficacy, highlighting the critical need to balance pathogen control with progenitor cell viability in contemporary endodontic protocols.

title: Quantum Kinetic Theory of Thermoelectric and Thermal Transport in a Magnetic Field
text_ai: We present a general quantum kinetic theory that accounts for the interplay between a temperature gradient, momentum-space Berry curvatures of Bloch electrons, and Bloch-state scattering. Using a theory that incorporates the presence of a temperature gradient by introducing a "thermal vector potential", we derive a quantum kinetic equation for Bloch electrons in the presence of disorder and a temperature gradient. Our formalism naturally yields a generalized Boltzmann-type equation where the thermal vector potential acts as an effective gauge field coupling directly to the energy current. By systematically solving this equation within the relaxation-time approximation, we obtain closed-form expressions for the thermoelectric and thermal conductivity tensors, explicitly revealing how anomalous velocity contributions from Berry curvature are renormalized by elastic impurity scattering and external magnetic fields. We demonstrate that the interplay between these geometric phases and the Lorentz force generates a pronounced transverse thermal response, fundamentally altering the conventional Righi-Leduc and Nernst coefficients. Furthermore, we establish a direct correspondence between our kinetic derivation and the linear-response Kubo formula, confirming the consistency of the thermal vector potential approach at finite temperatures. Applying our framework to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, we predict significant enhancements of the thermal Hall conductivity and a sign reversal in the thermopower under strong magnetic fields, effects stemming purely from band topology. These results provide a unified microscopic foundation for interpreting recent experimental observations in topological quantum materials, highlighting the critical role of Berry-phase physics in non-equilibrium heat and charge transport.

title: Preschool Gender-Typed Play Behavior at Age 3.5 Years Predicts Physical Aggression at Age 13 Years.
text_ai: Gender differences in play behavior and physical aggression have been consistently reported. Theoretical perspectives concerning evolutionary, social, and social-cognitive mechanisms suggest that male-typical play behavior during childhood increases subsequent physical aggression. The evidence supporting these connections is limited, however. To address this gap, the present longitudinal study examined whether preschool gender-typed play behavior predicts physical aggression in early adolescence. A community sample of 612 children (52% male) was followed from age 3.5 to 13 years. Trained observers coded direct play interactions using a validated gender-typed activity scale. Adolescent physical aggression was measured through multi-informant reports and laboratory-based conflict paradigms. Structural equation modeling evaluated predictive associations while adjusting for baseline aggression, socioeconomic status, and verbal ability. Findings revealed that elevated male-typical play at age 3.5 significantly forecasted heightened physical aggression at age 13 (β = .19, p < .005), even after accounting for concurrent temperament and family environment variables. Notably, female-typical play demonstrated no significant longitudinal linkage to later aggression. The association remained stable across varying degrees of parental monitoring and peer group composition, suggesting broad generalizability. Collectively, these results offer compelling empirical support for developmental frameworks emphasizing early activity segregation as a precursor to adolescent externalizing pathology. Specifically, identifying pronounced male-typical play patterns in early childhood may facilitate timely, developmentally sensitive interventions designed to disrupt escalating aggression trajectories before they become clinically entrenched.

title: Exocomets in the Proxima Centauri system and their importance for water transport
text_ai: The scenario and efficiency of water transport by icy asteroids and comets are still amongst the most important unresolved questions of planetary systems. A better understanding of cometary dynamics in extrasolar systems shall provide information about cometary reservoirs and give an insight into water transport especially to planets in the habitable zone. In this study, we investigate the population and dynamical evolution of exocomets orbiting Proxima Centauri, leveraging high-resolution spectroscopic observations alongside N-body simulations of multi-planet interactions. By characterizing transient Balmer-alpha absorption signatures linked to evaporating bodies on highly eccentric trajectories, we constrain the spatial distribution, mass-loss rates, and collisional cascade properties of the outer volatile reservoir. Our dynamical models reveal that secular perturbations induced by the super-Earth companion can efficiently funnel icy planetesimals across the snow line, maintaining a sustained flux of volatiles toward the circumstellar habitable zone throughout the system’s mature phase. Quantitative integration of these trajectories indicates that exocometary accretion could deliver water masses equivalent to multiple terrestrial oceans, heavily dependent on the primordial disk’s surface density profile and photoevaporative dispersal timescale. Such sustained volatile replenishment implies that Proxima Centauri b likely underwent prolonged hydrospheric development driven by stochastic bombardment events rather than solely nebular condensation. Collectively, these findings establish exocometary transport as a pivotal pathway for ocean genesis around magnetically active M dwarfs, highlighting the imperative for next-generation high-dispersion spectroscopy to directly probe volatile delivery architectures in resolved exoplanetary environments. These constraints will guide forthcoming observational campaigns targeting analogous young stellar systems.

title: Tidal evolution and diffusive growth during high-eccentricity planet migration: revisiting the eccentricity distribution of hot Jupiters
text_ai: High-eccentricity tidal migration is a potential formation channel for hot Jupiters. During this process, the planetary f-mode may experience a phase of diffusive growth, allowing its energy to quickly build up to large values. In Yu et al. (2023), we demonstrate that stochastic forcing during periastron passages drives a random-walk amplification of the fundamental mode, significantly accelerating orbital circularization. Here, we extend this framework by incorporating nonlinear mode coupling and frequency-dependent tidal dissipation into a comprehensive population synthesis model. We perform Monte Carlo simulations tracking the coupled evolution of orbital elements and stellar/planetary internal oscillations across a broad parameter space, varying initial semi-major axes, inclinations, and dynamical friction timescales. Our results reveal that diffusive f-mode excitation preferentially preserves moderate residual eccentricities ($e \gtrsim 0.1$) even after extensive tidal circularization, producing a bimodal eccentricity distribution that closely matches recent spectroscopic measurements of inflated gas giants. Furthermore, we find that the transition from diffusive to linear damping regimes critically depends on the tidal quality factor $Q'_p$, with lower values suppressing the high-eccentricity tail. These findings resolve longstanding discrepancies between theoretical predictions and observed hot Jupiter populations, suggesting that past studies underestimated the role of mode saturation in halting orbital decay. We conclude that high-eccentricity migration remains viable only when f-mode diffusive growth is explicitly accounted for, offering a unified explanation for the prevalence of slightly eccentric hot Jupiters and their anomalous radii. Future high-precision radial velocity campaigns targeting multi-planet architectures will provide decisive observational tests of this mechanism.

title: An Optimal Algorithm for Computing the Spherical Depth of Points in the Plane
text_ai: For a distribution function $F$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and a point $q\in \mathbb{R}^d$, the \emph{spherical depth} $\SphD(q;F)$ is defined to be the probability that a point $q$ is contained inside a random closed hyper-ball obtained from a pair of points from $F$. The spherical depth $\SphD(q;S)$ is also defined for an arbitrary data set $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and $q\in \mathbb{R}^d$. In this work, we present a deterministic algorithm that computes the exact spherical depth for every point in a planar dataset of size $n$ in optimal $O(n \log n)$ time. By exploiting the geometric structure of circular arrangements, our method circumvents the naive quadratic enumeration of all $\binom{n}{2}$ defining balls. We introduce a radial sweep framework coupled with a dynamic interval tree that tracks containment probabilities as angular sectors are processed. This decomposition reduces the combinatorial overhead while preserving exactness under mild general position assumptions. We rigorously prove that both time and space complexities are asymptotically tight within the algebraic decision tree model. Additionally, we analyze numerical stability and provide a robust floating-point implementation that mitigates precision errors arising from degenerate configurations. Our findings resolve a longstanding computational bottleneck in robust multivariate analysis, offering practitioners a scalable tool for contour extraction and outlier detection. Extensive benchmarks against existing heuristic methods confirm substantial runtime reductions across varied data distributions, validating theoretical predictions and demonstrating immediate applicability in high-throughput statistical pipelines. Extensions to weighted samples and parallel variants preserve optimality. Code is released for community validation.

The spherical depth $\SphD(q;S)$ is also defined for an arbitrary data set $S\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ and $q\in \mathbb{R}^d$.

title: Current laboratory performance of starlight suppression systems, and potential pathways to desired Habitable Worlds Observatory exoplanet science capabilities
text_ai: We summarize the current best polychromatic (10 to 20 % bandwidth) contrast performance demonstrated in the laboratory by different starlight suppression approaches and systems designed to directly characterize exoplanets around nearby stars. We present results obtained by internal coronagraph and external starshade experimental testbeds using entrance apertures equivalent to off-axis or on-axis telescopes, either monolithic or segmented. Across multiple test campaigns, we evaluate how wavefront sensing, active correction, and diffractive masking strategies scale with aperture size and spectral coverage. Coronagraphic architectures demonstrate robust integration efficiency and compact packaging but require stringent mid-spatial-frequency error control and complex Lyot stop optimization. Conversely, starshade concepts offer superior rejection at small inner working angles and relaxed wavefront tolerances, though they demand precision formation flying and deployable geometry stability. We quantify the residual leakage mechanisms—including chromatic phase errors, segment phasing residuals, and scatter from microroughness—and map these degradation channels against the Habitable Worlds Observatory’s baseline requirement of 10⁻¹⁰ contrast at 0.1 arcseconds. By synthesizing empirical data with scaling models, we identify critical technology readiness gaps in broadband high-order adaptive optics, low-stress membrane manufacturing, and closed-loop formation control. Our analysis outlines near-term developmental milestones and architecture trade studies that align current testbed achievements with HWO’s science-driven performance thresholds. Ultimately, this work provides a consolidated benchmark to guide investment prioritization, inform system-level architectural decisions, and accelerate the transition toward flight-ready starlight suppression hardware capable of delivering definitive biosignature detections.

title: Spatiotemporal model of a key step in endocytosis: SNX9 recruitment via phosphoinositides
text_ai: Clathrin mediated endocytosis (CME) is an ubiquitous cellular pathway that regulates central aspects of cell physiology such as nutrient uptake, modulation of signal transduction, synaptic transmission and membrane turn-over. Endocytic vesicle formation depends on the timed production of specific phosphoinositides and their interactions with various endocytic proteins. Despite extensive characterization of individual components, the quantitative dynamics governing Sorting Nexin 9 (SNX9) recruitment to nascent clathrin-coated pits remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we develop a reaction-diffusion framework that explicitly couples spatial phosphoinositide gradients with SNX9 binding kinetics to resolve this temporal bottleneck. Our model integrates experimentally derived rate constants for PI(4,5)P2 synthesis and hydrolysis with SNX9’s PX domain affinity profiles, simulating recruitment across varying membrane curvatures and lipid compositions. Simulations reveal that SNX9 accumulation exhibits a sharp threshold response strictly dependent on localized PI(4,5)P2 enrichment, which is further modulated by actin polymerization feedback. Parameter sensitivity analysis identifies phospholipase C activity and SNX9 diffusion coefficients as primary determinants of recruitment timing. Crucially, model predictions align quantitatively with live-cell fluorescence recovery after photobleaching and super-resolution microscopy data, confirming that transient phosphoinositide microdomains drive efficient SNX9 capture. Collectively, this spatiotemporal formalism not only elucidates the mechanistic basis of early endocytic maturation but also provides a predictive toolkit for probing how lipid dysregulation perturbs vesicular trafficking in disease contexts. By bridging molecular biochemistry with systems-level dynamics, our work establishes a generalizable paradigm for understanding protein-lipid coalescence during membrane remodeling.

title: NuSTAR + XMM-Newton monitoring of the neutron star transient AX J1745.6-2901
text_ai: AX J1745.6-2901 is a high-inclination (eclipsing) transient neutron star (NS) Low Mass X-ray Binary (LMXB) showcasing intense ionised Fe K absorption. We present here the analysis of 11 XMM-Newton and 15 NuSTAR new data-sets (obtained between 2013-2016), therefore tripling the number of observations of AX J1745.6-2901 in outburst. By combining multi-epoch spectroscopy with broadband coverage spanning 0.5–78 keV, we construct a comprehensive evolutionary track of the system’s accretion flow and circumstellar environment throughout the outburst decay phase. Our spectral decomposition reveals that the Fe K absorption complexes are best described by a partially covering, highly ionized wind with log ξ varying from 3.5 to 5.2 erg s cm⁻¹. The ionization parameter correlates tightly with the unabsorbed 2–10 keV flux, supporting a disk-wind origin launched via radiation pressure on iron lines. Furthermore, timing analysis uncovers quasi-periodic oscillations in the 0.1–0.3 Hz range whose centroid frequency scales inversely with the equivalent width of the Fe XXV/XXVI resonance lines. These temporal signatures suggest coupling between the inner accretion disk and the outflowing material. Photoionization modeling indicates mass-loss rates reaching 10⁻⁸ M☉ yr⁻¹, sufficient to impact the binary’s angular momentum budget. Collectively, our expanded sample demonstrates that AX J1745.6-2901 follows the canonical luminosity-dependent wind evolution seen in Galactic transients, while its eclipsing geometry uniquely permits probing of the absorber’s spatial structure. This work establishes AX J1745.6-2901 as a critical laboratory for studying magnetically channeled accretion and radiatively driven outflows in the Galactic Center environment.

title: Transcriptional Similarity in Couples Reveals the Impact of Shared Environment and Lifestyle on Gene Regulation through Modified Cytosines
text_ai: Gene expression is a complex and quantitative trait that is influenced by both genetic and non-genetic regulators including environmental factors. Evaluating the contribution of environment to gene expression regulation and identifying which genes are more likely to be influenced by environmental factors are important for understanding human complex traits. Here, we investigate transcriptional concordance between long-term romantic partners to disentangle shared environmental influences from inherited regulatory patterns. Using paired whole-transcriptome sequencing and whole-genome bisulfite sequencing from 186 couple dyads, we quantified genome-wide co-expression networks and correlated them with locus-specific DNA methylation profiles. We observed significantly elevated transcriptional similarity among cohabiting partners compared to sex-matched unrelated controls, particularly across immune response, metabolic, and stress-response pathways. This concordance strongly covaried with shared lifestyle variables, including dietary patterns, physical activity levels, and socioeconomic status. Statistical modeling confirmed that methylation changes at CpG sites near transcription start sites significantly predicted expression covariance (p < 0.001). Furthermore, longitudinal analyses indicated that transcriptional alignment increased with duration of cohabitation, suggesting cumulative epigenetic adaptation. Mechanistically, differentially methylated cytosines at promoter and enhancer regions accounted for a substantial proportion of partner-specific expression overlap, indicating that environmentally driven epigenetic remodeling directly modulates transcriptional output. Our findings demonstrate that prolonged co-residence induces measurable convergence in gene regulatory landscapes, primarily mediated by cytosine modifications responsive to shared behavioral and ecological exposures. These results underscore the plasticity of the human epigenome and establish a framework for linking communal lifestyles to molecular phenotypes relevant to disease susceptibility and clinical translation.

title: Intra-abdominal hypertension and the abdominal compartment syndrome
text_ai: The pressure within the abdominal cavity is normally little more than atmospheric pressure. However, even small increases in intra-abdominal pressure can have adverse effects on renal function, cardiac output, hepatic blood flow, respiratory mechanics, splanchnic perfusion and intracranial pressure. Consequently, the progressive elevation of intra-abdominal pressure precipitates a cascade of hemodynamic and metabolic derangements that culminate in multiorgan dysfunction syndrome. When sustained, this pathophysiological continuum defines intra-abdominal hypertension, which may rapidly evolve into abdominal compartment syndrome—a life-threatening surgical emergency characterized by end-organ hypoperfusion and irreversible tissue ischemia. Despite its well-documented morbidity and mortality, particularly in critically ill patients following major trauma, acute pancreatitis, or massive fluid resuscitation, abdominal compartment syndrome remains underrecognized in contemporary intensive care practice. Accurate diagnosis necessitates standardized intra-abdominal pressure monitoring, typically via indirect transvesical measurement, alongside rigorous application of consensus diagnostic criteria. Therapeutic intervention hinges on timely escalation from conservative measures, including sedation, neuromuscular blockade, and gastrointestinal decompression, to definitive surgical decompressive laparotomy when medical management fails. This review synthesizes current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathogenesis, and optimal management algorithms for intra-abdominal hypertension and abdominal compartment syndrome. Emphasis is placed on early recognition protocols, risk stratification frameworks, and emerging adjunctive therapies designed to mitigate secondary organ injury. By integrating contemporary guideline recommendations with practical clinical insights, this article aims to standardize diagnostic approaches and optimize therapeutic decision-making, ultimately reducing preventable mortality and improving outcomes in critically ill surgical populations.

title: Two-year follow-up of mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists for chronic central serous chorioretinopathy.
text_ai: To evaluate the long-term oral mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRa) treatment in chronic central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Patients with chronic non-resolving CSC (defined as foveal subretinal fluid (SRF) lasting >4 months with retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) alterations) treated with MRa only (eplerenone or spironolactone) for at least 6 months were retrospectively included. Clinical and optical coherence tomography parameters were assessed at baseline, 6, 12, and 24 months. Primary outcomes included complete SRF resolution and changes in central subfield thickness (CST). Secondary outcomes comprised best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) gains, relapse rates, and adverse events. Of 87 eligible eyes, median follow-up was 24.2 months. Complete SRF resolution was achieved in 54.0% at 6 months, increasing to 71.3% by month 24. Mean CST decreased significantly from 412 ± 68 μm at baseline to 248 ± 41 μm at 2 years (p<0.001). BCVA improved by 9.2 ETDRS letters over the follow-up period. Relapse occurred in 18.4% of initial responders, typically within 12 months upon dose reduction. Treatment was well-tolerated; mild hyperkalemia and gynecomastia prompted temporary discontinuation in two patients. Multivariate analysis identified baseline CST >450 μm as an independent predictor of incomplete response. Dose titration based on clinical response further optimized outcomes without compromising safety profiles. Long-term oral MRa therapy demonstrates sustained anatomical and functional benefits in chronic CSC. These findings support extended MRa regimens as a viable conservative management strategy, warranting routine ophthalmic and metabolic monitoring.

title: A GPU-accelerated Large-scale Simulator for Transportation System Optimization Benchmarking
text_ai: With the development of artificial intelligence techniques, transportation system optimization is evolving from traditional methods relying on expert experience to simulation and learning-based decision and optimization methods. Learning-based optimization methods require extensive interactions with highly realistic microscopic traffic simulators. However, conventional CPU-bound simulators struggle to meet these computational demands, creating a critical bottleneck for scalable algorithm development and rigorous benchmarking. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel GPU-accelerated microscopic traffic simulator specifically designed for large-scale transportation system optimization. Our architecture leverages massive parallelism through custom CUDA kernels, enabling real-time state updates for tens of thousands of interacting vehicles while preserving agent-level behavioral fidelity. We implement a heterogeneous memory management scheme that minimizes host-device data transfer overhead and integrate a high-throughput event-driven scheduling mechanism optimized for modern graphics processing units. Comprehensive benchmarking across metropolitan road networks demonstrates that our framework achieves up to 48× speedup over leading CPU-based alternatives without compromising simulation accuracy or convergence properties. Extensive ablation studies confirm that parallelized vehicle kinematics and intersection control logic maintain numerical stability across extended simulation horizons. Furthermore, we establish a standardized evaluation protocol to assess policy performance under varying traffic densities and infrastructure configurations. By bridging the gap between computational efficiency and microscopic realism, this simulator provides a robust foundation for next-generation reinforcement learning agents and enables systematic comparison of emerging optimization strategies. Our open-source release aims to accelerate research in intelligent transportation systems and foster reproducible, large-scale benchmarking communities.

title: Nature of excitons bound to inversion domain boundaries: Origin of the 3.45-eV luminescence lines in spontaneously formed GaN nanowires on Si(111)
text_ai: We investigate the 3.45-eV luminescence band of spontaneously formed GaN nanowires on Si(111) by photoluminescence and cathodoluminescence spectroscopy. This band is found to be particularly prominent for samples synthesized at comparatively low temperatures. At the same time, these samples exhibit a peculiar morphology, namely, isolated long nanowires are interspersed within a dense matrix of short ones. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy reveals that the elongated structures contain a high density of basal-plane inversion domain boundaries, whereas the shorter counterparts remain largely defect-free. Correlating spectroscopic data with structural analysis demonstrates that the 3.45-eV emission originates from excitons localized at these planar defects. Temperature-dependent measurements indicate a binding energy of approximately 30 meV, consistent with Coulombic confinement rather than donor-acceptor transitions. Spatially resolved cathodoluminescence mapping confirms that intensity maxima precisely overlap with regions exhibiting inverted polarity domains. We propose that the reduced growth temperature kinetically favors polar surface reconstruction, thereby promoting antiphase domain nucleation that coalesces into extended inversion boundaries. Spectral linewidth narrowing at cryogenic temperatures suggests minimal disorder scattering, indicating well-defined potential minima along the IDBs. These results establish a direct structure–property relationship between spontaneous nanowire morphology and defect-bound optical transitions, resolving longstanding ambiguities regarding the 3.45-eV feature in group-III nitrides. Ultimately, this work establishes a scalable route for engineering polarity-defect quantum emitters by tuning kinetic growth parameters during vapor-phase epitaxy, offering new insights into defect physics in polar semiconductors.

title: Current irritability robustly related to current and prior anxiety in bipolar disorder.
text_ai: Although current irritability and current/prior anxiety have been associated in unipolar depression, these relationships are less well understood in bipolar disorder (BD). We investigated relationships between current irritability and current/prior anxiety as well as other current emotions and BD illness characteristics. Participants comprised 142 adults meeting DSM-5 criteria for bipolar I or II disorder, recruited from outpatient mood clinics. Standardized instruments assessed irritability, state anxiety, and depressive severity, supplemented by structured interviews capturing lifetime anxiety diagnoses and comprehensive psychiatric history. Multiple linear regressions evaluated predictors of irritability while controlling for antidepressant use, manic symptomatology, and illness duration. Current irritability exhibited strong positive associations with both concurrent anxiety (β = .51, p < .001) and prior anxiety diagnoses (β = .44, p < .001), persisting after adjustment for depressive severity and psychotropic burden. Lifetime manic/hypomanic episode count correlated modestly with irritability (r = .29, p = .006), whereas suicide attempt history, substance use disorders, and illness duration failed to reach significance when anxiety metrics were included. Subgroup analyses confirmed analogous patterns across bipolar I and II diagnostic categories without significant moderating effects. These data demonstrate that irritability in bipolar disorder is specifically and robustly anchored to anxiety dimensions rather than general illness chronicity or manic polarity. Clinically, these results suggest that standard mood stabilization protocols may require integrated anxiolytic targeting to optimize outcomes in anxious-irritable phenotypes. Longitudinal investigations are warranted to determine whether this comorbidity delineates distinct neurocircuitry or represents a shared stress-hyperreactivity phenotype requiring tailored intervention.

We investigated relationships between current irritability and current/prior anxiety as well as other current emotions and BD illness characteristics.

title: RIDCP: Revitalizing Real Image Dehazing via High-Quality Codebook Priors
text_ai: Existing dehazing approaches struggle to process real-world hazy images owing to the lack of paired real data and robust priors. In this work, we present a new paradigm for real image dehazing from the perspectives of synthesizing more realistic hazy data and introducing more robust priors into the network. Specifically, we devise a physics-informed haze synthesis pipeline that integrates atmospheric scattering models with conditional diffusion guidance, yielding diverse yet photorealistic hazy-clean image pairs without manual annotation. To capture complex haze distributions, we construct a high-quality codebook prior through clustering latent features extracted from clean reference images. This discrete representation serves as a structural anchor, enabling the network to learn explicit haze-to-clear mappings while preserving fine textures and color fidelity. The proposed RIDCP framework seamlessly embeds these codebook priors within a multi-scale feature fusion module, leveraging adaptive attention mechanisms to dynamically weigh prior relevance across varying haze densities. Furthermore, a consistency regularization term enforces physical plausibility during training, mitigating over-smoothing and artifact generation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world datasets demonstrate that RIDCP significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Quantitative evaluations reveal improvements of up to 1.8 dB in PSNR and 0.04 in SSIM, while perceptual metrics confirm superior visual quality and structural preservation. By bridging the gap between simulated training distributions and real-world degradation patterns, our approach establishes a scalable, prior-driven framework for practical dehazing applications in autonomous driving, remote sensing, and mobile photography.

title: Vegetarianism and veganism compared with mental health and cognitive outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
text_ai: Vegetarian and vegan diets are increasing in popularity. Although they provide beneficial health effects, they may also lead to nutritional deficiencies. Cognitive impairment and mental health disorders have a high economic burden. A meta-analysis was conducted to examine the relationship between vegan or vegetarian diets and cognitive and mental health. Electronic databases were systematically searched through October 2023. Observational studies and randomized controlled trials comparing adherents of vegetarian or vegan diets with omnivores were included. Primary outcomes encompassed depressive symptoms, anxiety, and standardized cognitive assessments. Pooled effect estimates were derived using random-effects models, with heterogeneity quantified via I² statistics and publication bias assessed through funnel plots and Egger’s test. Subgroup analyses stratified by study design, dietary adherence, and demographic covariates were performed. The final synthesis incorporated twelve studies comprising 187,452 participants. Compared with omnivorous controls, plant-based dietary patterns demonstrated a modest but statistically significant association with reduced depressive symptomatology (standardized mean difference = −0.18; 95% CI: −0.31 to −0.05), whereas no significant differences were observed for anxiety disorders or global cognitive performance. Heterogeneity was moderate across mental health outcomes (I² = 46%), and sensitivity analyses confirmed result robustness. These findings suggest that vegetarian and vegan diets may confer selective psychological benefits without adversely impacting cognitive function, though residual confounding by lifestyle factors cannot be excluded. Future longitudinal investigations with rigorous nutritional profiling are warranted to optimize dietary recommendations for mental well-being.

title: The ileal FGF15/19 to hepatic FGFR4 axis regulates liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in mice.
text_ai: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) has been considered to modulate liver regeneration (LR) after partial hepatectomy (PH) at the tissue level. Previous studies have demonstrated that FGF15 and FGF19 induce the activation of its receptor, FGF receptor 4 (FGFR4), which can promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and regulate liver lipid metabolism. However, whether this enterohepatic signaling cascade directly orchestrates compensatory hepatocyte proliferation following PH remains unclear. Here, we investigated the functional role of the ileal FGF15/19–FGFR4 axis in murine LR using hepatocyte-specific knockout models and targeted pharmacological inhibition. Postoperative kinetics of circulating bile acids, ileal Fgf15 transcription, and hepatic FGFR4 activation were quantified alongside histomorphometric analysis of liver mass restoration and Ki-67 labeling indices. We found that PH robustly induced ileal Fgf15 expression and systemic FGF15 elevation, which coincided with peak hepatic FGFR4 phosphorylation and downstream STAT3 activation. Notably, circulating FGF19 mirrored these temporal dynamics, confirming enterohepatic ligand delivery as the principal trigger. Hepatocyte-specific deletion of Fgfr4 resulted in markedly blunted proliferative responses, delayed parenchymal regeneration, and sustained proinflammatory cytokine production relative to wild-type littermates. Administration of recombinant FGF19 partially rescued regenerative capacity in knockout mice only upon intact receptor availability. Moreover, selective FGFR4 kinase inhibition abolished STAT3 nuclear translocation and downregulated Cyclin D1, establishing strict pathway dependence. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the ileal FGF15/19–hepatic FGFR4 axis functions as a primary endocrine driver of LR via STAT3-dependent mitogenic cascades. Modulating this gut-liver communication network presents a promising translational avenue for augmenting hepatic recovery following major resection.

title: Optimized quantum implementation of elliptic curve arithmetic over binary fields
text_ai: Shor's quantum algorithm for discrete logarithms applied to elliptic curve groups forms the basis of a "quantum attack" of elliptic curve cryptosystems. To implement this algorithm on a quantum computer requires the efficient implementation of the elliptic curve group operation. Such an implementation requires we be able to compute inverses in the underlying field. Over binary extension fields, conventional inversion strategies incur prohibitive quantum resource costs due to deep reversible arithmetic circuits and extensive ancilla allocation. We present a novel framework for optimizing finite field inversion that minimizes both logical gate count and circuit depth while maintaining strict reversibility requirements. By exploiting the algebraic structure of normal bases and integrating a streamlined modular reduction pipeline, our construction reduces the asymptotic T-gate complexity from O(m² log m) to O(m¹·⁵⁸) through recursive subfield decomposition and optimized quantum Fourier transforms. We further demonstrate how this inversion primitive can be tightly coupled with point addition and doubling operations, yielding a fully integrated elliptic curve scalar multiplication routine. Comprehensive fault-tolerant resource estimates indicate a 42% reduction in total surface code cycles compared to prior reversible implementations, with ancilla reuse protocols keeping physical qubit overhead below 10⁵ for NIST P-256 equivalent parameters. We introduce a parameterized compilation strategy that dynamically balances T-depth and qubit allocation according to available hardware constraints. Collectively, these optimizations enable scalable quantum cryptographic analysis while providing concrete benchmarks for assessing post-quantum security margins against fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Reflection on young adult transitional care in the boston children's hospital perioperative care coordination clinic.
text_ai: The complexity of pediatric healthcare has increased due to advancement in research and identification of new treatment modalities. With these advancements, life expectancy has increased creating a greater need for young adult transition into adult medical settings and specialty care (Marani et al., 2020). This paper reflects on clinical experiences within the Perioperative Care Coordination Clinic at Boston Children’s Hospital to examine systemic barriers and facilitators in transitioning medically complex adolescents and young adults. Through a structured reflective framework, we analyze interdisciplinary workflows, communication protocols, and patient-centered readiness assessments that shape successful handoffs to adult-oriented services. Key observations highlight persistent gaps in health literacy, fragmented electronic health record integration, and variable provider preparedness across pediatric and adult specialties. The clinic’s standardized transition curriculum, paired with longitudinal case management and shared decision-making models, demonstrates measurable improvements in appointment adherence and reduced perioperative complications during the transition window. Nevertheless, structural limitations including funding constraints, inconsistent insurance coverage, and geographic disparities continue to impede equitable access. We propose integrating predictive risk stratification tools, expanding peer-led transition support programs, and standardizing competency-based training for both pediatric and adult clinicians. These strategies aim to foster continuity, enhance self-advocacy skills, and mitigate care fragmentation. Ultimately, sustainable transition frameworks require institutional commitment, cross-system collaboration, and ongoing evaluation of patient-reported outcomes. By embedding reflective practice into perioperative care coordination, institutions can better align developmental milestones with clinical readiness, ensuring vulnerable populations navigate the shift to adult care with resilience.

title: Beyond the Meta: Leveraging Game Design Parameters for Patch-Agnostic Esport Analytics
text_ai: Esport games comprise a sizeable fraction of the global games market, and is the fastest growing segment in games. This has given rise to the domain of esports analytics, which uses telemetry data from games to inform players, coaches, broadcasters and other stakeholders. Current analytical frameworks, however, remain heavily constrained by transient meta shifts, requiring frequent model retraining after each title update and severely limiting longitudinal comparability. To address this limitation, we introduce a patch-agnostic analytical paradigm that abstracts high-level gameplay patterns from volatile meta-dependent features by explicitly modeling intrinsic game design parameters. Our methodology employs a hierarchical representation learning architecture that encodes static mechanical attributes—such as movement vectors, ability cooldown structures, and spatial control metrics—into invariant feature embeddings. We validate our approach across three competitive seasons of a leading multiplayer online battle arena title, comparing against conventional patch-specific gradient boosting and graph neural network baselines. Experimental results demonstrate that parameter-grounded models maintain predictive accuracy within 4.2% of patch-tuned counterparts while eliminating the computational overhead associated with continuous fine-tuning. Furthermore, ablation studies confirm that explicit integration of design constraints significantly improves out-of-distribution generalization during transitional update periods. Production deployment confirms reduced inference latency and enhanced interpretability. By decoupling analytical signals from ephemeral strategic trends, this work establishes a sustainable foundation for cross-season performance evaluation, automated scouting systems, and real-time tactical decision support within dynamic competitive environments. Ultimately, leveraging foundational design parameters enables analysts to substantially transcend meta volatility, fostering more robust, interpretable, and temporally consistent esports intelligence pipelines.

title: Galactic Stellar and Substellar Initial Mass Function
text_ai: We review recent determinations of the present day and initial mass functions in various components of the Galaxy, disk, spheroid, young and globular clusters. As a general feature, the IMF is well described by a power-law form for $m\ga 1 \msol$ and a lognormal form below. This transition typically occurs near $0.5\,\msol$, consistent with the peak of the stellar number distribution. In the substellar regime, observations reveal a steep decline toward planetary masses, though recent deep imaging and microlensing campaigns suggest a possible flattening or turnover near $0.01\,\msol$. Environmental dependencies remain contested; while field populations exhibit remarkable uniformity, extreme starburst environments and dense cluster cores show evidence for top-heavy variants, likely driven by enhanced accretion rates and dynamical hardening. We critically assess systematic uncertainties arising from binary fraction modeling, mass segregation, and observational incompleteness, demonstrating that corrected present-day mass functions converge closely to their initial counterparts above $0.1\,\msol$. Moreover, the integration of multi-wavelength data pipelines reduces selection biases masking the lowest-mass objects. Theoretical frameworks linking turbulent fragmentation, disk accretion histories, and competitive feeding zones naturally reproduce the observed bimodality without invoking fundamental changes in the underlying physics. Collectively, these results constrain star formation efficiency across galactic scales and provide a robust baseline for population synthesis models, chemical enrichment calculations, and exoplanet demographic studies. Future high-resolution integral-field spectroscopy and space-based infrared surveys will further resolve low-mass endpoints and clarify whether local variations reflect transient dynamical states or persistent environmental regulation.

title: Long-segment posterior cervical decompression and fusion: does caudal level affect revision rate?
text_ai: Posterior cervical decompression and fusion (PCDF) is a commonly performed procedure to address cervical myelopathy. A significant number of these patients require revision surgery for adjacent-segment disease (ASD) or pseudarthrosis. Currently, there is no consensus among spine surgeons on the inclusion of proximal thoracic spine instrumentation. This retrospective cohort study evaluated whether the distal instrumented level influences postoperative revision requirements following extensive cervical arthrodesis. We identified 312 consecutive patients who underwent multilevel PCDF extending to the upper thoracic spine between 2015 and 2022. Patients were stratified into three groups based on the most caudal fused vertebra: group 1 (C7–T1), group 2 (C7–T2), and group 3 (C7–T3). Primary outcomes included time-to-revision surgery for mechanical failure, symptomatic pseudarthrosis, or clinically significant ASD. Multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression adjusted for age, comorbidities, smoking status, and baseline radiographic parameters. Over a mean follow-up of 38 months, the overall revision rate was 14.1%. Stratified analysis revealed significantly higher revision frequencies in group 1 (21.3%) compared to group 2 (11.8%) and group 3 (8.4%; p=0.032). Hazard ratios indicated that instrumenting through T1 independently increased the risk of subsequent intervention (HR 1.89, 95% CI 1.12–3.19; p=0.018). Extended thoracic extension beyond T2 demonstrated comparable biomechanical stability with reduced complication profiles. Collectively, these robust findings suggest that limiting caudal instrumentation to T2 optimizes the balance between mechanical support and long-term construct survival. Practicing spine surgeons should consistently consider this evidence when planning extensive cervical reconstructions to minimize revision burden and improve patient outcomes.

title: Windows over a New Low Energy Axion
text_ai: We outline some general features of possible extensions of the Standard Model that include anomalous U(1) gauge symmetries, a certain number of axions and their mixings with the CP-odd Higgs sector. As previously shown, after the mixing one of the axions becomes a physical pseudoscalar (the axi-Higgs) that can take the role of a modified QCD axion. We demonstrate how the resulting mass spectrum and interaction eigenstates depend critically on the underlying charge assignments and symmetry-breaking scales. By enforcing anomaly cancellation conditions and perturbative unitarity, we identify viable regions of parameter space where the axi-Higgs remains sufficiently light while evading stringent astrophysical bounds. In these alignment-dominant regimes, the effective couplings to fermions and gauge bosons exhibit characteristic scaling patterns that open distinct discovery windows across both fixed-target facilities and high-luminosity hadron colliders. We quantify the sensitivity reach for next-generation beam-dump experiments and precision measurements of electric dipole moments, showing that sub-GeV mass ranges remain largely unexplored yet highly accessible through resonant production channels. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of non-perturbative QCD effects on the axi-Higgs potential, demonstrating that thermal corrections during the early universe naturally select a stable vacuum configuration compatible with current dark matter relic abundance constraints. Our results establish a robust phenomenological framework connecting ultraviolet-complete gauge extensions to observable low-energy signatures, providing concrete targets for upcoming intensity-frontier programs and guiding the interpretation of anomalous flavor transitions and missing-energy signals in existing datasets.

title: Forced-induced desorption of a polymer chain adsorbed on an attractive surface - Theory and Computer Experiment
text_ai: We consider the properties of a self-avoiding polymer chain, adsorbed on a solid attractive substrate which is attached with one end to a pulling force. The conformational properties of such chain and its phase behavior are treated within a Grand Canonical Ensemble (GCE) approach. Within this framework, we derive the exact partition function for chains of varying lengths by mapping the system onto a transfer-matrix formulation that explicitly accounts for both substrate interactions and external tension. To validate the analytical predictions, we conduct extensive computer experiments utilizing off-lattice Monte Carlo sampling combined with pivot and reptation moves, supplemented by rigorous finite-size scaling analysis to locate the desorption threshold accurately. Our results reveal a distinct second-order phase transition driven by the competition between entropic elasticity and adsorption energy. We identify a critical pulling force that scales with chain length as f_c ∼ N^−φ, where φ characterizes the tricritical nature of the adsorption–desorption crossover. Furthermore, we map out the complete phase diagram in the temperature-force plane, demonstrating how increasing tension suppresses the adsorbed plateau and induces a continuous stretching transition. The computed order parameters exhibit universal scaling behavior consistent with tricritical polymers, while the parallel and perpendicular size distributions confirm the expected conformational crossover from flattened coils to extended rods. These findings establish a quantitative link between microscopic interaction strengths and macroscopic mechanical response, providing a robust theoretical foundation for interpreting single-molecule force spectroscopy experiments and designing stimuli-responsive polymeric interfaces.

title: Extracting black-hole rotational energy: The generalized Penrose process
text_ai: In the case involving particles the necessary and sufficient condition for the Penrose process to extract energy from a rotating black hole is absorption of particles with negative energies and angular momenta. No torque at the black-hole horizon occurs. We extend this discrete-particle framework to continuous matter distributions and classical fields, demonstrating that energy extraction remains fundamentally tied to the flux of negative conserved quantities across the event horizon. By analyzing the stress-energy tensor within the Kerr ergoregion, we derive a covariant criterion distinguishing super-radiant amplification from dissipative capture. Our analysis shows that zero-horizon torque persists only when the extracted angular momentum exactly compensates the absorbed negative flux, establishing a strict conservation relation between asymptotic energy gain and horizon area evolution. We further prove that maximal extraction efficiency occurs when the incident field’s phase velocity synchronizes with the horizon’s angular velocity, optimizing coupling to the spacetime’s frame-dragging geometry. Analytical predictions are validated through numerical relativity simulations of scalar and electromagnetic perturbations, achieving peak efficiencies near 20.7% for near-extremal spins. This unified framework reconciles discrete and continuum descriptions under a single geometric principle, offering a rigorous basis for modeling relativistic outflows and accretion dynamics. This resolves tensions in horizon thermodynamics, confirming compatibility with generalized second-law formulations. The resulting formalism directly applies to magnetohydrodynamic models of jet launching, where continuous field-mediated extraction dominates over discrete scattering events across diverse astrophysical environments.

title: When does proton pump inhibitor treatment become long term? A scoping review.
text_ai: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use has risen substantially, primarily driven by ongoing use over months to years. However, there is no consensus on how to define long-term PPI use. Our objectives were to review and compare definitions of long-term PPI use in existing literature and describe the rationale for each definition. A comprehensive scoping search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science from inception to December 2023. Studies reporting explicit time thresholds or duration-based criteria for long-term PPI therapy were included. Two independent reviewers screened records, extracted data, and synthesized definitions using thematic analysis. We identified 87 eligible publications spanning clinical guidelines, pharmacoeconomic evaluations, observational cohorts, and regulatory documents. Definitions varied widely, ranging from ≥8 weeks to ≥3 years, with the most frequently cited threshold being ≥12 months. Rationales were predominantly pragmatic, relying on arbitrary clinical milestones, health economic modeling parameters, or guideline committee conventions rather than robust evidence linking specific durations to distinct pathophysiological outcomes or safety endpoints. Several frameworks incorporated tapering protocols or indication-specific timelines, yet lacked uniform operationalization. The absence of a standardized definition impedes comparability across studies, complicates meta-analytic synthesis, and hinders the development of evidence-based deprescribing pathways. Establishing a consensus framework grounded in clinical indication, therapeutic response, and risk-benefit profiling is essential to optimize prescribing practices, streamline trial design, and inform regulatory policy. Future research should prioritize prospective validation of duration thresholds tied to clinically meaningful outcomes, particularly regarding mucosal healing dynamics and adverse event accrual rates.

title: Searching for exotic object companions in the dense core of NGC 362: a multi-wavelength and multi-epoch photometric analysis
text_ai: The dense cores of globular clusters (GCs) are efficient environments for the production of exotic stellar populations, including millisecond pulsars (MSPs), low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) and cataclysmic variables (CVs). Most of these objects likely form through two- and three-body interactions and are useful tracers of the cluster's dynamical evolution. Here, we present a systematic search for optical counterparts to known and candidate compact binaries within the central parsec of NGC 362. Leveraging deep *Hubble Space Telescope* imaging across multiple epochs, supplemented by *Chandra* X-ray catalogues and adaptive optics photometry, we construct high-resolution color-magnitude diagrams to isolate variable sources. Our multi-band variability analysis identifies several new candidates exhibiting periodic flux modulations consistent with accretion-powered systems. Radial surface density profiles reveal a pronounced central concentration relative to the field population, strongly supporting a dynamically driven formation channel. Cross-referencing our photometric sample with archival radio and X-ray detections yields updated luminosity functions and mass estimates for the binary sequences. The inferred companion mass distribution converges with theoretical models predicting orbital hardening via recoil ejection and mass-exchange reactions in high-density regimes. Notably, the scarcity of detached main-sequence companions implies that rapid mass transfer or common-envelope evolution predominantly shapes the observable population. These results constrain assembly timescales for compact objects and validate synergistic multi-wavelength monitoring for resolving crowded stellar environments. Upcoming *JWST* and *Athena* campaigns will further probe faint companion demographics and quantify dynamical heating governing NGC 362’s core evolution.

title: Basal and stimulated calcitonin levels in patients with type 2 diabetes did not change during 1 year of Liraglutide treatment.
text_ai: The administration of Liraglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist, is associated with C-cell adenomas and carcinomas in rats. In humans, GLP-1R is highly expressed in C-cells hyperplasia (CCH) and in medullary thyroid cancer (MTC), though no changes in basal serum calcitonin (bCT) levels were recorded in type 2 diabetic (T2DM) patients treated with Liraglutide. To further evaluate thyroid C-cell safety, we conducted a prospective, single-arm study enrolling 142 patients with inadequately controlled T2DM. Participants received once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide titrated to 1.8 mg over four weeks and maintained thereafter. Fasting blood samples were collected at baseline, months 3, 6, and 12 to quantify bCT and pentagastrin-stimulated calcitonin (sCT) concentrations using chemiluminescent immunoassays. Changes in hormone levels were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA and linear mixed-effects modeling, stratified by sex and baseline calcitonin quartiles. Across the full cohort, mean bCT remained stable (baseline: 5.2 ± 0.4 pg/mL; month 12: 5.4 ± 0.5 pg/mL; p = 0.61), with no clinically relevant elevations exceeding the upper reference limit. Similarly, peak sCT responses showed negligible variation (baseline: 18.7 ± 1.9 pg/mL; month 12: 19.1 ± 2.0 pg/mL; p = 0.73). Subgroup analyses confirmed consistent stability across sexes and baseline strata. Collectively, these longitudinal data demonstrate that sustained liraglutide therapy fails to trigger C-cell proliferation or calcitonin hypersecretion in human subjects with T2DM. Accordingly, routine biochemical thyroid surveillance remains clinically unwarranted for this demographic, thereby substantiating the favorable oncological safety profile of GLP-1R agonists in human populations despite documented rodent carcinogenicity signals.

title: YouTube as a source of patient information for stroke: A content-quality and an audience engagement analysis.
text_ai: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide following ischemic heart disease, and the fifth in the United States. The video-sharing database, YouTube, is the second most popular visited website with more than 2 billion users, thus it's increasingly being used as a medium for delivering health information. This study evaluates the clinical accuracy and accessibility of stroke-related YouTube videos alongside viewer interaction metrics. A systematic search identified top-ranked educational uploads, which were appraised using the DISCERN instrument and JAMA benchmark criteria to assess content quality, readability, and source transparency. Engagement data, including view counts, like-dislike ratios, comment volume, and upload recency, were extracted and correlated with quality scores via Spearman’s rank and multivariate regression. Among the final sample, only 19.2% met established thresholds for clinical reliability. Flesch-Kincaid scores predominantly exceeded grade-level recommendations for lay comprehension. Videos produced by licensed clinicians or accredited institutions yielded significantly higher quality ratings (p < 0.01). Notably, algorithmic popularity demonstrated no positive correlation with content validity; highly viewed videos frequently contained factual inaccuracies and lacked verifiable citations. Statistical modeling confirmed these associations independent of publication timing. These results demonstrate that while YouTube functions as a pervasive conduit for stroke education, significant disparities in medical rigor persist. Clinicians and public health entities should implement structured digital triage strategies and endorse evidence-based institutional channels to safeguard patient decision-making against unverified online health narratives.

title: Terminal Brain Damage: Exposing the Graceless Degradation in Deep Neural Networks Under Hardware Fault Attacks
text_ai: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have been shown to tolerate "brain damage": cumulative changes to the network's parameters (e.g., pruning, numerical perturbations) typically result in a graceful degradation of classification accuracy. However, the limits of this natural resilience are not well understood in the presence of small adversarial changes to the DNN parameters' underlying memory representation, such as bit-flips that may be induced by hardware fault attacks. To bridge this critical gap, we systematically evaluate the vulnerability of state-of-the-art convolutional and transformer-based architectures to targeted and random bit-flip injections across multiple memory layers. Using a combination of emulation-based fault modeling and physical voltage-glitching experiments on FPGA-deployed inference engines, we quantify the relationship between fault density, spatial distribution, and downstream performance collapse. Our findings reveal a sharp phase transition from nominal tolerance to catastrophic accuracy loss, contradicting the prevailing assumption of continuous error surfaces. We demonstrate that as few as 0.05% corrupted weights can trigger deterministic classification failures, particularly when faults concentrate within attention mechanisms and early-layer feature extractors. Furthermore, we introduce a novel metric, the Terminal Damage Threshold, which precisely characterizes the inflection point where incremental hardware errors induce non-linear model rupture. Extensive ablation studies confirm that conventional redundancy techniques offer negligible protection against spatially correlated bit-flips. These results fundamentally challenge current fault-tolerance paradigms and underscore the necessity for architecture-aware hardening strategies, including redundant encoding and dynamic fault isolation, to secure deployed neural systems.

title: Quasar Photometric Redshifts and Candidate Selection: A New Algorithm Based on Optical and Mid-Infrared Photometric Data
text_ai: We present a new algorithm to estimate quasar photometric redshifts (photo-$z$s), by considering the asymmetries in the relative flux distributions of quasars. The relative flux models are built with multivariate Skew-t distributions in the multi-dimensional space of relative fluxes as a function of redshift and magnitude. By jointly exploiting optical and mid-infrared bands, the framework captures the characteristic spectral energy distribution breaks and power-law continua that distinguish active galactic nuclei from stellar and galactic contaminants. The model parameters are constrained through hierarchical Bayesian inference calibrated against a spectroscopically verified reference catalogue spanning $0.5 < z_{\mathrm{spec}} < 6.5$. Cross-validation tests reveal that our approach maintains stable convergence even in regimes of low signal-to-noise ratio and heavy blending. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a normalized median absolute deviation of $\sigma_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.036$ and suppress catastrophic outliers ($|\Delta z|/(1+z) > 0.15$) to 3.2\%, substantially improving upon conventional template-matching pipelines, particularly beyond $z \gtrsim 4$ where UV absorption edges migrate into the infrared window. Crucially, the explicit modeling of flux asymmetry yields a quasar candidate purity of 94\% at completeness levels above 88\%, eliminating the need for redundant spectroscopic vetting. When applied to mock catalogues representative of the Rubin Observatory LSST and Euclid mission footprints, the algorithm accelerates source classification by an order of magnitude while preserving the statistical integrity of luminosity functions. This capability proves essential for managing the data volumes expected from modern transient surveys, directly supporting time-domain astrophysics and precision cosmology initiatives.

The relative flux models are built with multivariate Skew-t distributions in the multi-dimensional space of relative fluxes as a function of redshift and magnitude.

title: Fully On-board Low-Power Localization with Multizone Time-of-Flight Sensors on Nano-UAVs
text_ai: Nano-size unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) hold enormous potential to perform autonomous operations in complex environments, such as inspection, monitoring or data collection. Moreover, their small size allows safe operation close to humans and agile flight. An important part of autonomous flight is localization, which is a computationally intensive task especially on a nano-UAV that usually has strong constraints in sensing, processing and memory. To address these limitations, we present a fully on-board localization framework specifically designed for resource-constrained nano-UAVs. Our approach leverages multizone time-of-flight (ToF) sensors combined with a novel edge-optimized filtering architecture that minimizes data throughput and eliminates reliance on external positioning systems. By exploiting spatial redundancy across multiple sensor zones, the system achieves robust depth estimation while maintaining a peak power consumption below 180 mW. The core algorithm integrates lightweight scan-matching and probabilistic state estimation directly onto a commercial microcontroller unit, bypassing the need for dedicated graphics or neural processing units. We validate the proposed methodology through rigorous flight experiments in GPS-denied indoor corridors and cluttered industrial settings. Results demonstrate sub-meter position accuracy and centimeter-level rotational consistency at 30 Hz update rates, even under dynamic lighting and reflective surfaces. Furthermore, continuous operation over extended real-world missions confirms thermal stability and sustained energy efficiency. Consequently, this research establishes a scalable pathway for deploying field-deployable autonomous nano-UAV swarms in infrastructure inspection and search-and-rescue applications where weight, power, and computational budgets are strictly limited.

Moreover, their small size allows safe operation close to humans and agile flight. An important part of autonomous flight is localization, which is a computationally intensive task especially on a nano-UAV that usually has strong constraints in sensing, processing and memory.

title: Closure of Secundum Atrial Septal Defects by Using the Occlutech Occluder Devices in More Than 1300 Patients: The IRFACODE Project: A Retrospective Case Series.
text_ai: The Occlutech Figulla ASD device series (OFSO) shows an improved device design for interventional ASD closure, larger follow-up series are missing. We retrospectively reviewed the feasibility, safety, implantation properties, results, and follow-up of ASD closure using Occlutech devices over a 5 year period by establishing a multi-institutional collaborative result registry with 16 contributing centers from 11 countries (IRFACODE). Between January 2015 and December 2020, data from 1342 consecutive patients undergoing transcatheter secundum ASD closure were analyzed. Mean patient age was 48.2 ± 18.7 years, with a median defect diameter of 18 mm. Technical success was achieved in 98.6% of procedures, with a mean procedural time of 32 ± 15 minutes. Acute complications occurred in 2.1% of cases, primarily consisting of transient arrhythmias (1.3%) and minor vascular access issues (0.7%). Device embolization required surgical retrieval in 0.4% of patients. At a median follow-up of 36 months, echocardiographic evaluation demonstrated complete device integration in 97.8%, with only 1.2% exhibiting residual shunting less than 2 mm. Left atrial and right ventricular dimensions significantly regressed post-procedure (p < 0.001). Major adverse cardiac events remained low at 1.8% during long-term surveillance. These findings confirm that OFSO occluders provide high technical success, excellent hemodynamic recovery, and a favorable safety profile in contemporary practice, supporting their role as a reliable therapeutic option for anatomically suitable secundum defects.

title: First Light Curve Analysis of NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her Contact Binary Systems
text_ai: The first photometric light curve investigation of the NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her binary systems is presented. We used ground-based observations for the NSVS 8294044 system and Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) data for V1023 Her and V1397 Her. Differential photometry was performed to extract precise magnitude measurements, which were subsequently analyzed using the Wilson–Devinney computational code. Derived geometric and physical parameters reveal that all three objects are deep overcontact binaries with contact degrees exceeding 65%, indicating efficient thermal coupling between components. Orbital solutions yield periods ranging from 0.38 to 0.52 days, with mass ratios spanning 0.18–0.32. O–C diagram analyses indicate secular period changes driven primarily by continuous mass transfer from the more massive to the less massive star, alongside possible magnetic activity cycles on the cooler component. The derived absolute magnitudes and effective temperatures align with standard main-sequence sequences, though slight deviations suggest enhanced chromospheric emission typical of magnetically active contact configurations. Comparative analysis with established Galactic contact binaries places these systems within the late stages of conservative evolution, where angular momentum loss via gravitational radiation and stellar winds dominates orbital decay. These findings establish a foundational photometric characterization for future spectroscopic follow-up and refine empirical mass–radius relations for low-mass interacting binaries.

title: Mental well-being among the oldest old: revisiting the model of healthy ageing in a Finnish context.
text_ai: Purpose : This study aimed to examine how participants aged 80 years old or over describe their mental well-being-exploring the suitability of the model of healthy ageing when outlining the mental well-being concept. Methods : Six structured focus group interviews with 28 participants were conducted in Western Finland in 2017. Results : Thematic analysis revealed that the oldest old conceptualised mental well-being primarily through subjective life satisfaction, emotional regulation, and preserved autonomy rather than functional independence or disease absence. Participants consistently highlighted relational connectedness, meaningful daily routines, and adaptive acceptance of biological decline as core determinants. Although components of the established healthy ageing model aligned with their accounts—particularly concerning cognitive vitality and community involvement—the framework proved insufficient in capturing the profound influence of existential purpose and reciprocal family support. Respondents characterised well-being as fluidly reconstructed across later life stages, thereby contesting the model’s underlying assumption of static optimisation. Conclusions : The current healthy ageing paradigm necessitates substantive revision to accommodate the lived experiences of nonagenarians. Policy and clinical strategies must therefore foreground psychosocial resilience, intentional social integration, and individualised conceptions of psychological thriving. Integrating these insights will facilitate more ecologically valid gerontological models and strengthen targeted mental health promotion within Scandinavian ageing cohorts.

title: Next generation testing strategy for assessment of genomic damage: A conceptual framework and considerations.
text_ai: For several decades, regulatory testing schemes for genetic damage have been standardized where the tests being utilized examined mutations and structural and numerical chromosomal damage. This has served the genetic toxicity community well when most of the substances being tested were amenable to such assays. However, the rapidly expanding portfolio of novel chemical entities, engineered nanomaterials, complex biological therapeutics, and multifaceted environmental mixtures has progressively exposed the intrinsic limitations of these conventional paradigms. Traditional end-points frequently lack the sensitivity and mechanistic resolution required to characterize non-directly genotoxic agents that operate through chromatin remodeling, spindle apparatus disruption, oxidative stress cascades, transient DNA-protein crosslinking, or epigenetic dysregulation. Consequently, a fundamental reevaluation of testing architectures is imperative to capture early molecular perturbations, distinguish reversible adaptive responses from irreversible genomic injury, and predict long-term carcinogenic potential with enhanced fidelity. This paper presents a unified conceptual framework designed to transition genetic toxicology from isolated endpoint monitoring toward integrated, mechanism-driven genomic damage assessment. The proposed model synthesizes high-content screening platforms, multi-omics profiling, adverse outcome pathway (AOP) networks, and quantitative computational modeling into a cohesive evaluation cascade. By embedding experimental design within a systems toxicology context, the framework enables the systematic tracking of key events spanning initial molecular initiating events to downstream cellular phenotypes. Tiered testing sequences are central to the architecture, prioritizing rapid transcriptomic and epigenetic signature detection for primary hazard flagging, followed by orthogonal validation using functional assays calibrated for DNA repair kinetics, micronucleus induction frequencies, and chromosomal breakage patterns. This hierarchical progression maximizes throughput while preserving analytical rigor, thereby optimizing resource deployment across preclinical development pipelines. Computational toxicology serves as the integrative backbone, leveraging machine learning algorithms trained on curated historical datasets to extract latent structure-toxicity relationships. Predictive models are continuously refined through iterative feedback loops incorporating multi-omics outputs, enabling the generation of context-dependent quantitative structure-activity relationships applicable to chemically diverse scaffolds. Integration of physiologically based pharmacokinetic simulations further bridges the in vitro-in vivo extrapolation gap by converting nominal compound concentrations into tissue-relevant exposure metrics, substantially improving physiological relevance and reducing false-positive rates driven by metabolic artifacts or nonspecific cytotoxicity. Regulatory adoption of these advanced modalities requires meticulous method harmonization and transparent validation roadmaps. We advocate for internationally coordinated standardization initiatives addressing cell source authentication, culture medium composition, passaging limitations, batch-effect correction, and standardized bioinformatic preprocessing pipelines. Interlaboratory proficiency studies are recommended to establish reproducibility benchmarks, define limit of detection thresholds for rare mutagenic events, and certify platform readiness for guideline incorporation. The framework explicitly accommodates existing regulatory trajectories, including revisions to OECD test guidelines, ICH S2(R2) expansions, and EPA ToxCast/Tox21 modernization efforts, ensuring seamless compatibility with current compliance structures. Reference materials, certified control compounds, and benchmark dose modeling tools are proposed as essential infrastructure to guarantee cross-platform comparability and longitudinal data integrity. Ethical imperatives underpinning the reduction of vertebrate animal testing are intrinsically aligned with the framework’s design, satisfying the 3Rs principles and accelerating the transition toward fully alternative testing strategies. Practical implementation barriers—including data siloing, algorithmic opacity, storage requirements for high-dimensional datasets, and workforce competency gaps—are addressed through recommendations for open-access repository deployment, containerized analysis environments, modular software licensing, and interdisciplinary training curricula bridging molecular biology, bioinformatics, and regulatory science. Dynamic risk characterization modules embedded within the framework quantify parameter uncertainty, incorporate inter-individual variability distributions, and facilitate probabilistic safety margin calculations, thereby supporting more nuanced threshold determinations for susceptible demographic subsets. Economic scalability is considered through phased implementation pathways that allow industries to adopt compatible subsystems incrementally without requiring wholesale laboratory restructuring. Continuous post-market surveillance linkages are proposed to validate predictive performance against epidemiological and clinical outcomes, establishing real-world evidence feedback channels that inform subsequent framework iterations. Ultimately, this conceptual architecture aims to catalyze a systemic evolution in genetic damage evaluation, replacing legacy endpoint dependency with holistic, mechanism-informed genomic surveillance networks. Successful translation demands sustained collaboration among academic researchers, commercial laboratories, regulatory authorities, and standards organizations to align methodological innovation with policy expectations. Widespread integration of these next-generation strategies will substantially improve hazard discrimination accuracy, compress development timelines, lower attrition rates, and strengthen public health safeguards against emerging genotoxic threats. Ongoing investment in analytical infrastructure, algorithmic validation, and regulatory harmonization will be indispensable to actualize the envisioned testing paradigm. As scientific capabilities mature and institutional frameworks converge, the outlined considerations provide a comprehensive, actionable blueprint for modernizing genomic damage assessment in contemporary toxicological practice.
