title: Reflection on modern methods: visualizing the effects of collinearity in distributed lag models.
text_ai: Collinearity can be a problem in regression models. When examining the effects of an exposure at different time points, constrained distributed lag models can alleviate some of the problems caused by collinearity. Still, some consequences of collinearity may remain and they are often unexplored. To address this gap, we employ extensive simulation studies and empirical applications to illustrate how residual multicollinearity systematically distorts coefficient estimates, confidence intervals, and temporal effect profiles in penalized and spline-based lag structures. We introduce a novel diagnostic visualization framework that maps variance inflation trajectories across lag windows and reveals hidden parameter trade-offs. Our approach synthesizes dynamic heatmaps of correlation matrices with plotted stability regions for estimated lag-response curves, enabling researchers to precisely identify periods where collinearity-induced uncertainty is most pronounced. Simulation results demonstrate that even under stringent regularization, high inter-lag correlation inflates standard errors asymmetrically, frequently yielding spurious null findings or artificially inflated peak effects depending on the chosen penalty structure. In two environmental epidemiology case studies, our diagnostic plots uncovered substantial lag-dependent instability that conventional summary statistics completely obscured. By integrating these visual diagnostics into routine analytical workflows, practitioners can rigorously evaluate model robustness, communicate estimation uncertainty transparently, and prevent overconfident causal interpretations. This methodological reflection ultimately underscores the critical necessity of explicit collinearity assessment within contemporary time-series and environmental health modeling.

title: Impact of macronutrient supplements for children born preterm or small for gestational age on developmental and metabolic outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
text_ai: Nutritional supplements may improve development of infants born small (preterm or small for gestational age [SGA]) but may increase the risk of later metabolic disease. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the effects of macronutrient supplements for infants born small on later development and metabolism. Electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Web of Science) were searched from inception through December 2023. Eligible studies comprised randomized controlled trials evaluating early postnatal macronutrient supplementation—protein, lipid emulsions, or energy-dense formulations—versus standard care in preterm (<37 weeks’ gestation) or small for gestational age infants. Primary endpoints included standardized neurodevelopmental assessments at 18 to 24 months corrected age, school-age cognitive testing, and longitudinal metabolic indicators such as body mass index z-scores, fasting glucose and insulin concentrations, lipid panels, and blood pressure measurements. Secondary outcomes tracked anthropometric trajectories including weight, length, and head circumference percentiles. Independent data extraction followed PRISMA directives. Risk of bias and GRADE certainty ratings were independently applied. Meta-analytic pooling utilized random-effects models, accounting for expected clinical heterogeneity. Between-study variance was quantified using Cochran’s Q and I² statistics. Pre-planned subgroup examinations stratified by birth cohort characteristics, supplement composition, treatment duration, and initial nutritional status were executed. Publication asymmetry was interrogated through funnel plots and Egger’s regression. Forest plots visualized pooled effect sizes alongside 95% prediction intervals to account for between-trial variability. Twenty-three trials encompassing 4,187 participants satisfied inclusion criteria. Early macronutrient augmentation significantly enhanced composite neurodevelopmental performance at 18 to 24 months (standardized mean difference [SMD] 0.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.12 to 0.44; I² = 62%), with robust advantages across cognitive (SMD 0.31, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.48) and psychomotor domains (SMD 0.26, 95% CI 0.09 to 0.43). Longitudinal school-age evaluations from seven centers confirmed persistent gains in full-scale intelligence quotient metrics (SMD 0.22, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.39). Anthropometric surveillance indicated accelerated weight accrual during infancy (mean difference +0.42 kg, 95% CI +0.28 to +0.56) and superior linear growth velocity throughout the first twenty-four months. Metabolic phenotyping demonstrated no clinically meaningful elevation in pediatric adiposity indices (BMI z-score SMD 0.11, 95% CI −0.04 to 0.26; I² = 58%). Fasting insulin levels remained statistically equivalent between cohorts (SMD 0.08, 95% CI −0.15 to 0.31), while homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance exhibited negligible intergroup variation. Comprehensive lipid profiles and resting blood pressure at preschool intervals showed no significant divergence. Subgroup interactions tested via meta-regression confirmed that gestational age and protein dosage independently moderated neurodevelopmental response magnitudes. Confidence in neurodevelopmental findings was rated moderate, whereas metabolic endpoint certainty remained low secondary to heterogeneous assays and differential loss-to-follow-up. Exclusion of high-risk trials preserved all primary effect directions. Collectively, these synthesized data demonstrate that early macronutrient fortification in preterm and SGA populations delivers reproducible neurocognitive benefits without exacerbating cardiometabolic vulnerability markers throughout childhood. These results advocate for precision-guided protein and caloric enrichment within contemporary neonatal practice. Subsequent investigations must establish uniform metabolic biomarker panels, extend follow-up into adolescence, and elucidate optimal dosing architectures to maximize therapeutic efficacy.

title: Gluten-Free Products: From Dietary Necessity to Premium Price Extraction Tool.
text_ai: Every year, the Italian National Health Service (NHS) provides about 200,000 celiac people (based on 2017 data) living in Italy with financial support of about 250 million euro to cover the cost of their specific dietary constrains. However, contemporary market dynamics reveal a rapid commercialization of gluten-free goods that increasingly transcends medical necessity. This study examines the economic mechanisms driving price premiums in the Italian gluten-free sector, analyzing retail pricing trends, consumer demand patterns, and marketing strategies directed at both diagnosed celiacs and the broader wellness-oriented population. Using retail transaction data and consumer surveys, we estimate demand elasticities and quantify welfare transfers generated by non-medical purchasing. Our findings indicate that gluten-free products consistently carry markups ranging from 150% to 300% above conventional equivalents, predominantly sustained by perceived health narratives rather than nutritional differentiation. Crucially, over sixty percent of sales originate from consumers without celiac diagnosis, suggesting a structural decoupling between public subsidy objectives and actual market consumption. These results underscore significant inefficiencies in the current reimbursement framework and highlight the potential for strategic pricing exploiting information asymmetries. We recommend recalibrating NHS eligibility criteria, implementing targeted price monitoring, and strengthening labeling regulations to align public expenditure with genuine clinical needs while preserving market integrity.

title: Spurious modes in extended RPA theories
text_ai: Necessary conditions that the spurious state associated with the translational motion and its double-phonon state have zero excitation energy in extended RPA (ERPA) theories which include both one-body and two-body amplitudes are investigated using the small amplitude limit of the time-dependent density-matrix theory (STDDM). By mapping the STDDM equations onto the ERPA eigenvalue problem, we derive explicit constraints linking the one-body transition densities to the two-body correlation functions. These constraints reveal that exact cancellation of the spurious energy requires a strict balance between the direct and exchange contributions of the effective interaction, alongside a consistent treatment of the Pauli-blocking terms within the two-body amplitude sector. We demonstrate that standard truncation schemes often violate this balance, leading to finite spurious energies that compromise the physical interpretation of low-lying collective excitations. To restore translational invariance, we propose a modified closure relation that enforces the vanishing of the spurious mode without altering the genuine response channels. Numerical tests within a Skyrme-Hartree-Fock framework confirm that the proposed adjustment eliminates the spurious shift while preserving the strength distribution of genuine giant resonances. These findings establish a rigorous criterion for constructing consistent ERPA extensions, thereby improving the reliability of beyond-mean-field descriptions of nuclear dynamics and informing the development of next-generation energy density functionals.

title: DiffPoint: Single and Multi-view Point Cloud Reconstruction with ViT Based Diffusion Model
text_ai: As the task of 2D-to-3D reconstruction has gained significant attention in various real-world scenarios, it becomes crucial to be able to generate high-quality point clouds. Despite the recent success of deep learning models in generating point clouds, there are still challenges in producing high-fidelity results due to the disparities between images and point clouds. To address these limitations, we introduce DiffPoint, a novel diffusion-based framework that bridges the semantic and geometric gap between 2D observations and 3D representations. Our approach leverages a ViT encoder to extract robust multi-scale features from single or multiple input views, which are then seamlessly integrated into a denoising diffusion model. By conditioning the reverse diffusion process on transformer-derived embeddings, DiffPoint effectively preserves fine-grained structural details while ensuring topological consistency across diverse object categories. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both qualitative fidelity and quantitative metrics, including Chamfer Distance and F-Score. Notably, the architecture maintains computational efficiency through a streamlined latent-space sampling strategy, enabling practical deployment in limited hardware settings. These findings underscore the potential of combining transformer-based feature extraction with diffusion modeling for accurate, scalable point cloud reconstruction, paving the way for advanced applications in robotics, augmented reality, and digital twin generation.

title: A brain proteomic investigation of rapamycin effects in the Tsc1+/- mouse model.
text_ai: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare monogenic disorder characterized by benign tumors in multiple organs as well as a high prevalence of epilepsy, intellectual disability and autism. TSC is caused by inactivating mutations in the TSC1 or TSC2 genes. Given that the TSC1/TSC2 heterodimer negatively regulates the mechanistic target of rapamycin complex 1 (mTORC1), hyperactivation of this signaling cascade constitutes the primary pathogenic mechanism driving aberrant cellular growth and synaptic dysfunction. Rapamycin, a specific mTORC1 inhibitor, has demonstrated clinical efficacy in reducing tuber volume and mitigating seizures; however, its comprehensive impact on the cerebral proteome remains poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we performed quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomics on whole-brain lysates derived from adult Tsc1+/- mice following chronic rapamycin treatment versus vehicle controls. Samples were processed through tandem mass tag labeling, followed by high-resolution liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry and rigorous bioinformatic filtering to identify differentially expressed proteins with statistical significance (adjusted p < 0.05, fold change > 1.5). Pathway enrichment and protein-protein interaction network analyses were subsequently conducted to map altered biological processes. Proteomic quantification was rigorously validated using parallel reaction monitoring against independently prepared cohorts, confirming reproducibility across biological replicates. Additionally, spatial transcriptomic correlation supported the regional specificity of identified protein shifts within hippocampal and cortical subfields. Our dataset revealed robust modulation of over four hundred cerebral proteins, with significant downregulation of translation initiation factors, ribosomal subunits, and cell cycle regulators consistent with targeted mTORC1 suppression. Strikingly, rapamycin administration also induced compensatory upregulation of autophagy-related proteins, synaptic vesicle cycling components, and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation complexes. Network topology analysis highlighted a central regulatory hub encompassing cytoskeletal remodeling proteins and neuroinflammatory mediators, suggesting that therapeutic intervention extends beyond canonical metabolic pathways. Notably, proteins associated with dendritic spine morphogenesis and long-term potentiation exhibited normalized expression profiles, providing a molecular correlate for observed improvements in cognitive behavioral assays. Conversely, incomplete reversal of certain glial activation markers and persistent alterations in extracellular matrix organization underscored partial efficacy of single-agent therapy. These findings delineate a multidimensional proteomic landscape underlying mTOR hyperactivity and its pharmacological correction in TSC. By identifying both directly suppressed effectors and secondary adaptive responses, our data establish a comprehensive framework for understanding rapamycin’s pleiotropic actions within the central nervous system. Furthermore, the discovery of partially resilient pathways points toward rational combination strategies targeting parallel signaling nodes to achieve fuller neurological restoration. Collectively, this study not only validates the translational relevance of the Tsc1+/- murine model but also provides a prioritized catalog of candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets for next-generation precision interventions in tuberous sclerosis complex. Future investigations will leverage these proteomic signatures to stratify patient responses and optimize dosing regimens for sustained cognitive preservation.

title: Strategic Play By Resource-Bounded Agents in Security Games
text_ai: Many studies have shown that humans are "predictably irrational": they do not act in a fully rational way, but their deviations from rational behavior are quite systematic. Our goal is to see the extent to which we can explain and justify these deviations as the outcome of rational but resource-bounded agents doing as well as they can, given their limitations. We operationalize this perspective through a computational model of defenders and attackers operating under strict cognitive and temporal constraints within multi-stage security games. By limiting lookahead depth and heuristic decision rules, our framework captures how bounded deliberation shapes equilibrium selection and pattern formation. Simulation results demonstrate that when agents optimize locally rather than globally, their strategies exhibit structured biases consistent with empirical human data in cyber and physical defense scenarios. These patterns emerge not as cognitive errors but as adaptive responses to information scarcity and computation costs. Furthermore, we show that introducing modest informational feedback mitigates suboptimal clustering without requiring unbounded reasoning capacity. The findings bridge theoretical game theory with behavioral economics, offering actionable insights for designing security protocols that anticipate and accommodate realistic agent limitations rather than assuming perfect rationality. Treating boundedness as a structural feature rather than a defect yields robust defensive postures in adversarial environments.

title: Contextual Hybrid Session-based News Recommendation with Recurrent Neural Networks
text_ai: Recommender systems help users deal with information overload by providing tailored item suggestions to them. The recommendation of news is often considered to be challenging, since the relevance of an article for a user can depend on a variety of factors, including the user's short-term reading interests, the reader's context, or the recency or popularity of an article. To address these complexities, we propose a contextual hybrid session-based framework that leverages recurrent neural networks to model evolving user preferences within discrete browsing sessions. Our approach integrates multi-source contextual signals, such as temporal dynamics, location metadata, and real-time engagement cues, into a unified sequence representation. By employing a gated recurrent unit architecture augmented with attention mechanisms, the model captures both latent sequential patterns and explicit contextual dependencies. We evaluate our framework on benchmark news datasets, comparing it against established session-based baselines. Experimental results demonstrate statistically significant improvements in prediction accuracy, particularly in capturing abrupt interest shifts and long-tail article recovery. Ablation studies confirm the complementary contributions of contextual embeddings and recurrent session modeling. This work establishes a robust foundation for adaptive news delivery platforms, offering practitioners a scalable architecture that balances personalization with serendipity while maintaining computational efficiency. Future extensions will explore cross-session knowledge transfer and dynamic context weighting to further enhance recommendation resilience across diverse consumption scenarios.

title: Duration of antibody response following vaccination against feline immunodeficiency virus.
text_ai: Objectives Recently, two point-of-care (PoC) feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) antibody test kits (Witness and Anigen Rapid) were reported as being able to differentiate FIV-vaccinated from FIV-infected cats at a single time point, irrespective of the gap between testing and last vaccination (0-7 years). To empirically validate these claims across extended post-vaccination intervals and assess the temporal dynamics of antigen-specific antibody persistence under controlled experimental conditions. A prospective longitudinal cohort comprising 62 clinically normal, seronegative domestic cats was enrolled and stratified via block randomization into vaccination (n=31; intradermal administration of licensed whole-virion FIV vaccine) and unvaccinated control (n=31) groups. Venous blood collections occurred at baseline, day 28, and biannually through month 84. Paired serum aliquots underwent parallel screening using Witness and Anigen Rapid lateral flow devices, corroborated by validated recombinant protein ELISAs and immunoblotting procedures. Epitope-specific binding profiles were generated through competitive inhibition assays utilizing synthetic gp40, gp120, and p24 peptides. Kinetic parameters were modeled employing generalized estimating equations with autoregressive correlation structures, while diagnostic performance metrics were calculated via receiver-operating characteristic curve analyses. Sample processing adhered strictly to cold-chain preservation protocols, minimizing freeze-thaw artifacts. Inter-assay coefficients of variation remained below 8.5% across all calibration runs. Initial seroconversion manifested uniformly within 21 days post-immunization, yielding >98% sensitivity against reference standards during the first 24 months. Nevertheless, assay discrimination progressively attenuated thereafter. By month 36, false-positive classifications escalated to 19.6% for Witness and 16.2% for Anigen Rapid, driven primarily by sustained low-affinity IgG reactivity toward conserved capsid determinants. Multivariate decomposition indicated that the gp40/p24 binding ratio served as the most robust predictive marker, yet fell below optimal cutoff thresholds at month 42. Specificity estimates regressed to 89.3% (95% CI: 81.7–94.1) by the final evaluation period, fundamentally contradicting prior assertions of indefinite diagnostic stability. Unvaccinated subjects maintained unequivocal negativity throughout the study duration without serological crossover. Receiver operating characteristic optimization identified a modified optical density threshold that restored specificity to 96.1% during months 48–60, albeit with reduced early-detection sensitivity. Stratified analysis confirmed no significant confounding effects from breed, age, or concurrent FeLV exposure. Cross-validation with nested PCR confirmed zero endogenous viral replication in all designated vaccinated subjects, thereby isolating assay interference as the sole etiology for late-stage discordance. Logistic regression demonstrated that booster vaccinations initiated after year three temporarily elevated signal intensities but failed to reset the underlying epitope-binding profile. Implementation of dual-assay reflex protocols substantially improved positive predictive value, reducing misclassification events by 64% compared to monolithic testing paradigms. Contemporary rapid immunochromatographic platforms demonstrate reliable short-term utility for post-vaccination screening but lack durability beyond three to four years. Clinicians must therefore contextualize isolated positive outputs within comprehensive patient histories, prioritizing PCR-based viral load quantification for ambiguous cases. Regulatory bodies should mandate explicit labeling regarding temporal efficacy boundaries to prevent diagnostic overreach in shelter medicine and multi-cat household settings. These kinetic insights necessitate a paradigm shift from static cutoff interpretations toward dynamic, interval-adjusted reference ranges. Laboratories should adopt tiered confirmation algorithms incorporating recombinant glycoprotein displacement assays before rendering definitive infectious status determinations. Public messaging must emphasize that prolonged seropositivity alone does not justify quarantine in managed colony environments. Harmonized validation guidelines requiring standardized challenge models will ensure cross-study comparability. Standardized reporting of interval-specific sensitivity curves will facilitate evidence-based revision of vaccination schedules and improve resource allocation for targeted serosurveillance initiatives. Continuous refinement of assay design parameters will safeguard rapid testing utility while preserving ethical standards in companion animal healthcare.

title: METTL3-mediated m6A methylation negatively modulates autophagy to support porcine blastocyst development‡.
text_ai: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) catalyzed by METTL3 regulates the maternal-to-zygotic transition in zebrafish and mice. However, the role and mechanism of METTL3-mediated m6A methylation in blastocyst development remains unclear. Here, we show that METTL3-mediated m6A methylation sustains porcine blastocyst development via negatively modulating autophagy. To elucidate this mechanism, we performed integrated transcriptomic and methylome analyses across preimplantation stages, identifying a cohort of autophagy-related transcripts bearing METTL3-dependent m6A marks. Functional assays revealed that METTL3 depletion significantly upregulated autophagic flux, as evidenced by elevated LC3-II accumulation and autophagosome formation, which subsequently triggered premature cellular degradation and impaired blastocyst expansion. Mechanistically, METTL3 directly binds to the 3′UTRs of *ATG5* and *LC3B* mRNAs, promoting their destabilization via YTHDF2-mediated decay. Rescue experiments demonstrated that pharmacological inhibition of autophagy or genetic silencing of ATG5 fully restored blastocyst quality in METTL3-deficient embryos. Furthermore, single-cell RNA sequencing corroborated these findings, revealing stage-specific enrichment of m6A-modulated autophagy genes predominantly in trophectoderm lineages. Collectively, our data establish a novel epitranscriptomic regulatory axis wherein METTL3-driven m6A modification fine-tunes autophagic activity, thereby preventing excessive self-digestion and ensuring proper lineage specification and metabolic homeostasis during early mammalian embryogenesis. This study provides critical mechanistic insights into preimplantation development and highlights potential epigenetic targets for optimizing assisted reproductive technologies in livestock.

title: Can Large Language Models Match Tutoring System Adaptivity? A Benchmarking Study
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold promise as dynamic instructional aids. Yet, it remains unclear whether LLMs can replicate the adaptivity of intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)--where student knowledge and pedagogical strategies are explicitly modeled. We propose a prompt variation framework to assess LLM-generated instructional moves' adaptivity and pedagogical soundness across 75 real-world tutoring scenarios from an ITS. Our framework systematically manipulates contextual cues, prior interaction history, and specific error typologies to rigorously evaluate model responsiveness. Quantitative analysis reveals that while contemporary LLMs demonstrate robust surface-level personalization, they consistently underperform compared to engineered ITS in tracking latent cognitive states and delivering temporally coherent scaffolding. Independent expert evaluations indicate that LLM-generated interventions frequently exhibit pedagogical drift, misaligning with evidence-based teaching practices when confronting nuanced misconceptions. Notably, performance disparities widen substantially during extended multi-turn dialogues demanding sustained strategic adaptation. These empirical patterns clearly indicate that standalone generative architectures currently lack the explicit structural constraints required for dependable, classroom-scale educational deployment. To mitigate these limitations, we develop a hybrid prompting protocol integrating formal knowledge-tracing signals into autoregressive generation pipelines, yielding statistically significant gains in both adaptivity fidelity and instructional alignment across diverse subject domains. This research ultimately provides a validated benchmarking infrastructure for educational AI, demonstrating that scalable, pedagogically sound adaptivity necessitates the principled fusion of probabilistic language modeling with computationally explicit instructional theories and learner profiling mechanisms.

title: When Prompt Engineering Meets Software Engineering: CNL-P as Natural and Robust "APIs'' for Human-AI Interaction
text_ai: With the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs), they are increasingly applied in areas like intelligent customer service, code generation, and knowledge management. Natural language (NL) prompts act as the ``APIs'' for human-LLM interaction. To improve prompt quality, best practices for prompt engineering (PE) have been developed, including writing guidelines and templates. However, conventional PE techniques often suffer from brittleness, high cognitive overhead, and inconsistent outputs across diverse model architectures. Bridging this gap requires treating prompt design with the rigor of traditional software engineering. We introduce CNL-P, a structured natural language framework that formalizes prompt construction into modular components inspired by API design principles. CNL-P enforces structural constraints while preserving linguistic fluency, enabling systematic validation, version control, and automated testing of AI interfaces. We evaluate CNL-P across three representative application domains, comparing it against baseline template-based and instruction-tuned prompting strategies. Experimental results demonstrate that CNL-P reduces prompt-induced variance by 68%, improves task completion accuracy under distribution shifts, and lowers developer onboarding time. Furthermore, we release an open-source toolkit that integrates CNL-P compilation directly into standard CI/CD pipelines. This structured approach fundamentally transforms experimentation into a disciplined engineering workflow. These findings establish CNL-P as a scalable, reproducible paradigm for industrial-grade human-AI systems, offering a pathway toward reliable, maintainable, and interoperable language model integration. Future work will extend CNL-P to support multi-modal interfaces and runtime adaptation.

title: Amorphous SiO2 nanoparticles promote cardiac dysfunction via the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore in rat heart and human cardiomyocytes.
text_ai: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are promising systems that can deliver biologically active compounds to tissues such as the heart in a controllable manner. However, cardiac toxicity induced by nanoSiO 2 has been recently related to abnormal calcium handling and energetic failure in cardiomyocytes. Moreover, the precise mechanisms underlying this energetic debacle remain unclear. To elucidate these pathways, we investigated the impact of amorphous nanoSiO2 on mitochondrial integrity and contractile performance using both ex vivo Langendorff-perfused rat hearts and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs). Following systemic administration or direct cellular exposure, nanoSiO2 biodistribution and intracellular localization were quantified via inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy, confirming preferential mitochondrial matrix sequestration. Comprehensive functional assessments revealed a dose-dependent deterioration in left ventricular developed pressure and ejection fraction, paralleled by significant ATP depletion and suppressed maximal respiratory capacity. Advanced electrophysiological recordings and fluorescent Ca2+ imaging demonstrated profound intracellular calcium dysregulation, marked by delayed sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+ transient decay and augmented diastolic Ca2+ leak. Mechanistically, nanoSiO2 exposure precipitated rapid mitochondrial swelling, irreversible collapse of the electrochemical gradient (ΔΨm), and decisive opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP). This pore activation was rigorously validated through dual-calcein cobalt quenching assays, Western blot analysis of intermembrane space protein translocation, and immunofluorescence colocalization of VDAC1 with cyclophilin D. Crucially, pharmacological inhibition of mPTP opening using cyclosporine A or targeted siRNA-mediated knockdown of CypD completely neutralized nanoSiO2-induced bioenergetic failure, reinstated normal Ca2+ cycling kinetics, and preserved myocyte shortening amplitude across both preclinical platforms. Statistical evaluation via repeated-measures ANOVA confirmed highly significant attenuation of contractile decline (p < 0.001) following mPTP blockade. Concurrent multi-omics analyses identified pronounced transcriptional reprogramming favoring pro-apoptotic signaling, mitophagy impairment, and reactive oxygen species amplification, which collectively accelerated pore instability. Notably, variations in nanoparticle surface charge or hydrodynamic diameter failed to mitigate mitochondrial accumulation or subsequent functional deterioration, underscoring the dominance of core material properties over peripheral modifications. Collectively, these results definitively position mPTP hyperpermeabilization as the pivotal molecular switch driving nanoSiO2-associated cardiotoxicity, directly coupling nanomaterial sequestration to sarcomeric dysfunction and metabolic exhaustion. Our work highlights essential biocompatibility benchmarks for silica-driven drug delivery vectors in cardiology and proposes mPTP stabilization as a viable prophylactic strategy against nanoparticle-induced myocardial compromise. By delineating the precise organelle-level events bridging nanotoxicology and cardiac physiology, this investigation establishes a reproducible paradigm for evaluating next-generation cardiovascular nanotherapeutics and informs regulatory frameworks aimed at optimizing clinical translation.

title: Return to Play After Multiligament Knee Injuries in National Football League Athletes.
text_ai: Return to play (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes after isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears has been reported. However, no studies have reported on RTP of NFL athletes after multiligament knee injuries. NFL athletes with multiligament knee injuries have lower RTP rates and longer recoveries than athletes with isolated ACL tears. This retrospective cohort study evaluated professional football players who sustained multiligament knee injuries requiring operative intervention. Eligible participants were identified through institutional sports medicine registries and cross-referenced with comprehensive administrative data verification. Inclusion criteria mandated confirmed disruption of two or more primary stabilizing ligaments, primary reconstructive surgery, and a minimum two-year clinical follow-up. Primary endpoints comprised return-to-play incidence, operationalized as documented participation in at least one regular-season contest, and time to return quantified in days from index procedure. Secondary endpoints incorporated longitudinal performance analytics, including games initiated, offensive and defensive snap distribution, and positional efficiency metrics across the initial three postoperative seasons. Analytical frameworks utilized Kaplan-Meier survival functions and Cox proportional hazards regression to characterize rehabilitation trajectories relative to established benchmarks for isolated anterior cruciate ligament repairs. Among 43 qualifying athletes, predominant injury patterns featured combined cruciate-complex failures and multi-collateral disruptions. The aggregate return-to-play rate reached 67%, accompanied by a median convalescence duration of 405 days. Participants exhibiting concurrent cruciate and collateral pathology experienced markedly prolonged recuperation windows compared to isolated posterior cruciate or medial collateral lesions. Although the majority achieved competitive reinstatement, serial performance evaluation disclosed statistically significant occupational attrition throughout the inaugural postoperative 12-month interval, with parameters gradually normalizing by the third annual cycle. Multivariable modeling identified postponed surgical stabilization and extensive meniscal compromise as independent predictors of delayed rehabilitation. These data highlight the unique physiological and logistical hurdles confronting multiligamentous knee trauma in elite gridiron competitors. Although sustainable return to professional competition remains attainable for most affected individuals, the protracted recovery intervals and temporary functional deficits mandate highly customized, periodized rehabilitation architectures. Sports medicine practitioners must align athlete counseling with empirically derived timelines, clarifying that anatomical restoration does not automatically confer instantaneous pretrauma competency. Subsequent multicenter trials should prioritize standardized surgical algorithms and continuous kinematic surveillance to optimize safe, efficient, and clinically meaningful reintegration pathways within high-velocity collision sports.

title: Hidden momentum and the Abraham-Minkowski debate
text_ai: We use an extended version of electrodynamics, which admits the existence of magnetic charges and currents, to discuss how different models for electric and magnetic dipoles do or do not carry hidden momentum under the influence of external electromagnetic fields. Specifically, we demonstrate that conventional electric dipole models inherently possess position-dependent hidden momentum when subjected to nonuniform magnetic fields, whereas dual-symmetric constructions naturally incorporate compensating terms that preserve total momentum conservation. By systematically comparing point-dipole approximations with distributed charge-current distributions, we establish that the apparent discrepancy between Abraham and Minkowski momenta originates from an incomplete accounting of bound mechanical contributions within polarizable media. Our formulation reveals that each canonical momentum expression corresponds to a distinct partitioning scheme, yet both yield identical observable trajectories once hidden momentum is rigorously included. Furthermore, we derive generalized force-density equations that remain covariant under electric-magnetic duality transformations, thereby unifying previously fragmented treatments of electromagnetic stress-energy transfer. These results clarify longstanding conceptual ambiguities regarding radiation pressure in dielectrics and provide a consistent framework for analyzing momentum exchange in topological insulators and engineered metamaterials. Ultimately, this work reaffirms that all physical predictions are representation-independent, while emphasizing the necessity of explicitly tracking previously overlooked mechanical degrees of freedom in macroscopic electrodynamics.

title: Training and Serving System of Foundation Models: A Comprehensive Survey
text_ai: Foundation models (e.g., ChatGPT, DALL-E, PengCheng Mind, PanGu-$\Sigma$) have demonstrated extraordinary performance in key technological areas, such as natural language processing and visual recognition, and have become the mainstream trend of artificial general intelligence. This has led more and more major technology giants to dedicate significant human and financial resources to actively develop their foundation model systems, which drives continuous growth of these models' parameters. Consequently, designing efficient training and serving infrastructures has emerged as a critical bottleneck, demanding novel architectural paradigms to mitigate escalating computational costs and memory constraints. To systematically address these challenges, this survey presents a comprehensive taxonomy of contemporary foundation model systems, rigorously categorizing them along the lifecycle from distributed pretraining to low-latency deployment. We meticulously review state-of-the-art parallelism strategies, including data, tensor, pipeline, and context parallelism, alongside advanced optimization techniques such as mixed precision training, gradient checkpointing, and adaptive learning rate scheduling. Furthermore, we examine inference acceleration mechanisms encompassing speculative decoding, continuous batching, dynamic sparsity, and weight activation quantization. By synthesizing framework architectures, benchmark evaluations, and industrial implementations, we identify persistent scalability limitations and resource allocation inefficiencies. Finally, we delineate promising research trajectories, emphasizing automated system tuning, heterogeneous hardware co-design, and energy-efficient serving protocols to sustain next-generation intelligent infrastructure.

title: Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure Response to Exercise in Patients with Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis: Determinants and Prognostic Value.
text_ai: Pulmonary hypertension in response to exercise is a marker of the hemodynamic severity of mitral stenosis (MS). However, the factors related to elevated pulmonary pressure with exercise are not well defined. The aim of this study was to assess the parameters associated with the pulmonary pressure response to exercise in patients with pure rheumatic MS. A prospective cohort of 214 consecutive patients with pure rheumatic mitral stenosis underwent stress echocardiography. Exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension was defined as a peak pulmonary artery systolic pressure ≥60 mmHg. Baseline clinical characteristics, resting hemodynamics, biventricular function, and valvular morphology were documented. We evaluated associations between baseline variables and the magnitude of pulmonary artery systolic pressure increment during exercise via multivariable regression. Participants were followed for a median of 48 months for the composite endpoint of heart failure hospitalization, arrhythmia, disease progression, or cardiovascular death. Time-to-event analysis utilized Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for clinical confounders. At baseline, mean age was 58.4 ± 11.2 years, with 71% female. Mean resting pulmonary artery systolic pressure was 38.6 ± 9.4 mmHg, increasing significantly to 64.2 ± 15.8 mmHg at peak exertion (p < 0.001). Multivariable modeling identified larger left atrial volume index (β = 0.31; p = 0.002), smaller mitral valve area (β = −0.28; p = 0.004), elevated resting pulmonary vascular resistance (β = 0.34; p < 0.001), and impaired right ventricular longitudinal strain (β = −0.22; p = 0.008) as independent predictors of exaggerated pressure augmentation. During follow-up, 47 patients (22%) experienced the primary outcome. Peak exercise pulmonary artery systolic pressure >60 mmHg conferred a hazard ratio of 2.87 (95% CI 1.82–4.53; p < 0.001) for adverse events after covariate adjustment. Incorporating exercise-derived pressures into standard risk stratification significantly improved net reclassification improvement by 18.4% (p = 0.003). Exaggerated pulmonary artery systolic pressure augmentation during exertion is primarily driven by severe valvular obstruction, advanced left atrial remodeling, elevated resting pulmonary vascular resistance, and subclinical right ventricular dysfunction. Exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension independently predicts long-term cardiovascular morbidity and mortality beyond resting hemodynamics. Routine stress echocardiography enhances risk stratification in rheumatic mitral stenosis and supports earlier therapeutic intervention prior to irreversible right ventricular compromise.

title: Conservation laws, exact travelling waves and modulation instability for an extended nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
text_ai: We study various properties of solutions of an extended nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger (ENLS) equation, which arises in the context of geometric evolution problems -- including vortex filament dynamics -- and governs propagation of short pulses in optical fibers and nonlinear metamaterials. First, we systematically derive the infinite hierarchy of conservation laws by exploiting the underlying Hamiltonian structure and verifying Liouville integrability through the existence of a Lax pair. Subsequently, we employ the Darboux transformation technique to construct exact travelling wave solutions, encompassing bright and dark solitons as well as periodic cnoidal wave profiles. These analytical constructs are rigorously validated against numerical simulations of the initial value problem. Furthermore, a comprehensive linear stability analysis is conducted to map the modulation instability characteristics across diverse parametric regimes. By solving the characteristic dispersion relation, we explicitly determine the instability growth rates and identify critical threshold conditions where stable propagation transitions to spectral broadening. The derived results demonstrate that higher-order dispersive and nonlinear terms fundamentally alter the bandgap structure and energy localization mechanisms inherent to the classical model. Consequently, these findings provide a unified theoretical framework for predicting pulse evolution in nonlinear media, offering valuable design principles for all-optical switching devices and geometric modeling of macroscopic filamentary structures. Ultimately, this work establishes benchmarks for future investigations into generalized extensions of fundamental wave models.

title: Prognosis of French COVID-19 patients with chronic liver disease: A national retrospective cohort study for 2020.
text_ai: The impact of chronic liver disease on outcomes in patients with COVID-19 is uncertain. Hence, we aimed to explore this association. We explored the outcomes of all adult inpatients with COVID-19 in France, in 2020. We computed adjusted odds ratios to measure the associations between chronic liver disease, alcohol use disorders, mechanical ventilation and day-30 in-hospital mortality. From the national health insurance database, we identified 1,842,631 hospitalizations for severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection among adults aged ≥18 years between March 1 and December 31, 2020. Of these, 12,458 (0.68%) carried a primary or secondary diagnosis of chronic liver disease, while 8,712 (0.47%) presented with comorbid alcohol use disorders. Multilevel logistic regression models controlled for age, sex, comorbidity burden, socioeconomic status, calendar period, and geographic region. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to mitigate confounding by indication. Patients with chronic liver disease demonstrated significantly elevated risks for both invasive mechanical ventilation and day-30 in-hospital mortality compared to non-liver counterparts. Specifically, the adjusted odds ratio for requiring mechanical ventilation was 1.42 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.36–1.48), whereas the adjusted odds ratio for mortality reached 2.18 (95% CI, 2.09–2.27). Stratified analyses revealed that decompensated cirrhosis conferred the highest prognostic burden, with mortality estimates exceeding those observed in compensated disease (adjusted odds ratio, 2.84; 95% CI, 2.61–3.09). Alcohol use disorders independently amplified these adverse trajectories, particularly in cohorts lacking formal cirrhosis documentation, suggesting synergistic hepatic vulnerability. Complete-case and multiple imputation sensitivity analyses yielded concordant effect sizes, confirming robustness against missing data mechanisms and residual confounding. Propensity score matching further corroborated these associations, yielding marginal differences below the pre-specified threshold for clinical significance. These findings establish chronic liver disease as a critical, independent risk stratifier for severe SARS-CoV-2 pathology within contemporary clinical practice. Routine hepatological assessment and early antiviral intervention should be prioritized in this vulnerable population to optimize resource allocation and reduce excess morbidity. Healthcare policymakers should integrate hepatic screening into standardized triage algorithms to ensure equitable distribution of intensive care resources during subsequent pandemic waves. Future prospective investigations must delineate the immunometabolic mechanisms driving hepatic-decompensation cascades during acute viral insult, thereby informing targeted prophylactic protocols across European healthcare systems.

title: Decoupled two-dimensional superconductivity and continuous melting transitions in layered superconductors immersed in a parallel magnetic field
text_ai: Possible phases and the B-T phase diagram of interlayer Josephson vortices induced by a magnetic field parallel to the superconducting layers are investigated by Monte Carlo simulations based on the anisotropic, frustrated XY model. We identify distinct thermodynamic regimes separated by well-defined transition lines that delineate a rigid vortex solid from a disordered liquid state. At low temperatures and intermediate fields, a quasi-two-dimensional superconducting regime emerges wherein interlayer phase coherence is progressively suppressed, yielding independent layer dynamics. The melting of the Josephson vortex lattice proceeds continuously, as evidenced by the absence of thermal hysteresis and the divergence of specific heat anomalies. Finite-size scaling analysis places the transition firmly within the three-dimensional XY universality class, confirming its second-order character. Beyond a critical coupling threshold, the system undergoes a dimensional crossover into a fully decoupled 2D state governed by independent Kosterlitz-Thouless unbinding events within each plane. This decoupling mechanism alters the phase diagram topology, replacing first-order melting lines with continuous boundaries. Critical exponents from Binder cumulant crossings align with O(2) symmetry-breaking predictions across the explored parameter space, corroborating the continuous transition. The interplay between geometric frustration and layer separation suppresses latent heat release. These findings reconcile experimental reports on vortex dynamics in anisotropic compounds and establish a benchmark for interpreting transport data in layered cuprates and organic superconductors.

title: Sparsification and Reconstruction from the Perspective of Representation Geometry
text_ai: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) have emerged as a predominant tool in mechanistic interpretability, aiming to identify interpretable monosemantic features. However, how does sparse encoding organize the representations of activation vector from language models? What is the relationship between this organizational paradigm and feature disentanglement as well as reconstruction performance? We address these questions by analyzing the geometric structure of learned latent spaces through curvature, manifold alignment, and clustering metrics. By systematically varying sparsity constraints and regularization strengths across transformer layers, we quantify how compression alters the intrinsic dimensionality and separation of feature manifolds. Our analysis reveals that optimal reconstruction fidelity coincides with a specific geometric regime where latent features maintain high pairwise orthogonality while preserving local neighborhood structures of the original activations. Contrary to prevailing assumptions, excessive sparsification induces severe topological distortion, degrading both disentanglement and downstream recoverability. Furthermore, we demonstrate that intermediate-layer representations exhibit greater geometric stability under sparsification than output layers, suggesting a hierarchical organization of interpretability. To validate these insights, we conduct extensive empirical evaluations across multiple decoder-only architectures, demonstrating that our geometric criteria consistently predict training dynamics and recovery bounds. Ultimately, this work bridges phenomenological interpretability efforts with rigorous mathematical characterization, providing a unified lens for optimizing sparse latent representations in modern neural networks.

title: Efficacy of the combination of modern medicine and traditional Chinese medicine in pulmonary fibrosis arising as a sequelae in convalescent COVID-19 patients: a randomized multicenter trial.
text_ai: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) has led to a significant number of mortalities worldwide. COVID-19 poses a serious threat to human life. The clinical manifestations of COVID-19 are diverse and severe and 20% of infected patients are reported to be in a critical condition. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and safety of integrating conventional pharmacotherapy with a standardized Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) decoction in managing post-acute pulmonary fibrosis among recovering SARS-CoV-2 individuals. A double-blind, randomized controlled trial was conducted across twelve tertiary medical centers. Eligible participants were adults aged 18–75 years with confirmed prior infection, residual interstitial abnormalities on high-resolution computed tomography, and persistent dyspnea exceeding four weeks post-discharge. Patients were allocated (1:1) to standard-of-care regimens supplemented with either a proprietary TCM formulation targeting qi deficiency and blood stasis or a matched herbal placebo. The primary endpoint was the change in forced vital capacity (FVC) percentage predicted from baseline to week twelve. Secondary outcomes included six-minute walk distance, modified Medical Research Council dyspnea scores, quantitative HRCT fibrosis indices, and circulating TGF-β1 and IL-6 levels. Intention-to-treat analysis employed mixed-effects models. Three hundred twelve participants completed follow-up. At twelve weeks, the combination cohort demonstrated a significantly superior FVC %pred improvement compared to controls (+5.8% ± 2.1 versus +2.3% ± 1.9; P < 0.001). Functional capacity increased by an additional 47 meters in the experimental arm (P = 0.003), accompanied by substantial reductions in dyspnea severity and systemic inflammatory biomarkers. Quantitative imaging confirmed attenuated progression of reticular opacities and honeycombing. Treatment-related adverse events were predominantly mild gastrointestinal disturbances, occurring in 8.2% of recipients versus 6.5% of placebo subjects (P = 0.54). Subgroup analyses stratified by initial disease severity corroborated these primary outcomes, indicating consistent benefit across moderate and severe initial presentations. Integrating targeted TCM therapy with conventional management significantly ameliorates restrictive ventilatory impairment, enhances exercise tolerance, and stabilizes radiographic fibrotic progression in convalescent patients. These findings substantiate the clinical utility of adjunctive herbal interventions within multidisciplinary rehabilitation frameworks for post-viral interstitial lung disease, establishing a foundation for prospective mechanistic studies and standardized clinical guidelines.

title: Decoding and Reconstructing the Focus of Spatial Attention from the Topography of Alpha-band Oscillations.
text_ai: Many aspects of perception and cognition are supported by activity in neural populations that are tuned to different stimulus features (e.g., orientation, spatial location, color). Goal-directed behavior, such as sustained attention, requires a mechanism for the selective prioritization of contextually appropriate representations. One prominent candidate is the modulatory influence of posterior alpha-band oscillations, linked to the active suppression of task-irrelevant cortex and focal enhancement of attended locations. Despite extensive evidence correlating alpha power with attentional state, the precise dynamics encoding specific targets remain poorly characterized. Here, we combine high-density electroencephalography with multivariate pattern analysis to decode and reconstruct the continuous focus of covert spatial attention from scalp-recorded alpha topographies. Participants completed a cue-target paradigm while EEG was recorded at 256 channels. We trained support vector machines and ridge regression models to map inter-hemispheric alpha asymmetry onto exact target coordinates across a full circular visual array. Results demonstrate that attentional focus decodes reliably above chance, with reconstruction accuracy peaking at lateralized occipito-parietal clusters. Temporal generalization matrices reveal these representational codes emerge rapidly following cue onset and persist throughout the maintenance period. Crucially, reconstructed maps exhibit systematic distortions aligning with perceptual resolution biases, suggesting alpha topography encodes a fine-grained parametric representation of attentional weight rather than simple hemispheric inhibition. These findings establish alpha-band potentials as a robust, non-invasive substrate for tracking dynamic allocation of spatial priority.

title: The Milky Way atlas for linear filaments II. clump rotation versus filament orientation
text_ai: Dense clumps distributed along filaments are the immediate medium for star formation. Kinematic properties of the clumps, such as velocity gradient and angular momentum, combined with filament orientation, provide important clues to the formation mechanism of filament-clump configurations and the role of filaments in star formation. In this study, we analyze clump spin vectors relative to local filament axes using the Milky Way Filament Atlas. Combining high-resolution molecular line data with dust continuum maps, we derive angular momentum directions for over two thousand dense cores and reconstruct three-dimensional filament geometries via principal component analysis. We identify a bimodal alignment pattern: most clumps exhibit spin axes preferentially parallel to their host filaments, while the remainder display perpendicular orientations. This dichotomy scales systematically with clump mass and ambient turbulence, indicating that low-mass fragments inherit ordered angular momentum from convergent shear flows along the filamentary network, whereas massive cores undergo isotropic accretion disrupting alignment. Notably, we detect no significant link between spin-filament coherence and subsequent high-mass star formation rates, demonstrating that large-scale gas dynamics alone cannot predict protostellar clustering efficiency. These results support a hierarchical fragmentation model wherein interstellar flows organize material into linear structures, imparting coherent rotation to embedded clumps before local turbulence dominates collapse.

title: National registry of haemophilia and other coagulopathies: A multisector initiative in the Colombian Health System.
text_ai: Haemophilia is an orphan and high-cost disease worldwide and, especially in middle-income countries as Colombia. Given its burden of disease, in 2014, a national administrative registry was created to centralize demographic, clinical and economic information regarding to haemophilia and other coagulopathies. To describe the building and implementation processes of the Colombian registry of haemophilia and other coagulopathies. This prospective observational study employed a mixed-methods approach to map stakeholder engagement, technical architecture, and operational workflows across public and private health entities. Governance was established through a multidisciplinary steering committee comprising clinicians, payers, patient advocacy groups, and Ministry of Health representatives. Data integration leveraged interoperable electronic health records aligned with international classification standards, ensuring real-time validation and longitudinal tracking. Implementation spanned three phases: pilot deployment in six regional hubs, nationwide scaling, and continuous quality audits. Within the first two years, the registry captured data on over 1,800 patients, achieving 89% completeness for core clinical variables and demonstrating significant reductions in unreported bleeding episodes. The initiative successfully harmonised fragmented reporting mechanisms, enabling evidence-based budget forecasting and targeted therapeutic access. Findings underscore that sustainable rare-disease surveillance in resource-constrained settings requires explicit multisectoral coordination, standardised data protocols, and institutionalised funding streams. This framework offers a replicable model for middle-income nations seeking to optimise haemophilia care delivery and health technology assessment.

title: The role of ambient temperature and body mass on body temperature, standard metabolic rate and evaporative water loss in southern African anurans of different habitat specialisation.
text_ai: Temperature and water availability are two of the most important variables affecting all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes such as body temperature ( T b ), evaporative water loss (EWL) and standard metabolic rate (SMR). To elucidate how these factors interact across ecological gradients, we measured Tb, SMR, and EWL in 24 species representing distinct habitat specialisations across southern Africa’s arid, semi-arid, and mesic biomes. Individuals were acclimated to a controlled thermal regime (15–35 °C) while maintaining optimal hydration, allowing us to isolate the independent and interactive effects of ambient temperature (Ta) and body mass on physiological performance. Generalised linear mixed models revealed that Ta exerted a strong positive correlation with both SMR and Tb, consistent with ectothermic thermodynamics, but this relationship was significantly modulated by habitat type. Desert-specialist species exhibited flatter thermal slopes for SMR and markedly reduced EWL compared to their mesic counterparts, demonstrating adaptive constraints on cutaneous permeability and respiratory water loss. Body mass scaled predictably with all three parameters, yet the allometric exponents varied substantially among habitat groups; specifically, arid-zone taxa displayed shallower scaling relationships for EWL, indicating enhanced water conservation mechanisms at larger sizes. Furthermore, significant mass × temperature interactions emerged, particularly within terrestrial specialists, where larger individuals maintained more stable Tb trajectories despite thermal extremes. This size-dependent buffering likely mitigates cellular stress during prolonged heatwaves. Notably, species occupying ephemeral water bodies showed elevated baseline EWL rates but compensated through behavioural thermoregulation and rapid desiccation tolerance. These findings underscore that habitat specialisation fundamentally reshapes the thermal and hydric physiology of southern African anurans, decoupling strict metabolic dependencies from environmental fluctuations. Consequently, future projections of amphibian vulnerability under climate change scenarios must integrate species-specific physiological plasticity rather than relying on broad taxonomic assumptions. Our results provide a mechanistic framework for predicting how shifting temperature regimes and increased aridity will impact amphibian energy budgets and hydrological balances across heterogeneous landscapes.

title: Probing the near-IR flux excess in young star clusters
text_ai: We report the results of a recent study of young star clusters (YSCs) in luminous blue compact galaxies (BCGs). The age distributions of the YSCs suggest that the starburst episode in Haro 11, ESO 185-IG13, and Mrk 930 started not more than 30-40 Myr ago. Multi-band near-infrared photometry reveals a pronounced flux excess in the J and H bands for clusters younger than 50 Myr, deviating significantly from single stellar population predictions. By comparing observed spectral energy distributions with updated evolutionary tracks, we demonstrate that this enhancement arises predominantly from the combined contribution of red supergiants and early asymptotic giant branch stars. Binary interaction channels play a minor role, contributing less than 15% to the integrated luminosity. The derived mass-to-light ratios in the K band remain consistently lower than theoretical expectations, suggesting either a top-heavy initial mass function or localized dust extinction within dense environments. Our findings indicate that standard population synthesis models underestimate the near-infrared output of young systems by factors of two to three. Consequently, accurate modeling of near-infrared fluxes is essential for reliable age dating and mass estimation of star-forming regions in high-redshift analogues. These results underscore the necessity of incorporating detailed post-main-sequence evolution and binary fractions into current population frameworks.

title: Diverse tunable dynamics of two quantum random walkers
text_ai: Quantum walk research has mainly focused on evolutions due to repeated applications of time-independent unitary coin operators. However, the idea of controlling the single particle evolution using time-dependent unitary coins has still been a subject of multiple studies as it not only hosts interesting possibilities for quantum information processing but also opens a much richer array of phenomena including static and dynamic localizations. In this work, we extend this framework to investigate the collective behavior of two interacting quantum walkers subjected to periodically modulated coin operators. By introducing a tunable coupling parameter between the particles, we demonstrate that the system exhibits a rich spectrum of dynamical regimes, ranging from ballistic spreading and coherent oscillations to robust spatial localization and entanglement generation. We systematically map out the phase diagram by varying the modulation frequency and coin rotation angles, revealing sharp transitions driven by constructive and destructive interference in the multi-particle Hilbert space. Our analytical derivations, complemented by exact numerical simulations, show that the interplay between temporal driving and spatial correlations enables precise control over both individual trajectories and joint probability distributions. These results establish time-dependent coins as a versatile resource for engineering multipartite quantum states. This framework provides a systematic route to exploit time-varying coins for generating complex walker correlations within discrete quantum architectures, advancing quantum simulation protocols.

title: Characterising the VHE diffuse emission in the central 200 parsecs of our Galaxy with H.E.S.S
text_ai: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a longitudinal distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flux rapidly decreases. Spectral analysis reveals a hard power-law component with a photon index of Γ ≈ 2.3 ± 0.1 (stat) ± 0.2 (syst) that remains remarkably stable across the resolved angular bins. This spectral hardness, combined with the spatial correlation coefficient of 0.87 between the gamma-ray surface brightness and the molecular gas column density derived from CO surveys, strongly supports a hadronic origin via cosmic-ray proton interactions with interstellar matter. Instrumental background modelling and gas-to-gamma-ray conversion uncertainties are propagated, yielding a robust flux normalization error budget below 15 per cent. By assuming a locally enhanced cosmic-ray energy density relative to the solar neighbourhood, we derive a compression factor of f_CR ≈ 15–20 within the inner 100 pc, aligning with confinement models featuring turbulent magnetic fields or localized energetic injections. However, the abrupt flux truncation at l ≈ 130 pc cannot be reproduced by steady-state diffusion scenarios alone, suggesting either a genuinely time-dependent injection history or a pronounced sharp gradient in the ambient medium density. We further test alternative leptonic interpretations and find that inverse Compton scattering off the intense radiation field requires an unphysically steep electron spectrum and exceeds the observed X-ray upper limits. Consequently, the data favour a scenario where VHE gamma-rays predominantly trace hadronic collisions in the dense CMZ gas, modulated by complex diffusive transport mechanisms and potentially influenced by historical active galactic nucleus outbursts. These findings constrain cosmic-ray acceleration efficiencies and propagation timescales in extreme galactic environments, establishing key benchmarks for upcoming large-scale observatories and comprehensive multi-messenger Galactic centre studies.

title: Efficient State Space Model via Fast Tensor Convolution and Block Diagonalization
text_ai: Existing models encounter bottlenecks in balancing performance and computational efficiency when modeling long sequences. Although the state space model (SSM) has achieved remarkable success in handling long sequence tasks, it still faces the problem of large number of parameters. To address this limitation, we propose an efficient state space architecture that integrates fast tensor convolution with block diagonalization. By decomposing the high-dimensional transition matrix into structured low-rank blocks, our approach drastically reduces the parameter footprint while preserving the expressive capacity required for complex temporal dependencies. The fast tensor convolution module further accelerates sequence processing through optimized kernel factorization, enabling linear-time inference without sacrificing accuracy. Extensive experiments on benchmark language modeling and time-series forecasting tasks demonstrate that our framework achieves competitive predictive performance with up to 4.2× fewer trainable parameters and 2.8× faster training throughput compared to contemporary SSM variants. Ablation studies confirm that the synergistic interaction between block-structured state evolution and tensor-based feature extraction is critical for maintaining long-range dependency capture. Theoretical analysis further establishes convergence bounds under standard regularity assumptions, validating the numerical stability of the proposed decomposition. These findings establish a new paradigm for resource-constrained sequential learning, offering a scalable pathway toward deploying advanced state-space architectures in latency-sensitive and memory-limited applications.

title: Spectroscopic Observations of Selected Planetary Nebulae from the HASH Database
text_ai: We conducted research on the classification and physical properties of 10 objects from the HASH (Hong Kong/Australian Astronomical Observatory/Strasbourg Observatory H-alpha Planetary Nebula (PN)) database with small angular sizes (< 8\arcsec) in the northern hemisphere. The sample consisted of 6 Likely PNe, 2 new candidates, one emission-line star, and one object of unknown nature. High-resolution optical spectra were obtained using the 2.4 m Hiltner telescope at MDM Observatory. Emission-line diagnostics and photoionization modeling were employed to derive key plasma parameters, including electron temperatures, densities, and nebular radii. Our analysis confirms five objects as bona fide planetary nebulae characterized by high-ionization species and compact morphologies, while the remaining candidate exhibits low-excitation features consistent with a protoplanetary nebula phase. The emission-line star is identified as a pre-main-sequence object exhibiting strong [O III] and He II emission. For the unresolved source, deep imaging reveals a faint stellar continuum without extended nebulosity, suggesting a background galaxy or heavily obscured young stellar object. Ionic abundances were calculated relative to hydrogen, revealing moderate metallicity depletion typical of evolved Galactic disk systems. These results demonstrate that narrow-band Hα selection combined with follow-up spectroscopy effectively filters false positives in crowded fields. The refined catalog enhances our understanding of PN progenitor evolution and improves statistical samples for future population studies in the local universe.

title: COUNTDOWN: a Run-time Library for Performance-Neutral Energy Saving in MPI Applications
text_ai: Power and energy consumption is becoming key challenges to deploy the first exascale supercomputer successfully. Large-scale HPC applications waste a significant amount of power in communication and synchronization-related idle times. However, due to the time scale at which communication happens, transitioning in low power states during communication's idle times may introduce unacceptable overhead in applications' execution time. To address this fundamental trade-off, we present COUNTDOWN, a lightweight run-time library that dynamically exploits microsecond-scale idle intervals inherent in MPI collective and point-to-point operations. By integrating tightly with the underlying message passing interface, COUNTDOWN leverages hardware performance monitors to predict communication boundaries and applies adaptive voltage and frequency scaling exclusively during guaranteed non-critical gaps. Crucially, our approach employs a non-intrusive polling mechanism that ensures communication progress remains uninterrupted while processors safely enter deep C-states. We evaluate COUNTDOWN across diverse scientific workloads deployed on contemporary high-performance architectures, demonstrating consistent energy reductions of up to 28 percent relative to baseline executions. Importantly, performance degradation remains strictly below 1.2 percent, validating the library’s performance-neutral design philosophy. These empirical results confirm that strategic, application-aware power management can significantly mitigate operational costs without compromising computational throughput, thereby establishing a practical pathway toward sustainable exascale computing ecosystems.

title: Thinking Assistants: LLM-Based Conversational Assistants that Help Users Think By Asking rather than Answering
text_ai: Many AI systems focus solely on providing solutions or explaining outcomes. However, complex tasks like research and strategic thinking often benefit from a more comprehensive approach to augmenting the thinking process rather than passively getting information. To address this gap, we introduce Thinking Assistants, a novel class of LLM-driven conversational agents designed to scaffold metacognitive processes through guided inquiry. Rather than delivering direct responses, these systems employ strategic questioning techniques grounded in Socratic pedagogy to prompt critical reflection, hypothesis generation, and structured reasoning. We outline the architectural framework, which integrates dynamic dialogue management with real-time cognitive state estimation to tailor prompts according to user expertise and task complexity. Empirical evaluations across academic synthesis, policy analysis, and technical debugging demonstrate that participants using questioning assistants exhibit significantly deeper conceptual understanding, improved argument coherence, and higher information retention and longitudinal stability compared to baseline answer-generating models. Qualitative feedback further indicates reduced reliance on external sources and increased self-efficacy when navigating ambiguous problem spaces. These results indicate that reorienting conversational AI from information retrieval toward cognitive partnership substantially enhances human analytical capabilities. Our discussion outlines practical implications for pedagogical design, knowledge work workflows, and the development of AI architectures that preserve intellectual autonomy while mitigating over-reliance on automated outputs.

title: Dark Matter and Sterile Neutrinos
text_ai: Dark matter has been recognized as an essential part of matter for over 70 years now, and many suggestions have been made, what it could be. Most of these ideas have centered on Cold Dark Matter, particles that are predicted in extensions of standard particle physics, such as supersymmetry. Attention has increasingly shifted toward keV-scale sterile neutrinos as viable warm dark matter candidates. Emerging naturally from seesaw mechanisms, these right-handed fermions can be generated via oscillations in the early universe, offering a compelling resolution to small-scale structure tensions within the ΛCDM framework. In this study, we evaluate the phenomenological viability of sterile neutrino dark matter across astrophysical and laboratory frontiers. We derive stringent upper limits on the mixing angle θ by combining X-ray spectroscopic data from galaxy clusters with Lyman-α forest constraints, while evaluating indirect detection signatures through neutrino telescopes. Our results demonstrate that a narrow parameter window remains open around m_s ≈ 7–10 keV, consistent with unresolved emission lines observed in stacked Chandra and XMM-Newton spectra. Furthermore, we assess the compatibility of this mass range with phase-space density bounds and large-scale structure formation simulations. By synthesizing cosmological observations with particle physics constraints, we establish a robust framework for future experimental searches, highlighting the role of next-generation observatories and precision neutrino experiments in testing the sterile neutrino hypothesis.

title: Mobile Data Science: Towards Understanding Data-Driven Intelligent Mobile Applications
text_ai: Due to the popularity of smart mobile phones and context-aware technology, various contextual data relevant to users' diverse activities with mobile phones is available around us. This enables the study on mobile phone data and context-awareness in computing, for the purpose of building data-driven intelligent mobile applications, not only on a single device but also in a distributed environment for the benefit of end users. However, harnessing this pervasive information stream presents significant computational and analytical challenges. The inherent heterogeneity, volume, and temporal dynamics of mobile sensor streams necessitate robust preprocessing pipelines and adaptive learning mechanisms capable of operating under strict resource constraints. Furthermore, preserving user privacy while enabling cross-device collaboration remains a critical barrier to widespread deployment. To address these issues, this paper presents a comprehensive examination of mobile data science paradigms, systematically categorizing existing methodologies across data acquisition, feature engineering, model training, and inference phases. We evaluate representative architectures that leverage edge-cloud collaborative frameworks and federated learning approaches. Through comparative analysis, we identify key performance trade-offs regarding latency, energy consumption, and prediction accuracy. Additionally, we emphasize practical implementation guidelines and standardized evaluation metrics. Finally, we outline open research questions and propose a unified roadmap for developing scalable, privacy-preserving, and context-sensitive mobile intelligence systems, aiming to guide both academic inquiry and industry innovation in next-generation mobile computing ecosystems.
