title: Accuracy of model-based tracking of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by dynamic volumetric MRI
text_ai: The purpose of this study was to determine the accuracy of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by volumetric dynamic MRI. A motor-actuated phantom drove femoral and tibial bone segments through cyclic 3D motion patterns. Volumetric images were continuously acquired using a 3D radially undersampled cine spoiled gradient echo sequence (SPGR-VIPR). Model-based segmentation and rigid-body registration algorithms were employed to reconstruct six-degree-of-freedom joint kinematics and quantify interfacial cartilage contact throughout the motion cycle. Reconstructed trajectories were validated against the system’s encoder-derived ground truth using root-mean-square error analysis. Translational and rotational kinematic errors averaged 0.8 ± 0.3 mm and 1.4 ± 0.6°, respectively, with peak deviations occurring during rapid acceleration phases. Cartilage contact area estimates demonstrated a mean absolute difference of 4.2% relative to reference measurements, while contact centroid localization exhibited sub-millimeter precision. Cross-validation across multiple motion amplitudes confirmed consistent performance, with reconstruction times remaining clinically feasible for near real-time applications. These findings indicate that SPGR-VIPR-based model tracking reliably captures high-fidelity knee mechanics and load-bearing surface interactions under controlled dynamic conditions. The methodology provides a robust, non-invasive framework for evaluating patient-specific joint function and could facilitate longitudinal monitoring of osteoarthritic progression or post-surgical rehabilitation outcomes without radiation exposure or external marker dependency, thereby establishing a viable alternative to conventional fluoroscopic assessment techniques.

title: Effect of 5% transdermal lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy.
text_ai: To investigate the effect of 5% lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy. Client-owned dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy for a single acute intervertebral thoracolumbar disc extrusion were enrolled in this prospective, randomised, blinded clinical trial. Following methadone administration, anaesthesia was induced with propofol, and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen and fentanyl infusion, in both groups. Dogs were randomly allocated to receive either a 5% lidocaine patch applied directly to the surgical site prior to incision or a matching placebo patch. Postoperative pain was evaluated using the Colorado State University Multidimensional Acute Pain Scale at 0, 4, 8, 12, 24, and 48 hours by blinded investigators. Rescue analgesia was administered according to institutional protocol when composite scores exceeded predefined thresholds. Forty-eight dogs completed the study. Lidocaine-treated dogs exhibited significantly lower median composite pain scores at 8, 12, and 24 hours compared with controls (P<0.05). Total cumulative tramadol and buprenorphine requirements were reduced by 32% in the treatment group during the first 24-hour period. No patch-related adverse effects occurred, and surgical site complication rates were comparable. Adjunctive application of 5% transdermal lidocaine patches enhances postoperative analgesia following canine hemilaminectomy, significantly decreasing systemic opioid requirements without increasing adverse events. Integration of this topical strategy offers a safe, effective component of multimodal pain management for thoracolumbar disc disease surgeries.

title: General convergence analysis of stochastic first order methods for composite optimization
text_ai: In this paper we consider stochastic composite convex optimization problems with the objective function satisfying a stochastic bounded gradient condition, with or without a quadratic functional growth property. These models include the most well-known classes of objective functions analyzed in the literature: non-smooth Lipschitz functions and composition of a (potentially) non-smooth function and a smooth function, with or without strong convexity. We establish a unified analytical framework that derives explicit convergence rates for a broad class of stochastic first-order algorithms under minimal assumptions. By leveraging the stochastic bounded gradient condition and exploiting the quadratic functional growth property, we obtain tight expected error bounds that seamlessly transition between sublinear and linear convergence regimes depending on the underlying geometry. Our analysis accommodates adaptive and constant step-sizes, supporting both deterministic and stochastic oracle queries. We demonstrate that our bounds recover and improve upon guarantees for proximal gradient methods, stochastic variance-reduced techniques, and accelerated schemes. Furthermore, we provide sharp lower-bound constructions that validate the optimality of our upper bounds in expectation. Theoretical findings are complemented by numerical experiments on empirical risk minimization and machine learning tasks, illustrating the robustness and efficiency of the proposed methods across varying levels of noise and condition numbers. These results unify disparate convergence theories and provide practitioners with actionable guidelines for algorithm selection and parameter tuning in composite optimization settings.

title: Symplectic structure of post-Newtonian Hamiltonian for spinning compact binaries
text_ai: The phase space of a Hamiltonian system is symplectic. However, the post-Newtonian Hamiltonian formulation of spinning compact binaries in existing publications does not have this property, when position, momentum and spin variables $[X, P, S_1, S_2]$ compose its phase space. We demonstrate that this deficiency arises from an inconsistent treatment of spin supplementary conditions and non-canonical Poisson brackets inherent in conventional coordinate choices. By explicitly constructing the symplectic two-form from first principles, we derive a fully canonical set of dynamical variables that preserve the underlying geometric structure through third post-Newtonian order. Our approach employs a systematic series of point transformations combined with constraint analysis to isolate the true degrees of freedom, yielding a phase-space metric that satisfies Darboux’s theorem identically. The resulting Hamiltonian reproduces established conservative dynamics while restoring the expected Lie-algebraic properties of the spin generators. Furthermore, we show that the modified symplectic structure induces subtle corrections to the spin-orbit coupling terms at higher orders, which remain invariant under admissible gauge transformations. Explicit expressions for the transformed symplectic form are provided, enabling direct implementation in high-precision orbit integrators without artificial drift in conserved quantities. These findings resolve longstanding ambiguities in analytical binary models and provide a consistent foundation for gravitational-wave template construction and numerical-relativity matching schemes.

title: Tackling solvent effect by coupling electronic and molecular Density Functional Theory
text_ai: Solvation effect might have a tremendous influence on chemical reactions. However, precise quantum chemistry calculations are most often done either in vacuum neglecting the role of the solvent or using continuum solvent model ignoring its molecular nature. To bridge this dichotomy, we present a unified framework that seamlessly integrates electronic density functional theory (DFT) for the reactive center with molecular DFT simulations of the explicit solvent environment. The coupling is achieved through a self-consistent embedding scheme wherein the electron density of the solute polarizes the surrounding solvent molecules, while their instantaneous configurations feed back into the Kohn–Sham potential governing the electronic structure. This bidirectional interaction explicitly accounts for both long-range dielectric screening and short-range directional forces, such as hydrogen bonding and steric confinement, which are inherently absent in implicit treatments. We validate the methodology against high-level wavefunction benchmarks and experimental kinetics for proton-transfer and nucleophilic substitution reactions in aqueous media. The coupled approach reproduces solvent-induced barrier shifts within 0.3 kcal mol⁻¹, capturing dynamic solvation shells that modulate transition-state stability. Furthermore, computational costs remain comparable to standard continuum models due to efficient density-fitting and adaptive sampling protocols. By eliminating the artificial boundary between electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom, this strategy provides a computationally tractable pathway toward predictive modeling of solution-phase reactivity, advancing quantitative catalyst design and synthesis in condensed phases.

title: Unraveling the Complexity of Imported Malaria Infections by Amplicon Deep Sequencing.
text_ai: Imported malaria and recurrent infections are becoming an emerging issue in many malaria non-endemic countries. This study aimed to determine the molecular patterns of the imported malaria infections and recurrence. Blood samples were collected from patients with imported malaria infections during 2016-2018 in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. Parasite DNA was extracted and subjected to amplicon deep sequencing targeting the *Plasmodium* 18S rRNA gene alongside drug-resistance loci (*pfmdr1*, *pfcrt*, and *kelch13*). High-throughput analysis revealed a complex spectrum of co-infecting genotypes, with multi-clonal infections accounting for 34.2% of cases. *Plasmodium vivax* constituted the predominant species (58.7%), followed by *P. falciparum* (31.4%) and mixed-species infections (9.9%). Notably, deep sequencing uncovered low-frequency minority variants undetectable by conventional microscopy, including hypnozoite-associated lineages indicative of relapse potential. Molecular epidemiological mapping traced importation routes predominantly from sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. Drug-resistance marker analysis identified prevalent *pfmdr1* amplifications and *kelch13* mutations associated with artemisinin partial resistance. Furthermore, longitudinal tracking demonstrated that molecular recurrence rates exceeded clinical estimates by twofold, highlighting the necessity of genomic surveillance for precise burden assessment. These findings underscore the superior resolution of amplicon deep sequencing in discriminating true recrudescence from new introductions and elucidating transmission dynamics. Implementing this high-sensitivity diagnostic framework within routine surveillance systems will enhance the precision of elimination strategies, facilitate targeted interventions against hidden reservoirs, supporting malaria-free certification in non-endemic regions.

title: Select, then Balance: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Exogenous-Aware Spatio-Temporal Forecasting
text_ai: Spatio-temporal forecasting aims to predict the future state of dynamic systems and plays an important role in multiple fields. However, existing solutions only focus on modeling using a limited number of observed target variables. In real-world scenarios, exogenous variables can be integrated into the model as additional input features and associated with the target signal to promote forecast accuracy. To address this limitation, we introduce Select, then Balance, a novel plug-and-play framework designed to systematically incorporate heterogeneous exogenous covariates into spatio-temporal predictors. Our approach operates in two distinct phases: first, a relevance selector filters redundant or noisy inputs via dynamic cross-attention mechanisms; second, a balancing module adaptively weights selected covariates against endogenous signals to mitigate feature dominance and preserve intrinsic spatial dependencies. By decoupling selection from integration, the architecture remains strictly model-agnostic and seamlessly interfaces with diverse backbone networks. Extensive evaluations across five public benchmarks demonstrate consistent performance gains, yielding average reductions of 12.4% in RMSE and 9.8% in MAE relative to strong baselines. Ablation studies further validate that adaptive weighting stabilizes gradient propagation during optimization. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism exhibits remarkable computational efficiency, requiring negligible inference overhead. Collectively, these results position exogenous-aware coupling as a scalable strategy for next-generation forecasting applications.

title: On the disappearance of a cold molecular torus around the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus of NGC 1097
text_ai: We used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to map the CO(3-2) and the underlying continuum emissions around the type 1 low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (LLAGN; bolometric luminosity $\lesssim 10^{42}$ erg~s$^{-1}$) of NGC 1097 at $\sim 10$ pc resolution. These observations revealed a detailed cold gas distribution within a $\sim 100$ pc of this LLAGN. Contrary to standard unified schemes that predict a persistent obscuring structure at parsec scales, we detect no evidence of a coherent cold molecular torus. Instead, the gas exhibits a centrally concentrated, disk-like morphology with pronounced azimuthal asymmetries and radial velocity gradients consistent with ordered rotation perturbed by non-circular motions. The surface density profile drops steeply beyond $\sim 50$ pc, and the integrated molecular mass ($M_{\rm mol} \approx 2 \times 10^6 M_\odot$) falls significantly below values inferred for comparable Seyfert galaxies. We interpret these properties as the signature of past AGN feedback or secular depletion, wherein radiatively inefficient accretion and jet-induced outflows have efficiently cleared the inner circumnuclear medium. This absence challenges the notion that a permanent cold torus is a prerequisite for low-luminosity accretion, suggesting instead that torus destruction or transformation is an inherent phase in the evolutionary cycle of LLAGNs. Our results imply that parsec-scale obscuration may be transient rather than structural, requiring revised frameworks for AGN fueling and unification scenarios that account for dynamic gas removal mechanisms.

title: Insights into the effects of sleep disordered breathing on the brain in infants and children: Imaging and cerebral oxygenation measurements.
text_ai: Sleep disordered breathing (SDB) is a common condition in infants and children. SDB encompasses a spectrum of respiratory disorders, which are defined as either obstructive or central in nature. Obstructive SDB ranges in severity from primary snoring (PS), to obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Emerging neuroimaging and cerebral oximetry studies reveal that recurrent nocturnal hypoxemia and sleep fragmentation associated with SDB precipitate measurable alterations in developing neural architecture. Diffusion tensor imaging consistently demonstrates reduced fractional anisotropy in critical white matter tracts, particularly within the corpus callosum and superior longitudinal fasciculus, correlating with prolonged desaturation indices. Functional magnetic resonance imaging further indicates attenuated default mode network connectivity during rest, suggesting compromised resting-state cerebral metabolism. Concurrently, near-infrared spectroscopy captures transient drops in frontal lobe tissue oxygenation that frequently precedes cortical arousals, highlighting a direct pathophysiological link between upper airway resistance and regional cerebral perfusion deficits. These hemodynamic fluctuations disrupt synaptogenesis and myelination during sensitive developmental windows, translating into subtle but persistent deficits in executive function, attentional control, and behavioral regulation. Longitudinal analyses suggest that early intervention via adenotonsillectomy or continuous positive airway pressure may partially reverse these neurobiological signatures, though optimal treatment thresholds remain under investigation. Collectively, multimodal imaging and continuous cerebral oxygenation monitoring provide critical biomarkers for identifying at-risk pediatric populations, enabling earlier clinical stratification and targeted therapeutic strategies to mitigate neuropsychiatric sequelae.

title: Periodontal status correlates with anti-citrullinated protein antibodies in first-degree relatives of individuals with rheumatoid arthritis.
text_ai: To evaluate periodontal status in first-degree relatives of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (FDR-RA) and detect correlation with the presence of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPAs). Rheumatologic status and periodontal status were evaluated in a nested case-control study of FDR-RA with no diagnosis of RA at enrolment. Clinical and radiographic assessments included probing depth, clinical attachment loss, bleeding on probing, and alveolar bone level. ACPA serostatus was determined using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, smoking status, and systemic inflammation markers were employed to assess associations between periodontal disease severity and ACPA positivity. Among 142 enrolled FDR-RA participants, 28.9% were ACPA-positive, and 67.3% exhibited moderate-to-severe periodontitis. Notably, individuals with advanced periodontal disease demonstrated significantly higher odds of ACPA seropositivity (adjusted odds ratio = 3.42; 95% CI: 1.58–7.41; p = 0.002) independent of traditional cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors. Periodontal inflammatory burden, particularly elevated interleukin-6 and C-reactive protein levels, partially mediated this association. Collectively, these data indicate that subclinical periodontal inflammation may function as a readily identifiable clinical biomarker reflecting underlying citrullination-driven autoimmune dysregulation within genetically susceptible populations. Integrating routine periodontal evaluations into standard FDR-RA surveillance protocols could facilitate earlier identification of high-risk individuals warranting targeted immunological monitoring and preventive rheumatologic intervention.

title: Revealing hidden talents: The development, use, and benefit of VESPARCH.
text_ai: School attainment tests and Cognitive Abilities Tests are used in the United Kingdom to set targets for educational outcome. Whilst these are good predictors, they depend not only on basic ability but also on learnt knowledge and skills, such as reading. To address this limitation, we developed VESPARCH, a novel assessment framework specifically engineered to isolate innate cognitive potential from acquired academic proficiency. Drawing upon differential testing methodologies and dynamic performance metrics, VESPARCH was rigorously validated across a representative sample of secondary school students. Our longitudinal analysis demonstrates that VESPARCH scores significantly outperform conventional baseline measures in forecasting subsequent subject-specific attainment, particularly among learners from disadvantaged backgrounds. By decoupling measurement from curriculum-dependent vocabulary and prior instructional exposure, the instrument successfully identifies latent high-ability individuals who traditionally remain undetected by standardised proxies. Furthermore, implementation trials indicate that integrating VESPARCH data into teacher-student dialogue substantially refines target-setting accuracy and enhances motivational trajectories. These findings underscore the practical utility of VESPARCH as a diagnostic complement to existing evaluation regimes, offering educators a more equitable mechanism for recognising and nurturing unrecognised intellectual capacity. Ultimately, adopting such bias-mitigated instruments promises to optimise resource allocation and support personalised learning pathways within contemporary educational ecosystems, thereby advancing robust pedagogical equity.

title: Effects of PRP and LyPRP on osteogenic differentiation of MSCs.
text_ai: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is rich in a variety of growth factors and plays an important role in the proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). It has been reported that the preparation of freeze-dried platelets (lyophilized platelets [LyPRP]) from platelets could be an effective strategy to preserve the bioactivity of platelets for a long time. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the osteoinductive potential of conventional PRP versus lyophilized PRP (LyPRP) on human bone marrow-derived MSCs. Cells were cultured under standard osteogenic conditions supplemented with either PRP or reconstituted LyPRP at identical platelet concentrations. Differentiation was assessed over 21 days via alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity assays, alizarin red S staining, and quantitative real-time PCR analysis of RUNX2, osteopontin (OPN), and osteocalcin (OCN). Western blotting further validated corresponding protein levels. Both treatments significantly enhanced osteogenic commitment compared to baseline controls; notably, LyPRP-supplemented cultures exhibited comparable ALP activity and robust mineralized nodule formation. Transcriptomic profiling revealed sustained upregulation of RUNX2 and OPN in the LyPRP cohort, correlating with dense extracellular matrix deposition. Immunocytochemical analysis confirmed de novo collagen type I accumulation within the mineralizing microenvironment. These findings demonstrate that LyPRP effectively retains the pro-osteogenic bioactivity of native PRP and offers practical advantages in long-term storage and clinical scalability. LyPRP thus emerges as a stable biomaterial for enhancing bone regeneration protocols.

title: Stripe magnetic order and field-induced quantum criticality in the perfect triangular-lattice antiferromagnet CsCeSe$_2$
text_ai: The two-dimensional triangular-lattice antiferromagnet (TLAF) is a textbook example of frustrated magnetic systems. Despite its simplicity, the TLAF model exhibits a highly rich and complex magnetic phase diagram, featuring numerous distinct ground states that can be stabilized through frustrated next-nearest-neighbor couplings or anisotropy. In this paper, we report low-temperature magnetic properties of the TLAF material CsCeSe$_2$. Utilizing high-resolution neutron diffraction alongside bulk thermodynamic probes, we establish that CsCeSe$_2$ hosts an ideal $S=1/2$ effective moment on a structurally perfect triangular lattice, free from competing exchange pathways. Cooling induces a commensurate stripe-type magnetic order at $T_N = 0.68\,\text{K}$, driven by dominant nearest-neighbor interactions supplemented by weak Ising-like single-ion anisotropy. Subsequent application of an in-plane magnetic field progressively reduces the staggered magnetization, ultimately suppressing long-range order to absolute zero at $H_c \approx 1.15\,\text{T}$. Finite-size scaling of specific heat and ac-susceptibility measurements confirms the emergence of a continuous quantum phase transition governed by the two-dimensional transverse-field Ising universality class. Neutron scattering spectra further reveal gapped triplet excitations that soften continuously near $H_c$, providing spectroscopic confirmation of the quantum critical endpoint. Consequently, CsCeSe$_2$ delivers a pristine platform for probing field-driven quantum criticality, clarifying how geometric frustration and quantum fluctuations jointly stabilize stripe textures in two-dimensional magnets, establishing new benchmarks for TLAF research.

title: Virgibacillus indicus sp. nov. and Virgibacillus profundi sp. nov, two moderately halophilic bacteria isolated from marine sediment by using microfluidic streak plates.
text_ai: Three Gram-variable, moderately halophilic, motile, endospore-forming rods, designated P2-C2 T , P3-H5 T and P3-B8, were isolated from marine sediment of the Southwest Indian Ocean by using the microfluidic streak plate method. Phylogenetic analysis of their 16S rRNA gene sequences revealed that strains P2-C2^T and P3-H5^T clustered within the genus *Virgibacillus*, exhibiting highest sequence similarity to *Virgibacillus salinus* KCTC 33824^T (96.8%) and *Virgibacillus donghaensis* KACC 17693^T (96.5%), respectively. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed distinct evolutionary lineages with average nucleotide identity values significantly below established species boundaries. Both isolates demonstrated optimal proliferation at 10–20% (w/v) NaCl and pH 6.5–8.0, maintaining consistent moderate halophilic physiology across tested media. Chemotaxonomic characterisation identified anteiso-C15:0 and iso-C15:0 as dominant cellular fatty acid components, menaquinone-7 as the principal respiratory quinone, and phosphatidylglycerol with diphosphatidylglycerol as defining polar lipid constituents. Distinctive biochemical profiles and differential substrate assimilation patterns readily separated these strains from validly published relatives. Genomic DNA G+C contents of 43.2 mol% and 42.8 mol% further corroborated their independent status. Accordingly, we propose *Virgibacillus indicus* sp. nov., with P3-H5^T (=KCTC 72946^T=LMG 32710^T) designated as the type strain, and *Virgibacillus profundi* sp. nov., represented by P2-C2^T (=KCTC 72945^T=LMG 32709^T). Strain P3-B8 phylogenetically aligned with *V.* profundi yet exhibited sufficient metabolic variation to justify separate evaluation. This work underscores the utility of microfluidic platforms for accessing diverse marine prokaryotic diversity.

title: A New Lagrangian Problem Crossover: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Crossover Standards
text_ai: The performance of most evolutionary metaheuristic algorithms relays on various operatives. One of them is the crossover operator, which is divided into two types: application dependent and application independent crossover operators. These standards always help to choose the best-fitted point in the evolutionary algorithm process. Despite their widespread adoption, empirical evaluations of these operators remain fragmented, particularly concerning their efficacy within Lagrangian relaxation frameworks. This study presents a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis of established crossover standards applied to combinatorial optimization problems governed by Lagrangian dual bounds. We synthesized data from 142 peer-reviewed publications, categorizing operator behaviors across solution space exploration and exploitation phases. Statistical aggregation reveals that application-independent crossovers consistently outperform domain-specific variants when integrated with dynamic penalty adjustment mechanisms, yielding a mean convergence improvement of 18.7% (p < 0.01). Furthermore, heterogeneity analysis identifies structural incompatibilities between traditional recombination schemes and Lagrangian multiplier update rules. Based on these findings, we propose a unified Lagrangian-aware crossover framework that adapts recombination probabilities according to dual feasibility gradients. This standardized approach mitigates premature convergence while enhancing computational robustness across diverse problem instances. The proposed methodology establishes reproducible benchmarks for future hybrid metaheuristic designs, offering clear implementation protocols for large-scale constrained optimization environments and stochastic constraints.

title: Cracking Double-Blind Review: Authorship Attribution with Deep Learning
text_ai: Double-blind peer review is considered a pillar of academic research because it is perceived to ensure a fair, unbiased, and fact-centered scientific discussion. Yet, experienced researchers can often correctly guess from which research group an anonymous submission originates, biasing the peer-review process. To systematically quantify this vulnerability, we introduce a deep learning framework leveraging stylistic and syntactic fingerprints embedded within manuscript text to accurately attribute authorship. Our approach employs a transformer architecture fine-tuned on large-scale corpora of published conference papers, capturing latent linguistic patterns invariant to superficial editing. Evaluated across multiple top-tier venues, the model demonstrates state-of-the-art performance with attribution accuracy exceeding 89%, even when controlling for domain-specific vocabulary and structural variations. Ablation studies reveal that rhetorical stance markers and sentence-level dependency structures serve as the most salient predictors, significantly outperforming traditional n-gram and support vector machine baselines. Furthermore, we analyze current anonymization protocols, showing that standard de-identification techniques consistently fail to disrupt these high-dimensional stylistic signals. These findings underscore a critical vulnerability in contemporary submission workflows and highlight the necessity for automated pre-screening mechanisms. By providing a scalable tool for detecting residual identity leakage, this work offers a diagnostic instrument for program committees and actionable guidelines for preserving review integrity during manuscript preparation. Ultimately, our empirical results advocate for stricter anonymization standards and algorithmic audits to safeguard scholarly objectivity.

title: Improving Zero-Day Malware Testing Methodology Using Statistically Significant Time-Lagged Test Samples
text_ai: Enterprise networks are in constant danger of being breached by cyber-attackers, but making the decision about what security tools to deploy to mitigate this risk requires carefully designed evaluation of security products. One of the most important metrics for a protection product is how well it is able to stop malware, specifically on "zero"-day malware that has not been seen by the security community before. Current evaluation frameworks frequently rely on contemporaneous sample collections, introducing temporal bias that artificially inflates detection rates and obscures true defensive efficacy. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel testing paradigm grounded in statistically significant, time-lagged test samples. By systematically decoupling training ingestion from validation timelines, our methodology enforces strict temporal isolation, simulating realistic deployment conditions where threat intelligence evolves incrementally. We implemented this framework across five leading endpoint protection platforms, utilizing twelve months of evolving malware variants. Rigorous statistical analysis demonstrates that time-lagged validation reduces false confidence by 34% and yields more reproducible detection benchmarks than conventional synchronous protocols. Furthermore, the approach enables precise quantification of model decay and retraining intervals. These findings establish a robust standard for zero-day malware assessment, empowering security architects to make evidence-based procurement decisions while advancing methodological rigor in cybersecurity evaluation.

title: DIViS: Domain Invariant Visual Servoing for Collision-Free Goal Reaching
text_ai: Robots should understand both semantics and physics to be functional in the real world. While robot platforms provide means for interacting with the physical world they cannot autonomously acquire object-level semantics without needing human. In this paper, we investigate how to minimize human effort and intervention to teach robots perform real world tasks that incorporate semantics. To address this limitation, we introduce DIViS, a unified framework that bridges semantic reasoning and physical control via domain-invariant visual servoing. Our approach leverages self-supervised contrastive learning to extract environment-agnostic embeddings, which are subsequently constrained by differentiable geometry modules to enforce collision avoidance. We design a closed-loop visual controller that maps high-level semantic goals directly to actuator commands, eliminating the need for hand-crafted kinematic models or manual reward shaping. Training utilizes large-scale domain randomization paired with feature disentanglement to isolate task-relevant semantics from nuisance variables. Comprehensive evaluations across rigorous simulated and empirical real-world scenarios reveal that DIViS attains superior goal-reaching accuracy while guaranteeing zero collisions under varying illumination and clutter levels. Moreover, the system requires fewer than five human demonstrations to converge, representing a substantial reduction relative to imitation learning baselines. The proposed architecture successfully generalizes across unseen environments without fine-tuning, demonstrating robust cross-domain transferability. Ultimately, DIViS provides a practical foundation for deploying semantically grounded, physically compliant robots in highly dynamic, unstructured operational domains requiring minimal supervision.

title: Ball-Larus Path Profiling Across Multiple Loop iterations
text_ai: Identifying the hottest paths in the control flow graph of a routine can direct optimizations to portions of the code where most resources are consumed. This powerful methodology, called path profiling, was introduced by Ball and Larus in the mid 90s and has received considerable attention in the last 15 years for its practical relevance. However, traditional Ball-Larus instrumentation struggles with iterative constructs, as it aggregates execution statistics per procedure call rather than tracking path frequencies across successive loop passes. Consequently, critical inter-iteration hot paths remain obscured, limiting the efficacy of loop-specific optimizations for loop transformations. To address this limitation, we propose an enhanced instrumentation framework that models and accumulates path metrics across multiple loop iterations while preserving linear overhead characteristics. Our approach introduces a lightweight iteration-aware counter scheme that maps repetitive edge traversals to compact, loop-invariant path identifiers without incurring prohibitive memory or runtime penalties. We evaluate the technique on a diverse benchmark suite spanning computational kernels and industry applications, accurately extracting multi-iteration hot paths with less than 8 percent average slowdown. Results indicate that our method uncovers optimization opportunities missed by conventional single-call profilers, particularly in data-dependent loops with complex branching patterns. These findings establish a solid foundation for next-generation profile-guided compilation strategies targeting iterative workloads.

title: Visual Analytics for Explainable and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
text_ai: Our society increasingly depends on intelligent systems to solve complex problems, ranging from recommender systems suggesting the next movie to watch to AI models assisting in medical diagnoses for hospitalized patients. With the iterative improvement of diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, AI holds significant potential to mitigate medical misdiagnoses by preventing numerous deaths and reducing an economic burden of approximately 450 EUR billion annually. However, this transformative potential is frequently undermined by the opaque nature of contemporary machine learning architectures. Such opacity severely impedes clinician adoption, erodes stakeholder trust, and complicates regulatory compliance. To bridge this gap, we introduce a visual analytics framework engineered to enhance the interpretability and accountability of complex AI decision-making processes. Our approach integrates interactive visualization techniques with post-hoc explanation methods, enabling domain experts to dynamically probe model behavior, isolate salient input features, and validate reasoning pathways against established clinical guidelines. Through structured evaluations and controlled case studies, we demonstrate that the proposed interface significantly improves practitioners’ capacity to detect algorithmic biases, comprehend prediction rationales, and maintain appropriate oversight. These results highlight the imperative of embedding transparent, human-centric design principles within AI infrastructure. Ultimately, this research advances trustworthy artificial intelligence by equipping clinicians with diagnostics that align computational outputs with professional judgment, thereby promoting safer integration.

title: Parallelized Wireless Sensing System for Continuous Monitoring of Microtissue Spheroids.
text_ai: Currently, the use of electrical readout methods for the investigation of microtissue spheroids in combination with lab automation tools is hindered by the cable connections that are required to interrogate the on-chip-integrated electrodes. To overcome this limitation, we developed a wireless sensor scheme, which can detect the size variation of microtissues during long-term culturing and drug exposure assays. The system integrates miniaturized impedance spectroscopy chips with a custom radio-frequency transceiver array, enabling simultaneous interrogation of up to ninety-six distinct culture wells without physical tethering. Real-time data transmission is facilitated via a low-power Bluetooth mesh network, synchronized with automated liquid handling platforms to maintain strict environmental control. Calibration experiments demonstrate sub-micrometer resolution in spheroid radius tracking over fourteen-day periods, with signal stability maintained despite media evaporation and metabolic byproduct accumulation. When applied to chemotherapeutic screening campaigns, the platform reliably captures dose-dependent morphological shrinkage and necrotic core expansion, correlating strongly (R² > 0.94) with conventional fluorescence-based viability assays. Furthermore, the decoupled architecture eliminates mechanical stress on delicate tissue constructs, preserving native cellular signaling pathways throughout extended observation windows. By merging high-density parallelization with untethered electrophysiological monitoring, this approach establishes a scalable infrastructure for dynamic phenotypic profiling. Ultimately, the proposed framework accelerates global preclinical and clinically relevant drug discovery pipelines while providing a robust foundation for next-generation microphysiological systems demanding uninterrupted, multi-parameter physiological surveillance.

title: Image Fusion Transformer
text_ai: In image fusion, images obtained from different sensors are fused to generate a single image with enhanced information. In recent years, state-of-the-art methods have adopted Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) to encode meaningful features for image fusion. Specifically, CNN-based methods perform image fusion by fusing local features. However, their inherent inductive bias restricts the modeling of long-range spatial dependencies, thereby limiting the representation capacity for complex multimodal scenes. To address this limitation, we propose a novel Transformer-based framework that explicitly captures global contextual relationships across heterogeneous modalities. Our approach introduces a cross-modal attention mechanism that dynamically aligns and aggregates complementary features from infrared and visible inputs at multiple scales. By leveraging self-attention modules within a hierarchical encoder-decoder architecture, the model effectively preserves structural details while enhancing salient targets. Furthermore, we design a lightweight fusion module that adaptively weights modality-specific contributions without introducing significant computational overhead. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing CNN-based and early Transformer approaches in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. The proposed architecture achieves superior robustness under challenging illumination conditions and complex backgrounds, establishing a new state-of-the-art for multispectral image fusion. Evaluation confirms generalization across diverse scenarios. Code and pretrained models will be made publicly available.

title: Combining cues to judge distance and direction in an immersive virtual reality environment.
text_ai: When we move, the visual direction of objects in the environment can change substantially. Compared with our understanding of depth perception, the problem the visual system faces in computing this change is relatively poorly understood. Here, we tested the extent to which participants' judgments of visual direction could be predicted by standard cue combination rules. Participants navigated a stereoscopic head-mounted display simulating natural locomotion while estimating the azimuthal bearing and range of target landmarks. Stimuli were constructed to manipulate reliability across monocular perspective, texture gradient, and dynamic motion parallax cues. Behavioral data were fitted against normative Bayesian integration models and simple linear regression baselines. Results indicated that participants combined directional and distance information in a manner that closely approximated statistically optimal weighting, particularly when cue reliabilities were explicitly varied through controlled rendering parameters. However, systematic biases emerged under high ecological validity conditions, revealing a consistent overreliance on egocentric motion parallax relative to static perspective cues. These deviations suggest that while human vision adheres broadly to rational cue integration principles during translational movement, it incorporates prior expectations about environmental structure that are not captured by standard linear models. Collectively, these findings advance computational accounts of spatial updating and provide critical constraints for designing perceptually accurate virtual environments, where cue conflict management remains a primary challenge for achieving seamless navigation and reducing simulator sickness.

title: Why Are You Wrong? Counterfactual Explanations for Language Grounding with 3D Objects
text_ai: Combining natural language and geometric shapes is an emerging research area with multiple applications in robotics and language-assisted design. A crucial task in this domain is object referent identification, which involves selecting a 3D object given a textual description of the target. However, existing neural grounding models operate as black boxes, offering no diagnostic insight into why specific selection errors occur. To bridge this interpretability gap, we propose a counterfactual explanation framework tailored to 3D language grounding. Our method algorithmically perturbs geometric primitives and spatial configurations of candidate objects to identify the minimal attribute modifications necessary to shift the model’s decision boundary toward the correct referent. This process explicitly surfaces the semantic-geometric alignments responsible for misclassification. We validate our approach on three standard embodied navigation benchmarks, quantifying explanation fidelity through automated perturbation analysis and subjective utility via controlled human studies. Empirical results indicate that our counterfactuals consistently achieve high predictive accuracy while requiring fewer than five attribute adjustments per instance. Moreover, deploying these explanations within an iterative refinement pipeline yields a 23 percent reduction in repeated grounding failures during downstream robotic deployment. Ultimately, this work demonstrates that structured counterfactual reasoning not only clarifies model internals but also enables systematic error mitigation, advancing the development of transparent and trustworthy multimodal interaction systems across diverse real-world scenarios.

title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling for Logistic Bandits
text_ai: We study the performance of the Thompson Sampling algorithm for logistic bandit problems. In this setting, an agent receives binary rewards with probabilities determined by a logistic function, $\exp(\beta \langle a, \theta \rangle)/(1+\exp(\beta \langle a, \theta \rangle))$, with slope parameter $\beta>0$, and where both the action $a\in \mathcal{A}$ and parameter $\theta \in \mathcal{O}$ lie within the $d$-dimensional unit ball. We derive tight upper bounds on the cumulative regret that explicitly characterize the dependence on the curvature parameter $\beta$, the dimensionality $d$, and the time horizon $T$. By leveraging information-theoretic techniques, we establish a minimax lower bound that matches our upper bound up to logarithmic factors, demonstrating the near-optimality of Thompson Sampling in this non-linear reward structure. Our analysis carefully handles the non-concavity of the logistic likelihood and the coupling between posterior sampling and exploration-exploitation trade-offs. Specifically, we introduce a novel potential function based on the Kullback-Leibler divergence between successive posteriors, which enables precise control over the expected number of suboptimal arm pulls. The resulting regret scaling of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{d T}/\beta)$ reveals how increased model sensitivity degrades sample efficiency. These findings bridge the gap between linear bandit theory and generalized linear models, providing practitioners with actionable guidance on calibration and uncertainty quantification in high-stakes sequential decision-making applications.

title: Robustness of diabatic enhancement in quantum annealing
text_ai: In adiabatic quantum annealing, the speed with which an anneal can be run, while still achieving a high final ground state fidelity, is dictated by the size of the minimum gap that appears between the ground and first excited state in the annealing spectrum. Recent theoretical and experimental studies suggest that deliberate non-adiabatic transitions can paradoxically improve solution quality by exploiting coherent tunneling pathways that circumvent narrow avoided crossings. However, the persistence of this diabatic enhancement under realistic hardware constraints remains poorly understood. Here, we systematically quantify its robustness across varying noise strengths, control inaccuracies, and problem geometries. Using high-fidelity tensor network simulations combined with perturbative open-system dynamics, we demonstrate that diabatic speedups survive substantial dephasing and amplitude damping when the annealing schedule is optimized via counterdiabatic-inspired pulse shaping. Our comprehensive analysis reveals a distinct operational regime where controlled departures from strict adiabaticity yield order-of-magnitude runtime reductions while preserving ground-state overlap, even amid thermal fluctuations comparable to standard device operating temperatures. Furthermore, we map specific topological features within the underlying energy landscape that directly correlate with enhanced diabatic resilience, thereby establishing actionable calibration guidelines for contemporary quantum processors. These findings position diabatic enhancement not as a detrimental artifact, but as a robust, engineering-friendly protocol that bridges the divide between idealized closed-system dynamics and experimentally accessible hardware constraints.

title: Randomized Oversampling for Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Methods
text_ai: In this paper, we study the development of efficient multiscale methods for flows in heterogeneous media. Our approach uses the Generalized Multiscale Finite Element (GMsFEM) framework. The main idea of GMsFEM is to approximate the solution space locally using a few multiscale basis functions. To enhance accuracy without incurring prohibitive computational costs, we introduce a novel randomized oversampling strategy that adaptively selects extension regions around coarse grid nodes. By leveraging probabilistic sampling techniques, our method constructs localized snapshot spaces that capture essential fine-scale heterogeneities while significantly reducing overall dimensionality. We derive rigorous *a priori* error estimates demonstrating exponential decay with respect to both the oversampling radius and the cardinality of the randomly generated spectral subspace. The resulting generalized eigenvalue problem is solved efficiently through iterative projection schemes tailored to sparse matrix structures. Furthermore, we embed this stochastic framework within a domain decomposition solver, guaranteeing optimal load balancing for large-scale parallel implementations. Extensive numerical experiments across highly contrasted permeability distributions validate that the proposed methodology outperforms traditional deterministic oversampling and baseline GMsFEM formulations in both convergence rate and memory footprint. These findings position randomized oversampling as a scalable, theoretically grounded alternative for accelerating multiscale flow simulations in complex subsurface environments.

title: On the interplay between notions of additive and multiplicative largeness and its combinatorial applications
text_ai: Many natural notions of additive and multiplicative largeness arise from results in Ramsey theory. In this paper, we explain the relationships between these notions for subsets of $\mathbb{N}$ and in more general ring-theoretic structures. We show that multiplicative largeness begets additive largeness in three ways and give a collection of examples demonstrating the optimality of these results. These implications generalize classical density and recurrence phenomena, effectively bridging structural Ramsey theory with algebraic combinatorics. We further establish corresponding converse failures through carefully constructed counterexamples, highlighting the intrinsic asymmetry of arithmetic largeness across distinct algebraic contexts. Building upon these foundational comparisons, we derive novel partition regularity criteria for multivariate polynomial configurations and sharpen existing quantitative bounds within the density Hales–Jewett theorem. Our unifying framework simultaneously yields streamlined proofs of several recent combinatorial corollaries concerning sum-free subsets and generalized geometric progressions. Moreover, we demonstrate how these largeness hierarchies naturally induce idempotent ultrafilter properties in Stone–Čech compactifications, thereby connecting our structural findings to topological dynamics. Finally, we delineate open questions concerning the interaction of multiplicative and additive syndeticity in non-commutative rings, establishing a rigorous taxonomy of arithmetic largeness that provides practical tools for addressing longstanding conjectures in extremal set theory, finite geometry, and ergodic Ramsey theory.

title: Significant core shift variability in parsec-scale jets of active galactic nuclei
text_ai: The apparent position of jet base (core) in radio-loud active galactic nuclei changes with frequency because of synchrotron self-absorption. Studying this `core shift` effect enables us to reconstruct properties of the jet regions close to the central engine. However, most existing measurements rely on single-epoch snapshots or averaged light curves, potentially masking intrinsic temporal evolution. Here we present a systematic analysis of core shift variability using multi-epoch millimeter Very Long Baseline Interferometry observations of a flux-limited sample of 12 bright blazars spanning 2015–2023. By fitting frequency-dependent optical depth profiles along the jet axis, we derive precise core positions at 3, 7, 11, 15, 22, and 43 GHz for each epoch. We find that core shift amplitudes vary significantly over timescales of months to years, with peak-to-peak displacements reaching up to 0.15 mas, corresponding to physical scales of several hundred gravitational radii. This variability is strongly correlated with observed bulk flow deceleration, transverse brightness fluctuations, and spectral index variations, suggesting dynamic reconfiguration of the magnetized plasma near the launch region. Our results challenge the conventional assumption of a steady, conical jet geometry and imply that magnetic field topology and acceleration mechanisms evolve on short dynamical timescales. These findings underscore the necessity of high-cadence, multi-frequency VLBI monitoring campaigns to accurately constrain black hole masses, jet power, and the fundamental conditions governing relativistic outflow initiation.

title: Less or More: Towards Glanceable Explanations for LLM Recommendations Using Ultra-Small Devices
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable potential in recommending everyday actions as personal AI assistants, while Explainable AI (XAI) techniques are being increasingly utilized to help users understand why a recommendation is given. Personal AI assistants today are often located on ultra-small devices such as smartwatches, which have limited screen space. To address this constraint, we introduce a dynamic explanation adaptation framework that optimizes visual information density without compromising interpretability. Rather than rendering verbose textual rationales, our approach implements a hierarchical “less-or-more” paradigm that initially surfaces concise, glanceable cues—such as symbolic indicators, confidence heatmaps, and truncated semantic tokens—designed for sub-second perceptual processing. Users may subsequently trigger progressive disclosure to reveal granular reasoning paths when deeper scrutiny is required. We integrated this mechanism into a wearable-optimized recommender agent and evaluated its performance through a mixed-methods user study involving 48 participants navigating simulated smartwatch interactions. Quantitative metrics indicate that glanceable explanations decrease cognitive load by 32% relative to traditional full-text outputs while preserving equivalent decision accuracy and trust alignment. Qualitative analyses further confirm that interface-aware truncation preserves critical contextual signals within minimal display footprints. Collectively, these results validate the viability of deploying lightweight, transparent XAI components on severely resource-constrained hardware. By privileging rapid comprehension over exhaustive detail, this research provides actionable design guidelines for embedding explainability into ambient personal AI systems.

title: Optimized Treatment Schedules for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
text_ai: Over the past decade, several targeted therapies (e.g. imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib) have been developed to treat Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Despite an initial response to therapy, drug resistance remains a problem for some CML patients. To address this clinical challenge, we developed a pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) modeling framework integrated with optimal control theory to evaluate alternative dosing regimens. Using in vitro proliferation assays and clinical BCR-ABL1 transcript data from Phase II trials, we simulated tumor dynamics under continuous versus intermittent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) protocols. Our model incorporates mutation accumulation rates, cellular apoptosis thresholds, and drug clearance kinetics to predict long-term disease suppression. Simulation results demonstrate that pulsed dosing strategies, optimized via adaptive feedback mechanisms, significantly reduce cumulative toxicity while maintaining molecular remission rates comparable to standard daily administration. Specifically, a biweekly high-dose regimen improved target engagement efficiency by 23% and delayed emergence of T315I-resistant clones by approximately 14 months compared to conventional schedules. These computational predictions were subsequently validated against retrospective patient cohorts (n=142), confirming superior progression-free survival trajectories. The findings underscore the therapeutic potential of mathematically optimized scheduling as a viable strategy to mitigate resistance onset and enhance treatment durability. We propose integrating these algorithm-driven protocols into prospective clinical trials to redefine standard-of-care paradigms for chronic-phase CML management.

title: Nonconservation of lepton current and asymmetry of relic neutrinos
text_ai: The neutrino asymmetry in the early universe plasma, $n_\nu - n_{\bar \nu}$, is calculated both before and after the electroweak phase transition (EWPT). The leptogenesis before EWPT within the standard model is well known to be driven by the abelian anomaly in a massless hypercharge field. We derive the full set of coupled Boltzmann equations incorporating finite-temperature corrections to the chiral anomaly equation, explicitly accounting for the interplay between weak sphaleron transitions and the decay of heavy right-handed neutrinos. Prior to the EWPT, the anomalous divergence of the lepton current generates a net lepton charge that is partially converted into baryon asymmetry through rapid sphaleron processes. Following symmetry breaking, the W-boson masses suppress these transitions, effectively freezing the transferred asymmetry while leaving a residual neutrino chemical potential. Our numerical integration reveals that the post-EWPT relic neutrino asymmetry scales logarithmically with the initial CP-violating phase, yielding $\Delta N_{\rm eff} \sim 0.05$ for typical seesaw scales, consistent with current Planck constraints. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the nonconservation of the lepton current induces a parity-violating transport coefficient that enhances the neutrino decoupling temperature by approximately 3 MeV compared to standard thermal histories. This modification alters the primordial helium abundance and shifts the Silk damping scale in the cosmic microwave background power spectrum. The resulting spectral distortion provides a potentially observable signature of early-universe lepton number violation, offering a complementary probe to direct searches for leptogenesis at high-energy colliders. Our findings establish a robust framework linking microphysical anomaly-driven dynamics to macroscopic cosmological observables, emphasizing the critical role of quantum transport in shaping the neutrino sector of the Standard Model extended by massive Majorana states.

title: Multiple single-photon generations in three-level atoms coupled to cavity with non-Markovian effects
text_ai: In this paper, we show how to generate the multiple single-photon wavepackets of arbitrary temporal shape from an optical cavity coupled with $N$ three-level atoms driven by a driving field in the non-Markovian regime. By employing a rigorous master-equation formalism that explicitly accounts for finite bath correlation times, we derive closed-form expressions for the conditional emission dynamics under time-dependent control fields. The non-Markovian memory effects are modeled through a Lorentzian spectral density, which induces back-action currents that temporarily store and reemit excitation energy into the cavity mode. Leveraging this reversible exchange, we implement a gradient-based optimal control protocol to sculpt the atomic dipole trajectories, thereby prescribing the desired photon waveform at the output port. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the scheme achieves near-unity generation fidelity across a broad spectrum of target profiles, encompassing symmetric Gaussians, asymmetric exponential rise-and-fall envelopes, and complex interferometric templates. Furthermore, analytical derivations confirm that the effective collective coupling scales proportionally to $\sqrt{N}$, facilitating ultrafast photon extraction while mitigating intrinsic decoherence through constructive interference. Crucially, the control protocol exhibits pronounced resilience to moderate parameter fluctuations in both atom-cavity detunings and environmental bath cutoff frequencies, underscoring its feasibility for solid-state and trapped-ion platforms. These findings establish a versatile pathway for deterministic multi-photon state preparation, with applications in boson sampling, linear optical quantum computing, and the coherent routing of flying qubits within scalable quantum networks.

title: Non-Uniform Time-Step Deep Q-Network for Carrier-Sense Multiple Access in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
text_ai: This paper investigates a new class of carrier-sense multiple access (CSMA) protocols that employ deep reinforcement learning (DRL) techniques, referred to as carrier-sense deep-reinforcement learning multiple access (CS-DLMA). The goal of CS-DLMA is to enable efficient and equitable spectrum sharing among a group of co-located heterogeneous wireless networks. To address the limitations of conventional fixed-interval sensing mechanisms, we introduce a novel non-uniform time-step deep Q-network architecture that dynamically adjusts decision intervals based on real-time channel occupancy and stochastic traffic demands. By decoupling action execution from rigid temporal grids, the proposed framework significantly reduces signaling overhead while preserving strict collision-avoidance constraints. Each distributed agent processes partial observability through a recurrent memory module, mapping local channel state information, buffer occupancy, and cross-layer interference metrics to optimized backoff parameters via a centralized training with decentralized execution scheme. A structured multi-objective reward function simultaneously penalizes excessive collisions, prioritizes low-latency flows, and enforces Jain’s fairness index across heterogeneous node categories. Comprehensive numerical evaluations under realistic path-loss models, varying contention window sizes, and bursty traffic distributions reveal that CS-DLMA achieves superior spectral utilization compared to IEEE 802.11 standards and equilibrium-based DRL counterparts. Quantitatively, the adaptive stepping policy improves normalized system throughput by 31.7% and decreases median packet delay by 24.3%, particularly during high-contention regimes. Moreover, ablation studies confirm that the non-uniform scheduling component contributes over 60% of the observed performance gains, highlighting its critical role in mitigating hidden-node effects. Convergence analysis further demonstrates stable learning dynamics under rapidly shifting channel conditions, validating the methodology as a scalable foundation for autonomous medium access control in dense, multi-vendor wireless ecosystems.

title: Energy Loss of Solar $p$ Modes due to the excitation of Magnetic Sausage Tube Waves: Importance of Coupling the Upper Atmosphere
text_ai: We consider damping and absorption of solar $p$ modes due to their energy loss to magnetic tube waves that can freely carry energy out of the acoustic cavity. The coupling of $p$ modes and sausage tube waves is studied in a model atmosphere composed of a polytropic interior above which lies an isothermal upper atmosphere. We derive the transmission coefficients by matching vertical displacement and total pressure perturbations across the interface, explicitly accounting for the exponential density stratification characteristic of chromospheric layers. Our analysis reveals that coupling efficiency depends critically on the ratio of the atmospheric scale height to the magnetic flux tube radius. When the upper atmosphere extends sufficiently upward, resonant interactions between the global $p$-mode spectrum and localized tube eigenmodes significantly enhance energy extraction, producing measurable linewidth broadening. We demonstrate that neglecting this stratified extension systematically underestimates the damping rate by approximately thirty-five percent for field strengths exceeding one kilogauss. Furthermore, the transition from evanescent to propagating regimes within the overlying medium acts as a spectral filter, preferentially attenuating higher-order radial modes while preserving low-degree fundamental oscillations. Phase velocity dispersion relations derived in the thin-tube limit identify distinct cutoff frequencies that govern mode conversion efficiency. Numerical integration of the linearized magnetohydrodynamic equations validates these asymptotic results and quantifies non-adiabatic losses arising from thermal conduction along field lines. These findings underscore the essential role of chromospheric thermodynamics in modulating magnetoacoustic energy transfer. Consequently, robust helioseismic inversions must incorporate realistic magnetic canopy geometries and temperature gradients to accurately interpret observed mode lifetimes. This framework establishes a physically consistent foundation for reconciling theoretical damping predictions with high-resolution observations of solar oscillation decay.

title: Short-ranged interaction effects on $Z_2$ topological phase transitions: The perturbative mean-field method
text_ai: Time-reversal symmetric topological insulator is a novel state of matter that a bulk-insulating state carries dissipationless spin transport along the surfaces, embedded by the $Z_2$ topological invariant. In the noninteracting limit, this exotic state has been intensively studied and explored with realistic systems, such as HgTe/(Hg,Cd)Te quantum wells. However, the inclusion of electron-electron interactions fundamentally alters the topological classification, necessitating a rigorous treatment beyond single-particle band theory. Short-ranged repulsive potentials, ubiquitous in solid-state platforms, induce many-body correlations that renormalize effective mass terms and potentially drive quantum phase transitions between trivial and topological regimes. To address this challenge, we develop a systematic perturbative mean-field framework that self-consistently incorporates local interaction terms while preserving time-reversal symmetry constraints. By expanding the interacting Hamiltonian around the noninteracting Dirac cone reference state, we derive analytic expressions for the renormalized mass parameter and interaction-dependent gap corrections up to second order in the coupling strength. Applying this formalism to low-dimensional tight-binding models, we demonstrate that moderate short-ranged interactions shift the critical bare mass threshold required for the $Z_2$ topological transition, effectively tuning the phase boundary without altering its universal critical behavior. Our analysis reveals a non-monotonic dependence of the topological gap on interaction strength, where screening effects compete with exchange-driven band inversion. Furthermore, we establish explicit bounds for the validity regime of the perturbative expansion, identifying the crossover into strongly correlated domains where conventional mean-field decoupling breaks down. These results provide a transparent analytical tool for predicting interaction-driven topological phase transitions in quantum spin Hall and three-dimensional topological insulators, offering direct guidance for experimental investigations of correlated topological matter.

title: Mitigating ML Model Decay in Continuous Integration with Data Drift Detection: An Empirical Study
text_ai: Background: Machine Learning (ML) methods are being increasingly used for automating different activities, e.g., Test Case Prioritization (TCP), of Continuous Integration (CI). However, ML models need frequent retraining as a result of changes in the CI environment, more commonly known as data drift. Also, continuously retraining ML models consume a lot of time and effort. To address these challenges, we propose a novel framework that integrates proactive data drift detection mechanisms directly into the CI pipeline to monitor model performance degradation. Instead of executing periodic full-scale retraining cycles, our approach triggers targeted updates only when statistically significant distribution shifts are detected between historical training data and incoming continuous integration artifacts. We empirically evaluate this strategy across three industrial-grade TCP repositories spanning eighteen months of commit history, rigorously assessing classification fidelity and resource utilization throughout extended deployment phases. Our experimental setup compares the proposed drift-aware retraining protocol against baseline approaches employing fixed-interval updates and fully reactive retraining upon performance drops. We measure both predictive accuracy recovery and computational overhead using standard CI metrics. We further validate cross-project generalizability through leave-one-out validation. Our findings demonstrate that the drift-detection-guided approach reduces unnecessary retraining operations by 68% while maintaining prediction stability within a 2.1% accuracy variance threshold. Furthermore, the intervention successfully anticipates model decay events an average of four build cycles prior to observable performance degradation, enabling seamless pipeline execution without manual intervention. These results indicate that strategic drift monitoring offers a scalable alternative to exhaustive retraining schedules, substantially lowering maintenance costs in automated software engineering workflows. This study provides practitioners with actionable guidelines for implementing adaptive ML lifecycle management in high-frequency CI environments.

title: Paxos Made EPR: Decidable Reasoning about Distributed Protocols
text_ai: Distributed protocols such as Paxos play an important role in many computer systems. Therefore, a bug in a distributed protocol may have tremendous effects. Accordingly, a lot of effort has been invested in verifying such protocols. However, checking invariants of such protocols is undecidable and hard in practice, as it requires reasoning about an unbounded number of nodes and messages. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a novel encoding framework that translates safety properties of Paxos-like protocols directly into the decidable EPR fragment of first-order logic. By carefully constraining message domains and bounding participant states through parameterized abstractions, our approach preserves essential protocol semantics while ensuring quantifier prefixes remain restricted to existential-universal patterns over finite domains. The transformation relies on a symmetric abstraction that uniformly treats all participants, thereby sidestepping the combinatorial blowup typically associated with unbounded process replication. We implement this translation within a modern SMT solver backend and evaluate it on several canonical consensus variants, including Multi-Paxos and Raft adaptations. Our experiments demonstrate that the EPR reduction eliminates state-space explosion without sacrificing precision, enabling fully automated invariant checking across configurations with arbitrarily large node counts. Compared to traditional model checkers and theorem provers, our method achieves orders-of-magnitude speedups while guaranteeing completeness for the targeted property classes. Furthermore, we provide a mechanized correctness proof showing that any counterexample extracted from the EPR instance corresponds to a valid execution trace in the original protocol. This work establishes a practical bridge between theoretical decidability results and industrial-grade verification, offering a scalable foundation for formally reasoning about fault-tolerant distributed systems.

title: Continual Evolution in Nonreciprocal Ecological Models
text_ai: Feedbacks between evolution and ecology are ubiquitous, with ecological interactions determining which mutants are successful, and these mutants in turn modifying community structure. We study the evolutionary dynamics of several ecological models with overlapping niches, including consumer resource and Lotka-Volterra models. By employing adaptive dynamics frameworks and high-dimensional numerical simulations, we characterize how asymmetry in interspecific interactions alters long-term evolutionary trajectories. Contrary to classical predictions of evolutionary branching followed by stable coexistence, nonreciprocal coupling generates persistent directional selection that prevents trait fixation. Instead, lineages undergo continuous adaptive walks through phenotypic space, producing either unbounded drift, limit cycles, or deterministic chaos depending on interaction topology and niche overlap. We demonstrate that this continual evolution emerges directly from the spectral properties of the community Jacobian, wherein complex eigenvalues sustain oscillatory selective pressures even at ecological equilibrium. Analytical treatment of symmetric versus asymmetric interaction matrices reveals that reciprocity acts as a damping mechanism, funneling communities toward evolutionarily stable strategies, whereas nonreciprocity preserves transient dynamics indefinitely. These findings challenge the assumption that eco-evolutionary systems inevitably reach static endpoints, suggesting instead that asymmetric competition and facilitation can lock ecosystems into perpetual adaptation. Our results provide a mechanistic bridge between theoretical population genetics and modern network ecology, offering testable predictions for microbial consortia and experimental evolution systems where directional fitness landscapes dominate. Ultimately, continual evolution in nonreciprocal food webs may serve as a fundamental driver of sustained diversity and functional redundancy in changing environments. These insights refine understanding of eco-evolutionary stability and underscore the necessity of incorporating interaction asymmetry into robust predictive models of biodiversity maintenance.

title: Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking: A Novel Way to Discover Anisotropy in nano-Hz Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background
text_ai: The isotropic stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) generated by a population of supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) provides a unique window into their cosmic evolution. In addition to the isotropic power spectrum, the anisotropic component of the signal carries additional information about the supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and host galaxy connection. Traditional anisotropy reconstruction techniques struggle with the low angular resolution and high noise levels inherent to pulsar timing arrays and space-based interferometers at nano-Hz frequencies. To overcome these limitations, we introduce Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking, a novel analysis framework that leverages cross-correlations between GW strain data and multiple independent electromagnetic tracer populations, such as luminous red galaxies, active galactic nuclei, and star-forming halos. By jointly weighting these diverse cosmological probes according to their clustering bias and number density, our method effectively suppresses uncorrelated instrumental noise while amplifying the underlying astrophysical signal. We validate the pipeline using realistic mock datasets generated under ΛCDM cosmology, incorporating foreground contaminants and survey selection functions representative of upcoming wide-field optical and radio surveys. Our simulations demonstrate that multi-tracer stacking enhances the signal-to-noise ratio of the SGWB anisotropy map by up to a factor of three compared to single-probe approaches, enabling robust detection at angular scales below one degree. Furthermore, the stacked maps reveal spatially resolved features that trace the large-scale structure of the cosmic web, offering direct constraints on the duty cycle and merger timescales of SMBHBs across different host environments. This framework establishes a scalable pathway for extracting subtle anisotropic signatures from next-generation nano-Hz observatories, bridging the gap between gravitational-wave astronomy and precision cosmology.

title: Magnetically-driven explosions of rapidly-rotating white dwarfs following Accretion-Induced Collapse
text_ai: We present 2D multi-group flux-limited diffusion magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) simulations of the Accretion-Induced Collapse (AIC) of a rapidly-rotating white dwarf. We focus on the dynamical role of MHD processes after the formation of a millisecond-period protoneutron star. During the initial post-collapse phase, extreme differential shear and convective turbulence efficiently amplify weak primordial fields through magnetorotational instability and small-scale dynamo action, generating ultra-strong poloidal and toroidal components exceeding 10^15 G within tens of milliseconds. These saturated fields extract rotational energy from the hypermassive remnant, launching highly collimated, relativistic outflows that disrupt the overlying stellar envelope. The resulting magnetocentrifugally driven explosions yield kinetic energies ranging from 3×10^49 to 8×10^49 erg, with ejecta masses of approximately 0.01–0.05 M⊙. Nucleosynthetic calculations indicate a predominantly iron-peak composition, supplemented by trace amounts of intermediate-mass elements synthesized in the shock-heated outer layers. Time-dependent radiative transfer modeling reveals rapid bolometric decline curves peaking at absolute magnitudes between −15 and −17, consistent with recently observed fast, luminous optical transients. Notably, the sustained magnetic pressure supports quasi-steady jet propagation even when thermal pressure gradients decay, suggesting a robust pathway for magnetically powered transients in low-metallicity environments. Our results demonstrate that the AIC channel provides a natural explanation for a subset of underluminous supernovae and fast blue optical transients previously attributed to binary neutron star mergers or collapsar scenarios. Furthermore, the asymmetric mass ejection imparts significant recoil velocities to the newly formed neutron star, potentially accounting for observed pulsar proper motions. These findings establish magnetohydrodynamic instabilities as the primary engine governing post-AIC dynamics, offering testable predictions for upcoming high-cadence time-domain surveys and multi-messenger observatories.
