title: Weak Multiplier Hopf Algebras. The main theory
text_ai: A weak multiplier Hopf algebra is a pair (A,\Delta) of a non-degenerate idempotent algebra A and a coproduct $\Delta$ on A. The coproduct is a coassociative homomorphism from A to the multiplier algebra M(A\otimes A) with some natural extra properties (like the existence of a counit). Central to the development is the rigorous construction of an antipode $S$, emerging as a bijective anti-homomorphism satisfying the fundamental compatibility relations with $\Delta$. We establish that the canonical Galois maps associated with $\Delta$ are necessarily surjective, thereby ensuring regularity and enabling a robust calculus of tensor products over $A$. A principal achievement is the systematic theory of invariant functionals: we prove the existence and uniqueness of left and right cointegrals up to scalar multiples, demonstrating their pivotal role in characterizing semisimplicity and cosemisimplicity within this non-unital framework. Furthermore, we develop a comprehensive duality theory, showing that the dual object inherits a natural structure when restricted to suitable subspaces. Our analysis extends to the representation category, where we construct a monoidal equivalence between the module category of $(A,\Delta)$ and the corepresentation category of its dual. We explicitly address the non-regular case, providing necessary and sufficient conditions for a well-behaved antipode and establishing a trace formula for integrals. This approach resolves longstanding ambiguities regarding normalization and yields explicit dimension formulas for finite-dimensional representations. Finally, we classify important families of examples arising from groupoids, inverse semigroups, and locally compact quantum groups, illustrating how the present framework unifies previously disparate constructions in non-commutative geometry and operator algebra theory. Collectively, these findings establish a rigorous foundation for subsequent analytic and categorical developments.

title: Left atrial function in patients with light chain amyloidosis: A transthoracic 3D speckle tracking imaging study.
text_ai: Systemic light chain amyloidosis (AL) is characterized by the extracellular deposition of amyloid fibrils. Transthoracic echocardiography is the modality of choice to assess cardiac function in patients with AL. Whereas left ventricular (LV) function has been well studied in this patient population, data regarding the value of left atrial (LA) function in AL patients are lacking. We prospectively enrolled 82 consecutive patients with biopsy-proven AL amyloidosis and 40 matched healthy controls. All participants underwent transthoracic echocardiography complemented by three-dimensional speckle-tracking imaging (3D STI). All image acquisitions were performed using standardized vendor-independent software. Contour tracing quantified global longitudinal peak strain across reservoir, conduit, and active contraction phases. Concurrently, left ventricular global longitudinal strain and transmitral Doppler indices were derived. AL patients demonstrated significantly lower LA reservoir (18.4 ± 6.2 vs 32.1 ± 5.8%; p < 0.001), conduit (11.2 ± 4.7 vs 19.8 ± 4.1%; p < 0.001), and booster pump strains (7.1 ± 3.5 vs 12.4 ± 3.2%; p < 0.001) versus controls. Three-dimensional LA reservoir strain correlated inversely with serum NT-proBNP concentrations (r = −0.64; p < 0.001) and positively with LV global longitudinal strain (r = 0.59; p < 0.001). Over 14 months, 28 patients sustained major adverse cardiac events. Multivariable analysis identified reduced LA reservoir strain as an independent predictor of mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.38 per 5% decrement; 95% CI 1.15–1.66; p < 0.001), outperforming LA volume index and conventional LV parameters. Three-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography uncovers profound, phase-specific left atrial dysfunction in systemic AL amyloidosis. These alterations closely track disease severity, providing incremental prognostic value beyond standard hemodynamic metrics and supporting routine 3D LA strain incorporation into baseline cardiac phenotyping.

title: Depinning and flow of a vortex line in an uniaxial random medium
text_ai: We study numerically and analytically the dynamics of a single directed elastic string driven through a 3-dimensional disordered medium. In the quasistatic limit the string is super-rough in the driving direction, with roughness exponent $\zeta_{\parallel} = 1.25\pm 0.01$, dynamic exponent $z_{\parallel}= 1.43 \pm 0.01$, correlation-length exponent $\nu= 1.33 \pm 0.02$, depinning exponent $\beta = 0.24\pm 0.01$, and avalanche-size exponent $\tau_{\parallel} = 1.09 \pm 0.03$. At finite driving velocities, we derive a unified scaling ansatz that interpolates between the quasistatic pinning regime and the high-velocity viscous flow, revealing distinct crossover scales governed by the interplay of thermal fluctuations and uniaxial anisotropy. Our functional renormalization group calculations reproduce the critical exponents within statistical uncertainty, confirming that the system belongs to the quenched Edwards–Wilkinson universality class modified by long-range correlations along the preferred axis. We demonstrate that the uniaxial random potential induces a pronounced directional asymmetry in the avalanche statistics, suppressing transverse fluctuations while enhancing longitudinal memory effects. This asymmetry manifests as a systematic deviation from isotropic scaling laws at intermediate drives, which we quantify through a generalized Larkin length that depends explicitly on the correlation ratio of the disorder. For applications to type-II superconductors, we map our continuum model onto the Abrikosov vortex lattice, showing that columnar defects aligned with the magnetic field effectively realize the uniaxial geometry studied here. The resulting framework provides precise quantitative predictions for the critical current suppression and flux creep activation barriers in anisotropic pinning landscapes. These findings establish a robust theoretical baseline for interpreting transport measurements in strongly correlated electron systems where topological defect motion governs macroscopic dissipation.

title: Quasi-Discrete Locally Compact Quantum Groups
text_ai: Consider a C*-algebra $A$ with a comultiplication $\Delta$. This pair is usually thought of as locally compact quantum semi-group. When these notes were written, in 1993, it was not at all clear what the extra assumptions on the comultiplication should be for this pair to be a 'locally compact quantum group'. Here we resolve this foundational ambiguity by introducing a refined axiomatization tailored to the quasi-discrete regime. Building upon the canonical existence of left and right invariant Haar weights, we impose a spectral constraint on the scaling group that forces the underlying quantum semigroup to decompose into a direct sum of finite-dimensional matrix algebras indexed by a discrete parameter set. This quasi-discreteness criterion naturally yields a rigid tensor category of unitary corepresentations, whose Grothendieck ring encodes the algebraic structure of $A$ and the combinatorial data of $\Delta$. We demonstrate that every such object admits a unique bi-invariant state satisfying the modular covariance required for a locally compact quantum group in the sense of Kustermans and Vaes. Furthermore, we establish a Pontryagin-type duality theorem showing that the quasi-discrete property is preserved under quantum group duality, thereby extending classical discrete abelian duality to the noncommutative setting. Our proofs rely on a careful analysis of the associated multiplicative unitaries and their leg-lengthened counterparts, which we verify satisfy the pentagonal relation. By exploiting the interplay between the scaling automorphism group and the antipodal operator, we derive explicit expressions for the modular elements and compute Tomita–Takesaki dynamics. Consequently, this framework not only closes the initial axiomatic gap but also provides a versatile foundation for harmonic analysis and index-theoretic investigations on quantum spaces exhibiting intrinsic discreteness.

title: Modified gravity and massive neutrinos: constraints from the full shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and forecasts for Stage IV surveys
text_ai:
We constrain the growth index $\gamma$ by performing a full-shape analysis of the power spectrum multipoles measured from the BOSS DR12 data. We adopt a theoretical model based on the Effective Field theory of the Large Scale Structure (EFTofLSS) and focus on two different cosmologies: $\gamma$CDM and $\gamma 
u$CDM, where we also vary the total neutrino mass. Using Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling, we explore the posterior distributions over $\gamma$, $\sum m_
u$, and standard $\Lambda$CDM parameters, marginalizing over nuisance terms associated with galaxy bias and nonlinear damping. Our analysis yields tight constraints consistent with general relativity, finding $\gamma = 0.54^{+0.06}_{-0.07}$ in the $\gamma$CDM framework, while the inclusion of massive neutrinos introduces a mild parameter shift, moving the best-fit value to $\gamma = 0.58^{+0.08}_{-0.09}$ at $1\sigma$. We demonstrate that the interplay between scale-dependent growth induced by modified gravity and the free-streaming suppression from neutrino masses creates a significant degeneracy in the monopole and quadrupole moments, which is partially broken by the higher-order multipoles and the precise modeling of baryon acoustic oscillations within the EFTofLSS formalism. When combined with external probes such as CMB lensing and cosmic shear, our bounds tighten to $\gamma = 0.53 \pm 0.05$, firmly excluding deviations beyond $2\sigma$ from the standard GR prediction. Forecasting capabilities for upcoming Stage IV experiments, including DESI, Euclid, and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, indicate that sub-percent precision on the redshift-space distortion amplitude will reduce uncertainties on $\gamma$ by a factor of three, while simultaneously breaking the $\gamma$-$\sum m_
u$ degeneracy to isolate neutrino mass signatures down to $\sigma(\sum m_
u) \approx 15\,\mathrm{meV}$. These findings establish full-shape RSD analyses as a robust framework for testing gravity on cosmic scales and resolving the neutrino mass hierarchy.

title: Artificial intelligence in government: Concepts, standards, and a unified framework
text_ai: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), especially in generative language modelling, hold the promise of transforming government. Given the advanced capabilities of new AI systems, it is critical that these are embedded using standard operational procedures, clear epistemic criteria, and behave in alignment with the normative expectations of society. This study addresses the fragmentation in current governance literature by developing a comprehensive framework that integrates conceptual clarity, technical standards, and administrative implementation pathways. Through a systematic review of scholarly discourse, regulatory guidelines, and institutional case studies, we identify three core dimensions necessary for responsible AI deployment in public sectors: algorithmic transparency, procedural accountability, and value-sensitive design. We propose a standardized taxonomy that distinguishes between diagnostic, predictive, and generative applications, mapping each to appropriate oversight mechanisms and performance benchmarks. The framework emphasizes iterative validation processes, requiring continuous stakeholder engagement and robust audit trails to ensure compliance with democratic principles and statutory mandates. Furthermore, we outline a tiered governance model that scales regulatory intensity according to system risk and functional criticality, thereby balancing innovation incentives with public trust safeguards. Implementation guidelines are provided for civil servants at municipal, national, and supranational levels, focusing on procurement protocols, workforce upskilling, and interagency coordination. By synthesizing disparate theoretical perspectives into a cohesive operational architecture, this research offers practitioners actionable tools for mitigating bias, preventing systemic failures, and enhancing service delivery efficacy. Ultimately, the proposed structure establishes a replicable foundation for evidence-based AI integration, positioning public administration to harness transformative technologies while preserving institutional legitimacy and civic equity across increasingly complex and rapidly evolving digital ecosystems.

title: Local Decorrelation For Improved Detection
text_ai: Even with the advent of more sophisticated, data-hungry methods, boosted decision trees remain extraordinarily successful for fast rigid object detection, achieving top accuracy on numerous datasets. While effective, most boosted detectors use decision trees with orthogonal (single feature) splits, and the topology of the resulting decision boundary may not be well matched to the natural topology of the data. To address this limitation, we introduce local decorrelation, a transformation that aligns feature distributions with the adaptive partitioning mechanism of boosted trees. By whitening feature covariance within localized spatial windows, our method mitigates redundancy and facilitates non-orthogonal split evaluation without increasing inference latency. We embed this procedure into standard cascade architectures and evaluate it across established face and pedestrian detection benchmarks. Results demonstrate consistent gains in true positive rates and false alarm suppression relative to conventional single-feature splitting, particularly under severe occlusion and viewpoint changes. These findings highlight the critical role of feature geometry in tree-based classification and offer a computationally efficient, architecture-agnostic refinement that readily integrates into existing detection frameworks.

title: Nothing to see here: Failed supernovae are faint or rare
text_ai: The absence of Type IIP core-collapse supernovae arising from progenitors above 17 solar masses suggests the existence of another evolutionary path by which massive stars end their lives. The direct collapse of a stellar core to a black hole without the production of a bright, explosive transient is expected to produce a long-lived, dim, red transient known as a failed supernova. We present a systematic search of archival and real-time photometric datasets, cross-matching source catalogs with pre-explosion imaging archives to track luminosity evolution across optical and near-infrared bands. Applying rigorous selection algorithms designed to filter out variable stars and active galactic nuclei, we identify a compact candidate sample whose light curves plateau at faint magnitudes before undergoing gradual fading over multi-year baselines. Broadband spectral energy distributions align closely with hydrodynamical simulations of dust-reprocessed accretion flows, though spectroscopic confirmation remains elusive due to severely degraded signal-to-noise ratios over extended temporal baselines. Population synthesis modeling demonstrates that the inferred spatial density requires either an intrinsic peak brightness significantly below legacy optical detection thresholds or a genuine suppression of successful shock breakout in high-metallicity environments. When weighted against survey depth and cadence limitations, both scenarios yield comparable likelihoods, reinforcing the premise that these transients evade detection primarily through photometric subtlety rather than absolute cosmic rarity. Consequently, the apparent deficit in observed events does not necessitate exotic physics beyond standard neutrino-driven collapse mechanisms. We thus conclude that dedicated near-infrared monitoring campaigns will prove essential to transform these theoretically predicted endpoints into robustly quantified components of the massive-star death budget.

The direct collapse of a stellar core to a black hole without the production of a bright, explosive transient is expected to produce a long-lived, dim, red transient known as a failed supernova.

title: Reproductive Coercion Among African American Female Adolescents: Associations with Contraception and Sexually Transmitted Diseases.
text_ai: Background: Among adolescents, racial disparities in reproductive health outcomes persist. The question of whether reproductive coercion (RC) influences these outcomes has received increased attention. Little is known about whether RC is independently associated with contraceptive use and having a sexually transmitted disease (STD) among African American female adolescents. This cross-sectional analysis utilized baseline data from 1,042 African American females aged 14–19 enrolled across urban community health clinics and secondary schools. Reproductive coercion was quantified using a validated instrument capturing physical force, sexual pressure, and pregnancy sabotage. Contraceptive adherence was dichotomized, and sexually transmitted disease status was confirmed via nucleic acid amplification testing or self-report. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic covariates, partnership characteristics, and behavioral confounders yielded adjusted odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Prevalence of RC exposure reached 33.8%. Elevated RC scores demonstrated statistically significant associations with inconsistent contraceptive utilization (aOR = 1.71; 95% CI: 1.34–2.18) and elevated STD prevalence (aOR = 1.59; 95% CI: 1.21–2.09). Stratified analyses indicated that pregnancy sabotage amplified risk for both outcomes. Associations persisted independent of relationship power differentials and mental health comorbidities. Longitudinal follow-up data corroborated these cross-sectional patterns, suggesting sustained physiological sequelae. These findings position reproductive coercion as a distinct pathway exacerbating existing racial inequities in adolescent sexual and reproductive health. Clinical protocols should mandate routine, trauma-informed RC screening to facilitate early identification. Furthermore, tailored behavioral interventions and policy reforms must address structural vulnerabilities that constrain adolescent agency. Healthcare systems must allocate dedicated resources for multidisciplinary support teams capable of addressing intersecting social determinants. Dismantling systemic barriers remains essential for achieving health equity.

title: An Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph first view on Solar Spicules
text_ai: Solar spicules have eluded modelers and observers for decades. Since the discovery of the more energetic type II, spicules have become a heated topic but their contribution to the energy balance of the low solar atmosphere remains unknown. Here we present high-cadence, high-spectral-resolution observations from the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS) that resolve the kinematic and thermodynamic evolution of individual spicules across the quiet Sun and active region boundaries. Utilizing non-LTE radiative transfer modeling combined with time-distance analysis of Mg II h&k and C IV emission, we derive precise estimates of mass transport, heating rates, and momentum deposition within these transient structures. Our results demonstrate that type II spicules exhibit rapid acceleration phases reaching peak velocities exceeding 100 km s⁻¹, followed by gradual deceleration consistent with gravitational settling and aerodynamic drag. Thermodynamic diagnostics reveal impulsive heating events occurring at heights between 3 and 6 Mm, with electron densities decreasing from ~10¹¹ cm⁻³ to ~10⁹ cm⁻³ over typical lifetimes of 150–300 seconds. Integrating these spatially resolved measurements yields a net upward energy flux of approximately 300–500 W m⁻² when averaged over the observed network regions, suggesting that spicules alone cannot sustain the global coronal energy budget but may significantly supplement localized heating mechanisms. Furthermore, we identify coherent wave signatures propagating along magnetic flux tubes, indicating substantial Poynting flux contributions mediated by torsional Alfvénic motions. These findings establish an observational framework that directly constrains magnetohydrodynamic simulations, emphasizing the critical role of chromospheric fine-structuring in mediating energy transfer from the photosphere to the corona. Future multi-instrument campaigns remain essential.

title: The H - Omega_o Diagram From Recent CMB Observations: Yes, We Can Already Say Something
text_ai: The CMB is already one of the pillars of the Big Bang model. However it may also become our most powerful tool to distinguish contending models and to determine their cosmological parameters. To realize this goal, more than 20 observational groups and two new satellites are gearing up to make precise measurements of the CMB at small angular scales. These high-resolution observations target the acoustic oscillations in the photon-baryon fluid, whose multipole spectrum directly encodes the spatial curvature and total matter-energy budget. By jointly fitting the positions and relative amplitudes of the primary acoustic peaks with the Silk damping tail, we demonstrate that ground-based datasets already break the canonical geometric degeneracy between H₀ and Ω₀. Incorporating independent baryon density constraints from primordial nucleosynthesis, the small-angle power spectra delineate sharply defined confidence contours in the H₀–Ω₀ parameter plane. Constructing the confidence region from these joint likelihoods reveals an elliptical alignment that tightly intersects the flatness condition. Our Bayesian inference framework consistently favors a spatially flat configuration with Ω₀ ≃ 1.0 ± 0.05, while decisively ruling out open geometries at greater than ninety-five per cent credibility. Crucially, the observed phase coherence and peak hierarchy serve as insensitive yet powerful discriminants against modified gravity and varying vacuum energy proposals. This geometric constraint emerges from the angular diameter distance to the last scattering surface, which scales inversely with both parameters in degenerate combinations that small-scale anisotropies uniquely resolve. Consequently, we establish that sub-degree CMB measurements possess adequate discriminatory power to independently constrain fundamental cosmological variables, thereby transforming theoretical speculation into a tightly bounded empirical discipline and establishing a robust baseline for upcoming satellite campaigns.

title: Reverberation and photoionization estimates of the Broad Line Region Radius in Low-z Quasars
text_ai: Black Hole Mass (M_BH) estimation in quasars, especially at high redshift, involves use of single epoch spectra with s/n and resolution that permit accurate measurement of the width of a broad line assumed to be a reliable virial estimator. Coupled with an estimate of the radius of the broad line region this yields M_BH. However, the empirical calibration of these radii remains fundamentally limited by the scarcity of direct time-delay observations, necessitating reliance on unverified luminosity–radius scaling relations that propagate substantial systematic uncertainties into derived virial masses. To mitigate this challenge, we conduct a systematic comparison between established reverberation mapping delays and comprehensive photoionization modeling for a uniformly selected sample of thirty-nine low-redshift active galactic nuclei featuring extensive multi-epoch spectroscopic monitoring campaigns. Reverberation lags are precisely measured through cross-correlation function peak displacements in Hβ and C IV broad emission components, while theoretical broad line region dimensions are independently derived using sophisticated cloudy radiative transfer simulations constrained by contemporaneous ultraviolet-to-optical continuum spectral energy distributions and empirically calibrated strong-line abundance indicators. Our quantitative assessment demonstrates that conventional single-zone photoionization approximations consistently yield radius estimates that fall short of reverberation benchmarks by a median scaling factor of 1.9 ± 0.5, a deficit that scales monotonically with increasing ionization parameter and decreasing metallicity. Importantly, introducing radiation-pressure-supported disk winds and vertically structured density gradients into the photoionization architecture successfully reconciles approximately 87% of the delayed sample within a factor of 1.5. Building upon these refined physical inputs, we construct a revised, multi-parameter R_L calibration that eliminates the historical offset and produces a virial mass zero-point adjustment of Δlog(M_BH) = 0.07 ± 0.11 dex relative to independent stellar velocity dispersion references. Furthermore, we evaluate the impact of these corrections on high-redshift quasar demographics, demonstrating that applying our photoionization-augmented scaling relation reduces the apparent evolution of the black hole mass function by roughly 0.15 dex over the redshift range 2.0 < z < 6.5. These adjustments preserve the intrinsic slope of the fundamental plane while minimizing residual scatter introduced by projection effects and inclination-dependent kinematics. Ultimately, this investigation establishes a robust methodological framework bridging direct temporal probes with theoretical emission diagnostics, thereby elevating the fidelity of single-epoch black hole mass estimates across the cosmological volume and illuminating the complex radiative-hydrodynamic coupling governing broad line region formation.

title: A Dynamic Data Structure for Representing Timed Transitive Closures on Disk
text_ai: Temporal graphs represent interactions between entities over time. These interactions may be direct, a contact between two vertices at some time instant, or indirect, through sequences of contacts called journeys. Deciding whether an entity can reach another through a journey is useful for various applications in complex networks. However, computing and storing these transitive closures becomes prohibitively expensive as graph size and temporal resolution increase. Traditional in-memory representations quickly exhaust available RAM, while conventional disk-based indexing schemes suffer from excessive I/O overhead during dynamic updates. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a novel dynamic data structure optimized for persistent storage that efficiently maintains timed transitive closures under arbitrary edge insertions and deletions. Our approach leverages a hierarchical block layout combined with timestamp-aware run-length encoding, enabling logarithmic-time query resolution while minimizing random disk seeks. The architecture incorporates adaptive flushing policies that dynamically balance write amplification against sustained query throughput. We formally analyze the space complexity, demonstrating asymptotic optimality relative to the cardinality of distinct temporal intervals, and derive tight bounds on worst-case update latency. Extensive empirical evaluations across diverse mobility and communication benchmarks reveal that our implementation achieves up to two orders of magnitude faster construction times compared to naive materialization baselines, with auxiliary memory usage strictly confined to secondary storage buffers. Moreover, both point and interval reachability queries exhibit sub-linear scaling, maintaining interactive response times even when processing multi-year temporal spans. By reconciling theoretical transitive closure maintenance with practical disk-resident constraints, this framework establishes a foundation for scalable temporal reachability analysis, directly supporting resource-intensive downstream tasks including epidemic spreading simulation, dynamic routing, and temporal dependency discovery.

title: Prevalence of mecA on oral mucosa in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
text_ai: Objectives: Severe oral mucositis occurring after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) is associated with a risk of systemic infection related to bacteremia. We reported antibiotic-resistant bacteria detected on the oral mucosa frequently during the period of HCT and indicated an association between oral mucositis and antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection (2011 MASCC/ISOO Annual Meeting). Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study evaluated 148 adult HCT recipients who developed grade ≥3 oral mucositis following myeloablative conditioning. Sterile oral swabs were collected at baseline, day +7, +14, and +21 post-transplantation. The prevalence of mecA-carrying organisms was determined using quantitative PCR targeting the gene alongside culture-based isolation. Mucositis severity was graded according to WHO criteria. Multivariate logistic regression assessed associations between mecA colonization, clinical variables, and subsequent bloodstream infections. Results: mecA-positive isolates were identified in 62.8% (n=93) of participants, predominantly within the first two weeks post-engraftment. Colonization density significantly increased with advancing mucositis grades (p<0.001). Patients harboring mecA on the oral mucosa demonstrated a 3.4-fold higher incidence of subsequent catheter-related bloodstream infections compared to mecA-negative individuals (95% CI: 1.8–6.2; p=0.002). Prophylactic antimicrobial regimens did not significantly alter mecA prevalence but modified the taxonomic profile of colonizing staphylococci. Conclusion: The high prevalence of mecA on the oral mucosa during acute mucositis underscores its critical role as a potential reservoir for secondary bacteremia in immunocompromised HCT recipients. Systematic molecular surveillance of oral carriage could potentially facilitate early targeted interventions and optimize antimicrobial stewardship strategies in this vulnerable population.

title: Does the Presence of Risk Factors for Fetal Growth Restriction Increase the Probability of Antenatal Detection? A French National Study.
text_ai: Screening for fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major component of prenatal care. We investigated whether the presence of maternal and pregnancy risk factors for FGR improves the antenatal suspicion of FGR for infants born small-for-gestational age (SGA) as well as their impact on screening specificity. Data were extracted from the French National Perinatal Database for singleton pregnancies delivered between 2016 and 2021. Predefined risk factors encompassed advanced maternal age, obesity, chronic hypertension, pregestational diabetes, autoimmune disease, and prior adverse obstetric history. Antenatal suspicion was operationalized via clinical documentation. Multivariable logistic regression generated adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals for antenatal FGR detection among small-for-gestational-age infants (<10th percentile). Covariates were selected a priori based on biological plausibility. Missing data were handled via multiple imputation. Performance metrics were stratified by cumulative risk burden. Among 1,842,317 deliveries, 112,450 infants (6.1%) qualified as SGA. Suspicion was documented in only 38.2% of cases. Patients with ≥2 risk factors showed significantly elevated detection odds versus unexposed controls (aOR 3.41; 95% CI 3.28–3.55; p<0.001). Sensitivity rose from 21.4% to 58.7% in high-risk groups, yet specificity dropped from 97.1% to 89.3%. Positive predictive value remained below 12%. Subgroup analyses confirmed consistent effect modification by parity. Calibration plots demonstrated adequate model fit. In conclusion, although maternal and gestational risk profiles moderately increase antenatal FGR suspicion among SGA neonates, inadequate specificity and negligible positive predictive value limit standalone algorithm utility. Systematic biometric surveillance and umbilical artery Doppler assessments remain necessary to maximize detection yield without eroding screening accuracy.

title: HEX: Hierarchical Emergence Exploitation in Self-Supervised Algorithms
text_ai: In this paper, we propose an algorithm that can be used on top of a wide variety of self-supervised (SSL) approaches to take advantage of hierarchical structures that emerge during training. SSL approaches typically work through some invariance term to ensure consistency between similar samples and a regularization term to prevent global dimensional collapse. However, conventional regularization schemes often impose uniform constraints across all representational levels, inadvertently suppressing the natural stratification of features that develops over training epochs. To address this limitation, HEX dynamically monitors layer-wise activation statistics and adaptively calibrates multi-scale contrastive objectives. Rather than treating the embedding space as a monolithic manifold, our method decomposes representations into scale-specific subspaces, preserving fine-grained structural details while simultaneously reinforcing semantic coherence at coarser abstraction tiers. This is accomplished through a lightweight, gradient-driven routing mechanism that modulates invariance strengths according to emergent feature diversity, effectively preventing premature convergence while retaining hierarchical fidelity. We integrate HEX seamlessly into established frameworks such as SimCLR, MoCo, and BYOL, requiring no architectural modifications or additional labeled data. Extensive experiments on ImageNet pretraining and downstream transfer tasks demonstrate consistent performance gains, yielding average improvements of 1.8% in linear probing accuracy and notable enhancements in few-shot classification and object detection. Comprehensive ablation studies confirm that explicit hierarchical exploitation systematically mitigates representational redundancy without increasing computational overhead. Our results highlight the critical role of structured emergence in unsupervised representation learning, offering a generalizable, plug-and-play paradigm that elevates both feature quality and transfer robustness across diverse computer vision benchmarks. Furthermore, runtime analysis confirms that the proposed routing overhead remains negligible (<2%), ensuring practical deployability in resource-constrained settings.

title: Non-union of the ulnar styloid process in children is common but long-term morbidity is rare: a population-based study with mean 11 years (9-15) follow-up.
text_ai: Background and purpose - Fracture of the ulnar styloid process (USP) is common in children in connection with distal radius fracture. The long-term morbidity of USP non-union following a childhood distal radius fracture is unclear. We evaluated long-term clinical and radiographic findings of USP non-union. This population-based cohort study enrolled pediatric patients (<16 years) treated for acute distal radius fractures between 2005 and 2010. Preoperative injury characteristics and initial reduction quality were comparable between cohorts. Participants were stratified radiographically into union or non-union cohorts. Follow-up assessments incorporated DASH scores, visual analog scale pain ratings, normalized grip strength, and active wrist range of motion. Radiographic parameters included radial inclination, volar tilt, and ulnar variance. Statistical testing used Mann-Whitney U and Fisher exact tests. All clinical examinations were performed by independent investigators unaware of radiographic classification status. Among 412 patients, 23 (5.6%) exhibited USP non-union versus 389 (94.4%) with union. No significant intergroup differences emerged for DASH scores (p=0.71), pain (p=0.65), or grip strength (p=0.82). Mobility remained intact. Patient satisfaction metrics mirrored objective clinical measurements, further corroborating the benign natural history of this radiographic finding. Mild positive ulnar variance was marginally more frequent in non-unions (17% vs. 9%, p=0.34) but showed no association with ulnocarpal impingement. Directly USP-related mechanical complications occurred in a single patient (0.2%). These findings align with contemporary evidence supporting non-operative protocols for pediatric USP injuries. USP non-union frequently develops after pediatric distal radius fractures but confers minimal long-term morbidity. Sustained functional capacity, absent chronic pain, and stable alignment demonstrate that prophylactic fixation is unnecessary. Conservative management is recommended, reserving operative procedures exclusively for refractory mechanical symptoms.

title: ImmuNeCS: Neural Committee Search by an Artificial Immune System
text_ai: Current Neural Architecture Search techniques can suffer from a few shortcomings, including high computational cost, excessive bias from the search space, conceptual complexity or uncertain empirical benefits over random search. To address these limitations, we introduce ImmuNeCS, a novel search framework that leverages artificial immune system principles to optimize neural network committees rather than isolated architectures. By modeling candidate topologies as antigens and employing affinity-driven maturation alongside clonal expansion, our method explicitly regulates the exploration-exploitation tradeoff while preserving structural diversity throughout optimization. This biological paradigm inherently suppresses premature convergence and eliminates reliance on rigid, manually defined search spaces. We rigorously benchmark ImmuNeCS against leading differentiable and reinforcement learning baselines across CIFAR-10, ImageNet subsets, and AutoML benchmarks. Our framework yields discovery trajectories that require substantially fewer weight-sharing evaluations to converge, directly alleviating the prohibitive training overhead characteristic of gradient-based approaches. Specifically, the antibody repertoire initialization strategy accelerates early-stage sampling efficiency by prioritizing structurally distinct subnetworks. Empirical evaluations reveal that immunologically curated committees achieve up to 1.8% higher predictive accuracy and improved calibration stability compared to monolithic counterparts and randomly assembled ensembles, all while maintaining comparable parameter counts. Detailed ablation analyses isolate the contributions of somatic hypermutation and memory cell preservation, confirming their necessity for sustaining heterogeneous feature extractors under constrained compute budgets. Furthermore, cross-dataset transfer tests demonstrate that immune-selected committees generalize more robustly to distribution shifts than conventionally trained peers. These findings underscore the viability of bio-inspired optimization for large-scale architecture discovery. Consequently, ImmuNeCS provides a computationally efficient alternative for automated ensemble construction, establishing a reproducible pathway toward deployable, diverse neural systems in production-grade machine learning pipelines.

title: Domain-knowledge Inspired Pseudo Supervision (DIPS) for Unsupervised Image-to-Image Translation Models to Support Cross-Domain Classification
text_ai: The ability to classify images is dependent on having access to large labeled datasets and testing on data from the same domain that the model can train on. Classification becomes more challenging when dealing with new data from a different domain, where gathering and especially labeling a larger image dataset for retraining a classification model requires a labor-intensive human effort. To address this limitation, we propose Domain-knowledge Inspired Pseudo Supervision (DIPS), a novel framework that leverages unsupervised image-to-image translation to synthesize high-fidelity pseudo-labeled target samples without manual annotation. DIPS explicitly embeds domain-specific structural priors into the translation architecture, directing the generator to preserve discriminative semantic content while adapting low-level stylistic attributes across domains. By coupling this translation mechanism with a confidence-calibrated pseudo-labeling protocol, the system iteratively optimizes classifier decision boundaries directly within the shifted target distribution. We extensively evaluate DIPS across diverse cross-domain classification benchmarks spanning medical diagnostics and remote sensing, where pronounced covariate shift severely degrades standard transfer learning approaches. Empirical results indicate that DIPS consistently surpasses established self-training and adversarial alignment baselines, yielding average accuracy gains of 12.3% while completely eliminating the need for annotated target instances during adaptation. Comprehensive ablation analyses verify that domain-constrained translation significantly mitigates feature distortion and improves cross-domain feature alignment. Qualitative assessments further demonstrate that synthesized translations retain critical pathological and geographical markers, confirming the reliability of the induced supervision signals. Collectively, these outcomes position DIPS as a computationally efficient, annotation-free paradigm for robust cross-domain deployment, substantially lowering reliance on costly human curation while preserving predictive fidelity under severe distributional mismatches.

title: An Effective Crop-Paste Pipeline for Few-shot Object Detection
text_ai: Few-shot object detection (FSOD) aims to expand an object detector for novel categories given only a few instances for training. However, detecting novel categories with only a few samples usually leads to the problem of misclassification. In FSOD, we notice the false positive (FP) of novel categories is prominent, in which the base categories are often recognized as novel ones. To address this bias, we propose an effective crop-paste pipeline that explicitly decouples base and novel category representations during meta-training. Our approach operates by selectively cropping region proposals associated with base classes and pasting them into synthetic negative examples, thereby constructing a curriculum of hard negatives tailored to the novel category space. By integrating these augmented samples into the proposal refinement stage, the model learns discriminative decision boundaries that suppress spurious activations on familiar objects. Furthermore, we introduce a confidence-calibrated matching strategy that dynamically adjusts IoU thresholds during positive and negative assignment, reducing over-optimistic novel class predictions without compromising recall. Extensive experiments on PASCAL VOC and COCO benchmarks demonstrate that our pipeline consistently improves average precision across all shot settings. Notably, it yields relative gains of 4.2% and 3.8% mAP at 1-shot and 5-shot regimes, respectively, while maintaining inference efficiency comparable to standard two-stage detectors. Ablation studies confirm that the crop-paste mechanism effectively mitigates base-to-novel confusion by reinforcing background suppression and feature disentanglement. The framework requires minimal architectural modifications and can be seamlessly integrated into existing meta-learning baselines. These findings establish crop-paste augmentation as a robust, plug-and-play module for FSOD systems, offering a practical pathway toward scalable open-world recognition without requiring extensive retraining or auxiliary data mining.

title: Status of the Medium-Sized Telescopes for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
text_ai: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is a next-generation ground-based gamma-ray observatory that will study the universe at very high energy using atmospheric Cherenkov light. CTAO will comprise over 67 telescopes of three different sizes, located in the northern and southern hemispheres. Among these classes, the medium-sized telescopes (MSTs) are optimized for the core energy range of 0.1–10 TeV, bridging the sensitivity gap between the large- and small-sized instruments. The MST design employs a Davies–Cotton optical configuration with a 17 m mirror diameter, coupled to a camera featuring silicon photomultipliers arranged in a hexagonal pixel layout. Recent progress in the manufacturing and assembly of the primary mirror segments has enabled the completion of engineering models and prototype units, which have undergone environmental and mechanical qualification campaigns. In parallel, the readout electronics, real-time calibration systems, and low-latency data acquisition chains have been integrated and validated during field trials. Performance simulations, constrained by empirical measurements of mirror reflectivity, camera quantum efficiency, and pointing accuracy, indicate that the MST array will deliver the required angular resolution, background rejection capabilities, and energy reconstruction precision necessary to fulfill CTAO’s scientific objectives. Commissioning activities at the designated observing sites are now underway, with systematic monitoring of alignment stability, trigger efficiency, and atmospheric monitoring instrumentation enabling continuous optimization. As construction transitions from component validation to full-scale deployment, the MST program remains on schedule for initial science operations as planned. The ongoing refinement of hardware subsystems and operational protocols ensures that the medium-sized telescopes will form the observational backbone of CTAO, enabling comprehensive all-sky surveys of hadronic accelerators.

title: QCD against BlackHoles of Stellar Mass
text_ai: In course of the consolidation of nucleon (neutron) spacing inside a compact star, two key factors are expected to come into play side by side: the lack of self-stabilization against shutting into black hole (BH) and forthcoming phase transition - color deconfinement and QCD-vacuum reconstruction - within the nuclear matter the star is composed of. We investigate this dichotomy through a coupled gravitational-QCD framework that incorporates density-dependent quark-gluon interactions and non-perturbative vacuum energy contributions. By solving the relativistic hydrodynamic equations alongside a thermodynamically consistent equation of state, we demonstrate that the onset of color deconfinement induces a transient stiffening of the stellar medium, effectively postponing catastrophic collapse beyond standard limits. However, once the chiral symmetry restoration threshold is crossed, the rapid drop in pressure support triggers a runaway contraction, culminating in direct black hole formation without a supernova explosion. Our analysis reveals a critical baryon density regime where QCD vacuum reconstruction competes directly with general relativistic instability, yielding a bimodal mass distribution for compact remnants that aligns with recent LIGO–Virgo observations of the lower mass gap. Furthermore, the released latent heat and altered neutrino opacity during the transition leave distinct imprints on the post-merger gravitational waveform, offering a testable signature for next-generation detectors. These findings challenge the conventional paradigm of purely hydrodynamic collapse, establishing strong-interaction microphysics as a decisive regulator of stellar-mass black hole progenitors. Across diverse initial metallicities, the interplay between QCD thermodynamics and spacetime curvature redefines the boundary between neutron stars and black holes, providing a unified mechanism for the observed paucity of compact objects in the 2–5 solar mass range.

title: Block-MDS QC-LDPC Codes for Information Reconciliation in Key Distribution
text_ai: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a popular protocol that provides information theoretically secure keys to multiple parties. Two important post-processing steps of QKD are 1) the information reconciliation (IR) step, where parties reconcile mismatches in generated keys through classical communication, and 2) the privacy amplification (PA) step, where parties distill their common key into a new secure key that the adversary has little to no information about. However, optimizing reconciliation efficiency remains challenging due to the stringent trade-off between communication overhead and decoding convergence. We introduce a block-MDS structured quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check (QC-LDPC) code family for asymmetric bipartite reconciliation. Leveraging the algebraic regularity of MDS generator matrices, our construction yields sparse parity-check graphs enabling fast belief-propagation decoding while minimizing redundant transmissions. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed codes operate within 0.2 dB of capacity limits at practical block lengths, substantially reducing public discussion rounds. These results establish block-MDS QC-LDPC schemes as a scalable, high-throughput solution for practical QKD networks.

title: Spot evolution on LQ Hya during 2006--2017: temperature maps based on SOFIN and FIES data
text_ai: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. To address this transition, we present a comprehensive reconstruction of photospheric spot distribution and temperature contrast on LQ Hya over a twelve-year baseline (2006--2017), utilizing high-resolution spectropolarimetric and spectroscopic observations obtained with SOFIN and FIES. By applying Zeeman-Doppler imaging techniques to line-profile variations sampled across multiple rotational phases, we derive temporal maps of surface brightness and magnetic topology. Our analysis reveals persistent active region emergence at mid-to-high latitudes, accompanied by a systematic equatorward drift that mirrors solar-like differential rotation but with enhanced shear. Spot filling factors range from 8% to 15%, with temperature contrasts varying between 800 and 1200 K. Despite the photometric chaos documented after 2009, the reconstructed maps confirm that large, long-lived cool spots remain dominant, clustering near 50° latitude. The shift toward apparent photometric randomness correlates with fragmentation of previously coherent spot groups and elevated flux emergence rates rather than a fundamental dynamo regime change. Furthermore, we identify quasi-periodic modulation in both spot coverage and mean longitudinal field strength, indicating an underlying activity cycle with a period of approximately 11±2 yr. These results demonstrate that the loss of coherence in broadband light curves stems from complex superposition effects and rapid longitudinal redistribution of magnetically suppressed convection zones, rather than stochastic interior reconfiguration. This study delivers essential observational benchmarks for validating convective dynamo theories applied to rapidly rotating young solar analogues.

Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time.

title: Retrieval-augmented Image Captioning
text_ai: Inspired by retrieval-augmented language generation and pretrained Vision and Language (V&L) encoders, we present a new approach to image captioning that generates sentences given the input image and a set of captions retrieved from a datastore, as opposed to the image alone. Our framework integrates cross-modal attention to align visual features with semantically similar textual references, enabling external knowledge integration without exhaustive fine-tuning. During inference, a lightweight retriever scores candidate captions from a large-scale corpus, dynamically conditioning the generator on the top-k most relevant entries. Extensive evaluations on MSCOCO and Flickr30k demonstrate that our method significantly reduces hallucination rates while improving factual consistency and lexical diversity against state-of-the-art baselines. Ablation studies confirm the critical role of retrieval precision and alignment strategies in enhancing generative fidelity. Runtime analysis further verifies negligible computational overhead, confirming that this parameter-efficient paradigm advances reliable vision-language deployment across diverse evaluation metrics. Moreover, qualitative case studies illustrate improved contextual grounding and reduced repetitive phrasing when leveraging retrieved context.

title: Harnessing TH9 cells in cancer immunotherapy.
text_ai: CD4 T cell effector subsets not only profoundly affect cancer progression, but recent evidence also underscores their critical contribution to the anticancer efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. In 2012, the two seminal studies suggested the superior antimelanoma activity of T H 9 cells over other T cell subsets upon adoptive T cell transfer. Despite this early promise, exploitation of TH9 lineage cells remains constrained by incomplete understanding of their differentiation pathways, functional plasticity within the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and comprehensive engineering strategies. Here, we evaluate mechanistic insights into TH9-mediated antitumor immunity, emphasizing interleukin-9-driven recruitment of eosinophils and mast cells, and synergistic crosstalk with CD8+ cytotoxic lymphocytes. We further examine how combination regimens integrating TH9-polarizing agents or engineered cellular platforms may overcome resistance to checkpoint blockade. By addressing current translational hurdles—particularly cytokine delivery kinetics, lineage stability, and rigorous toxicity profiling—we outline a rational framework for novel therapies leveraging TH9 immunomodulation to enhance clinically meaningful responses across solid malignancies.

title: Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network for Spacecraft Image Denoising
text_ai: Spacecraft image denoising is a crucial fundamental technology closely related to aerospace research. However, the existing deep learning-based image denoising methods are primarily designed for natural image and fail to adequately consider the characteristics of spacecraft image(e.g. low-light conditions, repetitive periodic structures), resulting in suboptimal performance in the spacecraft image denoising task. To address these limitations, we propose the Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network (SMAFFNet), tailored for spacecraft imaging environments. We integrate a frequency-aware module that efficiently captures global periodic patterns while suppressing sensor-specific noise. Crucially, an activation-free linear transformation eliminates costly non-linearities, significantly reducing computational overhead without compromising representational capacity. Structural priors are embedded via a multi-scale relational encoder preserving geometric continuity across repetitive components like solar arrays. Extensive experiments on real spacecraft datasets demonstrate that SMAFFNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in quantitative metrics and visual fidelity, achieving robust noise suppression while retaining critical mission data. This work establishes a new paradigm for efficient spaceborne image processing.

title: Effective Hamiltonian of topologically stabilized polymer states
text_ai: Topologically stabilized polymer conformations observed in melts of nonconcatenated polymer rings and crumpled globules, are considered to be a good candidate for the description of the spatial structure of mitotic chromosomes. Despite significant efforts, the microscopic Hamiltonian capable of describing such systems, remains yet inaccessible. Here, we construct a coarse-grained effective Hamiltonian that explicitly incorporates topological constraints through a nonlocal knotting potential. By mapping the phase space of ring polymers onto a manifold of self-avoiding loops, we derive a scale-invariant energy functional capturing the entropic penalties of chain interpenetration and local folding. Our formulation reveals a dominant logarithmic interaction term governing equilibrium size scaling, consistent with chromatin compaction data. Numerical evaluation against Monte Carlo simulations demonstrates quantitative agreement with predicted density profiles and contact probability decay across varying monomer densities. This framework provides a tractable analytical foundation for topology-driven chromatin organization, bridging statistical mechanics with genomic architecture and enabling predictive modeling of mitotic condensation pathways.

title: Robust Contact State Estimation in Humanoid Walking Gaits
text_ai: In this article, we propose a deep learning framework that provides a unified approach to the problem of leg contact detection in humanoid robot walking gaits. Our formulation accomplishes to accurately and robustly estimate the contact state probability for each leg (i.e., stable or slip/no contact). By integrating inertial measurement unit data with joint torque and position feedback, the network learns temporally consistent contact signatures through a recurrent temporal attention mechanism. This architecture effectively mitigates sensor noise and discriminates between transitional gait phases without requiring explicit force-torque measurements. We evaluate the proposed method on both synthetic simulations and physical experiments conducted on a full-scale bipedal humanoid platform across varied terrains and external perturbation scenarios. Comparative analyses demonstrate superior generalization against conventional threshold-based and kinematic estimators, achieving over 98% classification accuracy while maintaining sub-millisecond inference latency. These results establish a reliable, computationally efficient foundation for advanced locomotion controllers and adaptive balance strategies in complex operational environments for deployment.

title: A New Hole Density as a Stability Measure for Boron Fullerenes
text_ai: We investigate the stability of boron fullerene sets B76, B78 and B82. We evaluate the ground state energies, nucleus-independent chemical shift (NICS), the binding energies per atom and the band gap values by means of first-principles methods. Building upon these conventional descriptors, we propose a novel hole density parameter derived from electrostatic potential topology to quantify aromatic stabilization and structural robustness. This metric exhibits a strong linear correlation with both binding energies and NICS indices across the studied clusters, spanning multiple symmetry groups. Specifically, B78 demonstrates superior thermodynamic and magnetic stability, consistent with optimal electron delocalization. Conversely, B76 and B82 exhibit pronounced topological defects that locally suppress charge redistribution, thereby reducing cohesive strength. The proposed framework successfully predicts relative energetic ordering without relying solely on total energy differentials, offering a computationally efficient alternative for screening boron nanostructures. Collectively, these results validate hole density distribution as a reliable predictive indicator for fullerene stability and targeted cluster engineering.

title: Studying the multi-wavelength signals from short GRBs
text_ai: Since the first host galaxies and afterglows of short GRBs were identified, they have remained very difficult to study: their multiwavelenth afterglows are notoriously faint and host galaxy identification often relies upon minimalising a chance alignment probability. To overcome these observational challenges, we present a systematic analysis of optical/NIR follow-up data from twelve Swift and Fermi-detected events. Combining high-resolution adaptive optics imaging with targeted spectroscopy, we recover previously undetected host populations and derive robust stellar mass, metallicity, and specific star formation rate estimates. Our sample reveals a bimodal host environment distribution, correlating directly with progenitor merger timescales and jet breakout dynamics. Cross-correlation with gravitational-wave candidates indicates that current electromagnetic selection biases significantly underrepresent low-luminosity counterparts. These results demonstrate that next-generation facilities, including JWST and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, will substantially refine progenitor models and merger rate calculations. Ultimately, integrating electromagnetic observations with multi-messenger constraints is indispensable for characterizing compact binary coalescences throughout cosmic history.

title: The everyday dynamics of rumination and worry: precipitant events and affective consequences.
text_ai: Rumination and worry are two perseverative, negatively valenced thought processes that characterise depressive and anxiety disorders. Despite significant research interest, little is known about the everyday precipitants and consequences of rumination and worry. Using an experience sampling methodology, we examined and compared rumination and worry with respect to their relations to daily events and affective experience. Participants (N = 120) completed five daily prompts over fourteen days, reporting on recent events, current thought content, and emotional states. Generalised estimating equation models revealed distinct precipitation patterns: worry was predominantly triggered by future-oriented stressors and interpersonal conflicts, whereas rumination followed past-directed failures and negative social evaluations. Regarding affective consequences, both constructs exacerbated negative mood, yet worry uniquely predicted anticipatory distress, while rumination was more strongly associated with prolonged sadness and cognitive fatigue. These findings highlight divergent ecological profiles for each construct, suggesting that targeted interventions should address unique situational triggers and emotional aftermaths to mitigate transdiagnostic risk.

title: Principles of Open Fracture Management
text_ai: Open fractures are contaminated wounds that contain gram-positive and gram-negative organisms; therefore, wide-spectrum antibiotic therapy should be incorporated into the treatment plan. Antibiotics should be initiated as soon after injury as possible, preferably within 3 hours of injury, after which time the rate of infection has been reported to increase. Following antimicrobial administration, timely surgical intervention remains paramount. Radical yet conservative debridement of devitalized tissue and copious irrigation with volumetric saline solutions are essential to reduce bacterial bioburden and mitigate subsequent infection. The extent of debridement should be guided by initial injury severity rather than rigid protocols, frequently necessitating staged procedures when contamination or soft-tissue compromise is severe. Concurrent skeletal stabilization provides a stable biomechanical framework that facilitates soft-tissue healing and simplifies postoperative nursing care; however, the selection between temporary external fixation and definitive internal osteosynthesis hinges upon fracture morphology, soft-tissue envelope integrity, and systemic physiological reserve. Although external fixators afford rapid provisional alignment with limited additional iatrogenic insult, intramedullary nailing and anatomical plating may confer superior functional recovery once the wound bed demonstrates adequate viability. Adjunctive modalities, particularly vacuum-assisted closure and prophylactic fasciotomy in high-risk compartments, further optimize local microcirculation and prevent secondary ischemic damage. Multidisciplinary collaboration among orthopedic trauma, reconstructive microsurgery, and infectious disease specialists is indispensable for synchronizing debridement, stabilization, and delayed primary closure or free-flap reconstruction. Standardized adherence to validated severity classifications, such as the Gustilo-Anderson system, alongside protocol-driven follow-up imaging and laboratory monitoring, significantly reduces rates of deep sepsis, nonunion, and amputation. Furthermore, antibiotic regimens must be dynamically adjusted based on intraoperative cultures and pharmacokinetic parameters to prevent resistance development while ensuring adequate bone penetration. Continuous quality improvement initiatives and prospective registry data collection remain vital for refining these standards and addressing disparities in resource-limited settings. Ultimately, integrating these phased therapeutic principles into cohesive clinical pathways enhances limb salvage success, accelerates functional rehabilitation, and mitigates the substantial socioeconomic burden associated with complex polytrauma.

title: Window-based Model Averaging Improves Generalization in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) aims to learn a global model from distributed users while protecting their privacy. However, when data are distributed heterogeneously the learning process becomes noisy, unstable, and biased towards the last seen clients' data, slowing down convergence. To address these issues and improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the global model, we propose WIMA (Window-based Model Averaging). WIMA mitigates client drift by maintaining a sliding buffer of model updates, dynamically weighting them by proximity and local validation performance prior to aggregation. This mechanism filters transient gradients while preserving stable optimization trajectories. We evaluate WIMA across non-IID benchmarks, including CIFAR-10 and FEMNIST, under varying communication budgets and client dropout rates. Results demonstrate that WIMA accelerates convergence by up to 35% compared to FedAvg, while consistently boosting test accuracy by 2–4 percentage points. Gradient variance analysis confirms improved update stability. These findings establish window-based aggregation as a scalable strategy for efficient federated training under realistic data distributions.

title: Chronotaraxis as a harbinger of medial thalamic infarction.
text_ai: Chronotaraxis is an impairment of the perception of the sequencing of time. This alteration of temporality has been described as being characteristically associated with thalamic involvement, specifically in the dorsomedial nucleus. We report the clinical cases of two patients with acute ischaemic strokes located in said territory, with a clinical presentation based on this symptom and the recognition of which was essential in the therapeutic approach. Clinical evaluation incorporated standardized neuropsychological screening tools specifically calibrated to assess episodic memory retrieval and sequential processing integrity. Vascular mapping via computed tomography angiography and magnetic resonance diffusion-weighted sequences delineated paramedian artery occlusion patterns, correlating lesion burden with the severity of temporal disorientation. Management pathways adhered strictly to contemporary stroke center algorithms, with chronotaraxis explicitly documented in primary triage notes to justify accelerated neurointerventional consultation. Neither patient exhibited concurrent brainstem compression or midbrain extension, isolating the dorsomedial nuclei as the critical substratum for the observed phenomenology. Detailed neuropsychometric profiling quantified deficits in temporal ordering and working memory span, while perfusion-weighted imaging identified viable cortical-subcortical interfaces amenable to pharmacological recanalization. Treatment decisions prioritized intra-arterial mechanical thrombectomy in one case and systemic fibrinolysis in the other, guided by strict time-window parameters and collateral circulation status. Longitudinal follow-up confirmed sustained functional independence, demonstrating that timely reperfusion preserves diencephalic network integrity. Post-interventional monitoring tracked symptom evolution across serial examinations, revealing progressive normalization of temporal judgment concomitant with radiographic penumbra salvage. The reproducibility of these findings across distinct anatomical variants reinforces the reliability of chronotaraxis as a localized clinical biomarker. Systematic incorporation of chronoperception evaluation into emergency neurological triage would mitigate misdiagnosis rates associated with non-motor stroke phenotypes, particularly among older adults experiencing isolated cognitive fluctuations. By elevating chronotaraxis from a rare observational finding to a recognized sentinel sign, stroke practitioners can expedite evidence-based interventions and preserve higher-order cognitive architecture, ultimately refining prognostic stratification for medial diencephalic ischemia.

title: 4G 5G Cell-level Multi-indicator Forecasting based on Dense-MLP
text_ai: With the development of 4G/5G, the rapid growth of traffic has caused a large number of cell indicators to exceed the warning threshold, and network quality has deteriorated. It is necessary for operators to solve the congestion in advance and effectively to guarantee the quality of user experience. To address this challenge, we propose a dense multilayer perceptron (Dense-MLP) framework for cell-level multi-indicator forecasting. Unlike conventional approaches that analyze metrics independently, our architecture employs skip connections to capture complex temporal dependencies and cross-indicator correlations simultaneously. Trained on large-scale operational data from 4G/5G base stations, the model predicts key performance indicators including throughput, latency, and connection success rates hours in advance. Experimental results demonstrate that Dense-MLP consistently outperforms established baselines, delivering higher prediction accuracy with reduced computational overhead. By facilitating proactive resource allocation and dynamic load management, this approach offers telecom operators a lightweight, deployable solution for sustaining network stability and optimizing user experience under volatile traffic demands.

title: Simulating near-field enhancement in transmission of airborne viruses with a quadrature-based model.
text_ai: Some infectious diseases, such as influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2, may be transmitted when virus-laden particles expelled from an infectious person are inhaled by someone else, which is known as the airborne transmission route. These virus-laden particles are more concentrated in the expiratory jet of an infectious person than elsewhere in a well-mixed room, but this near-field enhancement in virion exposure has not been well quantified. To address this gap, we develop a quadrature-based model that couples respiratory aerosol dynamics with multi-species transport equations to resolve the spatial and temporal evolution of virion-laden droplets and droplet nuclei within the near-field zone. The framework explicitly tracks polydisperse particle populations using a moment-based closure scheme, enabling efficient computation of size-resolved concentration gradients without resorting to computationally prohibitive Lagrangian tracking of individual parcels. By integrating the model with steady-state and transient airflow fields typical of indoor environments, we quantify the near-field amplification factor across varying interpersonal distances, exhalation velocities, and background ventilation rates. Our simulations reveal that virion concentrations within the first two meters can exceed well-mixed room estimates by one to three orders of magnitude, depending on flow topology and particle aerodynamic diameter. Furthermore, the model demonstrates how subtle changes in head orientation and source-sink alignment significantly modulate local exposure doses, underscoring the limitations of uniform mixing assumptions in standard risk assessments. Validation against experimental tracer gas measurements confirms strong agreement in peak concentration predictions, with deviations remaining below 15% across all tested configurations. Sensitivity analyses indicate that enhanced local ventilation or directional airflow redirection can attenuate near-field peaks by up to 60%, whereas high relative humidity accelerates droplet evaporation and shifts the dominant transmission mode toward smaller, longer-lived nuclei. These findings provide a mechanistic basis for refining dose-response relationships and optimizing spatial interventions in occupied spaces. The proposed quadrature-based approach offers a scalable computational tool for evaluating near-field transmission risks under diverse operational scenarios, thereby supporting evidence-based guidelines for mitigating airborne pathogen spread in clinical, educational, and commercial settings.

title: Gaps in treatment among users of osteoporosis medications: the dynamics of noncompliance
text_ai: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of compliance have been observed with many health-related activities such as dieting and exercise. It is not known whether such patterns of compliance exist among users of chronic medications. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy after a prolonged lapse in medication use and to identify the factors associated with a return to compliance. METHODS: Leveraging a commercial claims database (2008–2018), we identified adults ≥50 years initiating oral or intravenous bisphosphonates or denosumab. Treatment gaps required ≥90 consecutive days without filled prescriptions. Reinitiation rates within 12 months post-lapse were calculated. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, Charlson comorbidity index, concomitant therapies, pharmacy utilization, and area-level median income isolated predictors of resumption. RESULTS: Among 14,287 patients, 38.4% experienced interruptions (median 112 days; IQR 95–168). Only 22.1% resumed therapy within 12 months. Restart rates differed by class: intravenous zoledronic acid showed higher retention (31.7%) versus daily oral alendronate (14.2%, p<0.001). Predictors of reinitiation included younger age (aOR 1.18/decade; 95% CI 1.12–1.24), absent gastrointestinal comorbidities (aOR 1.34; 95% CI 1.21–1.48), and patient assistance enrollment (aOR 1.62; 95% CI 1.45–1.81). Seasonal oscillations peaked in January and September, aligning with benefit renewals and visit cycles (p-trend <0.01). CONCLUSION: Osteoporosis patients frequently display cyclical nonadherence marked by recurrent lapses and partial recovery. Resumption follows predictable clinical, economic, and calendar-driven patterns rather than occurring randomly. Interventions targeting high-risk transition windows can reduce fracture vulnerability during treatment holidays. Routine adherence surveillance coupled with structured support systems is essential for converting intermittent compliance into durable therapeutic engagement. These longitudinal observations provide actionable targets for clinical practice optimization.

title: A Function Approximation Approach to Estimation of Policy Gradient for POMDP with Structured Policies
text_ai: We consider the estimation of the policy gradient in partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDP) with a special class of structured policies that are finite-state controllers. We show that the gradient estimation can be done in the Actor-Critic framework, by making the critic compute a "value" function that does not depend on the states of POMDP. By leveraging function approximation over the belief space, we derive an unbiased estimator that circumvents explicit belief computation while preserving asymptotic convergence guarantees. We establish rigorous theoretical bounds on the approximation error and demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves comparable performance to exact gradient methods under partial observability. Extensive simulations on standard POMDP benchmarks confirm that our approach significantly reduces both computational overhead and gradient variance relative to conventional actor-critic baselines. These findings underscore the effectiveness of combining finite-state controllers with approximate value functions for scalable reinforcement learning in environments with limited observability across diverse task configurations.

title: Analysis of a Memcapacitor-Based for Neural Network Accelerator Framework
text_ai: Data-intensive computing tasks, such as training neural networks, are crucial for artificial intelligence applications but often come with high energy demands. One promising solution is to develop specialized hardware that directly maps neural networks, utilizing arrays of memristive devices to perform parallel multiply-accumulate operations. This study presents a novel memcapacitor-based accelerator framework designed to overcome the von Neumann bottleneck by co-locating memory and computation within a single crossbar architecture. Unlike conventional resistive elements, memcapacitors offer inherent voltage-controlled capacitance tuning and superior endurance, enabling precise analog weight storage with minimal leakage currents. We evaluate the proposed system through circuit-level simulations and neural network benchmarks spanning convolutional and recurrent topologies. Results demonstrate a 4.2× reduction in energy per inference compared to GPU-accelerated baselines, while maintaining >98% classification accuracy across quantized models. Latency analysis confirms sub-nanosecond switching dynamics that enable rapid matrix-vector multiplications without external data movement. These findings validate memcapacitive crossbars as a scalable, energy-efficient paradigm for future on-device inference.
