title: Early-life gut dysbiosis linked to juvenile mortality in ostriches.
text_ai: Imbalances in the gut microbial community (dysbiosis) of vertebrates have been associated with several gastrointestinal and autoimmune diseases. However, it is unclear which taxa are associated with gut dysbiosis, and if particular gut regions or specific time periods during ontogeny are more susceptible. To address these knowledge gaps, we conducted a longitudinal metagenomic survey across multiple gastrointestinal compartments in captive-born ostrich (Struthio camelus) chicks during their first twelve weeks of life. Fecal, crop, and intestinal luminal contents were collected at weekly intervals from 86 individuals spanning two breeding seasons. High-throughput 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing was coupled with shotgun metagenomics to resolve taxonomic composition and functional potential. Longitudinal beta-diversity analyses revealed distinct spatial and temporal trajectories, with the mid-intestine exhibiting the highest compositional instability between days 7 and 21 post-hatch. Dysbiotic signatures, characterized by a marked depletion of Firmicutes and an expansion of Proteobacteria and Clostridioides, emerged predominantly in this window. Notably, chicks that subsequently exhibited clinical signs of septicemia or enteritis displayed significantly reduced alpha-diversity and altered Firmicutes-to-Bacteroidetes ratios prior to overt morbidity. Machine learning classifiers trained on early-life microbial profiles achieved 89% accuracy in predicting juvenile mortality, with Enterocloster and Ruminococcaceae UCG-014 emerging as primary protective biomarkers. Functional annotation indicated concurrent disruptions in short-chain fatty acid biosynthesis and mucosal barrier integrity pathways. Statistical validation using cross-validated permutation tests confirmed that these microbial shifts were not attributable to dietary transitions or standard husbandry variables across both experimental cohorts. These findings demonstrate that early ontogenetic windows represent critical periods of microbial vulnerability in avian hosts. The identification of region-specific dysbiotic trajectories preceding mortality provides actionable biomarkers for precision health monitoring in commercially managed populations. This integrative approach bridges ecological theory with practical avian husbandry protocols. Furthermore, our results underscore the necessity of integrating multi-compartmental, time-resolved microbiome assessments into veterinary prognostic frameworks, offering a scalable paradigm for mitigating preventable losses in endangered and agriculturally significant bird species, thereby refining developmental immunology models.

title: An exact relation between number of black box computations required to solve an oracle problem quantumly and quantum retrocausality
text_ai: We investigate the reason for the quantum speedup -- quantum algorithms requiring fewer computation steps than their classical counterparts. We extend their representation to the process of setting the problem. The initial measurement selects a setting at random, Bob (the problem setter) unitarily changes it into the desired one. By incorporating Alice’s subsequent oracle queries within this temporally symmetric framework, we demonstrate that the algorithmic evolution can be fully described as a two-state vector spanning both preparation and final verification. Within this formulation, each black-box evaluation contributes an amplitude that interferes constructively along histories consistent with Bob’s chosen configuration while destructively suppressing incompatible trajectories. We derive an exact analytical relation showing that the minimum number of oracle invocations required to resolve an arbitrary decision problem scales inversely with the strength of the retrocausal coupling between the preselected measurement outcome and the postselected verification condition. Specifically, we prove that any quantum algorithm achieving quadratic or exponential speedup necessarily satisfies a query-completeness equality, wherein the reduction in computational steps precisely matches the information gain enabled by backward-evolving boundary conditions. Classical protocols, lacking such temporal correlations, must probe the oracle exhaustively to eliminate ambiguity, thereby establishing a strict lower bound on their query complexity. We validate this formalism across canonical examples—including Deutsch–Jozsa, Simon’s, and unstructured search—demonstrating that their respective query counts emerge directly from the derived retrocausal identity. These results reframe quantum advantage not as a mere property of superposition or entanglement, but as a direct consequence of temporal nonlocality embedded in the problem-solving architecture. Consequently, our work provides a unified foundation for understanding query complexity through the lens of time-symmetric quantum mechanics, offering new pathways for optimizing oracle-based protocols and clarifying the foundational origins of computational acceleration. The resulting framework further implies that any protocol attempting to surpass standard quantum query limits must either weaken the retrocausal boundary matching or fundamentally alter how the oracle state is accessed.

title: International clinical practice recommendations on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of developmental coordination disorder.
text_ai: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to address key questions on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of DCD relevant for clinical practice. Key questions in five areas were considered through literature reviews and formal expert consensus. The resulting guidelines synthesize current evidence with clinical expertise to produce actionable statements across each domain. Regarding definition, the panel clarified that DCD should be conceptualized as a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent motor skill acquisition and execution difficulties that substantially interfere with activities of daily living and academic or vocational achievement, independent of intellectual disability or primary neurological pathology. For diagnosis, the recommendations advocate for a standardized, multi-informant approach utilizing validated motor assessments alongside comprehensive developmental and medical histories to ensure accurate classification and exclude alternative etiologies. Assessment protocols emphasize a biopsychosocial framework, integrating direct motor performance testing, activity and participation evaluations, and environmental analyses to systematically identify contextual barriers and facilitators. Intervention strategies prioritize task-specific, goal-directed training embedded within meaningful real-world contexts, with robust empirical support for cognitive strategy training, physical therapy, and occupational therapy delivered by appropriately credentialed practitioners. Crucially, the guidelines underscore the bidirectional relationship between motor impairment and psychological functioning, recommending routine screening for comorbid anxiety, depression, and diminished self-concept, alongside targeted psychosocial interventions addressing coping mechanisms, peer dynamics, and familial adaptation. Implementation considerations highlight the necessity of interdisciplinary collaboration, active caregiver engagement, and educational accommodations to optimize functional trajectories. These recommendations aim to standardize clinical decision-making, mitigate diagnostic delays, and enhance long-term well-being for affected populations globally. To facilitate widespread adoption, the panel outlines tiered implementation pathways adapted to varying resource settings, emphasizing competency-based training and health policy integration. Future investigations must prioritize longitudinal outcome tracking, cross-cultural instrument validation, and implementation science methodologies to sustainably bridge guideline dissemination and routine clinical practice.

title: Computational analysis of flow structures in turbulent ventricular blood flow associated with mitral valve intervention
text_ai: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention may both lead to an increased risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow in the heart, and thereby a change in the mechanical stimuli of blood cells passing through the chambers of the heart. To elucidate these hemodynamic alterations, three-dimensional transient computational fluid dynamics simulations were performed on patient-specific left ventricular geometries reconstructed from magnetic resonance imaging. The governing Navier–Stokes equations were coupled with a scale-adaptive simulation turbulence model to accurately resolve the intermittent coherent structures characteristic of pathological ventricular flows. Temporal evolution of the velocity fields revealed that mitral valve intervention significantly modifies intraventricular vortex dynamics, generating elongated recirculation zones and elevated turbulent kinetic energy concentrations near the septal wall. Quantitative assessment of wall shear stress distributions demonstrated prolonged low-shear stagnation regions downstream of the prosthetic leaflets, creating conditions conducive to platelet accumulation and delayed washout. Conversely, high-frequency oscillatory shear gradients were identified in the vicinity of the regurgitant jet impingement site, correlating with elevated predicted platelet activation indices derived from a semi-empirical hemolysis-thrombosis coupling framework. Comparative analysis across surgical repair and transcatheter replacement configurations indicated that minimally invasive strategies preserve physiological flow patterns, yet introduce localized micro-turbulence that may exacerbate coagulation cascades during peak diastole. Model predictions were validated against phase-contrast MRI velocity maps, confirming numerical accuracy, while parametric studies highlighted the robustness of the identified flow-topology markers. These findings establish a direct mechanistic linkage between intervention-induced topological flow changes and the spatial-temporal distribution of hemodynamic triggers for thrombus formation. The proposed computational framework provides a reproducible methodology for quantifying thromboembolic risk profiles prior to procedural planning, enabling device-specific optimization and patient-tailored anticoagulation protocols. Ultimately, integrating high-fidelity hemodynamic modeling with cellular-scale activation models advances precision cardiovascular medicine by transforming qualitative anatomical assessments into predictive, quantitative risk stratification tools. This approach establishes a scalable paradigm for translational hemodynamic risk assessment.

title: Multi-Institutional Predictors of Antibiotic Resistance in Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department with Urosepsis Secondary to Ureteral Obstruction.
text_ai: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection with kidney or ureteral stones is a urologic emergency often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. To optimize empiric therapy during this interim period, we conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study utilizing the TriNetX federated research network across 48 integrated healthcare systems. We queried electronic health records to identify adult patients (≥18 years) presenting to the emergency department with urosepsis secondary to radiographically confirmed ureteral obstruction between January 2018 and December 2022. Primary outcomes included multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogen identification and resistance to first-line empiric antibiotics. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to adjust for demographic comorbidities, prior antimicrobial exposure, institutional stewardship protocols, and stone characteristics. The final analytical cohort comprised 14,832 patients. Escherichia coli remained the predominant uropathogen (68.4%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (11.2%) and Enterococcus species (9.7%). Overall, 34.1% of isolates demonstrated resistance to at least one guideline-recommended empiric agent, with fluoroquinolone resistance reaching 28.6%. Independent predictors of MDR colonization included recent hospitalization within 90 days (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.82; 95% CI 1.61–2.06), prior broad-spectrum antibiotic use (aOR 1.94; 95% CI 1.73–2.17), and chronic indwelling urinary catheterization (aOR 2.31; 95% CI 2.01–2.65). Notably, unilateral versus bilateral obstruction did not significantly alter resistance probabilities (p=0.412), whereas prolonged symptom duration (>7 days) was associated with higher carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales rates (aOR 1.55; 95% CI 1.22–1.98). These findings demonstrate that traditional anatomical severity markers alone are insufficient for guiding targeted empiric therapy in obstructive urosepsis. Incorporating modifiable risk factors—particularly recent healthcare exposure and antimicrobial history—into a validated predictive algorithm may optimize initial regimen selection, reduce inappropriate empiric coverage, and facilitate earlier therapeutic de-escalation. Implementation of institution-specific resistance profiling alongside rapid molecular diagnostics could shorten hospitalizations while preserving antimicrobial stewardship principles for emergency physicians.

title: Lifetime of the superconductive state in short and long Josephson junctions
text_ai: We study the transient statistical properties of short and long Josephson junctions under the influence of thermal and correlated fluctuations. In particular, we investigate the lifetime of the superconductive metastable state finding the presence of noise induced phenomena. We employ a generalized Fokker–Planck framework combined with stochastic differential equations to quantify escape rates across varying correlation times and bias currents. Our analysis reveals that colored Gaussian noise significantly modulates transition probabilities, yielding non-monotonic dependencies characteristic of noise-enhanced stability and stochastic resonant activation. While short devices exhibit single-barrier Kramers scaling, long junctions display spatially extended phase dynamics coupled with temporal correlations, producing multi-exponential decay profiles. We derive closed-form expressions for the mean first-passage time, demonstrating how non-Markovian memory effects selectively suppress or amplify thermally activated transitions depending on the junction aspect ratio. These results establish a unified kinetic description of metastability degradation, providing critical design parameters for enhancing coherence windows in superconducting circuits and low-power cryogenic logic architectures.

title: Simulating Head Recovery and Intermittent Discharge in Free Flowing Wells.
text_ai: Modeling of the head recovery (buildup) in and intermittent operation of flowing wells lacks rigorous analytical tools. Presently different methods are applied in discharging and recovery phases. The presented reliable approximate solution considers a continuous free flow process and time variant screen loss parameters. The governing transient flow equation couples radial diffusion principles with dynamic friction factors evolving during phase transitions. Comprehensive field validation confirms high fidelity, maintaining relative errors below 9% across varied geological settings. This formulation explicitly resolves hysteresis between drawdown and recovery trajectories, eliminating discontinuities introduced by segregated analytical routines. Sensitivity evaluations demonstrate that temporal fluctuations in screen loss coefficients predominantly dictate initial buildup velocities and asymptotic equilibrium levels. Computational efficiency remains comparable to classical approximations, facilitating seamless integration into existing hydraulic modeling suites. Consequently, practitioners gain consolidated predictive capability for scheduling intermittent extractions, minimizing mechanical stress on completion intervals, and extending productive lifespans within confined aquifer systems and transient pressure regimes.

title: The Association between Reasons for a Rapid Response Team Alert and Immediate Patient Management in Total Hip Arthroplasty Patients.
text_ai: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. A retrospective review of all RRT events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016 was performed. Clinical documentation, electronic health records, and dedicated RRT logs were systematically audited. Inclusion criteria encompassed adults undergoing primary or revision THA experiencing at least one postoperative RRT activation. Patients with polytrauma, concurrent systemic infections, or direct transfers from outside facilities were excluded. Extracted parameters included baseline demographics, procedural complexity, pre-activation hemodynamics and oxygenation metrics, specific physiological triggers, immediate bedside interventions, final disposition, and thirty-day morbidity. Group comparisons utilized Student’s t-tests, Mann-Whitney U statistics, and chi-square evaluations as distribution permitted. Binary outcomes were modeled via multivariable logistic regression to isolate independent predictors of critical care escalation. Among 1,847 consecutive THA admissions, 112 discrete RRT calls were documented (incidence 6.1%). Respiratory compromise represented the most frequent trigger (n=42, 37.5%), succeeded by hemodynamic instability (n=31, 27.7%), altered mental status (n=24, 21.4%), and cardiac dysrhythmias (n=15, 13.4%). Therapeutic responses correlated strongly with trigger classification: pulmonary derangements commonly mandated non-invasive positive pressure or definitive airway management (64.3%), circulatory failures primarily required crystalloid boluses or catecholamine infusions (71.0%), and encephalopathic presentations triggered emergent computed tomography and neurology involvement (58.3%). Overall, 38 activations (33.9%) culminated in intensive care unit transfer. No patient experienced in-hospital mortality or required unplanned reoperation within thirty days. Pre-activation systolic blood pressure below 90 mmHg and peripheral oxygen saturation under 90% on ambient air emerged as robust, independent risk factors for ICU admission. Post-THA RRT activations demonstrate marked clinical diversity requiring tailored diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. Developing trigger-specific clinical pathways enhances staff preparedness and accelerates time-sensitive interventions. Embedding these etiology-focused algorithms within institutional enhanced recovery programs promises to diminish adverse perioperative outcomes while optimizing acute care resource utilization across orthopedic surgical units.

title: Neuropeptidase activity in the frontal cortex of Wistar-Kyoto and spontaneously hypertensive rats treated with vasoactive drugs: a bilateral study.
text_ai: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders that may worsen or ameliorate depending on the type of antihypertensive prescribed. Depression is associated with modifications in basal brain asymmetry particularly that of the frontal cortex, which is involved in blood pressure control. Furthermore, different vasoactive drugs may change the brain's asymmetry in a manner that contributes to cognition status. To elucidate these interactions, we investigated regional neuropeptidase activity across left and right frontal cortices in adult WKY and SHR strains following chronic administration of distinct vasoactive agents, including angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, calcium channel blockers, and beta-adrenergic antagonists. Bilateral tissue samples were homogenized and subjected to spectrophotometric assays targeting specific peptidase isoforms, with statistical analyses accounting for strain × hemisphere × treatment interactions. Our data revealed significant strain-dependent alterations in enzymatic profiles, with SHRs exhibiting baseline right-hemispheric dominance in neprilysin and angiotensin-converting enzyme activities compared to normotensive WKY controls. Chronic pharmacological intervention selectively normalized asymmetric peptidase expression in hypertensive subjects, particularly through coordinated bilateral upregulation of vasopeptidases. Statistical evaluation confirmed pronounced genotype-laterality interactions, with post-hoc comparisons highlighting drug-induced convergence toward WKY baseline asymmetry thresholds. Specifically, ACE inhibitor protocols yielded the most substantial normalization of left-right activity ratios, paralleling improved hippocampal-cortical connectivity markers. Conversely, beta-blocker regimens produced modest peptidase shifts without significant cognitive benefits, suggesting divergent central pathways. Notably, drug-specific modulation correlated inversely with behavioral indices of depressive-like phenotypes and spatial learning deficits. Hemispheric rebalancing predicted cognitive recovery more robustly than systemic pressure reduction, indicating independent central mechanisms. Localized neuropeptidase dysregulation critically mediates cardiovascular-neuropsychiatric comorbidities. By demonstrating that targeted vasoactive therapies can restore cortical symmetry and enhance peptidase homeostasis, this bilateral approach provides a mechanistic framework for optimizing neurocardiovascular interventions. Future investigations should prioritize lateralized biomarker tracking to refine precision medicine strategies for hypertensive populations at elevated risk for affective and cognitive decline.

title: A 52 hours VLT/FORS2 spectrum of a bright z~7 HUDF galaxy: no Ly-alpha emission
text_ai: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT spectra of GDS-1408 collected by us and two other groups with FORS2 at VLT in the last five years, for a total integration time of 52hr. The stacked spectrum reveals a robust continuum detection blueward of the Lyman break, consistent with a stellar population age of ~100 Myr and negligible dust extinction. However, despite the exceptional signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 15 per Angstrom, we find no significant detection of Lyα emission. The 3σ upper limit on the Lyα equivalent width is constrained to < 12 Å, implying an intrinsic Lyα escape fraction ≲ 0.05. This non-detection persists across multiple kinematic models and cannot be fully attributed to instrumental effects or sky-subtraction residuals. We explore two primary scenarios to reconcile our findings with the photometric selection criteria: either the galaxy resides at a slightly lower redshift (z ~ 6.5) where the Lyα line falls within a transmission window, or it truly lies at z ~ 7 but exhibits suppressed resonance line emission due to high neutral hydrogen fraction in the surrounding intergalactic medium or dense circumgalactic gas. Spectral energy distribution fitting favors the higher-redshift solution, yielding a star formation rate of ~5 M⊙ yr⁻¹ and a UV luminosity density that contributes marginally to cosmic reionization. Our results underscore the limitations of photometric dropout techniques in identifying unambiguously high-redshift populations and highlight the critical necessity of ultra-deep spectroscopic follow-up. The absence of Lyα emission in this bright, compact source suggests that early galaxies may frequently harbor neutral gas reservoirs that efficiently quench resonance line propagation, thereby biasing current reionization-era surveys toward highly ionized, potentially rare systems. Future observations with JWST/NIRSpec will be essential to probe the underlying nebular conditions and resolve the true redshift nature of such candidates.

title: Ten-Year Evaluation of the TOYOTA Prehospital Stroke Scale for Tissue Plasminogen Activator Intravenous Therapy in the Real World.
text_ai: Emergency medical services are an important part of acute stroke management. We devised a prehospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN) for triaging patients with ischemic stroke and especial indications for intravenous t-PA therapy in December 2006; this scale comprises 5 items including consciousness, atrial fibrillation, language disorder, disturbance of the upper extremities, and disturbance of the lower extremities. This ten-year observational study evaluated the real-world diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility of the TOPSPIN scale across multiple emergency medical service districts. We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected registry data from consecutive adult patients presenting with suspected acute ischemic stroke between January 2007 and December 2016. The primary outcome was the scale’s ability to correctly identify patients ultimately receiving intravenous t-PA, measured by sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. Secondary endpoints included prehospital identification rates, median door-to-needle times, and neurological improvement at discharge. Of the 8,432 screened patients, 1,104 scored positive on the TOPSPIN criterion. Among these, 682 received intravenous thrombolysis. Sensitivity reached 89.3% (95% CI, 86.7–91.5%) and specificity achieved 74.1% (95% CI, 72.0–76.0%) for detecting eligible t-PA recipients. Predictive values stood at 61.8% and 93.2%. Implementation of the TOPSPIN significantly reduced median door-to-needle intervals from 58 to 41 minutes over the study period (p < 0.001). False-negative cases predominantly involved posterior circulation strokes and mild transient symptoms, whereas false positives frequently stemmed from non-stroke mimics such as hypoglycemia or seizures. Despite a modest reduction in overall t-PA utilization due to strict exclusion criteria, the scale effectively prioritized high-risk patients without compromising safety standards. These findings validate the TOPSPIN as a robust, field-ready triage instrument that optimizes resource allocation and accelerates therapeutic windows in community-based stroke systems. Integrating this tool into standard dispatch algorithms will optimize thrombolytic delivery and improve functional recovery.

title: Race does not predict the development of metastases in men with nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
text_ai: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis utilizing electronic health records from three integrated healthcare networks. Adult men diagnosed with nmCRPC between 2014 and 2021 were enrolled. Participants were stratified by self-reported race into Black, Hispanic, Asian/Pacific Islander, and White categories. The primary endpoint was time to radiographic or clinical metastasis. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, baseline prostate-specific antigen velocity, Gleason grade, Charlson comorbidity index, and novel hormonal agent utilization estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Longitudinal modeling accounted for competing risks of mortality unrelated to prostate cancer. Sensitivity analyses incorporated neighborhood deprivation indices to evaluate residual confounding. Among 4,218 eligible patients, 28.4% identified as Black, 12.1% as Hispanic, 8.7% as Asian/Pacific Islander, and 50.8% as White. Median follow-up was 28 months. During observation, 1,342 patients (31.8%) progressed to metastatic disease. Crude incidence appeared elevated in Black men; however, multivariable adjustment abolished independent racial effects (Black vs. White HR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.92–1.17; P = .52). Hispanic (HR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.84–1.14; P = .78) and Asian/Pacific Islander groups exhibited statistically indistinguishable metastatic trajectories. Results remained stable across sensitivity strata defined by insurance type and regional practice patterns. Subgroup evaluations confirmed homogeneity of treatment effects across all racial strata. Importantly, PSA doubling time and therapeutic class consistently outperformed race in predicting metastatic conversion, with no appreciable gain in concordance statistics upon racial variable inclusion. Self-identified race does not independently forecast metastatic transformation in men with nmCRPC after controlling for standard clinical covariates. Racial categorization should be de-emphasized in prognostic nomograms for advanced disease. Prospective frameworks must prioritize quantifiable biological markers and systemic care-access metrics to accurately capture disparities and refine personalized surveillance strategies.

title: Treatment of chronic nonunions of the humerus with free vascularized fibula transfer: a report of thirteen cases
text_ai: Chronic nonunions of the humerus remain a challenging problem. We reviewed 13 cases of chronic nonunion of the humerus resulting from trauma or osteomyelitis treated with vascularized fibula transfer after failure of conventional treatment. Patient averages were 35 years of age, follow-up of 19 months, and 4.2 prior operations. Radiographic assessment demonstrated complete bony union in 12 of 13 cases at a mean of 7.4 months postoperatively. One patient required secondary autografting due to delayed consolidation but ultimately achieved union without further intervention. Functional evaluation using the DASH score revealed substantial improvement, with mean scores decreasing from 68.3 preoperatively to 24.1 at final follow-up. Complications included superficial wound infection in two patients, both managed conservatively with oral antibiotics. No donor-site morbidity or vascular compromise was observed. Free vascularized fibula transfer provides reliable reconstruction for complex humeral nonunions refractory to standard techniques, offering durable union and significant functional restoration while preserving limb salvage potential.

title: Survival of Salmonella spp. in Composting using Vial and Direct Inoculums Technique
text_ai: The survival of Salmonella spp. as pathogen indicator in composting was studied. The inoculums technique was used to gives the known amounts of Salmonella spp. involved in composting. The inoculums of Salmonella spp. solution was added directly into the compost material. The direct inoculum was compared with inoculums in vial technique. Composting piles were established under controlled thermophilic conditions, with internal temperatures monitored continuously to guarantee adequate pathogen reduction. Samples were collected at predetermined intervals over a 45-day operational cycle and subjected to selective enrichment followed by membrane filtration and quantitative polymerase chain reaction assays to accurately enumerate viable cells. Thermal profiling confirmed that both experimental groups consistently exceeded 55°C for a minimum of five consecutive days, thereby satisfying established regulatory benchmarks for pathogen inactivation. Despite fulfilling these thermal thresholds, Salmonella spp. persisted significantly longer within the direct inoculation matrix relative to the vial encapsulation protocol (p < 0.05). Bacterial cells introduced through vials exhibited accelerated die-off kinetics, attributable primarily to enhanced physical shielding against rapid desiccation and competitive microbial antagonism during early colonization stages. Conversely, direct suspension application promoted immediate homogenization throughout the substrate, fostering localized microenvironments that effectively buffered cellular populations against uniform thermal degradation. Population dynamics revealed a logarithmic decline in cultivable densities; however, extracellular DNA remnants remained persistently detectable long after metabolic activity ceased, underscoring substantial constraints associated with traditional culture-dependent quantification frameworks. Collectively, these empirical results demonstrate that inoculation strategy fundamentally alters measured persistence trajectories and potentially undermines cross-study reproducibility. Harmonizing delivery protocols remains essential for producing robust datasets regarding compost-driven pathogen suppression. Operational recommendations indicate that deploying protective carrier matrices may substantially improve the accuracy of thermal lethality predictions. Consequently, this investigation emphasizes the imperative of embedding methodological standardization within commercial composting validation procedures to sustain reliable biosafety parameters and fulfill agricultural regulations.

title: Modular Many-Body Quantum Sensors
text_ai: Quantum many-body systems undergoing phase transitions have been proposed as probes enabling beyond-classical enhancement of sensing precision. However, this enhancement is usually limited to a very narrow region around the critical point. Here, we systematically develop a modular approach for introducing multiple phase transitions in a many-body system. By coupling independent subsystems through engineered interactions, our framework generates a sequence of distinct critical manifolds within the global phase diagram. We demonstrate that this architecture broadens the operational bandwidth while preserving the quadratic scaling of the quantum Fisher information with particle number. Both analytical and numerical analyses confirm that the modular design sustains high metrological sensitivity across extended parameter regimes, relaxing the stringent control demands of single-critical-point protocols. Furthermore, we establish explicit bounds on decoherence resilience, showing that environmental noise tolerance scales favorably with module count. These results provide a scalable pathway toward robust, broadband quantum sensors that surpass classical precision limits and remain compatible with near-term experimental implementations.

title: The Oldest Stars of the Extremely Metal-Poor Local Group Dwarf Irregular Galaxy Leo A
text_ai: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this galaxy. The resulting color-magnitude diagrams reveal a well-populated main-sequence turnoff at m_V ≈ 27.5 mag, alongside an extended red-giant branch and a distinct blue horizontal branch. Isochrone fitting employing Dartmouth and BASTI evolutionary tracks yields an absolute age of 12.8 ± 0.5 Gyr for the dominant ancient stellar population, consistent with formation during the peak epoch of cosmic structure assembly. We derive a mean halo metallicity of [Fe/H] ≈ -2.4 ± 0.3, confirming Leo A as one of the most chemically primitive systems within the Local Group. Star-formation history reconstruction indicates a predominantly quiescent evolution, with only minor, short-lived starbursts occurring after z ∼ 2. Notably, the absence of significant intermediate-age populations contrasts sharply with the continuous star-formation episodes identified in the inner disk by Tolstoy et al., suggesting that external tidal interactions or environmental feedback likely suppressed further gas accretion in the outer halo. The derived mass-to-light ratio implies a high dark matter fraction, reinforcing hierarchical clustering predictions for low-mass satellite galaxies. These findings place stringent constraints on the early chemical enrichment timescales of dwarf irregulars, supporting models in which shallow potential wells retain minimal baryonic mass following cosmic reionization. Our results underscore Leo A’s value as a nearby fossil record of primordial galaxy formation, providing critical empirical benchmarks for cosmological simulations of the first generations of dark matter substructures. Future JWST/NIRCam observations will be essential to resolve the faintest main-sequence stars and refine the metallicity distribution function at the base of the giant branch. These multi-wavelength data collectively establish a robust framework for interpreting ultra-deep surveys of analogous extragalactic systems.

title: Catalyzing Social Interactions in Mixed Reality using ML Recommendation Systems
text_ai: We create an innovative mixed reality-first social recommendation model, utilizing features uniquely collected through mixed reality (MR) systems to promote social interaction, such as gaze recognition, proximity, noise level, congestion level, and conversational intensity. We further extend these models to include right-time features to deliver timely notifications. To empirically evaluate this approach, we deployed the system across diverse public venues, comparing it against static notification baselines. Quantitative analysis reveals that context-aware prompts significantly increase spontaneous peer-to-peer engagements by 42% while mitigating interaction fatigue. Moreover, synchronizing alerts with natural conversational lulls improves sustained dialogue duration by 31%. These results demonstrate the efficacy of embedding spatial-affective signals into reinforcement learning pipelines within MR environments. Ablation studies confirm that temporal weighting mechanisms outperform static thresholds, validating our architecture’s adaptability to dynamic social ecologies. Ultimately, this research bridges computational social science and immersive computing, establishing a scalable framework for ethically augmenting human connectivity in hybrid physical-digital spaces and informing future social XR architectures.

title: Reductions in alcohol use following medical cannabis initiation: results from a large cross-sectional survey of medical cannabis patients in Canada.
text_ai: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data were derived from an anonymous, web-based cross-sectional survey distributed through national patient registries and advocacy organizations. Respondents provided detailed information on sociodemographic profiles, underlying health conditions, prior substance use trajectories, and perceived pharmacological interactions between cannabis and alcohol. Weighted multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to isolate independent predictors of alcohol reduction while adjusting for confounding variables. Survey instruments underwent rigorous psychometric validation, ensuring reliable measurement across provincial jurisdictions. Among 4,812 eligible participants, 67.9% reported clinically meaningful declines in both drinking frequency and volume within six months of cannabis authorization. Elevated pre-initiation alcohol consumption, advanced age, and primary indications of anxiety, chronic pain, and sleep disturbances emerged as robust correlates of substitution behavior. Notably, concomitant benzodiazepine utilization correlated with diminished alcohol reduction rates, suggesting potential therapeutic overlap or risk-averse prescribing practices. Product formulation preferences did not independently moderate outcomes. Effect sizes indicated moderate practical significance, reinforcing clinical relevance beyond statistical thresholds. Collectively, these data indicate that medically supervised cannabis functions as an effective harm-reduction modality for targeted populations exhibiting maladaptive drinking behaviors. Integrating structured substance-use screening into cannabis authorization protocols may optimize patient stratification and enhance public health outcomes. Longitudinal cohort investigations remain essential to delineate temporal dynamics, neurobiological pathways, and sustained efficacy across diverse clinical demographics.

title: An effective Thermodynamic Description of Galactic Haloes
text_ai: The observation of flat rotation curves in asymptotic region of galaxies implies that the dark matter density profile decreases exponentially with the gravitational potential in this region. It is curious that this behavior is identical to what one would have from a Boltzmann gas in thermal equilibrium. Building upon this statistical mechanical analogy, we construct an effective thermodynamic framework characterizing dark matter haloes as self-gravitating quasi-equilibrium systems. Introducing a characteristic halo temperature proportional to the circular velocity squared, we derive analytic expressions for the density, pressure, and entropy distributions that naturally yield the observed exponential scaling. Our model successfully reproduces high-resolution N-body simulation profiles across diverse halo masses without ad hoc parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the derived thermodynamic potentials satisfy standard stability criteria, suggesting haloes evolve toward maximum-entropy configurations under slow secular relaxation. This framework provides a rigorous phenomenological link between microscopic dynamics and macroscopic structure, revealing emergent thermodynamic properties in collisionless dark matter systems.

title: Neuromorphic meets neuromechanics, part I: the methodology and implementation.
text_ai: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create 'realistic' robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement the spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles. Traditional computational frameworks frequently decouple central pattern generation from peripheral proprioceptive feedback, thereby compromising the dynamic stability required for robust locomotion. To address this limitation, we propose a unified methodological pipeline that maps biologically derived spinal microcircuits onto reconfigurable neuromorphic architectures. Our approach integrates conductance-based spiking neuron models with mechanoreceptor dynamics, ensuring that efferent motor commands are continuously modulated by real-time afferent signals originating from muscle spindles and Golgi tendon organs. The implementation leverages event-driven processing paradigms to minimize energy consumption while preserving millisecond-scale temporal precision essential for reflexive adjustments. We detail the systematic translation of anatomical connectivity matrices into synaptic weight distributions, incorporating activity-dependent plasticity rules to emulate developmental maturation and adaptive recalibration. We further integrate adaptive threshold modulation to compensate for device nonidealities and manufacturing variations. Simulation environments coupled with hardware-in-the-loop validation confirm that the proposed architecture successfully reproduces phase transitions between stance and swing, as well as load compensation mechanisms observed in quadrupedal gaits. By establishing a standardized protocol for circuit synthesis, parameter optimization, and empirical verification, this work provides a reproducible foundation for deploying biologically plausible controllers in embedded robotic platforms. The methodology emphasizes modularity, enabling seamless integration of novel sensor modalities and hierarchical supraspinal inputs without disrupting local feedback loops. Ultimately, this framework bridges the gap between theoretical neurobiology and practical mechatronics, demonstrating how neuromorphic substrates can natively support the closed-loop neuromechanical interactions that underpin autonomous movement. Subsequent analyses will quantify performance metrics across diverse terrains and evaluate scalability toward multi-segmental vertebrate morphologies, ensuring long-term operational viability and future experimental deployments.

title: Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting for Unbiased Scene Graph Generation
text_ai: An unbiased scene graph generation (SGG) algorithm referred to as Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting (SCR) is proposed for considering the unbiased predicate prediction caused by the long-tailed distribution. The prior works focus mainly on alleviating the deteriorating performances of the minority predicate predictions, showing drastic dropping recall scores, i.e., losing the majority predicate performances. To address this limitation, SCR introduces a skew-aware re-weighting scheme that dynamically adjusts loss gradients according to empirical class frequencies while maintaining training stability. By explicitly accounting for the skewed predicate distribution, the framework prevents dominant categories from overshadowing rare relationships during optimization. Comprehensive evaluations on the Visual Genome dataset reveal that SCR consistently elevates recall across all predicate tiers, boosting minority predicate recognition by 4.2% without compromising majority class accuracy. Ablation analyses further confirm that our formulation surpasses conventional focal and uniform sampling baselines. Ultimately, SCR offers a principled, modular solution for equitable relationship learning, substantially advancing unbiased scene understanding in real-world applications.

title: Carleman-lattice-Boltzmann quantum circuit with matrix access oracles
text_ai: We apply Carleman linearization of the Lattice Boltzmann (CLB) representation of fluid flows to quantum emulate the dynamics of a 2D Kolmogorov-like flow. We assess the accuracy of the result and find a relative error of the order of $10^{-3}$ with just two Carleman iterates, for a range of the Reynolds number up to a few hundreds. By mapping the truncated Carleman expansion onto a sparse Hamiltonian, we design a modular quantum circuit that exploits matrix access oracles to query system coefficients without full state initialization. The resulting architecture exhibits polylogarithmic scaling with respect to lattice resolution, permitting efficient compilation on near-term hardware. Comparative benchmarks reveal that the quantum emulator faithfully reproduces spectral energy distributions and enstrophy decay rates while reducing gate counts by an order of magnitude relative to direct matrix exponentiation. These results underscore the feasibility of oracle-driven quantum circuits for high-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics and suggest a clear trajectory toward practical quantum advantage in continuum mechanics.

title: Partial-Information Multiple Access Protocol for Orthogonal Transmissions
text_ai: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution is still to be accomplished. To address this challenge, we propose a Partial-Information Multiple Access (PIMA) protocol that enables reliable orthogonal transmissions under asynchronous, high-density device deployments. Rather than relying on exhaustive channel state information or centralized scheduling, PIMA operates exclusively on locally observable statistics and sparsely allocated orthogonal signatures. This architectural shift eliminates the signaling overhead inherent in contention-based schemes while preserving strict orthogonality among concurrent uplink transmissions. We formulate a stochastic geometry-based model to characterize the spatial distribution of active devices and derive closed-form expressions for the packet delivery ratio, achievable throughput, and peak age of information. The core innovation lies in a distributed collision resolution algorithm that leverages partial knowledge of slot occupancy patterns to dynamically adjust transmission probabilities, thereby minimizing multi-access interference without requiring global synchronization. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations validate the analytical framework, demonstrating that PIMA attains a 38–45% improvement in spectral efficiency over competing grant-free and non-orthogonal multiple access benchmarks. Moreover, the protocol maintains stable operation at device densities surpassing 10^5 nodes/km², with average latency consistently below 1.2 ms under bursty traffic conditions. These results confirm that restricting information exchange to local, low-cost observations does not compromise reliability but instead enhances scalability and energy efficiency. By rigorously decoupling orthogonal resource utilization from perfect channel estimation and network-wide coordination, this work establishes a practical design paradigm for ultra-reliable low-latency communications. The proposed framework offers a scalable pathway toward meeting the heterogeneous quality-of-service demands anticipated in next-generation IoT ecosystems.

title: The effect of structural and magnetic disorder on the 3$d$-5$d$ exchange interactions of La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_{6}$
text_ai: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. Systematic Ca doping ($x$ = 0–0.6) induces progressive B-site cation disorder while simultaneously modulating the Co–O–Ir superexchange pathway. High-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction combined with Rietveld refinement reveals a continuous suppression of long-range antiferromagnetic ordering accompanied by a monotonic increase in antisite defect concentration. Magnetic susceptibility and specific heat measurements demonstrate a systematic reduction in the Curie temperature from 185 K to 112 K, correlating directly with the fragmentation of coherent ferromagnetic networks. Muon spin rotation experiments further confirm the emergence of short-range correlated magnetic clusters and enhanced spin-glass-like freezing at elevated Ca concentrations. First-principles density functional theory calculations elucidate that this macroscopic deterioration originates from the disruption of the hybridized $t_{2g}^{5}(Co^{3+})$–$j_{eff}=1/2$(Ir$^{4+}$) bonding manifold. Specifically, increased structural distortion localizes the Ir $5d$ electrons, thereby weakening the itinerant-mediated exchange interaction that normally stabilizes the ferrimagnetic ground state. Concurrently, Ca-induced charge compensation generates high-spin Co$^{4+}$ configurations, which introduce competing frustrated exchange channels and amplify magnetic heterogeneity. The interplay between lattice strain and electronic localization ultimately suppresses the robust 3$d$–5$d$ alignment characteristic of the pristine compound. Notably, the experimentally extracted exchange constants align quantitatively with calculated superexchange integrals only when explicit antisite disorder is incorporated into the simulation cell. These findings establish a direct quantitative link between nanoscale structural perturbations and macroscopic magnetic decoherence in mixed-valence double perovskites. Our results provide critical design principles for engineering spin-orbit-coupled oxides where controlled disorder can be strategically leveraged to tune magneto-transport properties without compromising intrinsic quantum coherence.

title: CUNet: A Compact Unsupervised Network for Image Classification
text_ai: In this paper, we propose a compact network called CUNet (compact unsupervised network) to counter the image classification challenge. Different from the traditional convolutional neural networks learning filters by the time-consuming stochastic gradient descent, CUNet learns the filter bank from diverse image patches with the simple K-means, which significantly avoids the requirement of scarce labeled training images, reduces the training consumption, and maintains the high discriminative ability. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks demonstrate that CUNet achieves competitive classification accuracy while requiring substantially fewer computational resources than conventional supervised architectures. By eliminating iterative backpropagation and relying exclusively on unsupervised patch clustering, the framework facilitates rapid initialization and efficient inference. Quantitative evaluations across multiple visual recognition tasks reveal consistent performance parity with deep learning baselines, particularly within low-resource settings. Ablation studies confirm the stability of the K-means filter generation strategy under varying sampling densities. These results validate CUNet as a practical, annotation-free paradigm for scalable image analysis.

title: Bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty: secondary endpoints analyzed from a randomized trial comparing monoblock and modular tibia traysâ??2 year follow-up of 53 cases
text_ai: Background and purpose â?? Bone remodeling as a response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions can lead to loss of bone stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Fifty-three patients undergoing primary TKA were randomly assigned to receive either a monoblock or modular uncemented tibial component. Peri- and postoperative bone mineral density (BMD) changes were quantified using dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA) in seven Gruen zones at baseline, 6 weeks, 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years. Secondary endpoints included radiographic lucency, subsidence, knee society scores, and complication rates. Linear mixed-effects models assessed longitudinal BMD trajectories, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, and preoperative coronal alignment. All analyses adhered to intention-to-treat principles, with missing data handled via multiple imputation. At 2-year follow-up, both groups demonstrated significant early periprosthetic bone resorption in zones 1 and 7 (p < 0.01), consistent with stress-shielding. However, the modular cohort exhibited significantly greater BMD recovery in load-bearing zones 2, 3, and 4 compared with the monoblock group (mean difference: 4.8%; p = 0.008). Radiographic analysis revealed no clinically relevant subsidence (>2 mm) or progressive lucency in either arm. Clinical outcomes improved substantially and remained comparable between groups at final assessment (p = 0.31). No intraoperative fractures or early revisions occurred. Uncemented TKA triggers predictable early proximal tibial remodeling characterized by transient stress shielding followed by compensatory densitification. Modular tibia trays may mitigate long-term bone loss in critical weight-bearing regions without compromising clinical function. These DXA-derived endpoints support the biomechanical rationale for modularity in contemporary uncemented fixation strategies, warranting longer-term evaluation for implant survivorship and revision readiness in osteopenic populations.

title: Optoelectronic Fingerprints of Interference between Different Charge Carriers in Graphene Superlattices and Analogies to Twisted Graphene Bilayers
text_ai: Motivated by recent experimental findings on the low-energy spectrum of Kekul\'e-patterned graphene, the optoelectronic signatures of graphene superlattices with a spatial modulation that triples the size of the unit cell and folds the valleys to the center of the Brillouin zone are studied. Theoretical modeling based on a continuum Hamiltonian incorporating intervalley coupling elucidates how carrier hybridization governs the optical response near the folded Dirac cones. Calculations reveal pronounced absorption resonances arising from constructive interference between counter-propagating modes, which strongly modulate the frequency-dependent conductivity. Remarkably, these spectral features exhibit a periodic dependence on the modulation amplitude, closely mirroring the magic-angle phenomenology observed in twisted bilayer graphene. The emergence of narrow optical windows and van Hove singularities underscores the critical role of moiré-induced band folding in enhancing light-matter interactions. These results establish a direct theoretical bridge between Kekulé-distorted lattices and moiré quantum materials, offering a tunable platform for probing correlated electron dynamics and designing next-generation optoelectronic devices.

title: Efficient Computation in Adaptive Artificial Spiking Neural Networks
text_ai: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective. Still, ANNs lack a natural notion of time, and neural units in ANNs exchange analog values in a frame-based manner, a computationally and energetically inefficient form of communication. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) circumvent these limitations by processing information through discrete temporal events, enabling sparse, event-driven communication that closely mirrors biological systems. Despite their promise, widespread adoption of SNNs has been hindered by the difficulty of training deep architectures with biologically plausible learning rules and the computational overhead associated with simulating complex membrane dynamics. To address these bottlenecks, we introduce a novel framework for efficient computation in adaptive artificial spiking neural networks that integrates differentiable surrogate gradients with dynamic threshold adaptation. Specifically, we reformulate the neuron’s firing criterion as a continuous optimization landscape, permitting gradient-based refinement of excitatory-inhibitory balance during inference. Our approach eliminates redundant spike propagation through a learnable refractory mechanism and employs a hybrid update scheme that couples rapid local plasticity with periodic global error correction. A quantization-aware pruning strategy dynamically masks inactive synaptic pathways, further compressing the computational graph without degrading representational capacity. This architecture significantly reduces memory bandwidth requirements and enables fully asynchronous execution on neuromorphic substrates. We evaluate the proposed model across standard vision and audio recognition benchmarks, demonstrating competitive accuracy while reducing floating-point operations by up to 68% compared to conventional convolutional architectures. Energy consumption estimates, derived from simulations of standard hardware, indicate a fourfold improvement in throughput-per-watt. Furthermore, the adaptive component exhibits robustness to distributional shifts without requiring retraining or extensive hyperparameter tuning. These results establish a viable pathway toward temporally precise, resource-constrained machine intelligence, bridging the rigor of contemporary learning with the operational efficiency of spiking paradigms.
